Warframe lets you live your dreams of Playing a Robot Ninja Warrior Assassin.
This 3rd person Sci-Fi/Shooter/Hacker game Plays well after you get used to the controls, Just like any Game.
The Playstyle is Dynamic as it is entirely up to you (and/or your party) to decide how you play.
Go in Swords, Bows, Guns and other assorted weaponary blazing and messing up anything that you come across,
or Stealth. no kill (Like Metal Gear) and achieve your goal or mix it up do both. No single game has to be the same.
With a massive Selection of Warframes/Tenno, Weapons, Mods, Missions and more this game can easily get you to sink in
many hours without realszing and thinking that you want to do a bit more.
An active community that are 90% of the time very friendly and good to be around
And an active upto date Dev Team that put out Good content on the regular, bonus they have a good support team.
As it is a free game there are micro transactions which is a let down, but needed (DID I JUST SAY THAT!?)
you can buy in-game currency and items but they allow you to buy community items too.
but you dont have to do that, you can get Majoirty of the items just by playing or grinding if you want to build something enough, and anything you dont want you can trade or sell to other (For Platinum) making it truley Free.
Good Grahics with plenty of option to play it how you like. However the game can be pretty intensive at time, causing you PC to run a bit slow, especially if you have a low Spec PC.
Sound Effects fit very well and sound like what youd expect they should.
Music plays well with the game.
Overall for a free game the time you can put into it, the quality of game you get it is a very good game.
Fun to play by yourself you a short time and great with Friends
I do reccomend trying this game even if you are unsure about it. Why? Becuse it's free you have nothing to lose.

People who write reviews probably have a lot of gameplay time on this game, over 100 hours, but as if you are getting this game you will probably be a new player with no idea how to play and as I am still in early game myself I felt this might be helpful for the new players looking to get stuck in.
The game itslef is a MMO CO-OP shooter in which you and a squad, or just you solo, tackle missions in order to gather resources, progress the story and reach other planets. The game can be a bit overwhelming at first but as you progress through missions you will unlock various things on your ship, like the foundary where you build items, and through ranking up, new mods and weapons. The game does try to slowly introduce these to try and let them sink in but overall you might feel a little overwhelmed by them.
The community itself is nice enough but not very welcoming or helpful to new players despite the best efforts of the developers to make it so, if you do find youslef stuck or confused a forum or YouTube guide will probably be your best bet.
All in all if you're intrested by it then pick it up, it's free, what's stopping you?

This game, is by all means a fun game. It has a very competitive learning curve, and a ton of interesting things to do. By all means you should buy this game. But I warn you, there is one thing that will just, ruin the game for you. There is a specific dino, called a Troodon; they seem like they can't do much but let me assure you, they are the most broken dinosaur in the game, one, they are faster than Raptors, maybe even faster than a Rex, two they come in packs of around 3-6 give or take, three, they have a ridiculous health pool to the point where my level 65 Argentavis with 199.26% damage picked up a level 26 Troodon and had to hit it a good 18 times before it died, whereas an equivelant Stegosaurus, (which is twice the size of a Troodon mind you) Took roughly around 12 hits or so, and that's not even the worst part, when a Troodon hit's your tamed dinosaurs it drains their stamina, now one Troodon wouldn't cause any issue, but because the game has them in packs? Your Dinosaur is going to be drained of stamina insanely fast, and Stamina is required to sprint and attack, which means your Dinosaur is literally, defenseless. ONTOP of that though! These little guys cause your Topor to rise if they hit you! A good 3 hits and you can guarentee you're going to sleep for a while, and they'll just keep hitting you once your asleep too because well, they can, which means if you have any dinosaurs nearby that are on passive or the likes and you have nice armor? You get to watch your dinosaur which you put a lot of time and effort into get killed all because the developers of this game thought these Dinosaurs were a smart and valid choice to put in the game. A common answer to their topor is just 'Oh well, you just have to use Stimulant to stay awake while fighting them!" Well, tell me when you do that successfully because every time these things get near you they do a leap attack, and oh by the way in case you forgot? They come in packs so the odds of you being able to down that stimulant before your♥♥♥♥♥is snoring on the ground are slim to none because they'll just overpower the stimulant without a second thought, "Well just use a torch and they'll run away" That is true, you can just use a torch and make them run away! At nightime, good luck with that during the day though, because the just won't care at that point, trust me I've tested it, oh and by the way! At night their power doubles ten fold. Now, you're thinking 'Well, if they're so strong they probably don't spawn very often.' and let me tell you, you're more wrong than you've ever been, not only are Troodon's common, I dare say they're just as common as a dodo bird on a beach. I understand games are supposed to offer a challenge, and there are many challenges in this game, Alpha dinosaurs, taming a Rex or a Spino, these are all very challenging things for you to do, that guides will often tell you to exploit the AI a bit to tame some of these every once in a while because they're that challenging, (I'm going to add that Troodon's specifically target players, it's literally in their AI to do so, they will stop WHATEVER it is they're doing to attack you, and their aggro range is the furthest aggro range I've ever seen in a game.) The developers recently nerfed these guys reducing their health pool by a whopping %30 percent. It did nothing to stop the frustration. These dinosaur's are literally the most frustratingly broken thing in any game, ever, because unless you have the highest gear available, with the strongest mounts you can get. There is not a thing you can do to these dinosaurs, they will literally ruin your experience entirely. Should you buy the game? Yes, it's fantastic to play with friends, but I strongly urge you look up a guide for how to replace them in the files with a Dodo bird, or your experience will be over just as quick as it began.

Your Dinosaur is going to be drained of stamina insanely fast, and Stamina is required to sprint and attack, which means your Dinosaur is literally, defenseless. ONTOP of that though! These little guys cause your Topor to rise if they hit you! A good 3 hits and you can guarentee you're going to sleep for a while, and they'll just keep hitting you once your asleep too because well, they can, which means if you have any dinosaurs nearby that are on passive or the likes and you have nice armor? You get to watch your dinosaur which you put a lot of time and effort into get killed all because the developers of this game thought these Dinosaurs were a smart and valid choice to put in the game. A common answer to their topor is just 'Oh well, you just have to use Stimulant to stay awake while fighting them!" Well, tell me when you do that successfully because every time these things get near you they do a leap attack, and oh by the way in case you forgot? They come in packs so the odds of you being able to down that stimulant before your♥♥♥♥♥is snoring on the ground are slim to none because they'll just overpower the stimulant without a second thought, "Well just use a torch and they'll run away" That is true, you can just use a torch and make them run away! At nightime, good luck with that during the day though, because the just won't care at that point, trust me I've tested it, oh and by the way! At night their power doubles ten fold. Now, you're thinking 'Well, if they're so strong they probably don't spawn very often.' and let me tell you, you're more wrong than you've ever been, not only are Troodon's common, I dare say they're just as common as a dodo bird on a beach. I understand games are supposed to offer a challenge, and there are many challenges in this game, Alpha dinosaurs, taming a Rex or a Spino, these are all very challenging things for you to do, that guides will often tell you to exploit the AI a bit to tame some of these every once in a while because they're that challenging, (I'm going to add that Troodon's specifically target players, it's literally in their AI to do so, they will stop WHATEVER it is they're doing to attack you, and their aggro range is the furthest aggro range I've ever seen in a game.) The Good: Excellent fight mechanics, well designed maps, all four classes are fun to play as, great graphics and sound, fun modes
The Bad: Not enough content overall, some server instability, not enough classes, controls have a steep learning curve
While everyone is playing Black Ops II and Battlefield 3 there is a little multiplayer game called Chivalry: Medieval Warfare. This knight-in-shining-armor online only game pits players against each other and lets them have at it with deadly swords, crossbows, flaming pots, shields, and various other Camelot era weapons. This is a different multiplayer game and will keep you hooked for dozens of hours.
There’s no story here at all so don’t worry about that, this game doesn’t need a story. You open up the game and you are greeted with a server list. There’s a tutorial that shows you the ropes of this game. There’s a bit more to it than just swinging around weapons. Each one has range, damage, and speed that you have to think about. In a small arena you probably want a short and fast weapon, while the more open maps you should use a javelin and a giant polearm. There are three basic attacks which are overhead, side to side, and jab swings. You can feint attacks as well to trick your opponent which is a key move you have to learn to master. You block, but you have to time it and you can’t just block aimlessly. You have to be looking at the weapon or the block won’t really connect. This is really a knight simulator and the game is just so much fun.
It doesn’t stop there though, there are some projectiles. The bow is great to use and has an arrow cam which helps you adjust your aim. There’s also a crossbow but reloading is very slow and you can’t see around you when reloading. Larger classes get axes to throw, while smaller ones get knives and daggers. I found a strategy where I’d use up my projectiles and try to get in some kills that way before going in. There are 4 classes, Man-at-Arms, Knight, Vanguard, and Archer. The Vanguard is the biggest class and can kill in just a couple of hits but is extremely slow. He, and the Man-at-Arms, have a charging attack that will devastate anyone in its path. If you use a kite shield with these classes it protects you from rear attacks which is actually how I died the most. I would be battling an enemy and I’d get creamed by two guys coming up from behind that I couldn’t see or hear.
Some levels have traps in them that you can activate to help your team or whittle down someone’s health before going in for the kill. Each class is a lot of fun to play and I found myself constantly switching between them unlike other multiplayer games. I just wish there were more classes. Four isn’t all that much, and there aren’t enough maps. Torn Banner is putting out free content, but it’s been slow coming since release last year. However, I still find myself coming back and playing a few rounds at least once a week, the game is very addictive.
The game modes are also lacking. There’s just Team Deathmatch, Free-for-All (Deathmatch), Capture the Flag, and Dueling which is 1v1. There are a couple more, but these are typical modes found in other games. One mode that is unique to this game is a siege type mode where you use battering rams, trebuchets, and various other long-range siege weapons to break into the enemy’s fortress and take it over. That is probably the most fun. On one map my team was trying to push a battering ram through a small village. We were trying to fight off the other team and it was a constant back and forth. Once we got to the front doors their archers made easy work of the battering team because their moat didn’t allow us to surround the team and defend them. We just had to do archer battles or hang back and wait for people to come out.
As it stand, Chivalry has proven to be a very popular and well made multiplayer game. The graphics are fantastic and everything looks superb. Hopefully Torn Banner can continue to dole out new content to make players happy and continue playing.
--Score: 8/10

You'd think 2K hours, probably spending almost that much money in this game (Maybe more.) and being one of the founders of the game would mean that I love it to death?
I did until the Devs changed a bunch of stuff, and started showing signs of bias and corruption within the community.
Good game at its core, albeit pay-to-skip. Has a decent, high octane combat system. It's a great power fantasy game, extremely fun. Gets a bit boring and grindy because you have to farm materials and pieces of gear based on RNG.
I personally don't feel like the Devs listen or care much. They've made many changes I'm not a fan of (In fact, I know a few people who hate the changes more than I do.), and if I ever go back to the game? I refuse to spend another cent on it.
Also, the community drama scene on Youtube with a certain Youtuber who I can't name because Digital Extremes often ban people just for even mentioning his name, being associated with him, or whatever.  Just shows how corrupt the developers are since they banned him for doing stuff that their Youtube partners do all of the time, yet they don't get banned. One of them even said on Stream that his fans and the other Warframe YT partners should send a hate mob to this unnamed YT'rs channel. Of course, after he got called out on this (Probably got a finger wagging from Digital Extremes), he tried to take down all evidence of the stream. Classy.
Oh, and new content becomes increasingly more difficult to get, as well as suffers from power creepage.
An example: A lot of the new Warframes and weapons require this stuff called Nitain extract. You often need a lot of this stuff just to build this new content, but you can only get it when a mission has been modified into a special kind of mission (Kind of like how it works with the new Relic system) called "Alert Missions" which only pop up for a few minutes or hours, depending.
Whilst I used to just buy the new stuff since I hate farming, my friends would often complain about how irritating it is to get Nitain simply because the alerts randomly decide when you're allowed to obtain it. You would often need a lot of it too, from my limited understanding, and that's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥.
The game also lacks endgame content. Once you have everything, there's just nothing to do other than help friends grind for the stuff that you got before them or w/e. This game will get boring very fast for you if you've sunk a lot of time and/or money into it.
*EDIT*
I should mention the new prime part system, in my opinion? Sucks.
It used to be that you would do a level that needed an easy to get key, getting the key and finishing the levels wasn't hard nor did it ever take long. When you finished the level, you would randomly get either a prime part, blueprints, or rare materials based on RNG rolls.
Now? You have to get these stupid relic keys, wait for an alert (kind of like Nitain) that has the class/level of relic that you need for the part that is in the specific drop table that the relic has. THEN you have to not only complete the standard level in its entirety, but you also have to do an annoying and needlessly finnicky minigame where you kill waves of enemies until you grab enough orb things to unlock the relic.  Needless change.
The only good thing about the changes in this is that everyone usually gets different parts, and if a squadmate gets something you wanted, but you got something nobody in your squad wanted, you can pick what your squadmate got for free, and he/she would still get their own copy.

Here are the ingredients you will need!
Ravioli Dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 pinch salt, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 2 eggs, 1 1/2 tablespoons water.
Ravioli Filling: 1 (8 ounce) container ricotta cheese, 1 (4 ounce) package cream cheese, softened, 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, 1/2 cup provolone cheese, shredded, 1 egg, 1 1/2 teaspoons dried parsley.
Pesto-Alfredo Cream Sauce: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 cloves garlic, crushed, 3 tablespoons prepared basil pesto sauce, 2 cups heavy cream, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 (24 ounce) jar marinara sauce.
1. Mound the flour and salt together on a work surface and form a well. Beat the teaspoon of olive oil, 2 eggs, and water in a bowl. Pour half the egg mixture into the well. Begin mixing the egg with the flour with one hand; use your other hand to keep the flour mound steady. Add the remaining egg mixture and knead to form a dough.
2. Knead the dough until smooth, 8 to 10 minutes; add more flour if the dough is too sticky. Form the dough into a ball and wrap tightly with plastic. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
3. While the dough is resting, prepare the ravioli filling. Combine the ricotta cheese, cream cheese, mozzarella cheese, provolone cheese, egg, and parsley and mix well. Set the filling aside.
4. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and pesto sauce and cook for one minute. Pour in the heavy cream, raise the heat to high, and bring the sauce to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the Parmesan cheese and stir until the cheese melts. Remove the pan from the heat and keep warm.
5. Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, warm the marinara sauce over medium-low heat.
6. Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Beat the egg with the tablespoon of water to make the egg wash.
7. Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets no thicker than a nickel. To assemble the ravioli, brush the egg wash over a sheet of pasta. Drop the filling mixture on the dough by teaspoonfuls about one inch apart. Cover the filling with the top sheet of pasta, pressing out the air from around each portion of filling. Press firmly around the filling to seal. Cut into individual ravioli with a knife or pizza cutter. Seal the edges.
8. Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the ravioli, and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the ravioli float to the top and the filling is hot, 4 to 8 minutes. Drain well.
9. Grease a baking sheet. Place the cooked ravioli on the sheet pan and bake in the preheated oven until brown, about 4 minutes.
10. To serve the ravioli, divide them among four warmed serving bowls. Drizzle the marinara sauce over the ravioli and then top with the cream sauce.

I have a love/hate relationship with Chivalry. On the one hand, I never tire of it. Combat is simple to grasp but offers layers of complexity, especially once you learn the etiquette of fighting within the community. On the other, the learning curve can be steep, especially now that many players are tough-as-nails rank 40+ that will kill you with ease.
If you do get into Chivalry you'll quickly see that weapons do unlock rather quickly, being about 100 kills to unlock a tier set (as I remember it, could be different these days!). The game doesn't push on you items to unlock or achievements to earn (although they are there) this falls into the Counter Strike style of multi-player, in that it's about the skill of the combat and the thrill of the fight and the heart in mouth euphoria of a fantastic victory. This can lead of moments of utter joy or complete anger but if you like skill based combat, then this is for you.

The conclusion from my review of Chivalry: Medieval Warfare over at TCXS.co.uk:
The game looks impressive and latency or lag is rarely noticeable in my experience, making this a fun experience to boot up if you have a spare half-hour and fancy pumping some adrenaline. However, beyond that it lacks replayability as matches tend be the same experiences. I have to make the comparison to Call of Duty titles, as they feel similar in terms of booting it up for a quick blast before finding something else to do.
To conclude, this is an excellent game for half of the price of a new AAA release, and is made by a developer worthy of your money and support. The visual and audio assets are high quality and never fail to please.
You'll like-
The high quality production
The drop-in, drop-out nature of game lobbies (with dedicated servers)
The general gore (it adds to the experience... Trust me)
You'll Dislike-
The grind to get better weapons, as well as the definite difference between effectiveness of upgrades
The connection issues to servers on busy nights
Eventually becomes a boring routine if played for excessive amounts of time

I really wanted to make sure there was a review up that captures the nuances of this game.
Too long won't read: The game has balancing issues that are constantly being sorted out but the mechanics of the game are a rewarding for those willing and able to master them.
The premise of the game is simple, take a fictionalized medieval battlefield and fill it with PC gamers in a COD-like multiplayer. The DLC "Chivalry: Deadliest Warrior" expands this to just about any culture that has picked up a sword including: Spartans, Pirates (Caribbean, not Somali), and Ninjas. And similar to COD, the game has the multitude of game-modes that you would expect: team death match, free-for-all, capture the hill, a dueling mode, etc. Likewise there is a meta-game that allows the player to unlock variations of weapons, for example kill enough people with a spear and you will unlock a quicker, shorter, less powerful pitchfork.
The gameplay is straightforward but deep. You click your mouse and your weapon swings, chops, or thrusts, and if it hits the opposing player then you damage them depending on hit location. The damage is done as a HP bar and any kind of maiming is done post-mortem or on the killing blow. Ranged weapons can be used but leave the archer/crossbowman/javelin thrower to rely on their short sword or dagger as backup. Blocking enemy attacks drains the player's stamina meter and so does missing your own attacks, this incentizives the players to dodge their enemy while aggressively and accurately attacking.
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare also divides the players into classes that have different perks and weapon selections. Archers can do bonus damage when attacking a player's backside. Men-At-Arms allow for shield-wielding players to quickly dodge attacks at the expense of stamina. Vanguards can use long spears and polearms to charge in with a powerful attack if they have sprinted long enough. And Knights have the highest health, lowest stamina consumption from blocking, and slow but powerful weapons such as a double-sided axe or a maul.
All in all the narrative is almost non-existant. There are two factions that use different taunts and colors, but the game does not go much futher than that. The setting is meant is meant to be a European-inspired fictional world, but raises quite a few questions: Is this a male-only society or species? Why are there crosses, a Christian symbol, in the architecture if this is a non-historical setting? However this is only a minor grievance as this a multiplayer game and thus most people hold it to a lower narrative standard.
The meta-game aspect seems to be less thought-out than one would hope. It only rewards players for kills and thus there is little reason to play the objective or assist a teammate in a kill. And players who feel compelled to unlock all of the weapons are also forced to muster through weapons they have little skill in or desire to use, this can create a grinding experience that just does not work when the gameplay is this engaging.
The gameplay's simplicity is perhaps its greatest strength. There is a great sense of satisfaction from ducking and aiming down as your opponent's blade swings over your head and allowing you to counter with a deadly chop to the head, or swinging your powerful warhammer into your opponent's shield and sending him or her into a spike pit. Moments like these make the game a delight to play and elevate it above the simple meta-game driven Skinner Boxes of other multiplayer games.

Chivalry is a First Person Slasher, It's fun to play and can get very competitive.
I advice you the next, the game is no different than playing CS 1.6, you cannot level up anything, you can choose 1 of 4 classes, get a weapon of choice, pick a server from the list and start killing dudes. There is a single player training, but it's short and under-developed. This game is meant for only multiplayer.
Pros: The combat system is very well design, you need pure skill to win, you can enter a map, and have a intense 1vs 1 with another player, or you can be almighty, defeating 4 opponents at a time. Dodging, Parrying, blocking, hitting and moving across the fields is not done with one button, you will need a lot of practice to get the skill you need to get things right!
Cons: The servers are not hosted by Torn Banner, they are hosted by people, so you will get the Counter Strike server experience. There is no easy way to  get a group of friends, make a party and start a game, you need a server. There is not barrier between a new player and a skilled player, you get what you get, and if you are a begginner, you will get your face splitted in two. There is no built in voice chat, just plain old text on the corner. There is also no AI (no bots), so you cannot make a map for yourself (or play offline) to practice.

If you find yourself not able to enjoy games like you used to: try this game. It's a progression based game, where you get stronger and stronger the longer/more you play. But the thing that makes this game different is how it handles farming.
It's really weird, cause the Clicker Heroes does almost everything for you except upgrading your army. It truly gives you this feeling of progression even if you aren't actively playing it. Although, I do sometimes sit and play this game actively for hours, you could play literally 10 seconds and then do something else without feeling weird about it, because the game will still farm for you. And the way the devs calcuated the progression difficulty is nothing but perfect. Will you farm/wait to get that new upgrade to get to a new zone? Or will you "ascend" (new game+ functionality) to build up your strength with the perks given when you ascend and beat new zones that way?
Clicker Heroes just does everything right, even the micro-transaction part. You can't buy anything with real money that you couldn't buy with the in-game currency that you earn while playing the game. And you earn this currency at a rather good rate, such that you don't feel the need to buy anything for real money - ever. Therefore, you will not feel gimped/punished about your progression.

The first time that I booted up Chivalry, I was excited. I had been waiting for a good, first person combat game for ages. What I didn't expect was how terrified I was. The spectacle of this game is incredible. Blood and limbs fly, knights yell excitedly for blood, and scream bloody-murder when hit. It was the first few moments of every combat that had me coming back for more. Imagine if you were put into the same situation as the knights in this game. I bet you would take the gamble of modern combat over medieval warfare any day of the week.
The graphics are incredible. The colors are vibrant, and the lighting pops. Everything looks smooth and proper, from the character models to the buildings. The animations are nice too- not to mention all of the dismemberment! The gameplay is very tight, although the learning curve for first time players is very high. One has to balance light/ heavy attacks with blocking and kicking. The system creates an interesting rock-paper-scissors mechanic- which I periodically forgot when attacked by more than one soldier. It's great fun! Tied together with several classic FPS game modes, and interesting maps, I'd say that Chivalry is the perfect game for any FPS or action game enthusiast. 8.25/10

So this is my first review on steam.
---
Note: For the whole of this review, I'm not going to blame everything on exploits and cheaters. There are already a lot of bad reviews going this path (also, take a look on reddit for more on this topic). And as I'm a casual gamer, playing a couple hours every couple days (mostly singleplayer as I recently gave up multiplayer), I'm not really affected by those.
---
I must say I really enjoy playing ARK. It has so many ways to be played, you can PvE, PvP, play single or multiplayer, just care to build up and tame, while exploring caves or take the challenge to keep your small kingdom healthy on PVP Official Servers, while raiding and joining tribes.
I've played enough to say it has plenty of bugs, but we can sort of live with them. They are annoying, sometimes even making you lose a good amount of hours due to dinos escaping through the floor or someone exploiting their way into your base. But that's ok... we are aware of most of the bugs and can just go with it.
But lately things got a bit too annoying for my taste. I gave up solo playing on Official Servers, PvE or PvP.
On PvE it is basically impossible to find a good spot due to people spamming stone pilars all around the map. It is really frustrating to find a place even to fit a small 1 by 1. And all the magic of the amazing landscape is also gone by all those pilars placed everywhere. On top of that, the spawns are disabled due to the proximity of those pilars, so you have less resources and dinos to interact with. And despite being PvE, there are some people that agro specific dinos and bring them to your base, just so they can destroy everything while you are afk. Happened to me once and it is not a pleasant surprise to login and find your (supposedly safe) PvE base destroyed. Maybe the offline raid protection fixed this, but I'm not sure.
On PvP you just can't play solo. Unless you are like those PvP youtubers (eg. Kishkoo) that only use 20% of what the game has to offer, and only care to raid, not taming anything nor gathering resources. These people can have a good amount of fun. But if you do plan to raise dinos, grow a small farm, tame endless creatures and build your nice tiny kingdom, then I'm going to save you some hours and say you're better off playing singleplayer. On Official Servers, if you are solo, you WILL be wiped almost every single day. You will go to sleep, come back the next day only to find most of what you have was blown up or killed. ARK's PvP is not for casual gamers. You MUST join an active tribe. By active I mean that you really need at least a couple people online around the clock, otherwise your whole tribe will be wiped while afk.
About a month ago I gave up on multiplayer after having my entire base blown up and all my dinos killed for the 20th time. Now I'm only playing singleplayer. It is fun and for my style of ARK it is being fun and I'm enjoying it. But... also in the singleplayer safe heaven there are downsides. Endless updates every couple days, some 100MB, some 1.8 or 3.5GB, summing up to 100GB+ of your disk. Not a real problem, you may say. And I agree with you, it is not an issue for most people. But for the casual game as myself, whose only wish is to play 1 or 2 hours before bed, this is annoying. I have a couple hours left on my day, so I turn on the computer, open steam only to find that there's a 1 hour long update waiting for me. I only wanted to play ARK. That's all I ask for. This is happening too often and is really getting annoying.
Only buy this game if you plan to really invest time in it. Playing 8h+ every day while maitaining a good relationship with every tribe on your server. Even those who play every day have issues, just Youtube for "GTJack3d" and check a few of his recent videos (July 2017). In July 2017 his ginourmous base was blown up by exploiters. And he did have a bunch of tribe mates. Even that wasn't enough to avoid it.
Overall it is a good game though. 6/10.
I'm going to say I'm not recommending it as there are many moving parts that, when combined, could give a way better outcome than in its actual state. Not sure if I would refer ARK to a friend.
Edit:
The last patch just reset my singleplayer settings... If you're going to buy it, get used to this kind of crap.

Personally I do enjoy this game and while this game certainly does have its ups and downs, I am not here to praise or criticize this game. I am here to offer a phenomenal 4 Cheese Ravioli recipe!
Here are the ingredients you will need!
Ravioli Dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 pinch salt, 1 teaspoon olive oil, 2 eggs, 1 1/2 tablespoons water.
Ravioli Filling: 1 (8 ounce) container ricotta cheese, 1 (4 ounce) package cream cheese, softened, 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese, 1/2 cup provolone cheese, shredded, 1 egg, 1 1/2 teaspoons dried parsley.
Pesto-Alfredo Cream Sauce: 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 cloves garlic, crushed, 3 tablespoons prepared basil pesto sauce, 2 cups heavy cream, 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, 1 (24 ounce) jar marinara sauce.
1. Mound the flour and salt together on a work surface and form a well. Beat the teaspoon of olive oil, 2 eggs, and water in a bowl. Pour half the egg mixture into the well. Begin mixing the egg with the flour with one hand; use your other hand to keep the flour mound steady. Add the remaining egg mixture and knead to form a dough.
2. Knead the dough until smooth, 8 to 10 minutes; add more flour if the dough is too sticky. Form the dough into a ball and wrap tightly with plastic. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
3. While the dough is resting, prepare the ravioli filling. Combine the ricotta cheese, cream cheese, mozzarella cheese, provolone cheese, egg, and parsley and mix well. Set the filling aside.
4. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and pesto sauce and cook for one minute. Pour in the heavy cream, raise the heat to high, and bring the sauce to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the Parmesan cheese and stir until the cheese melts. Remove the pan from the heat and keep warm.
5. Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, warm the marinara sauce over medium-low heat.
6. Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Beat the egg with the tablespoon of water to make the egg wash.
7. Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets no thicker than a nickel. To assemble the ravioli, brush the egg wash over a sheet of pasta. Drop the filling mixture on the dough by teaspoonfuls about one inch apart. Cover the filling with the top sheet of pasta, pressing out the air from around each portion of filling. Press firmly around the filling to seal. Cut into individual ravioli with a knife or pizza cutter. Seal the edges.
8. Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the ravioli, and return to a boil. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the ravioli float to the top and the filling is hot, 4 to 8 minutes. Drain well.
9. Grease a baking sheet. Place the cooked ravioli on the sheet pan and bake in the preheated oven until brown, about 4 minutes.
10. To serve the ravioli, divide them among four warmed serving bowls. Drizzle the marinara sauce over the ravioli and then top with the cream sauce.

TL:DR The game is well worth the $$. There are hundreds of hours of excitement and fun, even with the issues it has. Yes there are issues, yes its more fun with friends. Lastly, avoid the official servers if youre new. Pick a unofficial with a good ping and start making friends.
Now for the long story:
People are bandwagoning against this game because there are bugs that haven’t been fixed. I get it, we all want the bugs resolved. There are several things about the game that are annoying. Some of them cost you hours, days, weeks of your time spent just to start over. Yet you choose to spend your time that way. It was at least reasonably enjoyable while you were doing it or else you wouldn’t have done it in the first place.
You should look at this game as a source of entertainment. Look at the number of hours you’re getting out of the amount of money you’re spending compared to many other forms of entertainment. When you look at the return on investment these people have gotten out of the game, it’s a very good deal for the entertainment value.
For example, to go to the theater in the US here you’re going to pay ~$10 for a ticket to a 1.5-3hour movie and then you’re done. that return on investment is between $3-5/hour of enjoyment.
Going out to dinner at a decent place is going to cost you between $20-40/person, and you’re going to get maybe 5-8 hours of feeling full out of that. even at $20 for 8 hours, you’re looking at $2.5/hour of return for your investment.
I have 1300 hours in this game, at $60 US I’ve payed barely $0.045/hour played. For me that return on investment is well worth the price.
Now others might say "But were you really enjoying every minute you were playing. I bet there was some parts of that time you were annoyed as hell!" and to that I say,
You’re correct, there were several moments where I was annoyed at a glitch that cost me a prized T-Rex, and getting stuck in an alpha rex that cost me a perfect tame quetzal. Yet overall I was having fun with the game. I don’t always enjoy every second of every movie I watch. Yet I don’t hate the movie because a few minutes weren’t pure bliss. I don’t always love every piece of food on my plate, but I don’t hate the steak because the carrots weren’t cooked correctly."
The point im making is that this game overall is a world of fun and excitement that i think many people take for granted because you've had several hundred hours of it. You've forgotten the wonder of waking up on that beach for the first time and getting eaten immediately by a dilo only to respawn and think "what the hell was that." The excitement of being chased by a T-Rex through the jungle for the first time on your only raptor, hoping to god that it doesn’t catch you. There is so many hours of fun in this game that we've all experienced already that new players haven’t yet had a chance to. I’m sure that if you start to look at your money-to-hours ratio you’ll find that this game has given you more than its fair share.
Now I’m not saying the devs are off the hook for fixing the issues that this game has. Of course they need to fix things. They need to optimize things. They need to balance things. However, that doesn’t mean that this game isn’t worth getting. That means we need to continue to post of the bug forums, the idea forums, and let them know what the player base wants. Not drive new players away because we've forgotten all the fun we had when we first started.
If you've read this far, thanks. Hopefully you'll pick up a copy of the game and maybe I'll see you playing sometime.

This is a pretty fun survival experience with a long tech tree that I've never gotten to the end of. You will probably enjoy this game if you like survival games. However, if you play on a public server, at some point you will get wiped by an "Alpha Tribe," a group that has huge numbers with no real way to oppose them. I will tenatively thumb this up, but I bought this a long time ago, when it was much cheaper.

If your wondering how to obtain certain warframes or weapons there are wikis designed to walk you through each individual task.  There are mountains of things to unlock as well as do.
Pros:
-An expanding release of Warframes and weapons insures that this game is always different.
-Story mission releases insure that the storyline continues and that your interest isn't always in farming.
-Great graphics with fun physics allow you to move at an extremely fast rate.
-Levels are random, this means that replaying some missions will offer a new experience each time.
-Updates are frequent and bug fixes come quite often.
Cons:
-Grind, grind and grind.  Some items require you to spend days and even weeks farming for some materials.
-Interface needs some work, its hard to navigate to see what items you currently hold as well as to find out what type of currency you have forcing you to navigate several windows to find what your looking for.
-Spending 30 minutes on a level only to have the host leave can at points kick you from the match giving you 0 items.  I have even had my internet drop out on some missions that take quite a bit of time to do causing you to lose the mission and get nothing for your time spent.
-Buggy, often joining groups of people or missions will result in an auto cancel forcing you to go through 3 or 4 more menues to que back up for relic missions.  Its also hard to invite or join friends because at times it gives you error messages doing so.
-Huge learning curve.  What items do you equipt and what warframe do you go after and how?  What are relics?  What are profile levels what are formas and so on, this game can leave you in a state of confusion which can result in some players giving up early.
Just remember that if you have any questions there are answers out there and wikis set up to give you direction.  Its a wonderful game and worth checking out.

Since everyone is coming at this this from all directions with such wildly different expectations, it seems important to mention where I was coming from. I've had this game in my library for a long time now, playing it on and off as updates piled up. At the time I was looking for a single player survival/crafting/exploration game with an open world, decent graphics and lots of content to discover. As I played over the years the updates have been plentiful and timely, and the development process has been transparent enough for my purposes. The devs have largely delivered, aside from some growing pains that in my experience are perfectly reasonable within the limits of early access. I am highly allergic to gamer drama, so I haven't been following any news or community developments. I'm coming at this from a strictly singleplayer, casual, EA-experienced position.
WITH THAT SAID
Ark really has delivered on everything I personally wanted from it so far. For people who enjoy this sort of open world base building and exploration game, I'd say it's a must. (Or it will be after release, read on.) There's an impressive amount of customizability that makes playing single player a perfectly valid option. (For example, if you don't have an entre tribe to take shifts watching an egg until it hatches, you can simply set the hatching timer to a more manageable length and do it forever alone.) This does not strike me as one of those games that slaps a token single player label on what is essentially an MMO with some vestigal SP bits. There is no campaign, but there is base building and exploration and dinosaur taming, so I'm not complaining.
So far I've found the base building system fun and easy to use. Unlocking building and tool plans with level progression gives you something to work towards even without goals set by a campaign. I haven't explored all of it, not wanting to burn myself out on the game before release, but I've spent more hours than I thought I had simply building tree forts and palling around with my stego buddy chopping wood for my sunroom. It's quite relaxing until a raptor sneaks up on your interior designing♥♥♥♥♥to remind you that this is still a dinosaur survival game.
The modding community is robust and creative. If there's something the core game doesn't offer, chances are the workshop will.
I hope I've made it clear that I can't speak to the online component. I've taken a look at the community from afar, heard a lot of histrionics about alpha tribes and how the devs eat kittens tail-first, and I backed off again. I prefer my dinosaur island quiet and pristine.
So I would be playing this game around the clock if it wasn't for the poor optimization. Again, this is early access and the devs have their own priorities. Right now it's near unplayable until you turn the pretty graphics waaaay down. I'm playing on a mid-level rig, nothing fancy but no slouch either, and by the time the game is playable at a decent framerate (and I'm no twitch gamer, anything above 25 is fine by me) it looks remarkably like Turok. 1997 Turok.
Again, it's early access. It's weird that optimization is happening so late in the process, but it's within the limits the devs have set for themselves. While I wouldn't be surprised to see the launch date pushed back, I'm not complaining.
So all in all, great content, lousy optimizations, I am scared of online players. HIGHLY recommended to people who enjoy the singleplayer crafting/survival/exploration genre.

Perhaps it's the quantity of hours which I've spent playing Chivalry, but it's transcended the left click spamathon which it initially appeared to me. Duel is the true saving grave of this game, allowing genuine skill and experience to shine out. Against an equal or superior opponent, the combat is gloriously stressful, being slowly beaten back, watching your stamina bar diminish and diminish. Timing is vital, as well as footwork and positioning - being an inch out of range can make or break a duel. Duelling against an inferior opponent is pure satisfaction in gaming form, the initial charge towards your opponent with the smug knowledge that they are already a dead man walking is glorious. Throwing in a few cheerful apologetic emotes, and with one final swing, slash, smash, tear, stab, punch, kick, or maniacal laugh, you annihilate your opponent and cast him down before you. *Rematch*

Since everyone is coming at this this from all directions with such wildly different expectations, it seems important to mention where I was coming from. I've had this game in my library for a long time now, playing it on and off as updates piled up. At the time I was looking for a single player survival/crafting/exploration game with an open world, decent graphics and lots of content to discover. As I played over the years the updates have been plentiful and timely, and the development process has been transparent enough for my purposes. The devs have largely delivered, aside from some growing pains that in my experience are perfectly reasonable within the limits of early access. I am highly allergic to gamer drama, so I haven't been following any news or community developments. I'm coming at this from a strictly singleplayer, casual, EA-experienced position.
WITH THAT SAID
Ark really has delivered on everything I personally wanted from it so far. For people who enjoy this sort of open world base building and exploration game, I'd say it's a must. (Or it will be after release, read on.) There's an impressive amount of customizability that makes playing single player a perfectly valid option. (For example, if you don't have an entre tribe to take shifts watching an egg until it hatches, you can simply set the hatching timer to a more manageable length and do it forever alone.) This does not strike me as one of those games that slaps a token single player label on what is essentially an MMO with some vestigal SP bits. There is no campaign, but there is base building and exploration and dinosaur taming, so I'm not complaining.
So far I've found the base building system fun and easy to use. Unlocking building and tool plans with level progression gives you something to work towards even without goals set by a campaign. I haven't explored all of it, not wanting to burn myself out on the game before release, but I've spent more hours than I thought I had simply building tree forts and palling around with my stego buddy chopping wood for my sunroom. It's quite relaxing until a raptor sneaks up on your interior designing♥♥♥♥♥to remind you that this is still a dinosaur survival game.
The modding community is robust and creative. If there's something the core game doesn't offer, chances are the workshop will.
I hope I've made it clear that I can't speak to the online component. I've taken a look at the community from afar, heard a lot of histrionics about alpha tribes and how the devs eat kittens tail-first, and I backed off again. I prefer my dinosaur island quiet and pristine.
So I would be playing this game around the clock if it wasn't for the poor optimization. Again, this is early access and the devs have their own priorities. Right now it's near unplayable until you turn the pretty graphics waaaay down. I'm playing on a mid-level rig, nothing fancy but no slouch either, and by the time the game is playable at a decent framerate (and I'm no twitch gamer, anything above 25 is fine by me) it looks remarkably like Turok. 1997 Turok.
Again, it's early access. It's weird that optimization is happening so late in the process, but it's within the limits the devs have set for themselves. While I wouldn't be surprised to see the launch date pushed back, I'm not complaining.
So all in all, great content, lousy optimizations, I am scared of online players. HIGHLY recommended to people who enjoy the singleplayer crafting/survival/exploration genre.

Baby Sitter Simulator designed to keep you coming back every 10 minutes in the hopes that your annoyance and frustration will eventually lead you to spending real cash to advance.
I had most of my summer off from college, so I decided to dig in and give this game a real try (hence the hours played even though I'm complaining).
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1) Math Simulator ... game is nothing more then an exponential diffuclty curve being attacked by a linear progress curve (straight line). Google up "linear vs. exponential" to get an idea how this quickly becomes unfair.
2) Glorified Spreadsheet ... the interface is just a list of heroes, ancients, etc. The game could literally work just fine without the "combat window" showing enemies, gold flying in the air, etc. You're playing a glorified spreadsheet running a math simulation.
3) Addiction Triggers ... Game is designed to get certain folks hooked; folks that get off on attainment or the feeling of "one more (progress)" in the hopes that they will eventually get the upper-hand. To keep progressing against the exponential difficulty, you upgrade your linear attack curve by buying upgrades. You buy these upgrades via gold, and the gold racks up in linear fashion, too (eg: you get X gold per hit point you take off an enemy). These upgrades get HUGE over time (eg: +1000000% damage, next hero does 100x more damage, etc). This triggers some peoples' "happy" response in that they get a sense of attainment; like they're gaining power over the game. But, again, all this does is slowly raise your linear progress curve in the hopes that it can perhaps compete with the obscenely-escalating exponential difficulty curve that's quickly blowing it out of the water. You stalemate at an area. You buy a new hero or upgrade something to get an additional +1000000% damage ... sounds great! Then you realize all that does it let you progress another 10 stages. Whooopee.
4) Cheating Placebo ... the game is designed to use auto-clickers from the start. That's why there's achievements for clicking up to 40x/second. So, go ahead and cheat, because your arrogance gets you playing the game more.
5) No Ending ... Eventually you reach a level where the variable that stores enemy health can't handle such a high number. Instead of crashing, or tossing up a "you win" screen, the game has a built-in fail-safe that a) puts "InfiniK" for enemy health, and b) disregards all damage you do from then on. This is  around level 4200 or so. So, the only "satisfaction" you get from the end-game is by hitting a point where you could have broken it in 80's arcade game fashion (eg: Donkey Kong), but the game was designed to not break. You just stare at this screen watching the game mock you as it has the last laugh. This is hollow, and makes you realize how pointless the countless hours you put into the game really are.
6) Time Slave ... Everything is designed to bring you back every 10 minutes like a crack w#0r3. If you let the game sit for a day, you rack up a lot of gold... just to find out it only levels your heroes up enough to progress a few more areas. So, you need to micromanage them to level them up as they can, that way they're not wasting time grinding low levels for paltry amounts of gold. There's also active skills that cooldown; need to come back in a few minutes to use them again. There's clickable items that can get you rubies or skill use without cooldown, so need to watch for those... This is a never-ending cycle, and as your linear progress starts hitting the exponential difficulty wall, it becomes more and more of a baby-sitting job as you try to micro-manage everything. If I just get a little more gold to level-up this hero, or hire the next one, or wait a bit for that skill to cooldown, it'll just take a minute ... (look up at clock) ... holy cow I've been sitting here for two hours! Ok, I'll leave it alone. (10 minutes later). I need to check in to make sure my heroes can progress! (never ending cycle)
7) Free To Play ... ultimately they want you to spend cash in a store. They sucker you into this store after you click on a little fish that gives you a ruby. What are these rubies for? In the store, if you get 50 Rubies, and you can buy some awesome stuff ... for free without spending money! ZOMG! Aren't you clever! No, you're not. You'd literally need to camp the game the entire day to get 50 rubies, so, again, the game has you become it's time slave. Or... you could pay some cash to get Rubies. Then you realize game insults you with "$100 = 1300 Rubies" purchase options. Let that sink in ... it's a flash game ... that has an option to spend $100 on it. That's ludicrous. And those rubies barely make a dent in the game. You'd need to spend THOUSANDS of dollars on the game to make any appreciable progress. Like a casino game, you plop down tons of cash thinking you're hot ****, then in the blink of an eye you hit the deadwall of the exponential difficulty curve once again... and realize you're back to square one. Except your wallet is a lot lighter.
8) IT'S A MINI GAME ... Hit a deadwall? You can do a soft reset to start over called an "ascension". This lets you keep certain gear you found / bought in previous games, and it lets you cash in hero levels for Hero Souls. So, you're not really ascending... you're descending ... back to level 1. After you do this multiple times, you quickly realize that the hero levelling & monster fighting is actually a mini game. A long-winded "mini game", but a mini-game nonetheless. The REAL game is you going through that "mini game" countless times to collect Hero Souls to upgrade ancient artifacts to see if you can make a tiny bit more progress in the "mini game" next time you run it. So, again, you have to baby-sit the game until you hit a deadwall, then "ascend" to start the game over to cash in and get Hero Souls. Otherwise your heroes spend forever staring at a deadwall.
I'm not even joking about #7 ... the whole point of the game is to start it over countless times so you can get a few more Hero Souls and perhaps advance a stage or two more the next time you soft reset ... or,  until you get fed-up, annoyed or frustrated and spend real money to make faster progress.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Like all "free to play" games, it's basically designed to make you a slave to it in the hopes you'll eventually get fed-up at the lack of progress and spend real cash on it. It's like living with a relative with a gambling problem. They want your attention all the time, they hype you up about the "big score" they're going to land if they just get a bit of time and cash to go gamble, and at first they "need a few bucks" to make it happen. You watch them lose it all, but as time goes by "I swear, if you just give me another $100, that's it, we'll win, and we'll win big!" ... next day, they're broke and asking you for $200, and nothing changes and there's no end in sight other then you checking in with them every 30 minutes to see if they kicked their gambling habit or need more enabling / cash. Then you lift your head one day and realize you could have been doing somethign productive with your life.
The only positive thing about this game is that you can passively baby-sit it while doing other things ... surf the web, do the laundry, vacuum the house, etc. My apartment has never been cleaner. But, I did that stuff in 5-10 minute bursts while away from the game. I found whole days just♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥away on the game. Go change laundry, then I'll make some breakfast... oh, but I need to check in on the game for 5 minutes (spend 1 hour checking in on it), ok, I'll vacuum now... oh, but I need to stop vacuuming midway to check on the game for 5 minutes (another hour wasted on the game). Gee, it was morning just a while ago... now it's mid-afternoon. What happened to the day?
It was wasted on this game, being chained to it like a slave.
Just say "no" kids.

Spaghetti and Meatballs
INGREDIENTS
Sauce:
2 28-ounce cans whole peeled tomatoes in juice, drained, juice reserved, tomatoes finely chopped
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
2 medium onions, peeled, halved through root end
1/2 teaspoon (or more) salt
Meatballs:
1 cup fresh breadcrumbs made from crustless French or country-style bread
1/3 cup whole milk
8 ounces ground beef (15% fat)
8 ounces ground pork
1 cup finely ground (not grated) Parmesan cheese
1/3 cup finely chopped Italian parsley
1 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 large eggs
2 large garlic cloves, pressed
1 pound spaghetti
Freshly grated Parmesan cheese (for serving)
PREPARATION
For sauce:
Combine tomatoes with juice, butter, onions, and salt in large wide pot. Bring to simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat; simmer uncovered 45 minutes, stirring occasionally. Discard onions. Using immersion blender, process sauce briefly to break up any large pieces of tomato (texture should be even but not completely smooth). Season sauce with more salt and freshly ground black pepper. Remove from heat.
For meatballs:
Combine breadcrumbs and milk in small bowl; stir until breadcrumbs are evenly moistened. Let stand 10 minutes.
Place beef and pork in large bowl and break up into small chunks. Add 1 cup ground Parmesan, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Whisk eggs to blend in small bowl; whisk in garlic. Add to meat mixture.
Using hands, squeeze milk from breadcrumbs, reserving milk. Add breadcrumbs to meat mixture. Using hands, quickly and gently mix meat mixture just until all ingredients are evenly combined (do not overmix). Chill mixture at least 15 minutes and up to 1 hour.
Moisten hands with some of reserved milk from breadcrumbs, then roll meat mixture between palms into golf-ball-size balls, occasionally moistening hands with milk as needed and arranging meatballs in single layer in sauce in pot. Bring to simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until meatballs are cooked through, 15 to 20 minutes. DO AHEAD: Can be made 2 days ahead. Cool slightly. Chill uncovered until cold, then cover and keep chilled. Rewarm before continuing.
Cook spaghetti in large pot of boiling salted water until just tender but still firm to bite, stirring occasionally. Drain.
Using slotted spoon, transfer meatballs to platter. Add pasta to sauce in pot and toss to coat. Divide pasta among 6 plates. Top each serving with meatballs. Sprinkle meatballs with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and serve.

Baby Sitter Simulator designed to keep you coming back every 10 minutes in the hopes that your annoyance and frustration will eventually lead you to spending real cash to advance.
I had most of my summer off from college, so I decided to dig in and give this game a real try (hence the hours played even though I'm complaining).
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1) Math Simulator ... game is nothing more then an exponential diffuclty curve being attacked by a linear progress curve (straight line). Google up "linear vs. exponential" to get an idea how this quickly becomes unfair.
2) Glorified Spreadsheet ... the interface is just a list of heroes, ancients, etc. The game could literally work just fine without the "combat window" showing enemies, gold flying in the air, etc. You're playing a glorified spreadsheet running a math simulation.
3) Addiction Triggers ... Game is designed to get certain folks hooked; folks that get off on attainment or the feeling of "one more (progress)" in the hopes that they will eventually get the upper-hand. To keep progressing against the exponential difficulty, you upgrade your linear attack curve by buying upgrades. You buy these upgrades via gold, and the gold racks up in linear fashion, too (eg: you get X gold per hit point you take off an enemy). These upgrades get HUGE over time (eg: +1000000% damage, next hero does 100x more damage, etc). This triggers some peoples' "happy" response in that they get a sense of attainment; like they're gaining power over the game. But, again, all this does is slowly raise your linear progress curve in the hopes that it can perhaps compete with the obscenely-escalating exponential difficulty curve that's quickly blowing it out of the water. You stalemate at an area. You buy a new hero or upgrade something to get an additional +1000000% damage ... sounds great! Then you realize all that does it let you progress another 10 stages. Whooopee.
4) Cheating Placebo ... the game is designed to use auto-clickers from the start. That's why there's achievements for clicking up to 40x/second. So, go ahead and cheat, because your arrogance gets you playing the game more.
5) No Ending ... Eventually you reach a level where the variable that stores enemy health can't handle such a high number. Instead of crashing, or tossing up a "you win" screen, the game has a built-in fail-safe that a) puts "InfiniK" for enemy health, and b) disregards all damage you do from then on. This is  around level 4200 or so. So, the only "satisfaction" you get from the end-game is by hitting a point where you could have broken it in 80's arcade game fashion (eg: Donkey Kong), but the game was designed to not break. You just stare at this screen watching the game mock you as it has the last laugh. This is hollow, and makes you realize how pointless the countless hours you put into the game really are.
6) Time Slave ... Everything is designed to bring you back every 10 minutes like a crack w#0r3. If you let the game sit for a day, you rack up a lot of gold... just to find out it only levels your heroes up enough to progress a few more areas. So, you need to micromanage them to level them up as they can, that way they're not wasting time grinding low levels for paltry amounts of gold. There's also active skills that cooldown; need to come back in a few minutes to use them again. There's clickable items that can get you rubies or skill use without cooldown, so need to watch for those... This is a never-ending cycle, and as your linear progress starts hitting the exponential difficulty wall, it becomes more and more of a baby-sitting job as you try to micro-manage everything. If I just get a little more gold to level-up this hero, or hire the next one, or wait a bit for that skill to cooldown, it'll just take a minute ... (look up at clock) ... holy cow I've been sitting here for two hours! Ok, I'll leave it alone. (10 minutes later). I need to check in to make sure my heroes can progress! (never ending cycle)
7) Free To Play ... ultimately they want you to spend cash in a store. They sucker you into this store after you click on a little fish that gives you a ruby. What are these rubies for? In the store, if you get 50 Rubies, and you can buy some awesome stuff ... for free without spending money! ZOMG! Aren't you clever! No, you're not. You'd literally need to camp the game the entire day to get 50 rubies, so, again, the game has you become it's time slave. Or... you could pay some cash to get Rubies. Then you realize game insults you with "$100 = 1300 Rubies" purchase options. Let that sink in ... it's a flash game ... that has an option to spend $100 on it. That's ludicrous. And those rubies barely make a dent in the game. You'd need to spend THOUSANDS of dollars on the game to make any appreciable progress. Like a casino game, you plop down tons of cash thinking you're hot ****, then in the blink of an eye you hit the deadwall of the exponential difficulty curve once again... and realize you're back to square one. Except your wallet is a lot lighter.
8) IT'S A MINI GAME ... Hit a deadwall? You can do a soft reset to start over called an "ascension". This lets you keep certain gear you found / bought in previous games, and it lets you cash in hero levels for Hero Souls. So, you're not really ascending... you're descending ... back to level 1. After you do this multiple times, you quickly realize that the hero levelling & monster fighting is actually a mini game. A long-winded "mini game", but a mini-game nonetheless. The REAL game is you going through that "mini game" countless times to collect Hero Souls to upgrade ancient artifacts to see if you can make a tiny bit more progress in the "mini game" next time you run it. So, again, you have to baby-sit the game until you hit a deadwall, then "ascend" to start the game over to cash in and get Hero Souls. Otherwise your heroes spend forever staring at a deadwall.
I'm not even joking about #7 ... the whole point of the game is to start it over countless times so you can get a few more Hero Souls and perhaps advance a stage or two more the next time you soft reset ... or,  until you get fed-up, annoyed or frustrated and spend real money to make faster progress.
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Like all "free to play" games, it's basically designed to make you a slave to it in the hopes you'll eventually get fed-up at the lack of progress and spend real cash on it. It's like living with a relative with a gambling problem. They want your attention all the time, they hype you up about the "big score" they're going to land if they just get a bit of time and cash to go gamble, and at first they "need a few bucks" to make it happen. You watch them lose it all, but as time goes by "I swear, if you just give me another $100, that's it, we'll win, and we'll win big!" ... next day, they're broke and asking you for $200, and nothing changes and there's no end in sight other then you checking in with them every 30 minutes to see if they kicked their gambling habit or need more enabling / cash. Then you lift your head one day and realize you could have been doing somethign productive with your life.
The only positive thing about this game is that you can passively baby-sit it while doing other things ... surf the web, do the laundry, vacuum the house, etc. My apartment has never been cleaner. But, I did that stuff in 5-10 minute bursts while away from the game. I found whole days just♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥away on the game. Go change laundry, then I'll make some breakfast... oh, but I need to check in on the game for 5 minutes (spend 1 hour checking in on it), ok, I'll vacuum now... oh, but I need to stop vacuuming midway to check on the game for 5 minutes (another hour wasted on the game). Gee, it was morning just a while ago... now it's mid-afternoon. What happened to the day?
It was wasted on this game, being chained to it like a slave.
Just say "no" kids.

Spaghetti and Meatballs
INGREDIENTS
Sauce:
2 28-ounce cans whole peeled tomatoes in juice, drained, juice reserved, tomatoes finely chopped
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
2 medium onions, peeled, halved through root end
1/2 teaspoon (or more) salt
Meatballs:
1 cup fresh breadcrumbs made from crustless French or country-style bread
1/3 cup whole milk
8 ounces ground beef (15% fat)
8 ounces ground pork
1 cup finely ground (not grated) Parmesan cheese
1/3 cup finely chopped Italian parsley
1 teaspoon salt
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 large eggs
2 large garlic cloves, pressed
1 pound spaghetti
Freshly grated Parmesan cheese (for serving)
PREPARATION
For sauce:
Combine tomatoes with juice, butter, onions, and salt in large wide pot. Bring to simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat; simmer uncovered 45 minutes, stirring occasionally. Discard onions. Using immersion blender, process sauce briefly to break up any large pieces of tomato (texture should be even but not completely smooth). Season sauce with more salt and freshly ground black pepper. Remove from heat.
For meatballs:
Combine breadcrumbs and milk in small bowl; stir until breadcrumbs are evenly moistened. Let stand 10 minutes.
Place beef and pork in large bowl and break up into small chunks. Add 1 cup ground Parmesan, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Whisk eggs to blend in small bowl; whisk in garlic. Add to meat mixture.
Using hands, squeeze milk from breadcrumbs, reserving milk. Add breadcrumbs to meat mixture. Using hands, quickly and gently mix meat mixture just until all ingredients are evenly combined (do not overmix). Chill mixture at least 15 minutes and up to 1 hour.
Moisten hands with some of reserved milk from breadcrumbs, then roll meat mixture between palms into golf-ball-size balls, occasionally moistening hands with milk as needed and arranging meatballs in single layer in sauce in pot. Bring to simmer.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until meatballs are cooked through, 15 to 20 minutes. DO AHEAD: Can be made 2 days ahead. Cool slightly. Chill uncovered until cold, then cover and keep chilled. Rewarm before continuing.
Cook spaghetti in large pot of boiling salted water until just tender but still firm to bite, stirring occasionally. Drain.
Using slotted spoon, transfer meatballs to platter. Add pasta to sauce in pot and toss to coat. Divide pasta among 6 plates. Top each serving with meatballs. Sprinkle meatballs with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and serve.

Alright game, NOT worth $60. If it is $15 or less, it might be worth it. Playing it for a while now, and the most annoying thing is the toaster-tier servers.
Even with low ping, you cannot run in a straight line without rubberbanding the whole way there. Official servers constantly come down and lag out. If you can find a good unofficial, than that is 10000000000x better than the Official Toasters.
Enemies and Dinos randomly speed up and slow down because of the lag.
Hit detection is completely off. You'll have 10 arrows sticking out of a bird, but none of them will have actually been considered a "hit" and it will still be full health. Attacking something with a melee weapon is more reliable, but more often than not, you'll have no idea if you connected your melee attacks. The hit feedback is very buggy like that.
If you are a new player, watch out for Ichthyornis', a small bird near beaches. They are brutal to new players, or even veteran players making a new character. They steal and destroy your items, which is pretty bad. However, either due to lag or terrible hitboxes, it is nearly impossible to kill even a low level one. You'll have 10 crossbow bolts sticking out of its face, but it will not have taken damage from it. It lifted up a lystro, and killed it in front of me, with 30 arrows in it. This creature alone is enough to make me quit a night in frustration.
Early access game with paid DLC? Shame on these devs. Why make a DLC for a game that is terribly unoptimized, poorly managed, and NOT EVEN RELEASED? I think it's an attempt at parodying day one DLC by these devs. Now introducing, minus one year DLC.
To call the dinos AI would be giving the devs undeserved credit for making something that can remotely be called "intelligent". The dinosaurs constantly get stuck on terrain, resources, structures, and each other.
Flying dinos and birds have really wonky movements. They can turn on a dime, and yo-yo up and down like crazy. If you are using a bow or crossbow, good luck hitting one, even at point blank. Bolas? They help, but only if you can actually land one that doesn't just pop right through them. If you miss, you can't even pick it off the ground.
Studio WIldcard, the developers behind this game, are amongst the worst developers I've seen. The game has great potential. The only way for it to reach that potential would be to hand off the game to an actual studio with talented people, not these hacks.
With all that said, I'm glad I got the game when it was much cheaper ($20), but I'm still torn whether I feel it was a waste of a good $20, or an investment into a game that may one day be very good. It can be very fun with friends, but that fun is limited to mostly unofficial servers, and is often ruined by the games glaring flaws and bugs. $60 for this game is daylight robbery.

After playing this game for 4 weeks straight with an overall 250+ hours total game time achieved in this time period, i can say the game is well worth your time, even without my insane cabaility / time to commit to a game. (I'm still in school and unemployed = a lot of f**king free time ;) ).
anyway to be more specific im going to list both the pros and cons in a note system to further point out why this game is worth your time, and if it will be a game you would be willing to commit to.
CON'S :
-the game features a pay to obtain currency, this isnt surprising for a MMO, but the way the currency is styled is a bit... s**t. almost everything in this game can easily be obtained with platnium, (the games payed currency) this includes items that double your modding capacity, (gifting more access to applying high end upgrades to gear) and allowing purchase of every single weapon and warframe in the game. Although, the currency is overpriced and so are the things able to be purchased via platnium
-This game requires a lot of commitment and effort to be put into it, to get somewhere. This isnt necessarly bad, and its nothing like the grind of RuneScape, but it still will force casual, or people with little available time for gaming away.
-This game does feature PvP content, however, servers are hosted which makes playing with decent latency hard and its almost impossible to find a game without spending more then 15+ minutes waiting.
-Warframe is a bit more grindy then most standard action MMO's, you have to farm resources which isnt to bad, but to get end-game gear you have to require rare to uncommon parts to forge said weaponary, which can be hard, especially once difficulty of enemys progresses during missions.
-Since this game features a huge trading economy, it is extremely easy to get sharked, or baited into buying something from a d**khead who is a greedy bast**d, and its easily done once your new.
PRO'S:
now that we have the cons, which honestly, arent that bad out of the way, lets get into the +'s of this game:
-Warframe features a smooth, fluid parkour / movement system that is fun, and is impossible to get bored off / hate.
-The game features a huge economy of friendly-helpful people, which usually, will help out if simply asked. (the game is mostly PvE)
-fun, fast paced combat
-Warframe has a mass variety of weapons, and warframes, with each having almost no simularity to another; everything you use in this game is unique.
-Warframe has limitless content.
-This is both a con, and a pro, but the game consistes of instance based missions.
-for a MMO purely set on mass genecide and farming, it features a short, yet extremely well fitted and awesome story-line.
-Warframe features a clan / dojo system which can be used for competitive PvE action, or PvP, with most clans (from my experience) hosting events were the winner can snag a reward for being a part of said events.
-This game allows you to customize a wide variety of your warframes look, aswell as your ships, dojos, and well, everything. (although everything must be otained through platnium in this case : / )
-and last, Warframe features a huge trading economy which makes buying / selling your hard earnt prime / rare gear easy and fun.
That pretty much sums up my review, I know i missed a lot of stuff that could be listed here, but this is pretty much off the top of my head anyway, but with that being said, if you had read this far my conclusion is: This game is pure, social fun. Your GOING to meet people no matter what and have a fun time growing along side them and building a relationship with them. This game is awesome, however it requires alot of time to get rich / big / or have alot of options.
overall its a 8.5/10 for me.

So far I'm rather enjoying this game. It's pretty great when you want to play something but can't really decide what to play. It helps take up any time spent trying to figure out what else you might want to play.
It's also really great to play while tied and trying to fall asleep. (I struggle to fall asleep and most of the time can't sleep unless I fall asleep while doing something. Usually that something is gaming.) It keeps you clicking, but it's not so immersive that it risks waking you up more instead of letting you drift off to sleep.
While it is a free game that has a micro-transaction setup (one that's a pretty big ripoff, if you ask me) there's also the potential to earn rubies (the paid for currency) without ever spending a penny. It takes a while for them to add up, but not as long as with many many flash games I've played in the past that grant you small amounts of paid for currency in an attempt to lure you into spending real money on the game.
While the developer and publisher are listed as something different, it really reminds me a lot of AdVenture Capitalist. Especially the part about having to restart to redeem "souls" that provide bonuses during the next playthrough.
Overall, if you enjoy time wasters that give you something to do but you don't have to think about too much, and can run in the background and still progress if you become busy with something, I highly recommend this game. It's also a fantastic game to play while trying to fall asleep.
