There's just something so richly rewarding about crushing people's heads in with a ridiculously over sized warhammer, or slicing off the limbs of others with huge♥♥♥♥♥greatswords, and this is why I play Chivalry: Medieval Warfare. I would go as far to say that Chivalry has the best combat system of any game I've ever played, just for the sheer meatyness of it.
Chivalry doesn't boast beautiful graphics, or even a compelling badckstory to what you're actually fighting for (it's practically non-existant), but that doesn't matter as the combat makes up for everything that Chivalry lacks in. The unlocking of weapons after a certain amount of kills gives the player a good incentive to carry on, and the wide variety of game modes and weapons adds for a good amount of diversity, ensuring you won't get bored quickly.
If there was one thing I didn't like about the game, it was the archery. Maybe it was just because I sucked at it, but it was incredibley difficult to hit targets, and even after you did manage to hit one, there was no satisfaction of it, no PING or anything, it just felt stale, as if it was rushed into the gamejust beofre release  to give a bit more diversity (which in hindsight it probably was). Another thing is the arrow dip in this game, its really weird; one moment you arrow is travelling forward just fine, the next its plummetting towards the ground as if it hit a wall or something.
Having said this, Chivalry is DEFINATELY worth the buy, although I would recommend that you wait until its on sale, because this game goes on sale a lot. So pick it up with a few mates, sit back, and get ready to feel the thrill of crushing in a virtual skull with a virtual weapon whilst your real life friends look on and scream 'DUDE AWESOME! Ok look. This game is, in its entirety, a fun game. HOWEVER, here's what you need to know and I'll start with the cons.
1. Horrible performance optimization. The game uses more resources than are necessary and create FPS problems unless you have a monster gaming machine.
2. Clipping and hit box issues. Often times dinos will clip into eachother and get stuck and requires extensive effor to separate them. Also there are parts of a dino that don't register as hit locations like the wings of a Quetzel/Tapejara.
3. Poor AI scripting. Dinos will walk into walls and get stuck (ties back to clipping) and the dinos you set to follow you require careful attention because they'll get lost trying to walk around a simple rock, cactus, or tree.
4. VERY poor building mechanics. Download the S+ building mod. It mostly fixes everything that's wrong with the vanilla building mechanic but that isn't a good excuse for a game to give up development on their poor building design.
5. Crash issues. I don't personally have crash issues but all of my friends do and my game will occasionally freeze for 8-15 seconds at a time. I have a GTX 1080 TI Aurous Xtreme edition and an i7 7700K processor with 64 GB of ram. My computer cost me around $3,000 and I still have occasional performance issues. It's pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
6. Dino balancing. Guns do absolutely♥♥♥♥♥♥damage to dinos and the bosses do NOT scale to the # of players so if I'm playing on a private server with only 2-3 other players, fighting a boss is next to impossible.
I'm falling behind on my diablo 3 season 11 hardcore grift runs so I'll stop here but these are a few examples of why im including #7

So far I'm rather enjoying this game. It's pretty great when you want to play something but can't really decide what to play. It helps take up any time spent trying to figure out what else you might want to play.

While it is a free game that has a micro-transaction setup (one that's a pretty big ripoff, if you ask me) there's also the potential to earn rubies (the paid for currency) without ever spending a penny. It takes a while for them to add up, but not as long as with many many flash games I've played in the past that grant you small amounts of paid for currency in an attempt to lure you into spending real money on the game.
While the developer and publisher are listed as something different, it really reminds me a lot of AdVenture Capitalist. Especially the part about having to restart to redeem "souls" that provide bonuses during the next playthrough.
Overall, if you enjoy time wasters that give you something to do but you don't have to think about too much, and can run in the background and still progress if you become busy with something, I highly recommend this game. It's also a fantastic game to play while trying to fall asleep.

I'm sure plenty of people will disagree with me and enjoy this game. It's slick and well put together. I didn't catch any bugs while I played it and have no complaints about usability. But I actually like the original type of clicker game, I played the first cookie clicker when it came out and find that type of gameplay enjoyable. This game attempts to introduce a new layer to those games by adding monsters to kill to earn gold instead of earning currency directly with the things you buy. Again they do this very well, the graphics are cute, the sound effects and music not terrribly annoying, the heroes you buy are entertaining as well as surprisingly gender balanced. I was impressed by the lady samurai, the women aren't thrown in for sex appeal in tiny bikinis.
But the reason I don't recommend the game is that I don't think the extra layer of monsters works very well. They managed to replicate grinding in a form of game that was previously (in my opinion) perfectly geared towards constant motion. The only actual gameplay in these clicker games is balancing an exponentially increasing cost of upgrades against a linearly increasing income. A few other wrinkles don't really change that. But now there are time limited bosses that until you beat fast enough keep you from moving on to an increased income by fighting bigger monsters. I literally just walked away from the game and made myself lunch while grinding away on the previous level. I suspect they did this to try to make the "click" part of the game more important, because now your ability to click quickly is often the only thing allowing you to beat the "boss monsters." Unfortunately I think they guessed wrong, I don't think clicker games SHOULD have anything to do with clicking, it's an income management game. And this one doesn't add anything to that part of the genre.
Tl;dr, well made, but takes the genre in the opposite direction I would like to see. Not fun anymore for me.

If we ever manage to build utopia, the cornerstone of its educational program will be a forced hour-long session of Clicker Heroes that ends with students being informed that their genetic sequence has been inextricably attached to their game profile and that they will be unceremoniously exiled to labor camps on the Moon if they should ever demonstrate the feeble-mindedness necessary to return and play for a second time.
When the human race is finally enslaved by its mechanical progeny and harvested within illusory biofarm prison-paradises, our digital overlords will have no need of an elaborate computer simulation to placate our minds; for that they will have Clicker Heroes.

Over all I cannot recommend this product for its current price tag of $59.99. If the price tag was around $35-$40 I would recommend this game in a heartbeat.
TL;DR: Maybe after release the Devs will get better with interacting with players, and things will get better, we can hope. The Bad:
-Game littered with bugs, even with players pointing out issues, Devs rarely acknowledge the problems let alone publicly put it on their "To Do List".
-Building has gotten better but still needs a ton of polishing.
-Taming is either tediously boring or flat out obnoxiously annoying, there is no middle ground.
-Breeding is a disappointment, it could have been fun and interactive, instead prepare to have no life and never sleep or all those adorable babies blood is going to be on your hands.

-EXTREMELY poor optimization, have a base with more than 20 Dinos or the base is larger than a 10x10, prepare for a lag fest.
-Dev Support is underwhelming, we understand they are pushing for final release but having servers offline at times for days at a time is simply unacceptable. Players are constantly send pleas for help from dupers, and people taking advantage of glitches, and flat out cheaters using aimbots, those players for the most part seem to be getting ignored. Unless the tribe that is being accused is a well-known “Mega Tribe”, even then the Devs intervention is minimal and really doesn’t impact that “Mega Tribe” more than inconveniencing them for a few days.
-The DLC for this game IS STILL ITS FULL PRICE! Sure, in the beginning of that DLC’s life the $20 price tag was annoying but hey most of us paid $20 or less for the original game, so realistically most people right now are $26-$40 into this game. THEN YOU DRIVE UP THE PRICE OF THE CORE GAME TO $60 and don’t even include that DLC released during EARLY ACCESS! Outright deplorable business behavior on your new and upcoming customers.
The Good:
-At higher graphical settings, this game is simply stunning.
-Tons of different animals to tame and interact with.’
-Ability to custom make food / drink, one of my favorite features!

Maddeningly addictive, Clicker Heroes will keep you occupied for hours with more content than even Cookie Clicker and dozens of heroes to hire onto your ridiculous "adventure". Well, it certainly does become ridiculous, especially as the numbers representing things such as Gold, Monster Health, and DPS climb to insane numbers!
Here's a summary of the positives (+) and negatives (-):
+ Free to play! There is absolutely no cost to play Clicker Heroes.
+ Perfect for multitasking. If you want a solid game to play while doing something else, then this game is for you!
+ Fun, charming, and colorful. There is a decent bit of humor in this game, with some silly descriptions for some heroes and their abilities.
+ Extensive amount of items, heroes, mercenaries, and boosters keep powering you up into absurd levels of strength. There is at least a decent amount of depth here for a clicker game.
+ Easy to get into, with little to no learning curve.
+ Updated pretty frequently. There's plenty of new content on the horizon.
- With all the good that this game has, the gameplay is bare bones and most of it is in the strategy or planning.
- Microtransactions, although expected for a F2P game, simply provide a shortcut to the only thing the game has to offer anyway. Sadly, I gave in to these a few times.
= Can be repetitive and annoying when you're having fun progressing very far, then continue to hit the same "wall" over and over and over!
- Lag and performance issues when the screen is filled with numbers representing gold and damage.

Chivalry in concept is a medieval first person fighting game at its best, and is definitely a game worth checking out.  With multiple game modes from standard ffa or tdm to objective game modes where you siege a castle, or sabotage an enemy base, there is tons of stuff to do. Couple that with the multiple classes and unlockable weapons and cosmetics and you have a game that will keep you entertained for many, many hours to come.
In Medieval Warfare you can play as four different classes, an archer class that deals mainly in ranged weapons, a man at arms, who is a speedy fighter with a variety of tools and weapons at his disposal, a knight who can wield two handed weapons in one hand and carry a tower shield and finally the vanguard a fast class that hits had with two handed weapons. That all is only scratching the surface however! In the deadliest warrior DLC you are introduced to six new classes the, pirate, ninja, knight, viking, spartan, and the samurai! all of these classes play different than the last. Combine that with a new variety of maps, you are in for tons of fun if you like chivalry!
Overall I would strongly recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of melee combat or action fighting games. its got a little of something for everyone, and is easy to learn but hard to master.
A perfect model of a F2P game done right.

For Glory!
Chivalry brings forth a skill element to the fine art of warfare and swordsmanship. It is primarly focused on multiplayer so make sure to get your friends to play with. Fancy a broadsword? A mace? Perhaps a warhammer? No? Well Chivalry has a wide selection of pikes, spears, throwing axes, bows, crossbows and knives... Quite the arsenal at your disposal to conduct the bloody and glorious symphony of war! Out smart your opponent or pummel him down with brute force, the choice is your's.
I cannot overstate how brilliant the combat mechanics are designed, multiple angles of attacks, parries, feints even ducking and jumping requires a fair amount of skill to use effectively. But that's not all that is amazing, Chivalry contains many mode based "scenarios". Dueling modes, fortress siege... It's all there.
So if you'd like to feel what it's like rushing into a battlefield, the sound of charging footfalls, the battlecries of warriors and the clash of steel all around you; Chivalry: Medieval Warfare will give you the closest possible simulation of just that.

Very fun and livewire game, that always has you on the run, gunning down enemy troops, blasting through doors, throwing things at ohter things, killing grunts with a sword...
Except when it doesn't.
Thenit becomes a high-stakes stealth mission, as you run jump and fly over the heads of enemies, consolidating quick, quiet kills from the shadows with your bow and dagger, hacking into terminals...
Except when it isn't.
Then it becomes a economy game, with an open market where players can trade in-game items and weapons for other player's hard currency, which could normaly only be gained through micro-transactions.
That is what really sets this game apart. It falls out of the classic F2P MMO that is filled with paywalls and membership and "VIP Beniefits" and "Locked Weapons" (I'm looking at you Archeage, COD Black Ops 3, Wizard/Pirate 101, and just about every other F2P MMO). While it does have purchasable currency and items that can be bough easier with it, very most, if not all items can bought in-game using in-game resources and currency. And if you find an amazing thing that you just HAVE to use the Hard Currency on, then go to the trade chat, which allows you to trade items found on missions for the exclusive currency.
In conclusion, Warframe is an overall epic game, filled with intense action, livewire escapes, strategic stealth, a blossoming community, and a very long campaign that is constantly being added onto.
I would reccomend this game to anyone, and am sure that the game will get only better for years to come. Cheers!

Well there are good and bad things about the game but the bad are to the point of making the game broken in my opinion.  I will list both and wont exaggerate past the point.  I love survival games and starting to like sandbox with building.
First the good.  I absolutely love dinosaurs and the fact that you can tame them makes it even better.  The graphics are great (if you rig can handle it) but poorly optimized.   Lots of leveling up to do with a bunch of unlocks without the feeling of too much grinding.  Resources are hard to find at times and a bit difficult for the rare stuff but thats how its supposed to be and i do enjoy a difficult task.  Maps are huge with a bunch of different ecosystems in them which makes for LOTS of exploring and fun adventures as well.  Overall i would recommend this game IF it were not for these reasons below.
Now the BAD.  Absolutely horrible servers!!!!  Im not talking about people raiding and taking their high level characters to a new map and just wiping the whole map.  Or people loading into a server just to lock it out so their friends can wipe it and you cant log on to defend your base.  Im talking about basic server desync/crashes/staying offline in general.  If it happened once in a while it would be fine but the simple fact that it is constant is what makes the game unplayable and completely broken.  Along with the constant server lag/desync/outages, i took a break while servers were down for a week and logged on to find 2 of my bases completely gone and all of my tamed dinos(which takes a crazy amount of hours to tame and build a base with resources) were completely gone.  Yeah there is a timer it was less than a week and if you dont log on and spend time on the server your stuff will completely vanish without trace kind of like foot soldiers from ninja turtles.  When they are gone you are happy not when your hours and hours of hard work just disappear because of server problems.  Going back to the good graphics well there is some bad that goes along with that as well.
This is absolutely one of the most unoptimized games out there and it just seems to get worse.  I used to get more fps at launch and now the performance just keeps decreasing.  There are lots of other reasons that his game is bad but not to the point of making it broken so i wont go into more cons just from my own experience.
As the current status of the game i wouldnt recommend it.  I would recommend it if they stopped adding content and devoted more devs to solve the crazy amount of server problems but since launch of early access i havent seen the back end problems with the game improve just get worse with more dinos to have a poor gaming experience with.  I dont see the devs tackling the problems with the game itself only see them working on more ways to sell.  That is a poor business model in my opinion that seems to be the adopted norm at the moment with modern day titles.

You decide to tame a dino

Cry while you run down the stairs in your stone base
Get glitched into a wall in your base
Leave the game
Come back the next day to play again

Is it laggy and glitching? Yes but I'm willing to put up with it
Do I get bored and hate this game? Yes but only sometimes
Did I make friends on this game? Yes
Is this game unbalanced and have some op tribes? Yes
Do i recommend this game as it is now? No
Will I keep playing? hell yeah

Okay, first things first, this is an idle game. It has no point and is more or less plays itself. While you can adopt a playing style where you do something, that something IS nothing but clicking. The alternative is having the game sit idle, which works just as well or, depending on your style, is even more efficient. So let's get this out of the way, idle games are an odd genre, and arguably you may as well go out there and watch some paint dry.
Still, Clicker Heroes does everything right and if you ever played games like Cookie Clicker you'll see how CH does some things outstandingly well. The main idea is to click on a fantasy monster, dealing damage and eventually killling it to get some gold. That gold can then be spend on a wide range of heroes who'll fight alongside your mouse cursor, dealing damage and basically farming those endless rows of monsters.
And it never changes. You kill, get money, upgrade your heroes to deal more damage to the monsters who get more hitpoints, it's an endless balance. Still, watching those numbers fly across the screen and quickly reaching ridiculous dimensions (a trillion damage per second? why not!) is oddly addictive. While essentially a game that's all about numbers the heroes are a rather colourful troupe too, and their in-game descriptions and quotes are often hilarious if you're into that sort of thing.
Idling is absolutely okay: Not only can you open the game and let in run in the background; your heroes even farm money for you while you are NOT RUNNING the game at all. Shut down your computer. Invite some friends. Have an awesome party. Go out and, I don't know, party all weekend. Then return and launch Clicker Heroes and smile as your insane army hands over those trillion bazillion gold they farmed. Yes, it's sort of cool.
There's even the now standard "hidden layer" of strategy and playstyle- each and every hero has a little backstory and a set of skills to unlock and there IS some tactic involved to maximize your damage output.
When all's said and done, this is an over-the-top parody of action role playing games. Instead of playing through a massive game of lore and content, becoming stronger and battling forever growing dangers, here you click. And get the same result. I can really appreciate that. And in a way there is a story playing out, of some great danger and some dude who at one day started clicking a monster and soon becoming a hero and the leader of an army where actual gods walk among mere mortals (who can actually outpower said gods).
In addition to all mechanics playing out just fine, CH actually looks rather charming. The punny monsters are nicely animated, the heroes do have their unique visuals, and everything has a nice clean Flash look. Music's nice too, but you'll probably mute the game soon. Idling, y'know?
And, yes, it's a free game. No costs involved. You CAN purchase gems for real-life currency to buy some nice little advantages but the same gems are randomly awarded as you play the game. So... recommended? Depends on your view on idle games. If you don't at least get the joke, you won't like it. But if you want a time-waster that actually offers something... why not try out a full game that costs you nothing at all?

Clicker Heroes is a clicker game where you click on monsters and spend your reward money on hiring and improving more heroes to fight the continually stonger monsters. Basically, you click on monsters to get gold. You use the gold to buy and upgrade heroes. And through clicking, damage over time, and certain activated abilities you try to kill more and more to get further. There are bosses every so many rounds. You can ascend the world which starts you over but gives you a special kind of currency called hero souls. Having them raises your damage over time, but you can spend them for greater enhancements in the game. You can also sometimes find rubies, another type of currency you can use to buy certain enhancements to your game. Aside from a few other things... that's about it.
It's a lot of rinse and repeat gameplay. Lots of clicking, lots of idling, lots of waiting. Sometimes you'll leave it up in the background while other times you won't play for days just to earn lots of extra gold. Sometimes you'll have to keep checking back to make progress or do this or that. Ultimately it's pretty mindless. Honestly, it's not a very good game. It doesn't require any skill because you can never LOSE progress outside of hard restting all the data. Getting better at the game basically means following guides, working out math involved in damage to cost ratios, and timing your playing schedule accordingly. It's more like a time waster. It's a chore. It turns into just another thing you do because you do it.
I like the theming of the game. Using heroes to fight off monsters, getting gold, growing stronger somewhat like an RPG almost. But the gameplay comes down to math, making decisions, knowing when to be on or when to idle, and clicking. That's it. It's pretty dull. This works fine... as an app. It's something you can pull up and kill some time on here and there. But devoting time to playing it is just so dull and a waste. As an app, it's fine. As a GAME, it's bad.
So why recommend it? Well, it's FREE! You CAN pay money to get extra stuff and make it go faster, but there's no need to. It's a large waste of time, unless you have fun with it. So if the idea interests you, give it a shot and see how you feel about it. There's nothing stopping you. However, I'd recommend getting the app on your phone instead and just doing it to kill time rather than playing it like a game. There are plenty of free games on the internet and many of them are more fun as actual games. I played this one long enough myself. Giving it a score, I'll have to rate it as a GAME, because I'm a game reviewer, not an app reviewer and it's being presented here on Steam, a gaming platform, as a game. Clicker Heroes gets a 2 out of 10 for being a free thing to do in your spare time that is bound to get old. At least it's free, so you might as well see for yourself.

What the ♥♥♥♥.
I'm still blown away by how many hours I have put and am still putting into this game. That hour-count is getting close to my skyrim one now, and that's saying a LOT!
[TL/DR at the bottom]
Okay, let's start off with how the game starts: You click on a little blob a few times, and then it dies. You pick up the coin he dropped, click some more, and once you gather your first 5 coins, you get to buy your first little helper: Cid, the little clicker-booster. Boom, suddenly, your clicks don't do 1 damage, but 2!
You kill the other 5 enemies left in this stage and BOOM, you advance to stage number 2 where 10 new enemies are waiting for you. They have a tad more health, drop some more coins, and before you knowit, you've leveled your Cid the Kid up to level 5 and have bought your second helper!
Now this second guy has something really special. Something that's gonna define half the game for you: DPS, damage per second. It starts off not being much. Hell with this guy, I can click 10 times per second and that does like... 100 times more damage than your dps!
Well, yea, for the first 5 minutes that is totally so, but then, when you level him up some more, go up some stages, get him his first upgrade and maybe even buy your third helper, you reach the point where you're just seeing your enemies drop dead before your eyes.
Great, so, that's it then? From now on it's just waiting, buying heroes, and waiting more?
Well, yes and no. From there on out, it's completely up to you what you do with this game. Yes, you can turn it off for a week, come back after that, see you've collected 10,000,000,000,000,000 gold, buy a ♥♥♥♥♥on of heroes and close it for another week again. But if you start getting into it, knowing when to use upgrades, constantly buying the best hero combo's, upgrading the right ancients, etc. you get completely lost in this game.
TL/DR:
+ Rewarding gameplay from the first second
+ Customisable to your own playstyle once you get to the ancients
+/- Still WIP, being updated from time to time with new heroes, items and ancients.
+/- Highly addictive
- Becomes draggy after so many ascensions (one of the key elements of the game is starting over again, earning you "hero souls" that increase your damage)
- Visually not very appealing
- Once the numbers go from 100 - 1K - 1M - 1B etc. the 1^/1@/1#/1* become really confusing.
Overall GREAT fun for a F2P game.

I've been playing this game since it came out on PS4. I had it on PC for longer, but I didn't know because I bought it on a humble bundle, and assumed it was some random crap game. That having been said, onto the review:
This game is a perfectly executed fantasy I've had since I was 5 years old. Living in a world filled with dinosaurs, building bases modularly, taming said dinosaurs, dinosaur husbandry, exploring, hunting, riding and flying on dinos. It's a fantasy I know a lot of people share with me and it's finally been realized by Studio Wildcard. This is also one of the only games to feature full VR support. Not sure how many others can claim that, even from top AAA studios.
Onto the drama, because it's new and people attach to drama like flies to♥♥♥♥♥♥ The drama behind this game is that they're charging full price now that it's done, with the exception of a few glitches. I feel the flak is coming from ignorant gamers who don't understand how games are made, and who don't understand what terms like "alpha" and "beta" are. For people who trusted in ARK before it was fully released they gave Wildcard $10-40 of their hard earned money as a RISK, because ARK might have never been completed at the time. They trusted in Wildcard to finish ARK, and basically donated that money. The beta release that they got with that donation money, was simply a preview of the main game. Slowly, the preview started to look more and more like the fully released game, but it was STILL a preview.
In summary, people who trusted and believed in Wildcard for making ARK were rewarded by getting the game for $10-40 depending on sales or what not. People who did NOT believe in ARK (mainly, the people whining about the prices) are going to have to pay the full price for it now. This is the same developmental cycle for nearly ANY game, the only difference is that people who supported the developers, got a sample of the full game early. End of discussion.
Seriously, Wildcard has been amazing in the development of this game. It's an insanely fun game, filled with all kinds of amazing creatures, a lot that I never expected to even make it into the game. It's a wonderful journey, and one you can take with all your friends. So ripping this game for wanting to charge full price for an amazing game that's WAY better than most garbage that comes out these days for the same price is completely unjustified. I know you guys want to buy the game for cheaper, I get that, you should have bought it when it was in development, or you should wait(like any other poor person) for the game to drop in price before buying it. I mean good lord, it's like you're a bunch of 5 year olds crying cause they want a toy, and mommy and daddy said it was too expensive. Suck it up.
To Team Wildcard: Thank you guys so much for making my childhood fantasy a reality, and giving me the chance to ride on the back of the coolest creatures to ever walk this earth. You guys are amazing, and I hope you don't get discouraged and keep making amazing games for years to come. Cheers!

Chivalry is an amazing and unique title. The atmosphere is great and the developers behind the game are very passionate about their project. I have actively been on their forums and witnessed, without hesitation, developers and producers openly discussing and welcoming criticism to the game for growth.
Torn Banner Studios is an amazing example of what every studio, both new and small, hopes to become and I am very pleased to see their hard work pay off both in game and out.
This game utilizes the Unreal Engine and allows the player to engage in multiplayer battle like never before. The voice acting (believe it or not) is the utmost best in this game with the ability to shout and road and cry for help being the most ambient and hilarious factor in this game.
Each weapon is different and takes time for the user to properly use. The animations are a truly great as you will witness proper motion, reaction, and have access to full dynamic controls of your character. Kick, Shield Bash, Duck, Dodge, Feint Attacks, Combo Attacks, Switch Weapons and positions all within the heat of combat with, hopefully, one on one engagements!
Not only are the maps well done but you can use your environment to your advantage. This includes ballistae, boiling pots of oil, fire, mini trebutches, catapults and kick people off of heights to their demise!
Torn Banner has not left anything out as your weapons will react in full detail as they cut down or burst open your enemies. Heads will concave, explode, arms will slice off and drop on the ground, bodies will burn. Amazing job and courage.
Newly added character customization makes this game a real treat!

The game is fun, especially with friends. Riding dinosaurs, building forts, but it has some glaring issues that need addressing. First and foremost: the pricetag. $60 is a ripoff for this. This game does not deserve that much money. I lucked out and bought it for $13 back when it was still cheap. I recommend you wait until it's on a major sale. Second, everything is a grindfest. If you play on a server, make sure EXP, breeding, hatching, taming etc. are boosted, otherwise you will spend literal hours getting some of the larger dinos. Not to mention everything costs too many resources. Especially for lower level stuff, you will often find yourself dehydrated or starving in the middle of building due to how long it takes to gather the materials needed. Not to mention the angry dinos that like to show up suddenly and kill you.
Also, this game is FULL of bugs. (Literal and figurative.) People falling through floors, things breaking mysteriously, dinosaurs suddenly dying, terrible pathfinding (good luck getting your bronto through a forest, you will spend half your time trying to move around rocks and other such obstacles, especially if it's following you rather than being ridden.) and a very slow leveling system that requires you to level up immensely to get to the moderately good gear.
All in all, I'd say a 5.5 to 6/10. It's fun in the right conditions, but don't pay full price and definitely don't play without a little help starting off. The frustration has caused more than a few people to drop the game outright.

I like the creative element of the game and most of the player base (PVPer's included) are actually friendly.
The biggest cons of the game:
Server transfers.  I'm not opposed to server transfers but with mega tribes the move from server to server wiping out the player base, and then coming back to strangle off any stragglers who try to rebuild -over and over and over, needs to be adressed,  There wouldn't be so many vacant servers if this wasn't the case.
IMO a server transfer should be allowed to any server and you should be able to return to your server of origin but IMO if you transfer to a server and then transfer off, you should not be permitted to go back with the same character again.  This will make it more difficult for mega tribes to transfer in, wipe the server over and over and over.
Leedsicthys.  Ok, what is IMO the best way to servive until you can level a bit and get established,  has been utterly ruined.  The raft killer AI deliberately spawns one right where you drop the raft and the minute you move from skimming the shore, it kills the raft in 2 hits regardless of what kind of defenses you setup.
There needs to be a natural structure decay eliminating all structures that sit dormant for too long.  It's no fun logging in to a server where a mega triba has been through 50+ times wiped everone out and left bits and pieces of bases everywhere so that nothing (dinos, resources, etc) can respawn anymore.  If a tribe has had no members login for X amount of time, then structures should decay more rapidly to remove the over time.
Aside from a few other things that should be tweaked a bit or added, they are actually pretty decent with their updates despite a few nerfs which so drastically altered gameplay as to change the game mechanics completely (like the raft killer).
I would recommend this game if you enjoy survivalist style games.  This one will definitely keep you entertained.

This is my first review so I'm sorry if it's a bit jumbled.
So the great the thing about Warframe, besides being a badass Space Ninja, is its lastability. The devs are constantly adding new and extremely interesting content, including but not limited to new Warframes, weapons, and story missions.
I've stopped and restarted playing Warframe maybe three times, because even if it loses my interest within a few months to a year a whole bunch of awesome updates will rekindle my desire to play, such as when the Second Dream was first released, and more recently the War Within. It's free and some things you can only get by purchasing them (Prime Vault), but that doesn't take away from experience as the PvP is♥♥♥♥♥♥so there's no real way to Pay to Win. Pretty much everything is attainable just by playing, it just takes some time to complete (for example, building a new warframe will take 4 days or so after you've finally managed to farm all of the parts).
One thing that I quite like that I have to mention is the immersion contained in the UI and everthing you do in the game. The main menu is your spaceship, and you walk around it to get to different stations such as your armory and foundry. To get half the items the free way, you need to have a clan dojo and research the items in different labs, all of which are real, physical and beautiful places that you build yourself. Even levelling up your character level (aka Mastery Rank) is immersive. You don't just hit a certain amount of EXP and then suddenly level up, you have to grind that experience up by actually experiencing new things by levelling new items and Warframes, and then once you've gained enough experience they make you take a test to level up. If you fail, you have to start all over. It sounds annoying, but in my opinion really makes you feel like you're the badass parkooring Space Ninja the game says you are: after the all farming, and waiting, and levelling, and tests, the game really does make you feel good about the things you've built and gained. You EARNED that new weapon. You EARNED that new ability. Warframe is a game about earning things by playing the damn game, and the devs have done a great job of conveying that.
Basically, if you're looking for a free coop game with an engaging and constantly changing story, tight, responsive and fun controls, gorgeous graphics, an awesome amount of customization, and don't mind some farming, look no further than Warframe.

I've played warframe since 2013, and really enjoyed it, but here's the big info that you care about:
- There are multiple game types for PvE (which is the main focus of the game): Extermination, Capture (VIP), Excavation, Defense (defend target for intervals of 5 waves, you can leave after 5 waves except special cirumstances), Survival (Live, kill to get life support and/or activate life support drops), Interception (4-point defense, control zone for certain amount of time to capture it), and a couple other game modes.
- Glitches are pretty frequent, but usually not anything game breaking (though there is occasionally).
- The game itself is very grindy. To become better, you need mods, which you have to rank up by spending in-game credits and endo. You can "super-charge" weaponry (double mod capacity) by using certain items that are rarely obtained in game (you can pay for them as well).
- You get minimal slots to start out with, but some in-game premium currency. The best option is to buy weapon/warframe slots (as opposed to skins).
- New players will have a LOT of things to do for the most part. It is slower for newer players to progress due to facing less enemies and lower level enemies (which fits the lack of mods players have when starting out). As long as items (weapons/warframes) are crafted ahead of time, you'll always have something to work on.
- The developer, Digital Extremes (DE), sometimes makes major gameplay changes, and still have the game's state assigned as "beta" (for 3 years); take that however you will.

Let me start with this, this game is very well designed for a specific type of player and will not appeal to the masses of players. It has a very hands-off approach aside from introducing you the controls and the in-depth stat mechanics of the game, which will encourage -but not require- research on the wiki or forums. Premium currency in game is believed to be "pay-to-win", except in this case it's "pay-to-win-faster".
This game is a very good looking 3rd person game that blends an action game with a third-person-shooter as well as dungeon-like missions with varying objective types. A multitude of weapons and frames (the game's character types) to build and use.
Core of the game IMO (decide if you like this type of game or not):
- Collect resources and materials
- Build weapons and armor (requires realtime)
- Co-op PvE game (has limited PvP, but more of a add-on and not part of core game)
Premium currency is intimidating when you browse the store, however new players need to know that you can earn the Platnium (paid currency) through in game trading with other players as you earn parts and resources for certain equipment.
Paid currency is used for:
- Eliminating the build timers for items
- Buying weapons and armor without getting resources
- Unlocking more spaces in inventory (the game starts you off with some for this reason)
I will tackle a main reason it is a hit-or-miss game, why some have 100-1000 hrs and some have 10-30 hrs. The main reason is the wait. What to do when you have exhasted your resources or just finished maxing your equipment? Lots of players tend to lose intrest while others keep seeking more resources and materials. This all comes down to, how much of the world of Warframe does the player want to get their hands on? I for instance, went to do research and constantly look for new equipment as well as unlock more and more weapons the more I discover where and how to do it.
The Pros:
- Lots of weapons to collect and use
- Many Warframes/Characters to collect
- Very in-depth stat mechanic
- Tons of loadout customizing to fit playstyle
- Lots of information online (Wiki/Forums)
- Very involved community
The Cons:
- Lots of repetitive resource gathering
- Tedious drop rate percentages sometimes
- Zones need to be unlocked for certain resources
- Long wait times for item building (some players feel pressured to spend real money)
- Unique level system that is a bit complicated to grasp power gap between you and enemy units
The Verdict?
9/10
The game has a slightly high learning curve and requires a bit of knowledge of the game to effectively get you started. There is a codex in game that explains a lot more of the game outside of the tutorial however online wiki and forums are easier to digest the amount of information. Combine a MMO like Guild Wars with the stat mechanics like Dark Souls (a little less intense than dark souls but the same idea for hands-off learning). I personally only started learning how to play properly and learn all the mechanics at 60 hrs in.

I will start off by saying this, don't get attached to your Warframes as this game is ever changing and different Warframes will get either buffed or nerfed. With that out of the way, onto the review.
Warframe is a (primarily) co-op PvE game that takes futuristic weaponry and blends them with parkour-like/ninja elements. Without spoiling much, the game has an ever-expanding lore behind it that not only discusses the race that you play as, the Tenno, but also the different factions that you will come to encounter as you travel from planet to planet completing missions and quests. The first thing that I need to get off of my chest is the ideology behind Platinum because it is both something I love and hate with a passion. Platinum is the premium currency of Warframe and allows you to purchase things like more slots to hold your Warframe collection, weapons and weapon slots, and much more. I love being able to support the developers as much as I can when it comes to this game; however, my biggest gripe is that a lot of things require Platinum and Platinum does not come cheap or easy. Things that you would expect to be able to do with the other in-game currency: credits are Platinum exclusives like being able to rush the building process on certain things or even buying slots. It's questionable considering there is a multitude of ways you could easily circumvent this but it isn't the end of the world though. Just be weary when starting out that the game gives you 50 Platinum to start out and after that, you are on your own so use it wisely. Moving past that, the Warframes themselves in my opinion, are about as diverse as they possibly can be and can be easy to acquire as long as your committed to playing the game. Warframes are comprised of multiple parts that can be either acquired by grinding a certain boss on a specific planet, Void Relic missions (requires Void Relics which you can earn from other missions), and even by just completing optional lore quests. Each Warframe has its own role and purpose in the game; however, as mentioned in the first sentence of this review, don't get attached to them as the developers are actively changing how those Warframes work in terms of their abilities. Weapon diversity is a must in a game like this, and I've got to say that the game does not disappoint in that particular department. Leveling up takes time as I've found it to be based around not only completing missions/quests but also ranking up your Warframe and equipment. While leveling up, players are required to commit to a Mastery test which allows them to move onto the next level in their progression and these tests range from "Kill X amount of enemies in Y minutes" or "Hack X amount of consoles in Y minutes". Graphically speaking, Warframe has come quite a long way since its earliest days and is overall, a beautiful game to look at. Controls are slick and responsive since I would consider this to be a twitch-shooter to some extent since you never know when you'll have to be quick on your feet to take down a plethora of enemies swarming your location; that's to say for the main game where you are doing on foot missions. Archwing missions controls on the other hand (and just Archwing in general) is where I fault the game to certain extents because this is where things feel a bit more rushed and unpolished comparitively speaking to the rest of the game. Archwing is basically an aerial combat (or underwater combat) mode of Warframe and honestly, I really don't care for it because the controls don't feel as precise nor does the selection that you get for Archwing weaponry/equipment feel all that inspiring. Mission wise, there is plenty to choose from and again, the developers are always adding new things into the equation to make the game feel more fresh and new (especially with The War Within update).
At the end of the day, is Warframe a good game? I would honestly say yes. I mean, it's not perfect and it does have its faults and fair share of negative opinions and criticism; however, for a free to play title, it is one of the better ones that can be both enjoyed alone and with friends. It's worth checking out and diving into the lore even past all of the little nuances that exist for a title that has been out for quite some time.

Just look at my hours, they say it all. This game has given me experiences that can't be matched. Wether its meeting new people and learning to trust them and play with them to become strong on a server, or exploring the countless amazing places on each map. Every turn, every corner of the ARK is filled to the brim with amazing sights, dinos, and people. In the scheme of things ARK's players are some of the nicest people in a gaming community, compared to titles like Rust, Reign of Kings, DayZ, and Arma Survival mods. Obviously all of those titles are unique and much different than ARK. However, it is all player based survival, and player built worlds run by the players.
So many times have I logged onto an ARK server and said "what amazing things will I find or do today" This game has given me opportunities to make some really close new friends, and strengthen bonds with old ones. Its great to be able to start a tribe, as level 1 players. And just build and tame until you are the Alphas of a server. Not only are the PvE experiences extraordinary, the PvP is taken to a whole new level with the strategies and tactics that tamed dinosaurs bring to this game. With so many places to build, hide, and find. I remember exploring "The Center" map for about 100 hours, and still found new places that were even better than the last.
In general, this game, even with the price hike, is well worth every penny, Wether it be on an official server where you can really get attached to the people you meet and the dinos you tame. Or a 10x server where everything is much quicker, PvP or PvE it is a game like no other and is worth the investment in time, money, and effort.
And if you want someone to show you the ropes, just let me know :)
Good luck on your next ARK adventure!

The game was really fun when I played it...  Not denying it.  I played for a while on and off waiting for optimizations that came to be small optimizations.  DX12 never came sadly and along the way tames got nerfed.  Then new stuff came like craftables, a DLC, another tame nerf.... then some small optimizations and some more dlc stuffs.  Not sure how optimized it is now but DX12 seems to be a pipe dream and now with it doubling in price.... meh, I cannot recommend it.
MP Server Selection is really horrid.
SP well, from what I still read it still has bugs.  For a localized game I would think for 60 bucks SP should be bug free after 2 years of development considering only one person can play it.  (Rebalancing excluded.)
Nerfed tames, not like they were before and more so the need to nurse the stats before really taking them out exploring depending on the dino you tamed.  (Ex. Flying mounts speed nerfed - Why use a flying mount to hunt wild flying dino's when they can simply out run you?)
Biggest issue I have come across is from those that have a really good hardware setup and still cannot run the game without having graphical issues when they exceeded the recommended specs (though now recommended specs have been removed).  Issues like texture tearing, really low frame rate, had one guy have a problem loading the trees, dinos, foliage, sky, bushes, structures in one go.  That didn't go well in the end either.
MP PVE - Now I understand that some people like PVE over PVP and that is fine.  Though one thing that didn't really make much sense to me is the overpopulation of dinos in PVE.  Sure its an ecosystem and maybe breeding can happen.  Though to have more dinos in an area than the ground that they can stand on doesn't make much sense.  I am talking about dinos on top of more dinos on top of more dinos.  Like in anaconda when they find the breeding ball of snakes... I know PVE should have some sort of obstacle or difficulty to it but why are herbas, omnis, and carnis not fighting each other in the wild?  Literally were stacking on top of each other over and over again.  Instead of raising the difficulty of the dinos the solution was to put in so many different dinos one could not travel in some areas... rather large areas that didn't attack each other.  I just didn't get it at the time.
Maybe one day they will catch up with the bugs and balancing and probably more nerfing of tamed dinos with equipment.  For now this game will sit in the dark corners of my digital library until hopefully some of the base promises from 2 years ago will get met such as DX12 and other optimizations that the game sorely needs way more than content.  Especially for 60 bucks.

Vastly entertaining, very thorough, and well produced; definitely the only FPS (First Person Slasher) on the market. It has a slightly slanted community, with a lot of people at beginner level and a handful of people pub-stomping at the Master level, and not a lot of people running from Adept-Expert level. It is mildly accessible to new players, but a bit steep with its learning curve the more you persist with it. It's also very tropey, latency is definitely a major component of combat, as is grinding to get better weapons at times.
Having said that, it's not impossible to play, it's very fun and definitely unique. The game will give you many good hours, definitely worth a twenty-thirty dollar price tag. The world is also charming, and the amusing gameplay supports some realism. SOME realism. Being beaten to death with the haft of the Godfork for more damage than a mace swing is a bit of a physics conundrum, but, not gamebreaking.
Balancing issues sometimes upset people, and you can sometimes start a fight with the whole 'fair' issue. But, as long as you aren't an archer, you'll have plenty of fun playing the game. If you're an archer, you're a target and will be hunted and killed.

Chivalry: Medieval Warfare is great. The main thing with this game is multiplayer fighting with medieval weapons. And that is really fun, believe it or not. It's really that simple.
Perhaps it's the fast-paced real-time combat systems that makes it so satisfying. Or perhaps chopping off limbs and bashing heads with a giant hammer makes it satisfying... Yeah, that'd probably be it. The combat itself is very simple yet very hard to master. And the voice acting is brilliant and really funny.
The only bad thing really (except pesky archers but thats just personally...) is the bugs and glitches with rank and weaponry unlocks. But hey, let's face it: It's an indie game and none of the glitches have hold me back from playing this amazing game for lots and lots of hours.
The game is really nice looking and the combat system is really the thing with this game. If you like real-time fast-paced fighting with medieval weapons, or just gory fighting, this is for you.
I highly suggest buying this game and will give it a 9/10.

I've only played this game for a grand total of about three hours so far, but there's something that definitely necessitates a review this soon. I'll make it quick:
First impressions tell me this game is alright. I'm not sure I'd pay $60 for it, but I got it on sale. If you see it on sale and you really want to try it, go for it, but I wouldn't recommend buying at full price.
The big reason I haven't enjoyed this game as much as I would like to is that after only three hours of play, the disc space taken up jumped from around 50gb to 90gb. I'm sure the mods on the one modded server I joined didn't add up to 40gb of data, so I'm not sure where all that extra used space came from. After looking up that last issue online, I don't even have the worst of that problem, as I found multiple cases where the used disc space exceeded 120gb.
It takes quite a while to join servers (vanilla or modded) and the ping on all of the servers is quite high even though I have a fairly good internet connection. One server wouldn't let me join saying that I didn't have the required map installed even though I'm 100% sure that I did.
In conclusion, you can enjoy this game if you can take your mind off of some of the headache-inducing downsides, but I personally wouldn't spend $60 (and 90gb of my hard drive space) on this game.

So... The whole thing never pauses, does it? I guess that's part of its charm. That, and the interesting art direction. The first hundred levels are fun to 'play', then you realize the game has no more new environments or enemies to offer, and just keeps repeating everything and increasing enemy HP exponentially. It encourages you to try and cheat the system (if only to get the 35-click-per-second achievement), which is probably where it starts getting fun again, but after a few hours in the background, CH really makes you wonder why you're running it at all. If you find yourself addicted to it, just get a 100% save file off the web, and I assure you, you'll quickly lose interest, especially upon realizing that all CH has to offer for an 'endgame' is a buggy level 4725 you can't finish even with infinite DPS -- and featuring a potato head, how more anticlimactic can it get? Also, extra points for shamelessly ripping off the PotC main theme and looping it after a few seconds. For a game that wants to be played for hundreds of hours, it's an interesting consideration.

This game is pretty fun, especially with some friends in coop! I've played this game for a long time and I've even made the switch to console because all my friends are there. I've even spend some money on it because I liked it that much, something I usually don't do.
But... when you're focussed on unlocking that last frame or weapon, they throw in some more content which is ever so slightly different. That's when it hits you, this game is just a big huge grind and it gets repetitive rather soon, but you won't notice because you're thinking of that last little thing you need.
That is why this is the game that taught me Free to Play might be fun but in the end it's just one big waste of time, because it will never end. They need an active community so a few will keep their paychecks rolling.
In the meantime some awesome games with great stories and gameplay you CAN finish are rotting in your Steam library! Which is another downside to this game, because there is only a very thin story which connects the missions.
Personally I prefer a great storyline to guide me through a game, seeing this game doesn't really have that and I'm missing out on some great stories I quit this game a while back.
I would recommend the game but keep checks on your time spent in it, because you'll miss out on other great stuff if you get lost in it!

I will start off by saying this, don't get attached to your Warframes as this game is ever changing and different Warframes will get either buffed or nerfed. With that out of the way, onto the review.
Warframe is a (primarily) co-op PvE game that takes futuristic weaponry and blends them with parkour-like/ninja elements. Without spoiling much, the game has an ever-expanding lore behind it that not only discusses the race that you play as, the Tenno, but also the different factions that you will come to encounter as you travel from planet to planet completing missions and quests. The first thing that I need to get off of my chest is the ideology behind Platinum because it is both something I love and hate with a passion. Platinum is the premium currency of Warframe and allows you to purchase things like more slots to hold your Warframe collection, weapons and weapon slots, and much more. I love being able to support the developers as much as I can when it comes to this game; however, my biggest gripe is that a lot of things require Platinum and Platinum does not come cheap or easy. Things that you would expect to be able to do with the other in-game currency: credits are Platinum exclusives like being able to rush the building process on certain things or even buying slots. It's questionable considering there is a multitude of ways you could easily circumvent this but it isn't the end of the world though. Just be weary when starting out that the game gives you 50 Platinum to start out and after that, you are on your own so use it wisely. Moving past that, the Warframes themselves in my opinion, are about as diverse as they possibly can be and can be easy to acquire as long as your committed to playing the game. Warframes are comprised of multiple parts that can be either acquired by grinding a certain boss on a specific planet, Void Relic missions (requires Void Relics which you can earn from other missions), and even by just completing optional lore quests. Each Warframe has its own role and purpose in the game; however, as mentioned in the first sentence of this review, don't get attached to them as the developers are actively changing how those Warframes work in terms of their abilities. Weapon diversity is a must in a game like this, and I've got to say that the game does not disappoint in that particular department. Leveling up takes time as I've found it to be based around not only completing missions/quests but also ranking up your Warframe and equipment. While leveling up, players are required to commit to a Mastery test which allows them to move onto the next level in their progression and these tests range from "Kill X amount of enemies in Y minutes" or "Hack X amount of consoles in Y minutes". Graphically speaking, Warframe has come quite a long way since its earliest days and is overall, a beautiful game to look at. Controls are slick and responsive since I would consider this to be a twitch-shooter to some extent since you never know when you'll have to be quick on your feet to take down a plethora of enemies swarming your location; that's to say for the main game where you are doing on foot missions. Archwing missions controls on the other hand (and just Archwing in general) is where I fault the game to certain extents because this is where things feel a bit more rushed and unpolished comparitively speaking to the rest of the game. Archwing is basically an aerial combat (or underwater combat) mode of Warframe and honestly, I really don't care for it because the controls don't feel as precise nor does the selection that you get for Archwing weaponry/equipment feel all that inspiring. Mission wise, there is plenty to choose from and again, the developers are always adding new things into the equation to make the game feel more fresh and new (especially with The War Within update).
At the end of the day, is Warframe a good game? I would honestly say yes. I mean, it's not perfect and it does have its faults and fair share of negative opinions and criticism; however, for a free to play title, it is one of the better ones that can be both enjoyed alone and with friends. It's worth checking out and diving into the lore even past all of the little nuances that exist for a title that has been out for quite some time.

With the recent price hike, I might as well weigh in on ARK's stability.
TL;DR: Not worth the $60 base game, $20 DLC.
1. The game is a very big and nice game, but everything in the game comes at the price of optimization. Honestly, it is better optimized than it was at launch, but you still need amazing graphics cards to play it. For example, they recommend a Titan X for Ultra. A TITAN X, AT AROUND A $1,000. It runs on Unreal Engine 4, a great engine with chances for a beautiful game, but the optimization that ARK has makes it a dream to finally get the best result.
2. The game has a PvP and PvE mode. From what I have seen and heard, PvP is unbalanced, to the point of soloing a PvP server might as well be a baby trying to kill a bear. The official servers have what are called "Alpha Tribes", AKA tribes that can only be taken down by a huge amount of players banding together to specifically take down said tribe. With the flyer nerf that happened, flying dinos have become a joke to see, and PvE is just a type of slow experience now. You can have a huge base, with hours put into it, easily destroyed by an "Alpha Tribe" in PvP just because they didn't like how close you are to their power.
3. The price hike. Yes, this team of devs put the game up to $60 from $30. They are also the same team that RELEASED A DLC IN EARLY ACCESS, SERIOUSLY?! To say that the game is worth $50 (DLC included pre-price hike) is ok, but $80? I don't think so.
4. The devs are trash at responding to the community. They mainly focus on PvP players, and PvE players get thrown into the dirt. Once again, the flyer nerf shows it. The special PvP players snowflakes hated fast flying dinos, so the devs nerf the flyers to have a set movement speed. It basically was a huge middle finger to the PvE players, since they couldn't do anything to stop it. All the devs had to do was apply the nerf to PvP only, but they had to have the PvE players suffer too. A mod literally came out after the nerf which basically reverses the nerf, so flying dinos aren't trash (Thanks BTW, you understand the PvE struggle).
If I could refund this game and the DLC, I would. The game had potential, it lost it with greed and a dev team that can't listen to the players.

Alright. Third review for this game. It's been a rollercoaster.
At its core chivalry is a first person/third person fighter, with a simple (at first glance) combat system and a selection of 4 soldiers that will compose your brethren at arms on the field from each faction, the Agathians, a valiant kingdom, and the Masons, rebellious and battlehardened. First you have the Archer, a light hearted, silver tongued master at range, with a selection of bows, crossbows, javelins and  slings as his main weapons. Next you have the Man-at-Arms with his common weaponry as main (swords, maces, etc), hilarious voice acting and childish demeanour. His special trait is the ability to quickly lunge in any given direction, allowing him to dodge or close in on combatants.
The last two are the Vanguard and Knight, with similar weaponry at their disposal. The Vanguard being a burly brawler who is able to use smoke pots to block the view of opposing archers, and charge up a powerful charge attack, and the Knight being the manly 'shred and tear everything in his way' kind of guy, with his trait being health pool bonuses and reduced stamina usage on block. All of these (in the right amounts) can  together form an effective synergy on the battlefield.
On the subject of battlefields, each map you can play (and soon make, courtesy of one beta update in progress) is 100% self-dependant in its objectives. No need of an outside gameplay script file. This meaning map makers will have the freedom of team play objective creation. All the maps thus far in the game are clear in their order, theme, objectives and progression. A beautifully made example would be TO-Battlegrounds. A map of two warring castles amazingly immersive with nothing left out. There are trebuchets aiming at eachothers walls, the cry of scared citizens, the toll bells warning of a bombcart closing in on its gates.
About the tech, the game is built using the UDK for those familiar. A big improvement on the free sourcemod on steam. As you might know from most games such as CS:S and TF2, melee weapons are 'hitscan' with windup and release. This is a lazy (or optimized) strategy. Chivalry: Medieval Warfare scraps that and makes each weapon 100% hitbox based. Combine this with the fact that you can control your body with the mouse, and the ability to crouch and sprint, you have a solid foundation for footwork to come into play, with the oppurtunity to duck under blows and jump over mis-levelled attacks, and weave out of the opponants reach waiting for the right moment to strike. All in all (and because this is getting really long), Chivalry has extremely deep ties into combat and tactics, with hilarious voice acting all around.
This game has me hooked, and I'll probably not leave until it is dead. It keeps me coming back for the amazing moments when strangers familiar with the game and its tactics synergise together and go against impossible odds and succesfully defend a match, or silly matches when you manage to make the entire enemy team friendly and start huge fist wars. Theres so much more I want to write about, but this is starting to get bigger than anyone would be willing to read.
This is definitely (although late) my game/mod of the year.
AGATHAAAAAAA, over and out.

Clicker Heroes is a clicking-indie-game developed by Playsaurus and released on steam in 2015, however the game was
available on web browsers July 2014.
*Atratzu tactlessly copy pastes the description on steam into the story*  Okay, on a serious note, if there is a story it's that you're on an adventure and all these heroes are joining up to assist you. Where are you going? To get gold! That's about the whole thing, Scrooge McDuck.
in a word “clicking”. This is actually known as an “idle” or “afk” game. You don't give it very much attention once you start getting heroes, and you even get gold while you're not playing. However, you need to log in to purchase the next set of upgrades or beat the next set of levels/bosses.
When you first start out you need to click each time by yourself to take down the various monsters you're faced with. But soon you enlist the assistance of heroes to do all that clicking for you.
There are whole strategy guides out there on steam to help you maximize your efficiency while playing through the game, I personally just log in once before work, then when I get back home, then before bed. It's very easy to rack up hours on this game (since you can play it while you're doing other stuff) So it's very common to see people with many hundreds of hours.
To be honest, I thought “free game”? “Play while I'm afk”? “Just requires clicking”? “+Steam Acheivements”? Sign me up! That should be an easy 100% achievements.
Noooooooooooooooo....
At this time I have about a fourth of the achievements in the game. There are 65 achievements in total, the first 10 achievements are pretty much “give me's”, the hardest achievements are “Beat Zone 3,400”, “Kill 100K bosses”, “Open 10,000 Treasure chests”, and many more. Generally after getting to Zone level 160, Clicker Heroes REALLY starts.
While the game is very easy to play, and rather addictive, it is not an “easy 100%”
Clicker Heroes is completely free! So if you have free time to burn, this is your game. The only type of person I would warn about it is achievement hunters, because if you start this game your total game completion percentage will go down.
For everyone else.... Go ahead and give it a try! You'll at least get a good couple of hours of entertainment. And you might even get addicted.
In conclusion, this is a solid game, it's addicting, simple, fun, and free! It's definitely not a game that will hold your attention like Skyrim, GuildWars2, Bioshock, Left4Dead2, Counterstrike, or even other indie titles... but it doesn't try too! It embraces the definition of “afk game” and yet still makes it fun to play, in a strange almost mystical way.
I can easily recommend this to anyone with time to burn.

One game was made to rule them all... Chivalry.
Warning: Not for the feint of heart or poor sports. You will die, over and over and over again. Then some more.
This game is for you if:
1. After your first time watching Braveheart, you had day-dreams of weilding a weapon the field
2. You desire combat mechanics more complex than most FPS games out there.
3. You are a competative person, you have heart, and you come back for more until you learn how the pros do it.
4. You like the satisfaction of your sword lopping of limbs or heads.
5. You want to hear the clank of armor as you run and the clank of metal to metal when parrying a blow.
6. You want to hold a sheild to try and defend against arrows, rocks, hatchets, throwing spears and knives.
7. You want to learn how to out manuever another player to strike him in the side or back.
8. You want an even playing field as far as equipment and stats are concerned (there is no leveling or purchasing of better equipement in this game. All bought equipment is just for looks.)
9. You want to collarborate with your team to kill or defend your king (player with best score becomes king. Personally my favorite team objective scenarios).
10. Enjoy periodic updates to game even though this is a finished game and is not in alpha. I think it is awesome of the developers to keep working on this game. It shows that this is their baby and I hope they continue to make it awesome.
Don't play this game if:
1. You are just going to cry like a baby every time somebody else is better than you.
2. Don't like skill-based games because you have none or are too slow or uncoordinated.
3. Find no satisfaction in learning new fighting techniques every other day.
4. Hate the medieval era.
Pros:
Good graphics.
Good physics.
Good mechanics.
Good sound.
Very fun team gameplay.
They have huge sales often, so you get noobs that are fun to show off your skillz to.
This also creates new players, so you most always have a server with players on it.
There are multiple game types: FreeForAll, Team DeathMatch, Team Objective (like 10 or more different team objective maps with different objectives), capture the flag, king of the hill, 1 versus 1 duels. And other modes created by steam workshop.
Cons:
Some people are die-hards. I am pretty good at this game, but don't stand a chance against the elite players.
Higher ranked players are tired of losing, they'll join the winning team and pretty soon you have stacked teams (I don't have much of a problem with this because if I join a team, we either win or usually come pretty close to winning.) However, this can certainly be frustrating.
(Note: They do have servers dedicated to ranks 1 - 15. However, you get experienced players who buy Chivalry on another steam account so they can murder unsuspecting ranks 1 - 15. Losers, I know; but it happens).
Despite how good the game mechanics are, there are still glitches.
Despite the some of the cons, this is the best game ever made.

This is my first review so I'm sorry if it's a bit jumbled.
So the great the thing about Warframe, besides being a badass Space Ninja, is its lastability. The devs are constantly adding new and extremely interesting content, including but not limited to new Warframes, weapons, and story missions.
I've stopped and restarted playing Warframe maybe three times, because even if it loses my interest within a few months to a year a whole bunch of awesome updates will rekindle my desire to play, such as when the Second Dream was first released, and more recently the War Within. It's free and some things you can only get by purchasing them (Prime Vault), but that doesn't take away from experience as the PvP is♥♥♥♥♥♥so there's no real way to Pay to Win. Pretty much everything is attainable just by playing, it just takes some time to complete (for example, building a new warframe will take 4 days or so after you've finally managed to farm all of the parts).
One thing that I quite like that I have to mention is the immersion contained in the UI and everthing you do in the game. The main menu is your spaceship, and you walk around it to get to different stations such as your armory and foundry. To get half the items the free way, you need to have a clan dojo and research the items in different labs, all of which are real, physical and beautiful places that you build yourself. Even levelling up your character level (aka Mastery Rank) is immersive. You don't just hit a certain amount of EXP and then suddenly level up, you have to grind that experience up by actually experiencing new things by levelling new items and Warframes, and then once you've gained enough experience they make you take a test to level up. If you fail, you have to start all over. It sounds annoying, but in my opinion really makes you feel like you're the badass parkooring Space Ninja the game says you are: after the all farming, and waiting, and levelling, and tests, the game really does make you feel good about the things you've built and gained. You EARNED that new weapon. You EARNED that new ability. Warframe is a game about earning things by playing the damn game, and the devs have done a great job of conveying that.
Basically, if you're looking for a free coop game with an engaging and constantly changing story, tight, responsive and fun controls, gorgeous graphics, an awesome amount of customization, and don't mind some farming, look no further than Warframe.

If you don't have this game, BUY THIS GAME! This game is absolutely outstanding! Basically, you play as either an Archer (Ranged), a Man-at-Arms (Agile melee fighter), a Vanguard (polearm specialist), or a Knight (Tank).
You are separated into teams (or a Free For All) and you kill eachother and/or complete objectives (i.e. Pillage the Village, Burn the Fields, Storm the Castle, Kill the King, etc. You get it right? Medieval things.) There's also the 1v1 Duel Mode.
The combat in this game is spot on. The combat system revolves around tactical fighting. Every object has a hitbox, and each interacts in a unique way. Your hitbox is not a hitBOX it's a hitBODY. What I mean is that when you swing your weapon, you aren't just dealing damage to your opponent. Your body moves, your arms swing, your axe slices the air. Whether or not you hit is determined by whether or not the actual axe model hits your opponent. So, if an enemy has a shield on his right arm and you do a horizontal slash from his right to left, you may end up striking his shield, whereas if he blocks you might try an overhead chop over his shield.
Dodge, block, parry, feint, thrust, slash, chop, kick, jump, crouch. These are your tools. Do you choose to block your opponent's slash, feinting a thrust, and driving home a blade to his skull as he recovers from his confusion? Or would you rather stay back, unleashing a volley of arrows upon your foes? You decide!
Honestly, this is BY FAR some of the most fun I've had in a Multiplayer FPS in A LONG TIME. Last time I had this much fun was... actually I can't even remember the last time I had this much fun in a Multiplayer FPS. THAT'S HOW BADASS THIS GAME IS. Still not convinced? I used to enjoy this game quite a bit. It was easy enough to get started, the beaches were mostly safe to occupy until you got your level up, and got some better equipment. Then you could start moving inland, in which you had to be more vigilant, as dangers lurked around every corner.
However, after getting back to it from a break, I find out they've now put in an update which makes Alpha Raptors(which for those that do not know, are dinosaurs you cannot hope to beat until quite a bit later in the game), spawn two times more frequently than before, if you're playing multiplayer. Why they decided to make such an unnecessary change to a game that was challenging, yet enjoyable, is beyond me.
Now the fun has been drained out of the game for me. I've been trying to play with some friends of mine for a while now, but when your first(recommended) spawn point by the beach inhabits a Rex and three Alpha Raptors, with more arriving at regular intervals, and when you spawn somewhere else to try and start anew, you can't explore for longer than 3 minutes without running into red smoke(which signifies an Alpha Raptor), it doesn't really leave you much to go on when you start fresh.
I mean... I get that some people love the challenge, and some people probably found the update necessary, but at least give us an option to turn down the spawn rate. Until that is implemented, I can't recommend this game for new players.
