I played this game while I was between jobs in 2013 so I had a lot of time I could put into this game. It was good game if you enjoyed grinding and was just looking something to do but since then they have not really ended any real endgame and they have made the grind worse and worse.
Ultimately, in an mmorpg the grinding needs to be fun and it needs to have a purpose. At first, the grind was okay because the gameplay is pretty smooth and it does a good job making you feel powerful. You get mow down endless mobs and your character sprints, jumps, dashes, and wall runs everywhere; it feels great.
Sooner or later though it gets repetitive. You realize that all you've done is repeatedly do the same objectives over and over just so slightly improve your gear so that you can do it again. There's just no big endgame and without that you're just grinding for the purpose for grinding. The levels are procedurally generated but there are limits. They all start looking really similar, the game modes start blurring together, and the different warframes just don't feel different enough to be interesting.
I've heard that since I quit playing the grind has actually become a lot worse but warframe diversity has increased and that melee builds are not only viable, but preferred due to ammo issues at higher levels. This game also suffers from the "bullet sponge" fatigue that most shooters end up having. Its not really fun if you can empty an entire magazine into an enemies head and they still don't die.
There is a PVP but I never understood pvp in a game which requries grinding. PVP should be mostly about skill right? Why does a player who's played longer get a gear advantage? Additionally, this game was clearly designed as a PVE game from the get go so the PVP is unbalanced and a little clunky. Its hard to really fix PVP since it would adversely affect PVE as well so usually they end up alternating between catering to PVE and PVP which just makes both suck. They could have separate balancing within pvp patches only, which would work but introduces clunkiness. Why does my warframe behave differently in these different instances? Feels weird, I don't know if there's a good solution and I'm sure some companies found a good way to balance both PVE and PVP but they didn't do that here. Again, I don't know why MMOs blend PVE and PVP. Overwatch and other MOBAs exist guys, go play those.
Play it if you enjoy repeatedly doing the same thing over and over. Its fun at first but you very quickly notice that all the diverse guns, warframes, enemies, and levels aren't really that diverse.

This game is the main reason I bought the parts and built a gaming PC, because my old desktop computer was too old to play it. For me, ARK is like Harvest Moon has always been for me - a game that I can play in spurts; not play for a long time, but when I get back into it, I will play all day, every day, for days on end.
I have to admit that I would never pay £50 for this game, or any game in fact; I even find £35 expensive, but since I bought it way before the price spike I am very happy with the price I got it for, and as my hours on record show, I have spent a great deal of hours on this game. It may also help that I am a lover of animals and have studied Palaeontology to some degree, so I love just being able to tame, find and rear and ride the majority of creatures you can find in this game, which are largely extinct animals; if you're like me, I believe you'll also love this game.
Unfortunately, I have only recently gotten into the multiplayer aspect of this game, and over 300 hours of my gameplay I have played solely by myself, but I feel that both multiplayer and singleplayer saves have their own charm.
Although I generally avoid the games with mixed reviews, I have to let you know that it wasn't always like this - it used to be positive, and it's probably because of the price that it now has so many negative reviews. A lot of the comments are saying that the game still runs like rubbish, but I believe before it is actually released, it'll be much better; there have been a lot of large updates (>2 GB) in the last couple of weeks or so which shows how much the developers are working on it in these last few weeks. The only complaint I personally have about this is that it takes a very long time for me to actually download these large updates because of my slow internet speed, during which I can't play any games!
All in all, I would say I love this game to bits, but the final price of the game is indeed a lot. I'm just glad I got it when I did.

I will start off by saying this, don't get attached to your Warframes as this game is ever changing and different Warframes will get either buffed or nerfed. With that out of the way, onto the review.
Warframe is a (primarily) co-op PvE game that takes futuristic weaponry and blends them with parkour-like/ninja elements. Without spoiling much, the game has an ever-expanding lore behind it that not only discusses the race that you play as, the Tenno, but also the different factions that you will come to encounter as you travel from planet to planet completing missions and quests. The first thing that I need to get off of my chest is the ideology behind Platinum because it is both something I love and hate with a passion. Platinum is the premium currency of Warframe and allows you to purchase things like more slots to hold your Warframe collection, weapons and weapon slots, and much more. I love being able to support the developers as much as I can when it comes to this game; however, my biggest gripe is that a lot of things require Platinum and Platinum does not come cheap or easy. Things that you would expect to be able to do with the other in-game currency: credits are Platinum exclusives like being able to rush the building process on certain things or even buying slots. It's questionable considering there is a multitude of ways you could easily circumvent this but it isn't the end of the world though. Just be weary when starting out that the game gives you 50 Platinum to start out and after that, you are on your own so use it wisely. Moving past that, the Warframes themselves in my opinion, are about as diverse as they possibly can be and can be easy to acquire as long as your committed to playing the game. Warframes are comprised of multiple parts that can be either acquired by grinding a certain boss on a specific planet, Void Relic missions (requires Void Relics which you can earn from other missions), and even by just completing optional lore quests. Each Warframe has its own role and purpose in the game; however, as mentioned in the first sentence of this review, don't get attached to them as the developers are actively changing how those Warframes work in terms of their abilities. Weapon diversity is a must in a game like this, and I've got to say that the game does not disappoint in that particular department. Leveling up takes time as I've found it to be based around not only completing missions/quests but also ranking up your Warframe and equipment. While leveling up, players are required to commit to a Mastery test which allows them to move onto the next level in their progression and these tests range from "Kill X amount of enemies in Y minutes" or "Hack X amount of consoles in Y minutes". Graphically speaking, Warframe has come quite a long way since its earliest days and is overall, a beautiful game to look at. Controls are slick and responsive since I would consider this to be a twitch-shooter to some extent since you never know when you'll have to be quick on your feet to take down a plethora of enemies swarming your location; that's to say for the main game where you are doing on foot missions. Archwing missions controls on the other hand (and just Archwing in general) is where I fault the game to certain extents because this is where things feel a bit more rushed and unpolished comparitively speaking to the rest of the game. Archwing is basically an aerial combat (or underwater combat) mode of Warframe and honestly, I really don't care for it because the controls don't feel as precise nor does the selection that you get for Archwing weaponry/equipment feel all that inspiring. Mission wise, there is plenty to choose from and again, the developers are always adding new things into the equation to make the game feel more fresh and new (especially with The War Within update).
At the end of the day, is Warframe a good game? I would honestly say yes. I mean, it's not perfect and it does have its faults and fair share of negative opinions and criticism; however, for a free to play title, it is one of the better ones that can be both enjoyed alone and with friends. It's worth checking out and diving into the lore even past all of the little nuances that exist for a title that has been out for quite some time.

Best melee combat game I've played. The combat is quite deep, but no so complicated that you can't just jump in and start lopping off heads straight away (just avoid high ranked people).
There's a good amount of game modes. FFA, Duel, TDM, Capture the Flag, Last Team Standing and the best mode, Team Objective which has teams competing to attack or defend many varied objectives, like burning a town and killing all the peasants, to dumping corpses in a cistern, to sieging a castle and killing the king!
There 6 main weapons and 6 secondary weapons for each of the 4 classes to unlock, which won't take very long but will take a bit of dedication.
The 4 classes all feel very different. There are archers, who use crossbows, bows, javelins and slings, speedy man at arms who use light one handed weapons and can dodge around the place. Vanguards have the longest reaching weapons, including polearms and can do special sprint attacks. Knights are the tankiest class, with some of the heaviest hitting weapons like the maul. They are also have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ swords, which they can wield 2 handed or with a kite or tower shield.

I played the game when it was still just a browser game, and got to say that it’s fun as a time waster for Cookie Clicker clone, and quite a bit unique in its own right.
In all honesty, I like the game because it doesn't require a lot of attention and I can leave it on in the background while I play something else. The game can be conditioned to your taste as well using the Ancients, which are similar to perks, makes the level of activity you want to put into it up to you.
As an example, this combo of Ancients is good for minimal input:
Atman, Ancient of Souls: increases primal boss chance
Siyalatas, Ancient of Abandon: Increases DPS when inactive
Libertas, Ancient of Freedom: Increases gold drop when Inactive
Mammon, Ancient of Greed: Increases gold drop in general
Dogcog, Ancient of Thrift: decreases gold cost to level heroes
There is many more Ancients that can help but these are the best, if you are going strictly for very little input, when you are starting out. If that’s not your style and prefer a more active approach, there are many Ancients that can help you there as well.
The one thing I do have to complain about is the fact it does have a in game store, however, the currency used in it is easy to get and they don’t beg you to spend money. When I first saw it change in the browser version to include a store, I was afraid this would change the game for the worst. It instead didn’t affect the base game and is actually only there if you’re impatient and don’t mind dropping a few bucks for a small boost.
In conclusion, I think I can safely say that the game is a good time waster, has good art for what it is, and even though it does have an in game store, it’s not rubbed into your face telling you to buy and the currency is easy to get without money. The game is easy to pick up, as its gameplay is similar to Cookie Clicker and the like, along with the fact that it doesn’t require a lot of time put into it makes it easy to recommend. For casual players, it’s a good game to waste time with, for more hardcore players, it’s easy to sit it in the background while playing a more interactive game and still be able to progress through the game.

If you're playing coop, this game is a fun waste of time.  Single player gameplay can eventually become boring because you are more limited in experiencing what this game has to offer...
That said, this game is absolutely NOT worth $59.99.
1: The game has graphical glitches that have been unresolved for years.
2: It has rag-doll issues when a dino dies.
3: It has gameplay glitches (items falling through the world, sharks flying above the ocean, dino's stuck inside rocks, to name a few)
4:  Not a lot of substance to the actual game: the game maps are small and there is not much else to do other than explore, tame dinos, craft, summon and fight bosses, and engage with pvp battles with other tribes.   The developers have, over the years, augmented crafting, they've made the environment more immersive, and they've added more creatures, but they haven't added what this game needs: a focused story-line for the players to unravel, actual dungeons/elaborate ruins, and NPC AI the players must contend with.  That said, and I mentioned this before, the island is small...  To the point that even more creautes, like NPC's, would make the place even more crowded.  On another note, I find it funny that what is possibly the best map, Ragnarok, came in a form of a MOD which was so good they dev's picked it up; too bad Ragnarok is glitchy as hell and is only 1/2 done.

Works very well on low end PCs.  I ran it on an AMD Athlon X3 and Radeon HD6450 at low-mid at 30-60 FPS.
Overall, I would recommend.  However, I would warn interested people, the new player experience is HELL.  The game is VERY hard to completely understand at first, and weapon prices in the official market are quite sketchy, so avoid those.
Oh, and use warframe.wikia a lot.  It's basically your bible if you want to get into this game.

I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this game to anyone at this time. Especially for the ridiculous asking price currently listed. Look folks, the concept is fantastic. I bought the early-access and have played for about two weeks. I liked the concept and, wanted to love the game. I like a challenge which the game offers in spades. But....this game is so flawed currently it's simply not worth spending the money on. There are just way too many bugs. The servers crash constantly. You die endlessly and, needlessly on and off-line for no apparent reason. You then lose all your inventory which you farmed the resources for and, took the time to craft. You play for hours happily building a base to survive and prosper only to lose it all due to glitches, roll-backs, etc. Rubber-banding? Like a yo-yo. Constant dis-connects/server time-outs? Check. Game freezing? Check. Constant lag resulting in death by dino while you stand frozen? Check. Falling through a building or, the map? Check. Dying while off-line, secured in-base after logging off well-fed and watered? Check. I could go on and on. If you're taking the time to read the reviews BEFORE purchasing, kudos to you for being responsible. But, do yourself a favor...........do NOT buy the game in its current state. You WILL regret it. Wait until they officially release it, then do more reviews. Perhaps they will iron out the vast majority of bugs by then. Perhaps, they will delay the release responsibly as befitting a company that wants to be sucessful and, cares about its player base. Isn't that how you BECOME sucessful? As for customer support? Pretty much non-existent at this point. Submitting a ticket on-line is also currently a waste of time.  Don't expect replies. Folks, save yourself some heartache and refrain from purchasing this game despite whatever you might hear. It's simply not worth wasting your hard-earned dollars over at this time.
***Update***: After putting in over 700 hours into the game, I can definitely say it is not worthy of spending a dime on. The game was released for general distribution, broken. With each update something else breaks. Optimization is horrible. There's massive amounts of lag, rubber-banding, freezing and game-crashes. If you play with mods, each patch to the game causes conflicts with those which can lead to loss of game data. Imagine a month's worth of work(building,farming,etc.) gone in an instant. Even playing on an official server, you'll get no help from their so-called customer service base. Rarely even a reply. The only thing that made the game enjoyable was the modding community and, non-WC map-makers. They brought better, all-around gameplay. Even though WC encourages and, even pays some in the modding community, WC fails to support them through the release of regualr, Dev kit updates so they can fix their mods that WC's updates break. Do yourself a favor. STAY AWAY FROM THIS GAME!

ARK: Survival Evolved, is a game I have had for a bit of time, but never fully enjoyed up until recently.  With a slightly steep difficulty curve, based a lot on sheer luck, with no linear difficulty scaling to your character, it can be utterly frustrating starting out, especially if you dont know a single thing about the game or editing its settings.   However, after a bit of time, getting used to the game and its controls, it is a lot of fun, and very absorbing; I have found myself playing for HOURS at a time, and it felt like 20 or 30 minutes.   Multiplayer on a good, friendly server is a definite advantage in enjoying this game; or perhaps you LIKE a harsh, 'the strongest survives' kind of vibe, either way, you can find these and everything in between.
While there are glitches in the game (such as characters drowning in a millimeter of water if you log off standing in it or if your house is even remotely, slightly built on it.)  There are some slightly goofy animations at times, and controller support is... usable but not at all optimal on PC.. I cant really complain about my experience with this game, and would recommend it to anyone who had a half-decent rig and likes survival games, and dinosaurs.  Easily an 8 out of 10 for me.

When I first began playing this game I was very excited. Dinosaurs? Survival sim? Crafting bases, gear, weapons, taming dinos, all very exciting. Then, after playing a bit, I've realized a few problems. Okay, more than a few, I've realized this game, while having some fun points, has some severe problems that the developers have had plenty of time to address and failed to do so.
So let's begin.
The biggest problem, aside from PVP being uninspired and terrible, is how much grinding is necessary to do anything. You have to get a lot of metal and a lot other resources just to make a gun and a few bullets, and after all that grinding you might have enough for 15 minutes of actual fun. This game is full of unnecessarily tedious tasks that basically force you to buy the game for your friends just so you can grind at a slightly less agonizing rate. The grind/actual fun ratio is terrible, with it taking absurd amounts of time to tame dinosaurs, mine metal, etc. and then you lose it all.
Ark has a dinosaur breeding system. That system allows you to breed dinosaurs that are significantly more powerful than anything you can tame wild. Longstanding alpha tribe coalitions (allied groups of the most powerful tribes on servers) have dinosaurs that have been bred so much that they have 100,000 times the maximum number of mutations a bred dinosaur is supposed to have. As each mutation is a color change and/or a stat boost, you can imagine how it'd be hard to compete with dinosaurs that have literally thousands of stats higher than anything you can tame or breed yourself. The mutation cap is supposed to be 20, by the way, but Wildcard hasn't done anything to actually ensure that cap holds up. I've seen dinos with 2 million mutations or more on official Battleye (the ARK anti-cheat) PVP servers.
This results in alpha tribes being largely unchallengable. Abuse of this breeding system allows 2 people with 2 dinosaurs (with absurdly high carry weight stats of course) to fly around the map and mine all the metal on the whole map in less than 10 minutes, effectively halting the development of every other tribe/individual on the map until the metal nodes respawn, at which point those same 2 people go out again and again take all the metal on the map. Metal is a requirement for bullets, guns, crossbows, advanced technology, and metal base components, which have the highest health and resistance to attack.
While this breeding system allows abuse of the mechanics, the dinosaur maturation system leaves much to be desired. A mechanic called "imprinting" allows you to boost the stats of your dino if you "care" for it every 4 hours. This care must be given by you, and missing care lowers the imprint, and thus the stat bonuses when ridden by the imprinted rider. To anyone who hasn't guessed yet, this means kiss any semblance of an 8 hour sleep session goodbye for a couple days if you want to imprint a dino.
Furthermore, a dino baby must be hand fed for the first 10% of its life or else it will starve to death. 10% of a 2 day maturation is 4.8 hours. Ready to stare at an inventory screen for about 5 hours? You better be. And even if you do manage to do this, dinosaur babies have this nasty habit of dying from literally nothing. I've seen baby dinos that are past 10% maturity die from literally nothing. Not hunger (had full food meter), not oxygen, not damage, literally nothing. Like you can watch a baby dinosaur constantly and it can still randomly die for no reason. This happens much more frequently on PS4 and Xbox Ark than PC Ark, but it's still frequent enough on PC Ark to be a serious problem, and has remained unfixed through several updates and even the Scorched Earth DLC release.
Then there's PVP. PVP is absurd. Most of the time it's a group of people who go to another server, grief random bases as much as they can with c4 and riot shields, and then leave. 3rd party software tells these people whether the base owners are online, so they can attack while everyone is offline and dismantle said bases without real opposition. You'd think they'd take their fancy bred dinosaurs out on said griefing runs, but because those dinos when killed tell you what server they originated from, and that can lead a victim to the base of those that attacked them, dinosaurs are not often used in cross-server PVP. Furthermore people even have to change their Steam account privacy settings and profile names to make themselves untraceable, as others will use 3rd party software to track those players back to their home servers via looking up the server activity history on those Steam profiles if said steps are not taken.
PVP itself involves use of c4 almost exclusively. Turrets can be countered with shields, then disabled via C4 on a generator, and bam, base defense down. It's more effective to knock out and cage an enemy than it is to kill them, as the respawn delay for dying in pvp is about 3-4 minutes but a caged player can be disabled and taken out of the fight indefinitely. Torpidity is a separate stat from health, and a wooden club winds up being more effective in pvp than guns and bullets because of how knockout is more effective than killing players.
Then, there's the balance issues. On land, larger dinosaurs rule because their attacks are often area attacks and they can slaughter smaller dinos simultaneously, and they usually have armor. That being said, a Therizinosaurus, or "tickle chicken" as it is sometimes called, ignores armor with it's attacks and can effectively slaughter multiple larger dinosaurs at the same time. Most bases have large crowds of t-rex and brontos, which renders most other land dinosaurs unusable.
In air, it's mostly pteranodons, which are quick but cannot be shot from while riding, so aerial combat is a bunch of circling and trying to bite the other ptera. But of course aerial doesn't happen because nobody wants to fight other people who are online on other servers.
In sea, electric eels can stun a rider off of any dinosaur except a basilosaurus, and can stun lock any dinosaur to death (except a basilosaurus). So no matter what you have tamed, no matter what the stats, unless you have a basilosaurus you will be stun-locked to death and lose your dino and your gear. If you opt to use a raft and skip all that, no problem, you can be pulled through a stone wall by a kaprosuchus or sarco, or maybe a leeds will swim up and hit your raft core by no-clipping through stone walls and armoring and destroy your whole raft in a few hits.
And while on the topic of such, what's the deal with dinosaurs on land, in sea, and in air being able to use area attacks to hit you through walls? Do they just ignore walls? Being behind a stone wall should keep a "tickle chicken" from being able to hit me, but of course it just glitches halfway through the wall and hits me anyway because Wildcard doesn't know how to code a working box collider.
Finally, there's the cross-server problem of mega-tribes. A group of 60 people in a megatribe can log into a server, which has a maximum number of players of 70, and then attack. If 60/70 player slots are occupied by a mega tribe attacking, only 10 players can log in to defend. This means that as soon as a mega tribe logs in en-masse, the battle is already lost. This is a serious balance issue that, like all the other balance issues Wildcard ignores while pretending their game is somehow AAA quality (it's really not), ruins the balance and fairness that a competitive game requires.
This game isn't worth $60. It's not worth $30. Mildly pretty assets with terrible optimization and flawed core mechanics are the marks of a poor quality game. Releasing DLC without fixing major bugs first is a big deal. Doubling the price of an early access game with this many flaws is absurd. Wildcard, how about you drop the price to $1.99 until you fix the major flaws in your game, and how about you stop huffing glue and admit your game isn't close to done?

Chilvary is an outstanding indie game that amazed me with its addictive gameplay and high production values. It compensates the lack of depth in its mechanics with the variety of them - combat is a highly visceral, layered clash of tactical moves, unintrusive combos and well balanced weapons. Although individual soldiers still have a chance to defend themselves with delayed health regeneration, teamwork is essential for victory, and it can be enhanced by using tools such as fire grenades, ballistas, catapults, and even pots full of acid. Horizontal, vertical and forward strikes along with feinting, ranged weapons, shield bashing and kicking allow each player to develop their own play style and adapt it to the four classes' - archers, vanguards, men-at-arms and knights - respective strengths and weaknesses. The differing game modes - including team objectives and brawling - and excellent tutorials make the game an accessible, varied and yet repeteadly enjoyable affair with an active community that will never hesitate to flank and backstab your enemy, or lop your head off with a metre-long pike. An excellent game for an equally excellent price.

They haven't, and instead they're charging extortionate prices for a game that has no optimisations, and is becomming nearly impossible to play.

They've recently made it so mindwipe potions - a potion that allows you to reset your stats, so that you can optimise your character for a specific role; pvp, farming, crafting, weight mule - only work ONCE.
I feel it's in an effort to force players to buy the game more than once on seperate accounts just so they can get something done.
Sorry, kids. I'm not falling for it.
A cooldown timer would have made a lot of sense, of course - 7 days before you can use another potion, and it would make it impossible to abuse the damn thing - but now it's just another aspect of the game that has been rendered completely bloody pointless. Good job, team.

This massacre simulator pits you against an endless supply of completely passive creatures.
The key to victory here is that you must click on the creatures to attack them. If you are new to this kind of thing, don't worry! The creatures will just sit there, completely harmless, as they await their innevitable slaughter.
This game is an innovative and revolutionary step forward in the massacre simulation genre, as you do not even have to play the game to kill your opponents. Turn the game off for a few hours, then come back, and your 'heroes' will have massacred hundreds, possibly thousands of innocent creatures for you, collecting the coins that burst from their mangled corpses in the process.
In a world where some gaming companies make it more and more difficult to slaughter your enemies (I'm looking at you, Dark Souls), it is refreshing to see a game where you can literally advance closer to victory by doing absolutely nothing at all.
Highly recommended.

My review for ark is very simple with one word: defecate.
Through my playing experiences of ark is that this game isn't fun, all it promotes is wasting time into a game that could go one of three ways...
1. Get ahead and become an alpha tribe to rule the server.
2. Become a resource slave for the alpha tribe that is ruling the server.
3. Leave the server.
PvP
This game requires no skill when it comes to raiding other people's bases, all you have to do is knock out the enemy and destroy everything whilst they are sleeping on the floor, and then execute the survivors. Being ahead isn't that fun especially considering all you do is practically delete what someone else has spent hours of the life building, taming, farming all in a matter of minutes. you progress just and get soo much equipment for thrilling gunfight's just to never use it against other players, because there are other things that simply work more efficiently. being on the receiving end of a raid is never fun because it's just now redo all the wort that you have already done all over again, just for it all to be taken away again.
this game honours players that immediately started when a server started or just farmed a lot. as a starting tribe you farm a lot of resources to build a base to start getting tames to farm more efficiently, but that is very difficult to do if you literally need to spend hours checking up on the dino to see if it was killed or even has food in it to tame. it's the same with breeding, you spend soo much time and waste soo much time of your life checking up on whether it is alive or not.
PvE
so if you want to build houses, just farm out achievements and tame dino's, then play on PvE, possibly the most boring thing ever because there are people with bases that are inactive for weeks and you just want to build a base but can't because all the space is taken up. farm out resources just to take on bosses that aren't difficult what so ever to take out simply because you tamed several rex's to take on the boss EZPZ. but after that you get tech gear all to do nothing with, because you can't use any of it against players and that is where you move over to PvP, just to get more time wasted doing the same thing that you have already did.
This game is certainly not worth the money it is currently sold for, hell i would even pay for this game in the first place considering it requires a lot of processing power in order to be playable. you'll be better off using that money to purchase other games that you can spend your time elsewhere. The file size of this game isnt any better, my game once extracted is +-70Gb. This is probably one of the best free games out there, I know its made it to my top ten list.
One of this games handsome features to it is the fact that F2P players aren't at a disadvantege what so ever, infact, the only thing truly locked to free players is cosmetics such as color pallets, capes, armor, and warframe bodies. I don't think a lot of free games can say they have that. And earning premium currency isn't that hard either, farm for rare parts and sell them to people.
Another plus is that the game has wonderful looking graphics, some of the best I've seen out of free games.
Speaking of wonderful graphics, how about wonderful design? This game as some of the greatest original character, enemy, weapon, and world design I've ever seen in a video games, a lot of free games consist of your basic fantasy elfs, dwarfs and what not, but did you ever expect to see magic robot space ninjas? nither did I.
The combat feels wonderful, jumping around the map shooting and butchering hords of enimies with whatever junk you managed to built in the foundery, which is also another key feature in this game, crafting, hundreds of different weapons availible to you, most all are different in some way or another, it is impossible to find one that dosen't suit your play style.
The story is also something I'd like to touch on, for a free game, the lore is reletivly complex, and may sometimes leave you scratching your head. And there are little quests in the game, most of it is just farming and leveling gear, although the main questline is wonderful, it is pretty short, it probably won't stay that way, cuz oddly enough, even almost after four years of being released, they are still working on the main questline, and by the looks of it, they are taking their sweet time with it, and that may be a good thing, but I think its a little crazy that they are still working on it.
There is deffinitly more to write about this game, and I didn't even touch the surface of its flaws, but I will say this, it is a wonderful game if you don't mind a lot of farming, a third person co-op shooter, and its free, I see no reason you shouldn't at least give it a try.

I think it's time that I write this review as this game has been awaiting its praise that its finally getting, and for good reason.
If you are a potential returning WF player, I can tell you what has changed, but it vastly depends on when you left. Here's the jist of it
-The void is no longer your only tileset to play over and over again (Prime part changing is chaged to all over the star-chart)
-Lategame sorties have become much more rewarding, albeit they still need a little tuning (looking at you Nitain)
-Kuva mods have finally settled in a place I love. It's not hard to farm the rerolls for them and getting them and using them, and then getting all the materials for completing the full build feels so rewarding and awesome. Getting that trash-tier hind into a late-game sortie weapon is an amazing feeling

My recommendation is mostly positive, but there are some huge negative points I want to point out too.
Why do I recommend it?
It looks fantastic, specially the map called "Ragnarok". There are a lot of animals in the game, by far most of them are very useful for their own things, they are fun to have and you'll always feel progression even tho you play PvE or PvP.
There's a bit of fps in this game when you reach a good level and get some stuff.
It's very fun to play and it is very enjoyable to play.
It's also base defense, at least in PvP, there's always going to be raiders.
It is very much base building, you can be very creative or abuse certain .. I'll call them glitches, I don't think they are meant to be in the game. Such as stacking 10 walls upon eachother.
"NEGATIVE POINTS".
There are some bugs in it, non major bugs, just some annoying bugs.
It is very easy to be stuck in your dinos, or sometimes, when you fly a flying creature, when you pick someone up, they just teleport straight back to where you have picked them up, which is a bit annoying.
There are some very annoying and insanely pointless creatures that you meet far too oftent, such as two different kind of animals that steal a random item from you.
Oh well, to the by faaar biggest negative point I have. If you play on an official server.. If you don't know about it, you can transfer stuff/dinos/characters from server to server, which means that some big tribes can dominate their own server, gather a sh*t ton of metal, dinos, etc. and just transfer over to other servers to wipe out other bases or even servers.
Sadly, it's not rare to get raided by other servers and if you are new or a smaller tribe, then there is literally nothing you can do about it. It's so stupid, it should not be in the game.
So, this game might be very fun and enjoyable, until you realise how the end game looks. At least in PvP, which is by far more fun than PvE. You'll get ♥♥♥♥ed either sooner or later if you are not a very big tribe / have many big allies and even then, you might still be fked over. They should fix it, if not, it's just going to be a nightmare playing PvP Ark on Official servers.

When I first saw a couple of folks on my friends list playing Clicker Heroes, I was intrigued and decided to check it out.  After reading the store page description, I thought, "What kind of idiot would play THAT game?"
Hi.  I'm Larry.  I'm an idiot.
The premise of the game is ridiculously simple.  Click on a monster.  It dies, you get gold.  Get enough gold and you get to buy the services of a hero.  The hero either increases the damage of your click or gives you a damage per second (DPS) bonus.  This lets you kill more monsters, which gets you more gold, which lets you buy more heroes (or improve the once you have) until you decide you don't want to go any farther and then you just start the cycle over again.  But when you start over, you carry over certain bonuses, so in each cycle you get progressively stronger, faster, better smelling and downright sexier.
Sounds like nothing more than a Skinner box appealing to mindless time wasting, you say? Well, it is.  But it's an absolutely awesome Skinner box.  The graphics are wonderfully cartoonish, the music suitably rousing, and the sight of monsters going kablooie from nothing more than your sheer force of will amazingly gratifying.  And..it's free.  Genuinely free.  Yes, there are microtransactions in the form of 'rubies'.  But the currency actually drops (albeit a bit slowly) in game so you aren't forced to pay anything.  That's a tough combination to beat.
So, if you're looking for a mindless time waster that looks reminsicent of Saturday morning cartoons and scratches the itch of your inner sociopath, give Clicker Heroes a shot.  You might find that being an idiot can sometimes be a refreshing blast.

This game could be really fun. But there is some many things that are wrong since day one that can make the game pretty frustrating without you doing something wrong.
I wont talk about the game mechanics (taming, balance,...) because there are a lots of review about this, so I will focus on one thing : the physic !
How can a game have a physic that bad ? I mean, you can get stuck by literally nothing, just try to walk near a dino and enjoy the stuttering. Sometimes you get stuck in your dino, then you manage to move away, and the server makes you rollback to your previous position and you just have to try again, and again, enjoying the rubberbanding hopping the server let you move.
And this is with one dino. Imagine when you have 5 Rex following you, with their heads clipping into your body, or when you're on a Rex trying to kill small dinos that manages to clips into your Rex, making you unable to move and to attack.
I can talk about the hitreg with bows, crossbows or guns that is awful. On a server with hit indicator enabled, you can see that you hit by the blood effect, but a lot of times, the server won't register your shot. The inverse is possible, you miss your shot (no blood) but the server considers you hit correctly.
Fun facts, if you stand on the Quetzal (a big bird) and you try to shoot something down, you have a high probability of shooting you own birds even though you are absolutely not shooting on it (you can sometimes see the arrows stuck in the void).
Really, this is mostly what makes me not recommend this game, because these problems are mostly what (literally) kills me most of the time : being stuck, shooting my own dinos, and not hitting the others.

The first time I heard about Ark was in reading an article on Polygon about how tribes got tired of a griefer attacking newbs who then found him and put him in a cage for days as punishment. The more I read about the game and basically how open it was made me want to play. I hesitated for about two years because I know how in to any mmo I get. Well, then came a steam summer sale and I got it for a price that was too good to refuse lol. Since then I've played a lot and really enjoyed it. It is a great game and an awesome premise. I would love to see more communication beyond initial statements from the Wildcard team though. One of the biggest components of any game succeeding is a strong and committed initial user and fan base. When they get frustrated and leave it is never good for the game. I think that despite the amazing promise of the game there is a risk of that unless communication gets a bit better from the team to the users.
Servers can be wildly unstable and as the patches are coming out there are some very bizarre lags and resets happening. There isn't enough communication when this happens. For instance my server has been down for over 24 hours and there hasn't been a single official post about it despite many people talking about it and submitting bug reports. It is an early access game and we will all forgive issues but we need updates.
There are frequent patches. This is definitely a pro. But can lead to some weird bugs so just remember this is still an early access game and give it some leeway.
The only other real thing is that the game isn't for the weak of heart. It is mostly based around pvp and that means you will get raided. You will get wiped. Often it is for no other reason than because someone is bored. But if you try to talk to people on your server and get to know them it really does help.
It's a fun game and I'd recommend it even with its bugs. The team is clearly trying to improve the game every day.

Just a forewarning for anyone considering purchasing the game: Do not. Or at the very least, wait. Game was recently raised to a $60 price tag - which you may be thinking means there is a good chance its polished like other AAA games that are sold for a similar price. That thinking would be wrong.
I bought this game thinking with the release date being set and the price raising, it must be in a pretty good spot. Optimization is what everyone who plays the game keeps saying they are waiting on, but it seems like the game just runs poorly. Lag and rubberbanding are frequent on even the official servers. You'll have to spend 2-3 hours adjusting settings to get decent FPS.
Don't even get me started on the community. Extremely toxic. New players on a PVE server can't build anything because tribes have "pillars" over all buildable land. They say it is to prevent people from building over important resources, but internet trolls then become the gatekeeper for an entire server. The servers are relatively old as well, the majority of non-pillared land is taken. You're pretty much out of luck unless you find a private server which is a time consuming process.
Overall, I'd give it a 2/10 - its a cool idea, its just poorly implemented, doesn't seem to be improving, and there are just too many game breaking bugs, even for an early access (and ESPECIALLY for an early access at $60).

People who keep complaining about performance must be judging based on the online experience. Yes, the official servers are a horrible experience, lots of stuttering and random rubber banding. However thats where the complaints end, single player and private servers (less than 15 people) run fantastic. One of my systems has a gtx 770 and a FX-8350 and runs this game between 30-40fps at epic and high settings (low AA). The 2 settings that lag this game to death are "Screen Space Ambient Occulsion" and "Ground Clutter Distance".  Turn the ambient occulsion off and gain at least 15fps. The Ground Clutter Distance is a strange one, anything below about 50% of the bar is fine but as soon as I put the slider at the halfway mark or higher frame rate drops by 10. Can be 45% of the bar and be fine but soon as it hits 50 its like something changes drastically.  Alter those 2 settings and you should be able to run this fine. Dont listen to people saying the same old crap for the last year when it comes to performance.

Short Answer:
This game is an addiction, and is the "prime" definition of a mixed bag. It is a very strong Multiplayer game with a stong foundation, but is plagued with drama, grind, frustration, toxcicity, and many many years of Developer controversy. As a devoted veteran since the early days of only 1 tileset and "Excalibabe", I can tell you I am not sure it was all worth it.
Long Answer:
PROS:
Consumability
This game is the pinnacle of "just five more minutes". It holds a large amount of content for co-op PvE, which it handles very well. The large variety of characters you can play as have diverse strengths that contribute to the team aspect, and there are so many weapons to fit any playstyle. The mission variety also is lagre, varying from fast captures, to invested defences, all with a large array of foes to face. The game has a wealth of content that can give many hours of playtime to those who look.
Progression
This game also has fantastic and intricate player customization, being fondly named "FashionFrame". There is a strong sense of player progression trhough Mastery Ranks that you achieve through all the weapons and characters you used. For those who have friends online and in day-to-day, having them play with you and making a clan is the best way to play, creating a solid community in the process. Overall the PvE of Warframe is some of the best I have seen in a multiplayer game.
CONS: This has been a long time coming...
"Free to Play"
In giving the pros for this game I omit one thing: this game is... "Free to Play", which turns out to mean its motto of "ninjas play free" is really "ninjas pay a lot actually". While not technically "pay to win", it is definately not very far. Ever since you discover you can't get your third character since you reached your "warframe slot capacity" it becomes apparent that the Grind in this game is very, very, VERY real. I have met many players in my three+ years in game who are avid players since day 1, and are still grinding there way to get Platinum, the secondary currency in Warframe that DOES NOT DROP IN GAME. You must either pay up or grind for hours to sell items to players who also paid up. In either way you get Plat, somone pays. Almost all cosmetics, whether it is skins, armors, basic color palettes to simple standing animations; all must be bought with Platinum, and have no other way to aquire. Recently (2016), Warframe has been releasing TennoGen, a player made skin project where they have players make their skins for them, sell them in-game for REAL CASH  (not Platinum anymore, forget the middleman), and only give the creator 30%. Its a front to make more money at best. It seems as if Warframe is increasingly pressuring new and old players alike to spend their money with less and less to offer.

Verteran Wall
To continue the list of grievances, once you either paid your way or grinded your way to the highest Mastery Rank by getting all weapons and characters, you soon discover that there is no endgame. The high level missions that are meant for experienced players, such as Sorties and Trials, become both boring and repetative. Warframe focuses their content on new players and how to get their engagement and money than their most devoted players, echoed by popular content creators like Tactical Potato, and Mogamu. The game hits a hard wall, where you feel stolen of your time and money after so long.
Exclusives
If you are any type of collector or completionist, you should beware Warframe, this game has many items that are exclusive, reigon locked, and just plain impossible to get. Currently you cannot even get all of the game achievements, since they inherently pad the game time with directly connecting the Mastery Rank to the amount of weapons in game. Many skins, cosmetics and even entire characters are unable to get at this time, such as Excalibur Umbra, Vaulted Primes, and the timed exclusive cosmetics. This is an obvious scheme to create rarity and demand where there is none, not only opening the door for Prime Acess Packs, but for Prime Unvaultings in the future.
Updates
Also updates are rarely substantial. For a game that stands consistantlt as the 20th MOST played game on steam, the immense income that DE earns does not show in the release of content. While new content does comes out, it is either in the form of Prime Acess packs, exclusive new pemium items that you must buy or grind for, or just to infrequent. It is also common knowledge that Warframe has no story whatsoever. Only 2 quests actually have cutscenes, or even what can be defines as a "narrative". All the "quests" besides the Second Dream and The War WIthin are horrid excuses for a plot, and are just glorified versions of the missions you play dozens a day. It is widely known that Warframe has a weak storyline at best.
"PvP"
While the game has excellent PvE, the "PvP" in the game is almost unplayable. An obvious overthought, the competative modes are broken in both the balancing and mechanics. All the character powers, stats, weapons and mechanics have to be mangled to be "balanced", and even then most matches are dominated by certain characters and weapons of unparralelled meta. The addition of a lacrosse-like mode Lunaro was nice, but even there the time to get a match is extememly long due to lack of players. When you finally find a match after a gruelling wait you will either be  swept by players using cheap tactics or have an unsatisfying match due to one team having more players than the other.
Community
While not on the fault of the game itself there is a part of the Warframe Community that is some of the most hateful I have seen to date. The group is abeit small, buts is very vocal and extremely toxic. I have seen racist slurs, death threats and persistant bullying that have cut many deep occasionally, since no one is expecting such diatribe. Also many take any form of criticism, constructive or not, as heresy, and "White Knights" are rampant in the forums. You are often silenced for having anything not positive to say about the game. While it is obvious that debates can be healthy, anyone knows when the discussion turns to mob mentality.
Developers
To nail the coffin shut, there is the Developer controversy. While I have grown with them ever since Steve went on all fours like a dog, and the game was still blooming, I still stick with them in hopes that they will do the right thing (Rebecca even added me as a friend in-game). Yet they have a support team from Hell. Their question desk is actually quite responsive and kind, which I thank for, yet then why do I have such animosity toward them then? They are more ban-hammer happy than ANY GAME I EVER PLAYED. I have had several friends, some with HUNDREDS of dollars in-game be banned or being warned that they might be banned for activity they do not know, and when they appealed it, they recieved a copy-pasted email with no answer and were all banned from support. I fear that I may have a similar fate, and many share my grievances.
To All that Read this Rant this Far
I do not mean to demean the developers, or their community, since I am part of it. I have played over one THOUSAND hours into this game, and spent more than I ever wish to disclose. I have been a part of thr community for years and made many friends. I still play the game and often enjoy it too, despite my complaints, yet it has been long past the golden days. I often play out of almost obligation, I spent so much time and money it would be a waste not to play. I have fond memories, and you will too, but it is bittersweet nostalgia at best. For how popular, rich and old this game is with these points, I cannot reccomend this game.

Ark is by far one of the most impressive games to have ever come on Steam. Many of their buffs, nerfs, and changes have been an amazing addition to the game. But the stupidest thing they could have ever come up with is cross-server transferring. Now I understand why, because some dinos only spawn on certain maps. The issue here is that devs still has not done much to curb the rampant duping in this game.
For example, one server I had explored on had a tribe who built on EVERYTHING and blocked as much as they could to prevent newer players from experiencing the game. The Center map that they were on (but no longer logged onto) had various spawn areas blocked. Volcano Island had nothing spawning on it anymore due to the massive amount of metal foundations planted everywhere and the dinos they had duped sitting there. How can you tell they were duped? Same level, appearance and at least thirty of them. If their base is massive, yet not a sign of any gathering dinos, you can tell something is off.
Then let us not forget the cross-server dupe raiders, that when they get on the server, aim to kill everything. They use lights to dupe hundreds of C4 to not only blow open into tribe bases, but to wipe out every foundation, gates, and owned dino on the map. How can you tell they're duping? The constant "123 has joined the Ark" if you have the notifications turned on. If you see that constantly spamming, you know you're going to have an awful time.
This has been going on for a while now, and there hasn't been much effort into stopping this. They say that they are recoding servers to prevent duping when the game releases, but I'll believe it when I see it. I WON'T recommend this game to anyone until they fix this disgusting exploit. This game isn't worth the $60 if new players will only face duping raiders who will destroy everything they have.
My review on this game is subject to change if they actually come through and fix the duping issue.

OLD REVIEW BELOW THIS TEXT:
830+ hours (downloaded outside of steam). I would rate Warframe 4 out of 5 stars.
Pro:
- Truly free game. I've used the trade chat and farming to make enough money to get almost anything I've ever wanted in this game. And if I couldn't afford it, there was enough other options to get by with that I didn't care.
- Great action combat between every weapon type imaginable. Shotguns/ assault rifles/ great swords/ lasers/ katanas/ ninja stars/ scythes/ cannons/ grenade lauchers/ etc.
- HUGE variety in weapons, classes-(frames), and mods-(builds) that allows a broad selection of play styles. The builds can be changed at any time for free.
- Super active community full of helpful people. The region chat is always active, no matter what time I log on.
Cons:
- Not enough content. I was bored very early in this game, but I found goals to keep me playing. Mostly farming for a weapon I thought was interesting, or a frame, trying different builds for weapons and frames, etc.
- Very fast paced and antisocial in most public games with strangers. Not enough time to communicate because players rather compete for the most kills or the highest damage, then rush to the extraction and never see them again. It's better with clan members though.
- I can see it slowly transitioning into the endless RNG grind that mmorpgs are notorious for. They've recently added Riven mods (extremely strong mods), which cost kuva, kuva takes a long time to farm. You use kuva to reroll the stats on a riven mod. Also, riven mods are for random weapons. You don't get to choose which weapon it will be for. As you reroll the random stats, it begins to cost more kuuva each time, forcing you to go grind more kuva, searching for those perfect stats.
They said Riven mods were to encourage players to use older, weaker weapons, but they also gave riven mods to the META, the best weapons... That's not going to encourage us to play older/weaker weapons. It's going to force us to buy or grind for Riven mods for the BEST weapons if we want to keep up. And since players are selling these Riven mods for THOUSANDS of platinum, the grind is becoming ridiculous.
Can I stop this and play a real game now? Please??

OKAY. I have never felt qualified to actually leave a steam review before. But with this many hours played on this account, and at least fifty on another, let me tell you what I think.
The concept as a whole is probably the single most awesome concept for a game I have seen (or will see) In a while. I am incredibly partial to dinosaurs as a whole, so seeing this about a year or so ago I had to get it. It had mixed reviews then, too.
So, let me start with the pros as best I can:
It has a solid survival element that you definitely don't get to overlook until you've EARNED enough to gain modern type convieninces. It's beatuiful. Each map is entirely different from the next and incredibly large. There are SO MANY different ways to play and enjoy the game, It has yet to shake my interest and I haven't accessed everything. I have tried to get all of my friends to come and play it with me. It appeals to many different types of playstyles. If you want to design and build things? This is a great game for you. You want to go ape sh*t and go axe, sword,bow,gun,explosively detonate murder every  living thing you see? This is the game for you. You want to explore an expansive and diverse world? This game got you covered. If you want to quell every mighty beast into submission to fight and serve by your side, this fufills that need. There's even a really cool way you can breed, genetics and coat colors being inheritive factors.  There's just so much to this game. To top it all off, you can choose to go multiplayer, or just play with you and your friends. Adding an entirely different dynamic to it. There is constant updating both fixing issues and adding content. I have grown with this game, and am entirely proud of where it is today. It has exceeded my expectations.
Alright, a few cons:
The online community has been incredibly hit and miss for me. Between alphra tribes squashing everything into submission, and the amount of people who have fun picking on newly spawned is ridiculous. Starting out by yourself is incredibly hard. Log off for too many hours and come back to have all your things destroyed, and raided and you have nothing once again.  Don't get me wrong, there has been some really awesome pvp servers, and I've had fun times. there's always PvE mode as well. Just not enough to be worth it for me.
It can also be glitchy sometimes. It takes a lot from my computer to run and there tends to be a decent amount of server lag. Sometimes you get stuck or caught on things and not get out of and have to suicide. I would put more cons to balance out the pros if I could think of anything else.
So,
This game can be insanely difficult. You're a pudgy naked person dropped in the middle of a dinosaur infested island and it's up to you to survive. It's only common sense that you should expect to die a LOT if you don't make the right decisions. The challenge makes everything you achieve more worth it. This is by far my favorite game. I do not plan on putting it down anytime soon, and I have been literally it nonstop for a year.  I absolutely highly reccomend this game for creativity, gameplay, and general overall badassery.

NINJAS. IN. SPAAAAAAAAACE.
The game starts off with a very compelling tutorial that both gives you a very good grasp of what the gameplay's like, and leaves you curious as to what the world has to offer. Movement may take some getting used to - and even later on, it can still feel a bit... slippery, but it still feels amazing to run along walls, slide beneath gaps, glide through the air shooting at enemies... Gunplay and swordplay are simple and fun; with a vast array of weapons to choose from and mods to modify them. And there are plenty of Warframes - that is, playable characters - to craft or buy. Killing enemies by the literal hundreds in a single mission is very satisfying.
The game might not really LIVE on the story, but there are a handful of quests that tell it EXTREMELY well. Without spoiling, the Second Dream, Sands of Inaros and War Within have amazingly well-told stories that made me love this game even more.
As a Free-to-Play, I found this game to be the most fair with its premium system; some of its daily rewards can be discounts on buying Platinum, and you can earn most if not all of the weapons/frames/etc if you're willing to really work for it. And for a Free-to-Play, it looks DAMN good and runs DAMN well.
On the downside, sometimes doing things solo can be more difficult - even when you have no choice but to solo when the mission you're looking at has no one else to party up with. Makes it very frustrating for certain quests - especially the Jordas Precept. (Although, with the exception of Archwing missions, Valkyr makes it VERY easy to solo missions with her Ultimate power. Which is probably why she's my main...) And this may be par for the course in a game with crafting, but farming some rarer resources can be a real drag.
Bottom line:
PROS:
+Fun blend of sword and gunplay
+Slaughtering enemies by the hundreds - sometimes you can perfectly, vertically bisect an enemy with a single powerful shot.
+Wide variety of Warframes, Weapons and Mods
+Some utterly FANTASTIC Story Quests
+The Archwing - basically a Gundam
+A great business model that seems to truly value its players, not feeling like it DEMANDS your money
CONS:
-Farming stuff can be agonizing - good luck finding the Void Relic you want, and good luck getting your desired item from it. RNGesus is king when it comes to loot.
-Some missions may demand you go solo - which might not be a viable solution. Maybe find a Clan to join, and find someone who can help you out.

ARK is a double-edged sword.  Is it a great game? Yes. Is it a bad game? Yes, sort of.  As far as the gameplay, graphics, sound, etc.  the game is easily 8/10, but the game has it's problems.  Most notibly is the community.  There are pockets of good people, but for the majority of the servers you will ask a question and all you will recieve is a "OMG NOOB GET OUT!" kind of response...keeping it PG there.  Then there's the problem of PvP.
This actually isn't a PvP game at all.  It's a Player vs Offline game.  I have only ran into 3 people or groups of people, yes THREE, that actually wanted to PvP.  Most of the time you will log off, and the log back in to find all your dinosaurs you spent hours taming, and base that you spent even more hours building destroyed while you were gone.
So you think, "I'll just go play on a PvE server"  Well there's one glaring problem with that...99% of the land is taken on PvE servers.  You can literally spend hours running around trying to find a spot to place a campfire to cook food, let alone actually build a base.  I hope you like berries, because that's about all you're going to be eating.  The community on PvE servers is also usually just as toxic as on PvP servers.
The game itself is a great game, but the players ruin it and there have been no measures taken to fix the glaring problems with the community.  I can't recommend the game, but instead of a 8/10 I'd have to give it a 3/10, because you simply can't play the game at times due to the players.

Clicker Heroes is a game in the making, currently at version 0.19 at the time I played it; as such, I think I can forgive it for not having much in the way of content.  It is, however, also an idle game -- meaning that you can, in theory, "play" much of this game without actually being around to witness your progress.  Sure, you have to be there in the beginning to click enemies to death and you always have to be there to spend money you've amassed on hiring and/or training new characters to help you keep up to pace, but there is a certain charm to the idea that you can accomplish something while also doing something else, and if that's what you're looking for, this fits the bill: it has incredibly low system requirements, allowing you to do most anything else (including playing another game entirely) while progressing through this game.  But is it worthwhile to do so?
I remember being in the first or second grade, silently lording over my classmates that I knew not only what came after a million (a billion), but that I knew what came after that (a trillion), and
(a quadrillion!).  Before this game, I could really only go up to an octillion before having to think about it ("Is it a
tillion, a
tillion, or what?").  This game goes far beyond that.  Far, far beyond that.  In a game filled to the brim with exponentially rising damage and health, what starts out at 1 damage per click, 10 health per enemy, and foe each worth about 3 gold in the first stage quickly turns into having quadrillions upon quadrillions of damage per second, almost irrelevant damage per click unless you have the click speed of a god, enemies with over 8 quintillion health and a bounty easily in the hundreds of trillions.  And that's in the unmodified, first playthrough.
You probably won't be able to pass level 140 (of at least 3,600 to 4,725 depending on where you think the game really ends) on your first playthrough of the game.  The giant, writhing tentacle boss there has over a nontillion HP, and without grinding out the previous level for at least a day straight, you may well never attain the funds needed to upgrade your semi-colorful cast of compatriots to adequate DPS (Damage Per Second) to take it down in the 30-second timeframe all bosses start off having.  So what do you do?  You start over, of course!  A character you usually get access to around level 80, Amenhotep, has an ability that effectively resets the game, save for a few things: You get to keep your in-game achievements and the bonuses thereof, items called Relics that only appear
the first playthrough, gilded heroes that permanently increase the damage of certain members of your squadron, and objects called Hero Souls that can come from random bosses starting at level 100.  You can use Hero Souls to purchase and upgrade beings called Ancients (that also carry over) that can provide all kinds of bonuses to help you get not only past that level you couldn't get to before, but also get to it much faster than before.  After the first playthrough is where the game really starts to gain any sort of depth.  A playthrough that can easily take at least a full day to complete.
Clicker Heroes is an ungodly long game.  I will admit right now that I utilized some... outside help to speed things along when the game slowed to too much a crawl for my tastes.  This is clearly meant to be played across the span of months, if not even a couple years, but I managed to complete the game and experience what it has to offer in just under 40 hours by playing at at least 100x the speed for most of my playing experience.  The main appeal, I find, is in finding what combination of hero levels, ancients, ancient levels,  gild spots, Hero Soul count, relics, and whatever else the game throws at you at what time can get you through the game the fastest.  What combination in the right order can get you from level 1 to level 3,600 and help you deplete that boss's novemseptuagintillion* health in the shortest amount of time?  Attempting to find out is quite the time investment though, and the error side of trial and error could potentially set you back months of work.  I would honestly not be surprised if this game was used as the basis of some kind of thesis for a college senior mathematics major.
With a cute and inoffensive presentation, Clicker Heroes can satisfy the needs of any idle-game addict, and maybe even attract a few newcomers to the genre.  Between clicking down monster flowers and troll/ogre hybrids and trying to find that optimum build, you could be kept busy with this game for months on end if you find yourself engrossed in the gameplay going on.  I find it perfectly understandable to think this game a colossal waste of time, or just not even fun.  I really don't think it's a fun game myself, once the huge numbers lose their appeal and the sense of progression dies down because the most recent boss has a higher jump in HP than the others so far and I don't want to wait hours to grind out the gold to beat it and the next four levels after it.  I do think it's an interesting experience that should be tried for curiosity's sake.
So do I recommend this game?  Yes.  Not for the fun, but for the experience.

So, this is a mixed bag for me, but I'm going to tackle it in the most level-headed way I possibly can to articulate my points. I'll start with a pros vs cons of the game then write a little blurb at the end encompassing my thoughts on the game and studio as a whole. Without further adieu,
PROS:
-Visually stunning. The textures and lighting are top notch on MAX settings.
-Variety of creatures and wildlife. They do their own things, from denning to hunting, and have different uses for players.
-Varied gameplay. You can almost always find some task to complete or progress.
-Large community. A decent amount of players play ARK daily.
-New content. The devs do try to put new content in frequently, but this is a double edged sword.
-Huge tech tree. The tech tree, or "engram" menu is expansive and varied. You can make everything from piping to firearms.
-Customization. The character creator is decent, and you can customize your base any way you like, so player choice is HUGE in this game. It's YOUR story of survival on the island.
-Fun. For what it's worth there are quite a few moments in ARK I just found myself having downright fun with my friends. (^ As always it's less about the game with this one and more about your personal group of gaming compatriots. ^)
CONS:
-HORRIBLE Optimization. It struggles to run sometimes on absolute beasts of systems. I managed about 90 FPS on MAX with my current build, specs available on my profile, and I know others that struggle to run it at all with even high end card and processors. BEWARE THE SYSTEM REQs.
-Filled with visual bugs and glitches. From popping in textures to missing assets, it's all here, folks. You will run the gamut of standard visual bugs barring some of the more extreme variants in other games. Models fold in on themselves and distort, which can lead to some interesting moments.
-Can get boring. There is a point in time that you will eventually exhaust the current tree of things to build, and are left with few options. If you're on a PvE server, it's usually pick a new place and expand or start over. On PvP it usually comes down to beat the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of everyone else on the server until they cry and understand you are the ALPHA.
-Lack of PvE content. Aside from taming, and the "Ultimate Life Form" Boss-like encounters, there's a surprising lack of things for players to do with the environment. Aside from hit things with other things that is.
-Widlcard Studios' greedy nature. Somewhat of a personal gripe at the moment, but could become an issue later on after full release. SWC has already doubled the price of the game (BEFORE FULL RELEASE - It is $59.99 as of writing on 7-16-17) and released a $19.99 "expansion" during Early Access. This company truly does care more about your dollars than your opinion, so be forewarned about it.
(This one is kind of a personal thing and isn't WC's fault so I'll list it down here separately from the main list.)
The community. The commmunity in this game is pretty damn toxic. Aside from playing with my friends, on a PvP server it's generally people putting pillars up everywhere to prevent other players from building due to the proximity feature or "ALPHA" tribes running around servers pushing people's♥♥♥♥♥♥in for no reason. Might be you said one of them looked off one day so they decided to raid you. For some this is a plus as rebuilding adds replay to an extent, but for me it comes down to being more of the "Bully smashes my sandcastle because it's more creative than what he made" principle. Doesn't even have to be that honestly, just know that most of this game's player base is a bunch of hot heads that love making other's experiences hard. It is what it is.
And finally, my overall thoughts. Is ARK a bad game? No. It has its flaws and its successes, but overall it's just kind of bland in my opinion. Gameplay quickly becomes walk here hit this make things repeat until you have base. Taming Dinos takes exorbitant amounts of time on official servers (Hours for the bigger guys) and if you turn the multipliers up so it takes less time it feels like you're cheating the system. I will not personally be spending my time on the game any longer because of SWC's business tactics, but even if that hadn't happened, I still don't have the kind of love for the game that will drive me to play every day even. It was fun for the few hours I put into it, but overall I still feel the game isn't even close to complete. For this game to be pushed out as a full AAA title in the state it's in is wrong. Overall, wait until it's on sale for a fraction of the price and try it for yourself. In no way, shape, or form is this game worth $60 though.

So, this is a mixed bag for me, but I'm going to tackle it in the most level-headed way I possibly can to articulate my points. I'll start with a pros vs cons of the game then write a little blurb at the end encompassing my thoughts on the game and studio as a whole. Without further adieu,
PROS:
-Visually stunning. The textures and lighting are top notch on MAX settings.
-Variety of creatures and wildlife. They do their own things, from denning to hunting, and have different uses for players.
-Varied gameplay. You can almost always find some task to complete or progress.
-Large community. A decent amount of players play ARK daily.
-New content. The devs do try to put new content in frequently, but this is a double edged sword.
-Huge tech tree. The tech tree, or "engram" menu is expansive and varied. You can make everything from piping to firearms.
-Customization. The character creator is decent, and you can customize your base any way you like, so player choice is HUGE in this game. It's YOUR story of survival on the island.
-Fun. For what it's worth there are quite a few moments in ARK I just found myself having downright fun with my friends. (^ As always it's less about the game with this one and more about your personal group of gaming compatriots. ^)
CONS:
-HORRIBLE Optimization. It struggles to run sometimes on absolute beasts of systems. I managed about 90 FPS on MAX with my current build, specs available on my profile, and I know others that struggle to run it at all with even high end card and processors. BEWARE THE SYSTEM REQs.
-Filled with visual bugs and glitches. From popping in textures to missing assets, it's all here, folks. You will run the gamut of standard visual bugs barring some of the more extreme variants in other games. Models fold in on themselves and distort, which can lead to some interesting moments.
-Can get boring. There is a point in time that you will eventually exhaust the current tree of things to build, and are left with few options. If you're on a PvE server, it's usually pick a new place and expand or start over. On PvP it usually comes down to beat the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of everyone else on the server until they cry and understand you are the ALPHA.
-Lack of PvE content. Aside from taming, and the "Ultimate Life Form" Boss-like encounters, there's a surprising lack of things for players to do with the environment. Aside from hit things with other things that is.
-Widlcard Studios' greedy nature. Somewhat of a personal gripe at the moment, but could become an issue later on after full release. SWC has already doubled the price of the game (BEFORE FULL RELEASE - It is $59.99 as of writing on 7-16-17) and released a $19.99 "expansion" during Early Access. This company truly does care more about your dollars than your opinion, so be forewarned about it.
(This one is kind of a personal thing and isn't WC's fault so I'll list it down here separately from the main list.)
The community. The commmunity in this game is pretty damn toxic. Aside from playing with my friends, on a PvP server it's generally people putting pillars up everywhere to prevent other players from building due to the proximity feature or "ALPHA" tribes running around servers pushing people's♥♥♥♥♥♥in for no reason. Might be you said one of them looked off one day so they decided to raid you. For some this is a plus as rebuilding adds replay to an extent, but for me it comes down to being more of the "Bully smashes my sandcastle because it's more creative than what he made" principle. Doesn't even have to be that honestly, just know that most of this game's player base is a bunch of hot heads that love making other's experiences hard. It is what it is.
And finally, my overall thoughts. Is ARK a bad game? No. It has its flaws and its successes, but overall it's just kind of bland in my opinion. Gameplay quickly becomes walk here hit this make things repeat until you have base. Taming Dinos takes exorbitant amounts of time on official servers (Hours for the bigger guys) and if you turn the multipliers up so it takes less time it feels like you're cheating the system. I will not personally be spending my time on the game any longer because of SWC's business tactics, but even if that hadn't happened, I still don't have the kind of love for the game that will drive me to play every day even. It was fun for the few hours I put into it, but overall I still feel the game isn't even close to complete. For this game to be pushed out as a full AAA title in the state it's in is wrong. Overall, wait until it's on sale for a fraction of the price and try it for yourself. In no way, shape, or form is this game worth $60 though.
