The premise of ARK: Survival Evolved sounds great on paper. It sounds like an amazing game, with an amazing concept, that has also borrowed many design philosophies from other survival games like Rust and maybe even Space Engineers. However, all of the niceties of the concept wash away from the moment you begin to play.
Usually I don't buy early access games on principle - but a lot of my friends told me that I should grab it while it's on sale. In hindsight, I should have trusted my instinct. It's always a good start when the developers say that early access was supposed to end in June 2016, according to the waffle under the Early Access header on the Steam page (I archived it in case they changed it after this post has been written:
)
I'll only list some of the issues I have with this game, because I don't want to waste my time reviewing a game that really shouldn't even really be in Public Early Access.
Firstly, there is an update every week. This sounds good, until you realise that the
adds superfluous stuff that is really not necessary. I have a relatively small data cap, and I simply can't do weekly updates. Especially ones that don't fix the major issues that the game has at the moment - more on those later.
Secondly, the levelling system is completely ƒucked. Player levelling is alright - I don't understand why I generate XP for doing nothing, but whatever, players mostly progress the same way as one another. But the dinosaurs are completely different. They can spawn with a level as high as 120 - which means if you even encounter one, which often you can't react to until it is too late - you can say goodbye to everything you were holding at that point in time. But that's not even all. If you manage to tame and breed one of these high level dinos, you can level them up to have a ridiculous amount of health, melee damage, and so on, through a stupidly complex breeding system, that requires a lot of math, calculations and statistics. Not only is it ridiculously complicated - it's in real ƒucking time. That means that you will have to wait for days - real time days - to get some dinosaurs to breed. Some breeds take up to
to mature. And you need to keep the eggs in a certain temperature to incubate, which requires a lot of grinding to get the materials and engrams (blueprints) to actually go about doing this.
While we are on the topic: this game's crafting is so ƒucking unbalanced it beggars belief. A small camera costs more than a fabricator, for example. Or a refrigerator. Or an industrial sized grill. I understand that this is just one example - but nothing correlates to anything else in terms of crafting requirements.
Also on the subject of time: This game is not something you can just log out of, or go AFK on. Everything takes so long to do, requiring a lot of real life time that I just don't have. There is no flexibility, no mercy and no chance for you to be "successful" in this game, if you don't play for 15 hours or more a day.
There are other smaller bugs - for example: sometimes on login, all my dinos are underground. So I have to punch where I think they are in order to get them to re-appear. And if you crash or log off while out, say goodbye to any dinos you had with you. This glitch makes them impossible to see. I have lost 2 Griffins this way - which are not easy to tame.
It appears the devs either are incompetent, or just don't care. I'm opting that it's a bit of both. They say that they are a "veteran team with some major hits behind our leads" (their words - check the archive link), which in honesty, they do have some titles behind their senior staff, but not much leadership expertise. They've also been caught censoring and banning people who give the game critique on the forums. They have not made their own games before - this is Wildcard's first game, and it shows. It's sad really, because, conceptually, it has such great potential, but the developers have proven to be misguided, and can't get their priorities straight - they instead shovel out waves of new broken content weekly.
This brings us to the crux of this review, and ultimately the game. The one thing that made me stop playing it. The fact of the matter is, is that it's not even close to being optimised. I have a fairly decent PC that can run most things just fine (i5-4690K, GTX 970, 16GB RAM). And it runs like absolute shît. It has such a bad memory leak that I have to either a) restart the game every hour or b) add 10 different launch options that force it to run with 4GB of memory, run in high priority, run in DX10, without SM4, and with no sky effects. I understand that the GTX 970's memory bandwidth issue could be a problem - but it hasn't shown in any other game I've played. I simply don't understand how they managed to get Unreal Engine 4 to look this bad, and perform like absolute dogshît. It amazes me.
The only good thing I can say is that the netcode appears to be quite good, with ping of around 18-20ms to a server that is over 950 kilometres away.
Lastly - I bought this game on sale, for about $15. That's all it is worth at the moment. It is most definitely not worth $59.99. Don't give the developers money - they are just greedy, and charging $60 USD is an absolute ƒucking joke.

13 months and 1200 hours later... I still love this game, and I hate it to... But that goes for any game really.
Do I recommend it? For actionpacked pretty gfx and gameplay. Definately! For solo/contruction junkies, not so much.
The Pro's:
Teamplayer oriented. No team, no fun (basically). One friend is enough to enjoy the co-op play though.
This game works really well on relatively weak computer configurations as well.
Cinematics and storyline quests are very good. But more of them would definately be nice.
Customisation of avatar and most things related are also quite good.
Controls, animations, graphics are all extremely well made for such a fast paced shooter/hack-n-slash.
I love the fact that you are not bound to certain uber-builds to even stand a chance. So many games die with unbalanced classes and the likes. Warframe does not. Go berzerk, melee, sniper, stealthy, blazing machineguns, just about anything will do the job for the most part. Just a matter of prefered playstyle really. :)
Last but not least, it's Free to Play and it will not hurt you one bit to stay that way. There are no pay-gates to godmode items. Put money in it for gamecurrency (platinums) and trading with players will only get you some things quicker, but same things can be aquired through playing as well.
It's quick and easy to get some missions run so this game is well suited for players that don't have time to sit several hours at once in order to complete large timeconsuming raids or similar. You can log on for as short as 15-30 mins at the time and still accomplish something.
The Cons:
Soloing gets boring extremely fast. Too grindy at times and some things are stupid hard to get either due to low droprate or simply silly hard missions. The repetative re-runs of same missions for certain items are also annoying as heck.
Steep learning curve for new players and bad BAD lack of tutorials/information.
Some aspects of the game, such as Archwing, need a lot more love from the DE's. The concept and thought behind Archwing is really good but poorly executed and neglected by the DE's.
Warframe is hosted by the players computer for co-op play and this can cause bad connection lag problems from time to time.
Summary: Made and maintained by a small team of developers, I can tolerate most of the glitches and bugs. The community is good and the game is full of helpful players. This game is definately designed for playing with friend(s) and using voice communication of some sort. But if you have that, it'll be lots of fun for quite some time.
Just make sure you have other hobbies as well for the waiting times between new storybased progressive quests are sadly quite long. It will take you some time to get to that point as a new player though. New players will be busy for some time before hitting that wall. :)

Alright alright alright, I'll do a serious review, but before you ask...
This game has a heavy difficulty curve, do not be discouraged if you die alot. You will die. Alot.
Ark takes the hands of the player in a survival against the whole world style, multiplayer building and enviormental survival game. Players start off with literally nothing, and must learn about the world they are stuck inside.
Personal experience: I love Ark, Love it. As a longtime gamer and developer, I've come to be very fond of the way the game flows and how it plays out. Naturally progressing difficulty and a demand to actually learn about the world makes ark a unique game to play. "Oh but madman! I hear the devs are morons!" Aha, dear reader, you would be wrong, but not totally. While the devs make amazing video game material, the people in charge of PR and selling the game are a little bit greedy and detached from the rest of the world. I must say however, the dlc everyone hates on? If you get the FREE dlc Ragnarok, you get to basically have the DLC for free, with more. I respect that.
Unique and truly natural progression based on player experience. You'll have to learn alot through trial and error before you rise above the need to survive. Taming and breeding of dinos feels natural, and really helps you bond with your new pals.
Hit and miss, it is a game about using dinos to attack other dinos, ranged weapons feel severly under powered, but the game dosen't force you to use just the crossbow and longneck rifle.
Sometimes the sound is a bit too loud, a bit too quiet, a bit off and unprocessed, but over all the fact that they made so many unique and natural sounding noises and calls amazes me.
Depending on your rig, Ark could be one of the most beautiful and breathtaking games you own, not on par with The Witcher: 3, but within spitting distance. Textures are high quality, and skin and fur textures are believeable.
This is a big one for alot of people, so I won't sugar-coat it. The community is better than most survival games (Rust is literally cancer, and this game makes everyone look like jesus in comparison) so it has a good run-in-to-killed ratio for player interaction. Often times you will find yourself talking around a campfire with a total stranger exchanging sights and stories for whole hours while your tribe mates talk about the day's events. Truly a wonderful feeling to feel after a long day of hard work when someone compliments your beautiful new Tapajara.
I'd give ark a 92/100 for the actual game. The people behind the screens give off a caring vibe from the devs, but a sinisiter money grab feel from the publisher. If you want a recommendation to buy art for full price, I would say yes. Jump right in. The price tag jumped when it left Early Acess, but thats ok. The game deserves to shine in its glory, even if it is covered in blood and mud.
Oh, and a little bit of gamer tears.
The game is fun. I really recommend it.

Like many reviewers here I've invested a fair whack of time into this game. Having bought the game back on the 26th of November 2015 it has significantly changed over that time. I understand I've played the whole time in 'Early Access' but feel it's essentially been a complete game for long enough now anyway.
Again, like many others have said in the past, the game ended for me when the flying dino's were speed nerfed. It made doing trivial things or helping out new players a complete chore. I had also been breeding a whole lot of flying dino's and when they were nerfed a lot of them were rendered useless. Fortunately I had established bases and stockpiled resources before the flyer nerf so It wasn't as big an impact, but for new players I could see it being very frustrating setting up base on 'The Island' in the south and taking 20 minutes to fly north to gather resources in the snow (just one example).
When the flyers were nerfed my time spent playing took a significant nosedive. I went from playing every day to simply logging in once or twice a week to feed dino's. The last straw for me was logging in the other week to find one of my level 150 Quetzals had died of hunger.
The game used to be fun for me, but it became a chore and I've finally quit playing. Gave away all my resources and dino's upon exit and have to say feel relieved that it's over.
Can't say I didn't get my money's worth, paid roughly $15USD and was my go to game for a very long time. Currently priced at $60USD with the current setup I'd find it hard to recommend for new players, maybe wait for a steam sale if you want to have a look at it. If I was writing this review a year ago I'd have recommended this game, but for me personally some of the changes have ruined my experience.

Pros:
-Very beautiful Graphics for the type of game it is

-A very friendly and helpful community both in game and outside of game
-Quests/ Codex entries that expand upon the in game lore
-Has alternative means to get Platinum (Real life currency) for people not wanting to put their money into it necessarily.
Cons:
-Can be very grind-heavy if you are looking to obtain a specific item.
-Can be very repetitive in the late game (they have been implementing new things such as the Conclave (PvP) and Dailies for late game items (Sorties))
-You can find yourself hitting a paywall of progression if you don't either put money into the game or the time to grind for items people want to buy.
-Little to no end game yet
This game is very much a "anihillate hordes of enemies" style of game with its own leveling system and plenty of stuff for you to entertain yourself. The only real deterrent that this game has is how much time / money you are willing to spend on it. Each Warframe, weapon, animal compainion / pet, etc... takes up equipment slots in your arsenal, and while it may be easy to afford a decent amount (depending on what type of slot you are getting) it can take some time grinding up the items to sell on the in-game market for Platinum, or you can just put some money into the game to make it easier.
This game is not Pay-to-win as you still have to level everything yourself and even if you bought the mods upgraded from people it doesnt mean you know how to build anything to make a weapon effective. The PvP aspect of the game also locks mods from being equipped so it is a level playing field for the majority. Anything else outside of that is pure PvE and going out on missions.
TL;DR
If you have time to kill/money to spend and like this type of game, you will love this. If you lack both those things, you can still enjoy it, but it will take a lot longer to progress in the vein of aquiring items. (you don't need everything in the game to get to the end game content, but it is nice to have those options available to you)

Pros

-Servers need a frequent reset, this is the biggest problem with the game for me and why I wouldn't buy the game at this point personally if I was a new player
-Servers in PvE are overflowing and there is very little room to build anywhere, plus players have such massive bases and large amount of dinos that your frame rate will get cut in half or worse
-PvP servers also need a wipe to bring balance back, majority of official servers are own by an alpha tribe and you have to obey their rules or get griefed
Final Thoughs
-Honestly the game is fun solo on your own server or in PvE
-Downside is this game takes a lot of time to accomplish anything and the hours can fly by
-At this point in the game, I wouldn't buy it. If you can get it for $30 might be worth the risk but the game needs some balance and the engine performance is lacking for 2017.
-I'd personally hold off unless your fairly certain you'll enjoy solo on your own sever or maybe with 1 or 2 friends
-Side note if you play with a friend on your own server, unless you install the dedicated server tool and set up your own server for you and your friends. You will be tethered to your friends with a very short distance cap, preventing you from venturing too far from one another.

Blocking also has to be precisely timed and aimed, meaning each block feels earned. On top of this, with each attack you can feign, pulling back at the last second, and fool your opponent into blocking early.

Let me preface this by saying that with my 600+ hours I do feel that I got a good value for the money I spent.  However, recent behavior from the developer has me questioning their business practices.  When Ark initially launched I was skeptical as it looks like just another survival sandbox with crafting, the timing had me especially cynical as the release coincided with Jurrasic World releasing in theaters in the US.  A few months down the line I looked at the stats and development continued at a good pace and the community was still highly active.
As for gameplay its fairly standard for survival games, the graphics are ok and a lot more needs to be done for optimization.  The biggest issue with the game play is taming, some dinos can take 12 hours or more which leads to the game being busywork or babysitting.  The crafting is also fairly basic and sometimes pieces fail to clip together properly, the system could use more fleshing out.  The hitboxes are also fairly bizarre which allows for the incompetent AI to be cheated making taming easier.  What I mean by this is most dinos can damage thatch, a few can damage wood and almost none can damage stone.  If you build a stone wall and lure a dino towards it, its head will pass through the hitbox of the wall because of the bad collision detection.  You can then shoot the dinosaur in the head to knock it out for taming.  This works for virtually every predatory creature in the game.
At one point on the official wiki they were promising upcoming features such as more advanced AI, weaponizing fire so predators would be afraid of the fire.  Some dinos more active at different times of day, at the time of writing these promised features have been removed from the list and to my knowledge have not been implemented.
The first non game play issue that cropped up was the feature creep which led to delays, when the game launched in May of 2015 in early access the release date was June of 2016.  June came and went it was pushed back to December, then February 2017 and finally at E3 2017 we recieved a release date of August 2017.
Next the paid DLC, while I own it and feel that at the time I bought it that the developer had delivered content to keep me going for hundreds of hours I understand how scummy the behavior is.  Couple that with the fact that the retail version does not include Scorched Earth.  I could have understood $60 for the  complete package with ALL existing DLC, not the community made maps that Wildcard cleaned up a bit and released as official DLC.  This now means that for someone looking to get into Ark today they are spending double what anyone spent during the early access period.

TL;DR Veteran player, cannot support the multiplayer in this game anymore. Get ready to be griefed or just not connect in the first place. Single player is great though.
After taking several months off from ARK me and a friend decided to get back into the game. I have almost 300 hours in the game and my buddy has probably twice that. We use to play the game hardcore about a year ago so we were pretty excited to get back into it together. However we quickly ran into some problems.
One new issue we had when trying to get started again was finding a server. When we pulled up the server lists I would see something along the lines of Server A, Server B, Server C, and Server D (just simplifying server names here), but my buddy would only see Server A, Server B, Server E, and Server F. Now this might not be a problem since we bother have Servers A & B, but these servers would have a ridiculously high ping for both of us and would be unplayable. However, after some patience we were able to get the same servers to pop up for both of us. Yet, upon finding a server we could both join we had issues connecting or maintaining connection to any server.
Once we did manage to get into the game and start playing we ran into the age old problem of this game, posts. People cover the map in fence posts so that other players cannot build their bases in those areas. These posts essentially "claim" land for the players and blocks other players from building bases in any kind of decent area. This mean unless you're one of the first people onto the server you are not going to have a practical area for a base. Also, upon spawing into the game we found that nine times out of ten you spawned inside someones base, or simply within a spawn zone trap. These traps are simple fenced in areas that have no way out and are meant to simply trap new players so they cannot play, even in PVE only servers.
Ignoring all of these issues, this game can be very fun. I have had many great times playing this game and wish i could play it again. But with poor servers, abusive land grabbing, and the constant loopholes players find to grief I can  not support this game at this time.
On the brightside, this game has great singleplayer, but really multiplayer is where the fun is at.

TLDR; Warframe is awesome. Try it, it's free. Don't like it? Fair enough, but you lose nothing by trying.
So, I have played Warframe for quite some time, on and off for about 4 or so years now.
Since it was announced I supported it, and now as I write this review I have realized that I never regretted it.
I have not played Warframe as much as some, but it has had an impact on what I expect out of many other games.
I can't recommend a free to play game more than I recommend Warframe. It's just fun.
Dynasty Warriors meets Star Wars: Jedi Outcast and had a threesome with Devil May Cry while going to class with an attractive art direction to learn and secretly have an affair with all of these (developing) story points.
Really, if you like action games, try it, it's free. If you like Devil May Cry, do yourself a favor and make this party crazy! Try Warframe. If you enjoyed Jedi Outcasts interesting combination of lightsaber and gun play and third person gameplay, Warframe feels very much like a game I'd been missing. Do you like being a man blender of blood and gore as you spiral through hordes of enemies that peel apart under the force of your advance like wet cardboard to a well forged blade, until you meet the inevitable leader of the cardboard men's group and have a real fight for a while before inevitably coming out as the better, and run off with all the spoils of the battle and victory in your hands?
Yeah, bet you can't tell if I just described Dynasty Warriors or Warframe, can you? Guess what, I'll tell you a secret. (It's both)
Strap on some wonderful RPG style mechanics and a similar card collecting system to upgrade your arsenal and you have a game that I never knew I needed, but I had it from the beginning and it's only now that I realize just how much it means to me.
Warframe is a game you need to try, it's free, it runs VERY well on almost any system in my experience, and it's above all really dang fun.
Get it.

This game has been in my library for a few years now and I always find myself coming back to it.
Pros:
-Very beautiful Graphics for the type of game it is
-Beautiful Soundtrack
-Customization galore (for those interested in playing "FashionFrame")
-Multiplayer / Co-op
-A plethora of weapons at your disposal that you can customize (sometimes even asthetically) to suit your playstyle
-Each Warframe has their own playstyles that allow you to find what you like or become a jack of all trades.
-The ability to modify a warframes attributes to make each of their powers work differently
-A very friendly and helpful community both in game and outside of game
-Quests/ Codex entries that expand upon the in game lore
-Has alternative means to get Platinum (Real life currency) for people not wanting to put their money into it necessarily.
Cons:
-Can be very grind-heavy if you are looking to obtain a specific item.
-Can be very repetitive in the late game (they have been implementing new things such as the Conclave (PvP) and Dailies for late game items (Sorties))
-You can find yourself hitting a paywall of progression if you don't either put money into the game or the time to grind for items people want to buy.
-Little to no end game yet
This game is very much a "anihillate hordes of enemies" style of game with its own leveling system and plenty of stuff for you to entertain yourself. The only real deterrent that this game has is how much time / money you are willing to spend on it. Each Warframe, weapon, animal compainion / pet, etc... takes up equipment slots in your arsenal, and while it may be easy to afford a decent amount (depending on what type of slot you are getting) it can take some time grinding up the items to sell on the in-game market for Platinum, or you can just put some money into the game to make it easier.
This game is not Pay-to-win as you still have to level everything yourself and even if you bought the mods upgraded from people it doesnt mean you know how to build anything to make a weapon effective. The PvP aspect of the game also locks mods from being equipped so it is a level playing field for the majority. Anything else outside of that is pure PvE and going out on missions.
TL;DR
If you have time to kill/money to spend and like this type of game, you will love this. If you lack both those things, you can still enjoy it, but it will take a lot longer to progress in the vein of aquiring items. (you don't need everything in the game to get to the end game content, but it is nice to have those options available to you)

Where to start with this game?
I'm mainly going to talk about the pve on a private server experience, as I noticed that PvP without serious time investment is not going to be fun (well it depends on the server).
Well, first of all, the potential is HUGE and the attention to detail in the overworld is noteworthy. The world the devs created is rather big and only in a few places did I feel a lack of detail. It feels alive, everywhere there is something going on which can be interacted with (albeit on a basic, kill/run/tame, level). This is sadly, it all stops. I don't have the best rig in existence, just some old and new stuff put together to make it work. Even on the lowest settings the game stutters and freezes and is riddled with glitches and frame drops. For some reason reflections on the oscean happen without regard to distance, making me see massive trees reflected on the water a kilomoter away. But enough with the pc specific stuff.
During my 250+ hours of gameplay I've lost a lot of gear and tames to bugs and glitches that haven't been fixed at all, through the last couple of years that I own this game. Not only that the game is also riddled with weird and questionable decisions made by the devs.
One of the worst bugs are the physics/clipping bugs. As example, I give you one of the early game enemies you'll fight, the raptor. The raptor has high speed and damage so it's best to take it down from a distance, but if you get ambushed running away is the most viable option, which can both be really easy or impossible. If there is any object between you and the raptor, you're safe cause it gets stuck, it always gets stuck on EVERYTHING. If there isn't you're dead, because they run into you clip through you and then well, then you can't move. (yep salt levels are high with me on this one, guess why). The same happens with players and every other dino in the game. If they get to close they get stuck. Often this also leads to rubber banding, random teleportation and being mauled by the predator that phased through an object.
Another bug that took a lot of lives is the fact that sleeping (being offline) makes you phase through floors. It often happened that a tribemate went to sleep and fell through the floor to land on the other side of the settlement wall so he got either killed or raided during his absence.
The game is riddled with many more bugs that hamper gameplay a lot. But now onto the game design.
Ark by its very nature is a more pvp orientated game. As real dangers to your settlement, outside from other players, aren't present. For example, all walls up from stone are impervious to wild dino damage. It even goes as far to make player made structures interfere with world spawns such as dinos and resources. This is of course a good way to troll. In 3 different servers, all metal and crystal deposits were gone because a tribe decided to build right on top of it, making it near impossible to progress. This wouldn't be the worst of a problem if it didn't have a 15 minutes timer after the last tribe member logs of to make EVERYTHING indestructible. (based on playing on official servers). Other bad game design is the occurrence of swamp fever a disease added a while back. It isn't lost on death and adds a lot of annoying status effects that can only be cured by a high-level item which is a pain to make and impossible to do by newer players. The occurrence of a dino that takes your stuff is not the worst idea, but giving it the ability to take complete stacks of non-food items such as an entire stack of bullets/explosives is horrendous and not really logical.
Another dino gripe is the massive stun locking/instakills that some dinos have. A low-level jellyfish killing a high level megalodon just because it gets instantly stun locked. Or dinos that pierce others and slowly kill it without it being able to resist in any way.  Or the ones that rip you from the saddle, making you unable to help your mount defend itself.
Now to my main gripe, the taming. The essence of taming (with a couple exceptions) is stuff it with tranq darts/arrows or club it on the head so it faints, then stuff its inventory with its favourite foodstuff (kibble, which is a pain to make works the best) and once in a while give it more narcotics to keep it unconscious.... so it can eat???? and then it follows your every will until it dies or is released. I guess it's just a gaming thing so real taming won't happen, but it's one of the most boring parts of the game, and at the same time one of the most important ones. Some taming can take up literal real-life hours and they always have to be babysit. The hunt itself is exhilarating and intense, as long as it's not one of those, kind of essential but almost never found ones of course (looking at you quetzal). But then comes the waiting game, hoping that no other predator comes close enough to start munching on the unconscious new friend (slave). Whilst keeping it downed with premade narcotics/found narco berries as it munches on food.
Meanwhile the more "no life/ hardcore" players have already built unbeatable bases (for low level players) and are terrorizing the entire island whilst cheaters zip around giving everyone swamp fever and killing dinos.
Let me also add that this game is made by the same devs that found it a good idea to make the entire island snowy during Christmas, making it so new players will freeze to death multiple times before they even unlocked the engrams for campfires and basic clothing.
The game also has a soft cap on levels, where in the first few days you'll level up relatively fast, unlocking fun stuff to try out, new types of weapons, saddles, building materials etc. Then around lvl 50 to 60 it suddenly takes way longer to unlock the next level, until you're grinding for weeks to even get a single level, unlocking a single engram.  Now at this stage, you've been having a decent amount of fun, had some crashes, found loads of bugs, and you've been increasing your friends (slaves).
Now I’ve been talking about bases a bit. Building bases is pretty straight forward, build a foundation, built walls and a roof and a door. DONE. base complete. you’ve got a cube. it's that simple, but it doesn’t really change later. Every base will be cube shaped, massive cubes. Maybe some stuff sticking out, but that’s probably because placement of foundations is hard, as even the smallest difference in ground height makes it impossible. Now you think, there are slopes I can use and pillars. But then you didn't know that the pillars have snap points at different heights than walls and foundation. making building downwards NEAR IMPOSSIBLE without making it look horrible.
To summarise what I mentioned before, it’s a buggy, unfinished and unpolished mess of hope, believe and poor decision-making, which is now OVERPRICED. Yep they increased the price because apparently, it’s going to be finished and released soon.
BUT WAIT you think, doesn’t it already have a dlc? Yes, it does, it does have dlc even though it isn’t finished. But it doesn’t stop there. The newly added tek items, such as tek armour is split between base game and dlc. Want to get the chest piece and the pants, buy dlc. So not only is it an unfinished mess of a game, it also has unfair dlc and a sudden increase in price.
TL:DR It’s buggy, it’s not well thought out, not well balanced, it is beautiful (in the pictures), it has horrible dlc and is overpriced.

Played this almost constantly when I got it with friends. Stopped playing around the time when the scorched earth DLC came out (since dlc shouldn't exist in an EA game that isn't complete anyways).
Game was fun for $30, but hiking it up to $60 isn't right, especially with that extra tacked on DLC that shouldn't exist. Three bad moves won't win people over.
Right now if you plan on buying this, I'd wait for a deep sale at 75% off at least, with how much grinding, griefing and bugs you can encounter in this game (many of which haven't changed in the past year since I last played) yet the price keeps going up, I wouldn't touch this game until many of them are ironed out (if at all).
Edit:
Optimization of this game was really bad when it came out, and is still plagued with it to this day. Systems that are on the low end or even the highest end run into the same issues. I have what would be considered a 3-4/10 rig right now, yet I could play this game fairly well, yet my friends who have 1070s-1080s could barely play this game with constant FPS drops, frame stutters and crashes.
PvP isn't bad, at least if both sides are somewhat fair, you can spend hundreds of hours or even months worth of time just building your defenses for them to be destroyed in minutes because someone else raided you at night, or other reasons.  I guess that keeps the grind going, but in the end it gets stale especially when alpha tribes hop servers onto yours just to flatten it in a few minutes - that you spent 500+ hours creating.
PvE is.. alright I guess, it gets stale but just a bit faster. You can get away with things like building huge monuments (assuming that the server doesn't crash because if you build something too big it flips out and might crash people if they get too close). Yet if there isn't a PvP aspect it gets a little stale (but to each their own).
They added many PvP items like traps, and cages, when optimization was neglected among other things. Ultimately they have made some questionable decisions (like the aforementioned DLC in an EA game that still isn't fully released yet still plays like a poorly optimsized EA game!), that have put a bad taste in many a mouths.
This game is far from a worthy value of 60 dollars, it's much closer to the original 30 or less that it was at previously. This game isn't nearly ready, it isn't optimized enough, and even if it has "4 times the content of when it came out (said their lead developer)" it still isn't worth 60 dollars + another 20 if you want their DLC.   It's really a shame too, this game, like many others, could've been so much more if the developers weren't so focused on money.

Ark : Survival Evolved is, in short a Survival based open world game based on taming dinosaurs and then using them to help make your life easier, or use them to protect yourself from the environment, or other players. This game is still in Early Access, however seeing the jump in price, and the game was planning to come out of early access anyway, im going to write a review for it anyway.
I can't recommend this game. At least not in its current state.
Ill start with the more subjective points I have about this game, and then move onto the bigger issues that I know most people have.
Firstly, the game is focused mostly on combat and PvP. Surviving isn't hard, and there aren't many repercussions for having poor survival knowledge or skills. You can get food nearly everywhere in the map, and while eating raw meat does decrease your health, its pretty much negligible, and you can just dive into the nearest water source and spam e, even if its the ocean, to fix water. The most difficult parts of survival is monitoring heat, which isn't a big deal because you can often walk into a new zone which never is too far from another to increase or decrease the ambient temperature.
Caves, which are required to fight bosses are long stretches of combat, just fighting a set theme of enemies over and over until you finally reach the end. There are no puzzles, there isn't much variation between them, and most can be done in a few minutes if you know what you are doing. (Even less if someone's just been in there, if there wasn't any enemies in the cave to begin with, im sure that most people would be able to do most of them in under a minute. ) The bosses themselves are kinda boring, being difficult in terms of the sheer HP they have.
Secondly, whilst the game itself looks beautiful, and the dinosaurs have been brought to life really well, I can't like how the game looks. I know this is very subjective, but the entire game seems, well in a word unnatural. Its kinda like taking the Unreal Engine, and then making an art-style out of the couple of pack in games that come with it. Everything looks kinda like cut and paste assets, and the only exception I can think off of the top of my head is caves, which looked beautiful after the remaster update, even though they were still combat gauntlets.
Okay now for the less subjective points...
The game is very very poorly optimized. Top end PCs are getting what should usually be minimum fps values, people without machines would be crashing most of the time, and the game loves to eat up RAM. Its not Adobe levels of greedy but ive seen it take 14 GB of ram before it crashed.
Keep in mind, the average gaming PC would have 8.
The game is heavily social based, most of the fun you'll be having will be with friends and communities you forge together. As to why this is a problem, anyone can do this, and with how this game balances, you CAN have people with laser rifles, as well as the best dinosaurs in the game, completely destroy a group of friends that join a server, fighting them off with spears. There are groups like this called Alpha tribes, some of which basically own public servers, setting up automated defenses all across the map wherever someone may spawn, making it impossible to play unless you yourself are part of that tribe. PvE servers would have massive bases around where resources could spawn and only members would be able to reach it
Even if there isn't a tribe, public servers are often very very crowded, with very few spaces where someone new can be set up. IF you are going to play this game, hire out a server for you and some friends, its one of the few ways I can claim its enjoyable.
It is impossible to play the game solo with the engram system. Unless you are very very smart with how you play, and hoard those points, you will not be able to advance far into the tech tree. Level ups themselves can be stupid. On the server I hired, my character invested all his points into speed and carry weight. I was able to outrun a giga in the end, and dinosaurs were able to become stupidly overpowered compared to wild counterparts due to how the player would invest stats.
I could keep ranting but this is long enough as it is so ill end it with this point about updates.
Ever since I started playing ark, updates have been mostly about adding new dinos, adding in new high tier weapons and making the game look prettier. Dinosaurs share the same role now, several times over, (Just how many dinos have berry collecting as a specialty now? Oh but they are different because you can't get the best one straight away, and the others can do some other minor roles.) Instead of making the game more interesting which can be done by having less dinos, but have what they do be more unique, but at this point it seems like Wildcard is comprised of very few programmers, and just artists and community managers. The game is still buggy and unoptimised, basic survival is still♥♥♥♥♥♥easy, assuming you aren't attacked by other players and the combat is uninteresting and mostly about who has the bigger numbers, who has been grinding more.
There is something interesting here, and I would have said yes, this is something worth paying money here for assuming you can get your own server and have fun goofing around with friends, but at a $60 price, per person? Its just too much for a game that barely works as it is. If by some miracle this game is on sale for $15, id say give it a shot. (and yes, this does mean im placing ark as something you should pay about the same as an average indie game on steam. ) Keep in mind this is from someone who paid $20 originally for the game, paid an extra $20 to buy his friend a copy, and then paid an extra $120 to hire a server out for a few months telling you that $60 is overpriced.
♥♥♥♥♥♥ optimization coupled with the doubling of the price from what it was, this game is not worth it.

TLDR; Warframe is awesome. Try it, it's free. Don't like it? Fair enough, but you lose nothing by trying.
So, I have played Warframe for quite some time, on and off for about 4 or so years now.
Since it was announced I supported it, and now as I write this review I have realized that I never regretted it.
I have not played Warframe as much as some, but it has had an impact on what I expect out of many other games.
I can't recommend a free to play game more than I recommend Warframe. It's just fun.
Dynasty Warriors meets Star Wars: Jedi Outcast and had a threesome with Devil May Cry while going to class with an attractive art direction to learn and secretly have an affair with all of these (developing) story points.
Really, if you like action games, try it, it's free. If you like Devil May Cry, do yourself a favor and make this party crazy! Try Warframe. If you enjoyed Jedi Outcasts interesting combination of lightsaber and gun play and third person gameplay, Warframe feels very much like a game I'd been missing. Do you like being a man blender of blood and gore as you spiral through hordes of enemies that peel apart under the force of your advance like wet cardboard to a well forged blade, until you meet the inevitable leader of the cardboard men's group and have a real fight for a while before inevitably coming out as the better, and run off with all the spoils of the battle and victory in your hands?
Yeah, bet you can't tell if I just described Dynasty Warriors or Warframe, can you? Guess what, I'll tell you a secret. (It's both)
Strap on some wonderful RPG style mechanics and a similar card collecting system to upgrade your arsenal and you have a game that I never knew I needed, but I had it from the beginning and it's only now that I realize just how much it means to me.
Warframe is a game you need to try, it's free, it runs VERY well on almost any system in my experience, and it's above all really dang fun.
Get it.
It's addicting.

There are tons of Free-to-Play games on Steam, and some of them are even good. The general problem with the genre most often isn't whether or not the developers knows how to craft fun gameplay (although that often is a problem as well), but more often whether or not the developers understand how to successfully deal with the delicate intricacies of freemium-based money-making. Be too nice with your players and no one will ever give you a cent, people will utterly love the game and yet you'll still end up dead all-too-soon despite your fame. Be heavy-handed and only the whales will be able to make any real progress after a certain point, a harsh reality that will lead your game on a slow inevitable crawl towards its demise. That people like playing Warframe shouldn't be a question given the massive amount of fans it has on Steam, the real question should be how has its Freemium-economy been structured? Wisely there is no way you can buy victory in this game, with the only purely cash-shop based items all being 100% cosmetic (with no perks attached). Anything actually worth a damn in the cash shop can easily be earned in-game (even if you have to look up a guide as to how), and many other things - often of a very desirable nature - must exclusively be earned within Warframe. In fact, nine  times out of ten the only thing saved by going through the cash shop will be the time it took to craft a weapon. Beyond not having access to a new toy until it's finished crafting, Warframe - unlike many others - doesn't penalize your in-game effectiveness during the crafting process. Additionally, Warframe contains no artifical gear-checks where you'll be locked out of places until you have hard-to-find gear. Power in Warframe is more about your mods - which are predominantly earned and/or traded for - than the gear you're holding, and skill will always trump the power of someone's boomstick.
I'm not going to write a dissertation on how great this game is - even though I do love it - as countless others already have, instead I'm merely here to ensure you this is a rare shining beacon of Free-to-Play done right.

Clicker Heroes - "this looks like a Flash game". Yep, it is. Steam ported it over, gave it a few Achievements, that's it.
This game is all about Farming. There is NO strategy, NO skill, NO storyline, NO failure whatsoever. Just level up 1000x, kill that ultra-hard boss, then find yourself doing all that over and over again. If you are stuck, there is a pay-to-win system. I cannot imagine myself breaking my gaming mouse over this game, and had myself an Auto-Clicker software after 4 or 5 minutes within the game.
If you are a big fan of endless MMORPG's that focus on that, this is just right for you! But if you are not an obsessive-compulsive person that expects something more than doing stuff over and over again, stay away from this. The comments tell the true, this one is extremely addictive and will drag hours away from your life without giving a thing in return. Funniest comment I heard so far: "Game of the future, plays itself so you don't have to".
Don't get me wrong, the game works just fine. I did not find any bugs within 7 days of gameplay, the characters are well drawn and kind of cute, and there are even performance-driven options (lower gfx quality, removing damage and gold text - why not removing all gfx at all?) and muting sound effects and background music - there is only one, repeated to exaustion.

The review:
The not-recommendation of mine boils down to a single design plus implementation choice / flaw.

Nothing (of actual value) is kept / saved in case mission / session failure or abortion. no matter the reason.
Items of actual value includes but not limited to are blueprint-drops, objective-points (E.G. excavation), mission-rewards (E.G. Defense every fifth-round); you get to keep nothing of these (alongside of course losing the mission-completion credit-reward and +1.5-affinity / exp-multiplier extra)...


In other words, this a "online"-game, which is heavily relying on looting and such, has zero-fail-safes or anything resemblance implemented (alongside seemingly not even has any plans either).


“Funny” thing is, this was a deliberate change from almost 4-years ago now and there is zero-reasons or benefits of it especially nowadays (at least I personally see no financial-geniousness in this practice, but then again, these are the same people that keep telling us that they will go bankrupt if they start hosting their own dedicated-servers or otherwise offer hosting-services via datacenters and such):


...And during these past 4-years, they have yet to also not fix the doors and making enemy-spawning fully functional...


And no, the support-folks cannot / won’t help with that / this / these-things either; I’ve contacted them quite a many times for losing rare-rare drops that their system conveniently failed to save.
Regardless the amount of evidence (from screenshots to actual locally saved(?!) log-files, they simply say “Can’t help you with that; better luck next time”, to summarize the thing…

On extra note about support-folks, who (for the most part) are, in fact, pretty much not all that helpful / useful to begin with:
They actually semi-deleted some of the cash-shop items I had bought long-time ago (avatars / glyphs, which are outrageously expensive to begin with alongside the colour-pickers...) saying that they “improved” them, even though they’re pretty much nothing like they used to look (E.G. one avatar had a 2/3rd-face view, and now it is a side-profile image of just the face, background cannot be almost seen at all).

(( I noticed the link to images hosted on Mediafire was removed, so I re-added it again as an Steam-”art”-upload. ))


To semi-quote “Vay Hek”: Thieves! Leave my glyphs alone!!!”


Okay yeah sure, there was that time their bot-system false-positively perma-banned my account that one time and I semi-quickly got my account-unbanned.
Thing is though, that whole process was simply waste of time and other resources, since that shouldn't have happened in the first place, that ban that is...it's a amazing how much these developers are so much fighting about cheating and such, while it is the legitimate fair'n'square-players that gets "shafted", just like with most of the DRM-things...



As always though, credits where due: I like the lore art-things and such.

I just wish the game itself was actually more playable and otherwise player-friendly (especially ergonomics wise; why is that the (friendly-NPC-AI-)bots / specters are allowed to have a turbofire-function but not the players, for example...).


Now it just feels extremely gimped and shoddy console-port in every mechanics, presentation (E.G. “menus” are actually part of character-models and such), and generally this game just feels dysfunctional...

---

But yeah, play this game at your own risk; I am not saying this as a joke.
And always be prepared to see your work ending up to, well, nothing just because the game felt like doing so like pretty much always; again, I am not joking, so you simply do hours-of-hours-work just to end up with nothing-nothing.

Kinda like drawing with Flash:


...No seriously, that's just how bad this game is. And there is nothing to apologize to link to video because it is a truth...

((But to those who think I am accusing of Digital Extremes / Warframe-team not fixing anything: No, what I am actually saying is that their priorities and many other general development decisions are very questionable and often very hypocritical far too many times, as they pretty much always have been...))

When this game first showed up in early access, it proved to be one of the most monotonous, grindy, difficult games I had ever played...
And I loved it.
Our 3 person tribe made up of RL friends quickly latched onto an official PVP-Hardcore server, and away went our free time. For over a month we struggled to survive against the harsh environment, large alpha tribes, and worst of all... the many game crashes, glitches, and bugs. Gathering pearls, or even flying in those days was extremely risky, as any one of the many game crashes would cause an instant loss of 70+ levels. But I would be lying if I said I didn't enjoy the adrenaline rush that this game had to offer.
The consequences of any real conflict with other players in hardcore were... severe. However, these consequences also served as a form of protection in and of themselves. What tribe would want to risk their own livelihood to take out another? It felt as though there was a constant tension in the air. These hardcore servers promoted careful planning, tactics, and execution... moreso than any of the other game modes offered. Slow and methodical would be the two words I would use to describe the whole experience. Go too fast and... you might just slip off a cliff... lose 35 levels. Stand under a chest from a beam... get pushed under the map and lose 42 levels. You see what I'm getting at. Risk aversion was the name of the game.
I mention all of this to say that in no way, shape, or form does this game retain ANY of these aspects. With the current state of server transfers, there is no time to plod along at a slow or methodical pace. You WILL be wiped within a few days. You are no longer simply worrying about the other players on your server... you're worrying about EVERY player on EVERY server. It is in my opinion asking too much of a small tribe to deal with this. It would relegate us to Hardcore-PvE servers if we ever decided to come back and play, a concept which I am not too fond of.
Additionally, the devs' support of the hardcore community is nearly nonexistant at this point. There still isn't a single official hardcore server of any type for The Center or the newest maps. Just another nail in the coffin of enjoyment I once had for this game.
To tell you the truth, I don't care about the price of this game. If the game was still like it was two years ago, I would have payed it. I would have payed twice this amount for the great memories I had with my friends, my dinos, and my hours of rock-gathering(ok, maybe not that). So with that said, can I recommend this game to you, my astute reader? I think it depends on many factors, but mainly on what types of games you enjoy. If you have friends to play with, and you think you might enjoy a pure PvE experience, then I think I would still be able to give a recomendation. Dinosaur taming, breeding, and leveling remains a very strong mechanic and allows for many possible hours of fun, even in the game's current state.
If however, you enjoy difficult, rewarding gameplay, I just can't recommend this game. The current PvP-Hardcore experience is a shell of its former self. If Studio Wildcard ever decides to show support for our small community, or if server transfers get removed or changed in a big way, I will update this review. Until then, I will continue lurking in the discussion boards and patch notes with all of the other disgruntled former players of this once great game.

I have 2280+ Hours in this game, I've been playing off and on since it first came out basically.  The reviews for this game currently sit at "mixed"...and rightfully so.
Pluses:  The content has just kept coming.  More dinos, more gear, more maps, more, more, more.  Bugs, exploits, cheats, and sloppy AI have been slowly patched over the Early Access patches.  This game once had so much wrong with it that I was surprised it was fun :)  Now it's more or less patched up.
Cons:  Man.  For an online game, Wildcard seriously can't figure out how to do networking reliably.  This is a game that is, for the vast majority of players, played exclusively online, and yet, the official servers are at times unplayable.  The game lags so hard, not just a tiny pause or a rubber band, I'm talking a 45-60 second lag spikes.  Sometimes the lag spikes will be much less than that...which would be a good thing you'd think.  Except when you land your Argent and press E, and then the lag spike releases with out warning and you find out you dismounted 4 yards away and subsequently have fallen off a mountain and died. :)
This game is hard enough without fighting the game itself.  If Wildcard wants to price themselves at AAA price range, and act like this game is worthy of that kind of money, then they should present a game that is similar in quality to a AAA title.  This game is close, but it's fails at the fundamentals.
I would not suggest that you buy this game unless it is on sale.  And if you do buy it, be ready for a love/hate relationship.  It's very hard to have all your hard work and efforts destroyed not by a dinosaur, or by your own inability, or by the skill of another player, but just simply because the game can't do basic things well enough.  You will waste days raising babies just to have them die from a glitch or a server crash.  You will lose important dinos and gear because the game crashes at the worst possible moment for you.  You will spend countless hours gathering materials and crafting building components just to fight the poorly executed building mechanic snap points.
The Official servers are kind of a mess.  Extremely overcrowded, completely unmoderated, and don't use enough resources on the server side to run the game optimally.
I could keep bashing the game.  It's fun.  It's really cool to play at times.  At times I wish I'd never started lol :)

Let's be honest. Any game that you put 300+ hours into has to be good. For me, this was one of those games. I've probably played this than any other game in the recent years. The combat is precise; swordplay, archery, and everything else is realistic to the point I can compare it to the real thing. This isn't a combo-ridden, over the top slasher; this is the real deal. With plenty of different weapons (each with unique stats), game modes, character diversity, and over all experiences, I have to say the game is completely enthralling. The game is polished, and has a wonderful team of developers. All in all, if I was to assign a score to Chivalry, I'd definitely give it a 9 out of 10. There are no drawbacks in the game, as I do not count the very uncommon (but of course occuring) player nuisance. I recommend this game to ANYONE who enjoys some great, up-front combat.
UPDATE: Still a good game, and I still play it, but I take back what I said about the developers- they changed Chivalry a little too much without fixing bugs and listening to player demands.

There is a list of reasons for my thumbs down below. All you need to know if you're looking to buy is this:

Let me start off by saying I have a great and many hours on this game. I started playing more than a year ago, when things were a lot more fun. As time went on, the enjoyment started to sink away. I beat a good part of the learning curve and began to shine more. I would have recommended this game, and did. I brought friends to play with. Sadly, in the end, key things broke my loyalty.
1: Community. The community of this game will make you hate all of humanity. They're (not all, but many) childish and insulting. Totally unhelpful. You will run into "that guy" that kicks you over and over again on your own team to goad you into attacking him so he can votekick you for team damage.
2: The patching. I'm not going to sit here and say something about the ballance between classes with the patches. No. It is that each time they patch the game, more of it seems to break. Be it your weapon unlocks, your rank, or the whole screen going black while you play- Torn Banner is all out of free passes in my book to get this process right.
3: Hacking. There are two types of people that will tell you this doesn't happen. 1 is the guy that defends this game and thinks you're just a noob. 2 is the hacker. I knew hackers in this game, and to stop a votekick on themselves, they'd just say to the kicker "You mad bro? learn to play, don't votekick." and the players would vote no. They'd keep the hacker in the game by assuming the kicker was simply  mad about losing.
Nothing is more frustrating than knowing the hacker personally and watching them game the system that easy because the community is so poor.
Again, there was a time I would have been all in for this game. I'd have defended all it's flaws. But as of late, after Deadliest Warrior (which is also not very good), I would tell you only to buy this game  if all of the above won't bother you.

If anyone truly can reconcile 2000 hours of entertainment for 10 bucks total cost and not recommend this? How insane are you to complain about .005 cents per hour of entertainment? Mk. Lel.
And for those that complain the price hike is unjust, tell me exactly what can entertain you in equal measure for .03 cents per hour over 2,000 hours? You realize that it cost more to run your rig in electric bills than the actual hourly rate for the game? Lol.
What is Ark?
Whatever you make of it.
Risk vs reward, set your own goals and challenges and find interesting and unique meta to achieve them.
Small or big? Wide or Tall? Pvp , pvpe, RP? Solo? Whatever you want, you can achieve it in this game. All you need is a curious mind, a strong will and an ever EVOLVING point of view, strategy, and implementation methods to meet your goals.
Bugs: Enhance the meaning behind your assets:
Yes, many....but they eventually get fixed.....or sometimes not...
I have lost more dino assets on this game due to random bugs  than my entire  2,000 plus hours on official pvp. ( RIP Battletoad, your toadness will never been seen again among all the arks to come – killed by infinite falling bug in redwoods cave…the Devs had a moment of silence for him when even they could not save him…lol)
The lows of bugs create the highs in game:
It does feel terrible when you spent plus hours taming your first quetz solo ( prior to x2 EZ mode) and it had THE BEST EVER stats and a rad color and a bug or unscheduled restart messes it up and you don’t get it and its 1 bite away from perfect tame….....but you know what? When i got the next 150 with great stats...it MEANT something to me and that is a success.
Every time you take a dino out, you risk it. There is this thing called consequences and♥♥♥♥♥♥will go wrong. So plan for it. Think of every dino you get as a boat, it can and will sink....even if you leave it docked….so have many many backups. USE  Strategic thinking...
PVP Official
One/cluster server Alpha/ mega tribes:

FOR THE SHORT REVIEW;
I like this game, its fun to play alone or with friends and it looks nice to boot.  But no, it is not worth the $60 price tag.  Get it when it drops back down to $30 or less during a sale.
FOR THE LONG REVIEW, KEEP READING.
Ark is fun regardless as to whether or not you play it solo, with friends, or online in a public server.  The base building is great, the graphics are the best as far as I have seen for an Early Access game with only maybe one exception but even then there are more things to see in Ark so it still wins in my opinion.  The gameplay could be a little better, but with everything else that is in this game it is more than acceptable.  The only thing thus far that I would really like to be fixed is;
1) some pretty heavy dino balancing (Spino can get surrounded, swarmed and killed easily by troodons and other small and quick dinos, and it can't really fight back cuz it's head can't reach them when they attack it's sides, then there's the raft-killing-whale-sized-fish in the ocean.  I mean really?  At least make it hostile to 'ALL' except the other ocean predators unless they're player-owned.  Also, when a Rex, Spino, Carno, or whatever else is surrounded by a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of other species' predators like Dilos, Raptors, and what have you, THAT should be turning into a damn bloodbath, not a 'gang-up-on-the-herbivore/player' party.  Getting pretty tired of going to the edge of the swamplands and seeing everything attack one Trike or Parasaur, kill it, and then walk off like they have paperwork to file.)
2) possibly vehicle construction to be expanded into a jurassic park theme (right now the raft is the main thing I can build as a vehicle, then theres the more advanced♥♥♥♥♥♥but that takes a much longer than I'd like)
3) and of course it goes without saying but bug fixes as well.
I have yet to try out the primitive plus game mode, but I'm looking forward to it since it seems like it'll be a throwback the original goal of the game.  Survival.
Lastly, this is probably the most controversial thing but, the price tag.  I'll say this in caps so that it's understood where I stand.
THIS GAME IS *NOT* WORTH $60.  I REPEAT, THIS GAME IS *NOOOT* WORTH SIXTY DOLLARS ($60)!
This is a good game.  A great game when playing with friends.  Even so it is only worth in it's current state the original $30 price tag.  Maybe after some more heavy balancing and bug fixes it will be worth $40-50, but not $60.  For $60 I would need to be seeing in addition to everything else, 1) Cinematics/Cut-Scenes, 2) NPCs and NPC settlements/structures with quests/missions and a plot-line, and 3) Reasonably priced DLC.  I'll tell you right now, I will never pay $20 or more for DLC unless it fully expands on the gameplay, story, mechanics, and game modes of a game, and I suggest you do as I do as well.

What i can fairly say about the game after years of gameplay:

I have been playing early access for a little over 1.5 years.  I will list a few pro and con items here.  The game world is amazing and fun from that first time you wake up naked on the beach to the many times you die as a newbie and wake up naked on the beach again, it is a blast.
--Public Servers--
The biggest drawback by far is the complete appearance of apathy when it comes to official server performance.  Any time the game becomes unplayable (and in full transparency, it is now as I write this), there is never a response or acknowledgement from any official Wildcard Studios perspective.  They will mention performance optimizations, but that seems to only be focused on the single player version or the game code for unofficial (privately hosted) servers.
If, moving forward, this would change, I would certainly come back and update this review as I feel that this factor alone pushes this to negative which would otherwise be more neutral or slightly positive.
In fact, many moves recently have added to time syncs, nerfs, or restricted players in ways that makes private servers or single player the only options.  To help compensate some, there are occasional “Evolution Events” which increases yields from harvesting resources and experience.  Those have actually been fairly frequently recently, which is nice.
--Dino Cap--
Another big driver to go to an unofficial server is the dino cap per tribe.  It is currently 500 on official servers.  Now that totally makes sense if you are in a small tribe.  However, if you are in a larger tribe, especially one really in to dino breeding, it is a big hindrance.  Five hundred things sounds like a lot, right?  Why would anyone need more than that?  There are several utility animals everyone in the tribe wants to breed for the imprint buff and station at a couple of strategic places around the map.  Next, you need a certain set of eggs to make kibble needed to care for babies and improve their stats while raising them.
You need some backup animals due to deaths while hunting, death in caves, and deaths while fighting bosses.   Not to mention, if you’re going for the best lines of just a few species, you need several different breeders available with different stats.
Some amount of restriction certainly needs to be in place, but it should scale with tribe membership.  We have a few friends we would really like to have in our tribe, but can't add them because we hover at the dino cap.  Scaling the restriction seems much better than just forming an alliance with another tribe.  Sure people share, but now you have two sets of egg-layer requirements for kibble for breeding.  They just need to scale it and everyone wins (probably with an overall lower dino count on the server).
--Time Sinks--
The game has many challenging time sinks to get some of the bigger rewards that borderline on insanity.  Some of the better dinos require an unhealthy amount of time to raise.  I will fully admit my tribemates and I have done this many times.  It is fun in a demented kind of way.  There are several general maintenance tasks such as maintaining food stores, gas (to power electricity needed to preserve all kinds of things in refrigerators, etc.), and similar chores that take more attention.  Gas is getting more expensive to make and lasts a shorter time.
--Graphics--
The graphics of the game are mind-blowing.  Problem is, you will only get to see graphics of that level if you just want to turn them on in a safe place to look around.  It isn’t realistic to play it with graphics all the way up even with awesome hardware.  I have a 1080ti and can play with some things on Epic, but not everything.  Overall, even with some settings lowered, the graphics are pretty good.
--Nerfs--
Lots and lots of nerfs, but hey, it is early access.  When you find something useful and it is taken away, it is, of course, quite annoying.  That being said, I don’t think new players would know what they were missing with some of the nerfs we have seen in early access.  Some of the nerfs as we approach the official release date really have me scratching my head.  There are enough time syncs built in, I don’t think any of them need to be any harder.
I would think most of these would be over by the official release, so probably not a big factor to consider really if you are deciding whether or not to buy the game.
--The Game Concept/Content—
There are a lot of things to do.  I love dinosaur articles, games, documentaries, and movies; I love the content of the game because of that.  There are a lot of fun things to do.
You can:
+ Build from a small hut to an elaborate fortress to a multi-building base to meet your needs as you advance
+ Hunt – on foot or on dino
+ Collect and care for bees to get honey
+ Breed and raise dinos
+ Go SCUBA diving to tame dinos, harvest resources, breed sea animals, or explore underwater caves
+ Sail around the world on a boat (oops, they created a sea critter to destroy boats – sorry)
Bottom line, there are tons of things to do when the lag allows.  There are weekends I have had so much I wanted to do that I have a hard time deciding which to do first (or second and third).
--Expansions—
Scorched Earth was a fairly good expansion.  It introduced new items and resources and a few new dinos.  It is slightly harder there (much harsher environment), so for the more experienced player really, but a newbie could probably get by eventually.
--Conclusion—
So should you buy it?  If you plan to play on official servers, buy with caution until they show a little more respect for that player base.  I am sure they care.  They are a company trying to make money after all.  It is just the fact that I have not seen them acknowledge or show effort to resolve lag issues on public servers.  I am not talking about occasional lag spikes.  I am talking about a day or days of servers being completely unplayable.  I have played on several servers, so it is not just experience based on one or two.
Single player and private server are awesome.  There may be a few glitches here and there, but it is a ton of fun when you are a little more control of support.  That can also be a drawback to a lot of privately hosted servers admins try to overcorrect for the pain points of official servers and end up making it too easy which ruins the fun too.
I hope to see a change of direction when it comes to communication regarding official servers and will be back to update!
[Addition Edit]
Now the game has launched and, as we have come to expect from Wildcard, there are too few official servers.  There is, of course, still room on the Legacy servers which receive little to no support, but most people want to play on the new ones since they allegedly have support.  Servers are constantly full during primetime play and the game is still loaded with bugs, causing you to crash.  Should you get lucky enough to be online, you'll eventually get a random disconnect and then not be able to log back in because servers are full.

ARK: Survival Evolved can be a great game when it wants to be. There are plenty of reasons to play it, plenty of moments to enjoy, plenty of moments that make you feel satisfied with your purchase. God knows from looking at my play hours that I've certainly gotten a lot of time out of the purchase.
But this is a review and this is where I'm supposed to recommend the game to you or not. And, in that, I cannot do so with good conscience.
You see, the thing about ARK is that this game eats away at you in many, many ways. The developers suffer from a tried and true systemic issue of thinking they're smarter than they are, and thinking they know what's best for you when they actually don't. They don't design the game to be fun - they design the game to be "correct." They don't design the game to be easy - they design the game to fit "their vision." They don't design the game based on what a player would actually want - they only design the game around what THEY want to see in their game. So on and so forth, you get the point I'm trying to make.

Chivalry is about three things:
1) Screaming
2) Dismemberment
3) Bugs
The controls and balance of the numbers make for an extremely fast-paced, blood-pumping action game. Most of the time you're only two solid blows from death, and the fast majority of your defense is active. Everything is determined by the actual animations, so turning your view in the direction of your swing makes it hit, and you have to aim just so to properly parry an attack. This all works very well and generally after a minimum of experience you can tell more or less what you did wrong to wind up a bloody mess on the ground. There are several gametypes, from standard capture the flag, king of the hill, and team deathmatch to free-for-all, duels, and several objective-based maps ranging from a siege where the highest-scoring player on the defending team becomes king to an assault on a trebuchet-fortified keep.
Overall the game is chaotic, but the penalty for dying is usually miniscule and it lends itself to a certain mastery. Unfortunately, the game is also buggy - from animations that play when they shouldn't to animations that simply don't sync with the hit boxes. These can be extremely frustrating to face, and often the one using them may not even realize they're exploiting something. Still, rarely is there a game-breaking issue or something that completely stymies fun if you learn to counter it.
A brief aside on the game's aesthetic; the combination of the player models and the slightly-cheesey voice commands make for a feel that is distinctly the game's own and add personality to a game otherwise featuring somewhat drab and generic environments.
Overall the game is strong, and if you're looking for a visceral action game I'd recommend it. The caveat regarding bugs yet applies, of course. If numbers are your thing, I'd give it a 7/10.
