I wake up to a world without a name, alone, and nothing of possession besides the clothes on my back. What was it exactly that I was here for? As I wondered about my purpose in the empty place, a small Monster appears in front of me. Suddenly I feel an urge to Click on the Monster. Strange, before I arrived in this world, there was no such action as ‘Clicking’.
Unable to hold back the desire, I ‘Click’ on the Monster. The Monster that was screaming in agony and suffering didn’t seem to bother me. It didn’t even try to attack back, shouldn’t I feel guilty over harming such a delicate creature? But all the thought disappeared when the Monster was slain. From the disintegrating body, fell coins that started to satisfy me in a way I’ve never deemed possible. I didn’t know what I was here in this world for but now, I wanted these Monsters dead and to take their coins.
Soon after a couple of more battles, I met a fellow Adventurer of these lands named Cid. Strangely, I feel friendly with him. Did I know this man before..? No, that can’t be, this is surely my first encounter! Not dwelling on the thought, we decide to travel together for a small price to hire the Adventurer. And so, I made my first companion in this journey across this strange world.
My first day in this world has come to an end. However, despite my fatigue and need for sleep, I am unable to quench my thirst for these Monster’s demise and their loot. Thankfully, during my journey with Cid, I’ve met and partied with more people that wished to venture alongside with me. A mythical Wooden Grunt that strayed from its Great Forest; a former colosseum fighter that now spends his day washed away in alcohol; a self-proclaimed princess that seem to speck in an uncomfortably familiar tone of language; and a lost Fisherman who has lost his motive in the sea. These members have decided to see to my journey and are working as a team to fight against the foes that dare cross our paths.
But just where this hunger could be coming from, I did not understand. Was it some sort of effect the world had on the inhabitants? It seemed that the only one affected in my party was I. The more I slaughtered these Monsters, the more blood I wished to shed. My new companions who are gifted in the arts of assassination, war, and magic state that it’s nothing to be worried about. They say it is thanks to that burning drive for the death of these Monsters that, they themselves are given the opportunity to stand and fight.
Months have passed and my party has grown vastly. In front of me stands two beings that wish to change the land for the better and the worse. I can’t tell which is what. To my left is a mass formed by all the monsters I have slain. In its eyes, I can see the hate and disgust for me. The demand that I should be degraded and humiliated like the monsters I’ve killed is felt from the aura it emits. But Abaddon, simply smirks stating that it wishes for my assistance. To my right, is a God of many worlds; Amenhotep frowns at the decisions I have made with Abaddon. The deals I agreed to assist in order to bring myself more power. But he doesn’t say anything; because the reason he’s here is to simply measure my worth before the other Gods.
Today, I wake up to myself and my friends being swallowed by the darkness emitting from the ground. It was the same darkness I had assisted Abaddon during his Dark Ritual for Power. I could hear my friends scream as the darkness slowly eroded their bodies into ashes and consume it whole. And I simply stood there watching, tears falling from my eyes, powerless and regretful of not being able to save them. Then suddenly, Amenhotep appeared giving me a choice. To fade away into the Darkness and vanquished with Abaddon or start anew with his Rebirthing Spell of ASSENSION. I wanted a second chance. I wanted to save my friends. I wanted to fix my choices with Abaddon. And most importantly, I wanted to continue killing the Monsters of this World. Desiring all this, I put my life on Amenhotep’s hands as the world shines anew.
...
I wake up to a world with nothing except the clothes on my back. But this time, I feel somewhat stronger. No doubtable weaker than when I was surrounded by friends but still stronger than the time when I first arrived in this world. Did this have to do with something regarding my experience in the previous world? I thought this as I unconsciously mowed down the Monster Foes without worry. But then, a familiar face appeared into my view. I drop to my knees as I embrace Cid in my arms. Cid, the friend who stayed by my side until the end. Cid, the friend who always watched my back. Cid, the friend that understood me the most. He was standing healthy and energetic as ever in front of me.
But… it seemed that he had no recollection of our past encounter. Unfazed by it, I place my hand on his shoulder as I journey towards the Monsters than will fuel my thirst for vengeance and desire. Unfortunately, to do this… I would need Abaddon’s assistance once more.
Many ASSENSIONS later, I stood before Solomon, the Ancient of Wisdom. During my travels here, I had sacrificed my friends for power, and no longer felt the guilt as they shed their tears from the betrayal I have committed. Sometimes, I would not encounter some of these friends during my travels. Whether it was the factor that I traveled too quickly or I missed a trigger of opportunity that was presented, I continued to travel along my hunt of Monsters. Despite this, the three individuals that I was never able avoid were Abaddon, Amenhotep, and my trusty Cid.
I stood facing the eye of Solomon, reflecting upon my recent decisions. What has this world done to me that so many of its creatures deserve to die? Even the monsters in other universes are not safe from my wrath. I realize that you desire to kill them all, and to take all their gold, but am not entirely sure why... You feel the urge to contemplate many things. But as I turn my back, I forget everything as I return to my battleground.
“You done praying already?” asked Astraea, standing in lead of her team of rangers of worlds. With a smirk, I reply “Hmp, I just want to ‘Click’ on more fools.”

How do I review this game? I was a fan since it was a mod, was involved in the earliest alpha stages of it, was a part of the team behind it for a year, and I even found some time to actually play it, too. As far as first person melee games are concerned, there's no doubt in my mind that Chivalry is top dog - but that's not saying much considering first person melee is a genre that hardly exists. If we extend this criteria to encompass all melee games, you start drawing comparisons to things that are really not the same at all. So reviewing this game is also difficult because there is very little to compare it to.
Even War of the Roses, a game cited as Chivalry's primary "competitor", is really a far cry from Chivalry in just about every aspect except for both of them featuring primarily melee combat (though War of the Roses has a much bigger ranged combat element) and both of them being medieval themed (though Chivalry is an unapologetic anachronistic fantasy world while WotR tries to be as authentic as possible to a real world time period). Everything else from the aesthetic to the combat, the primary modes of play, even the perspective used and how that perspective molds the gameplay are all vastly different.
So I guess what I'm left with is this - setting aside as much bias as possible, which is difficult because I've been very involved in this game both as a supporter and a part of its development, and speaking as a player; it's not perfect, it's still got some pretty obvious bugs after over a year, but overall I can think of few games that I've had more fun with, and even fewer that have managed to hold my attention and remain consistently fun for as long as Chivalry has.
In the end, for all its faults, Chivalry's the uncontested king of first person melee combat, and as treasonous as it might sound, I truly hope something comes along soon to dethrone it; because this is a genre that has so much untapped potential and maybe the unexpected success of Chivalry will prompt more people to try their hand at it.

This is, simply put, an excellent game. Not only is it consistently a fun and enjoyable experience, but it's one of the few games I've found myself returning to time and time again, year after year, for each major update. The one weakness I'd say the game has is that it is intensely based around grinding and farming, which means it needs to lean fairly heavily on making that enjoyable. And it works. If you like the core gameplay of frantically jumping around and murdering space clone Nazis with a flamethrower that shoots explosions out to 300 yards while having your pet space cat tear the throats out of enemy snipers, then this is a fantastic and enjoyable game. And that's not even mentioning the incredibly nice community.

ARK, at its core, is one of the most fun games I have ever played. The idea of growing and getting better in a world full of things to explore, dinosaurs with unique abilities to aid you in your survival, and a sense of excitement every time you level up to unlock the next unique craft-able item that will make mastering the world that much better. So, now the question is: why do I not recommend this game to anyone?
The answer has to do with a common problem a lot of titles have: too much effort, not enough reward.
At it's core, ARK is fun, I have it on both PC and Xbox and until recently, have played it quite regularly. The last straw came shortly after the release of the recent update which locked the map "The Center" unless a player reached "gamma" level, meaning that a player has completed the game for one of the two unlocked maps.
Now, a friend of mine and I had a file on the center that we had spent a bit of time on and wanted to play. This was problematic because of the previously mentioned update. This left me and my friend with 2 choices: cheat or do things honestly.
Well we both were against cheating, so we were going to do things honestly.
To be brief, requires surmounting 9 incredibly difficult caves (I use that loosely, some are difficult, some not) a minimum of 3 times a piece (two if my friend and I go together), hunting 6 of the rarest spawning animals in the game, and defeating 9 separate bosses, each requiring hours of preparation to face. This grueling regiment is softened by the fact that beating bosses grants you the ability to craft some of the best items in the game, however the resources required to make and operate these items are so rare, that it will take hours to make, and only a few minutes to actually use.
In conclusion, my complaints are not that the game is too hard, not about graphical issues nor mechanics, not a pvp element that attracts♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥bags like magnets attract iron. No, my problem is the hours and hours and hours and HOURS of time spent for virtually nothing, like working for food service for 10% of the minimum wage.

In my Opinion, Clicker Heroes is the best idle game out there and I have played alot of them. The game is very easy to understand, yet, there's deep strategy involved. You click to deal damage, you buy heroes (and upgrades) to deal damage over time and you buy (and level up) ancients to improve your damage, your gold gains or even reduce the amount of monsters you have to kill to progress.
There are tons of ways you can play the game, just by the way you build your ancients. You can focus on having your skills last for a long time, you can focus on dealing as much damage over time as possible without clicking or you can make it so your clicks are extremely strong. Of course, with a lot of time and effort, you can buy and level up any ancients, but the amount of time it takes to get there depends on how good your strategy is.
Also, they are always adding new content to the game and improving it, so if you ever get bored, come back 3-6 months later and you will have new heroes, ancients and/ or features that will have been implemented!
PROs:
-It's free.
-It's fun.
-It's easy to play.
-The game is being updated every few months.
-You can leave the game closed and you keep progressing.
-You can play this game while waiting for multiplayer games to start or when you have 5 minutes of free-time at work.
-The achievements are great and there are many to unlock (most of them are also Steam Achievements).
-The replayability of this game is endless...
-The monsters and backgrounds are really cool.
CONs:
-There's only 1 music in the game.
-It does get repetitive, but starting over or waiting for updates usually does the trick.
I totally suggest ANYONE try out this game. It's really great and it's free. Also, you can obtain rubies while playing (so no, it's not pay-to-win). Also, beware that this game is tremendously addicting! Do yourself a favor and download it, enjoy the game. :)

I bought this game practically when it came out but unfortunately was unable to play it on my 8 year old gaming PC. That's fine, I was due for an upgrade anyway. Almost a year later I got the parts for a current generation gaming PC. Lets break down the cons;
- The game still crashes due to memory leaks (constantly)
- Both the unofficial and official servers are unstable ( half the time I get connection timeouts on official servers the other half the time the servers are offline or doing rollbacks.
- I will sometime spend 40 minutes to an hour trying to connect to an official server that is maybe hosting around 30 players.
"this isn't a me problem, it's a you problem".
My wife's gaming computer goes through the same issues and I've played a great assortment of games on a very fast internet connection without issues.
- The mechanics in the game for base building specifically are so awful and non-forgiving ( laying pipes and electrical is just the worst experience ever )
- PvP Server jumping sucks♥♥♥♥♥ Tribes just load their dinos from another server onto yours, and go around crushing all the noobies. Their needs to be some legit PvP rules on how and who you can engage.
Feature Request:  A tribe leveling system could fix part of this so SUPER high level tribes simply can't destroy low level tribes, griefing is far too common and simply unfun. Having a level range of who you can attack could help curb some of the PvP problems. The game experience is much more enjoyable in a PvE enviroment as the game is currently. Only reason I would ever play on a PvP server again is to grief other players which is exactly the problem currently.
What I love about this game;
- So many creatures to discover
- When the game is running and working at its best the graphics blow me away
- I love Dinos! I love taming mechanics! I love flying!
- I love how the creatures interact with each other, killing and hunting prey ect. Very cool to watch.
- I like most of the crafting systems ( pipes and electrical being the exceptions so far )
Bottom line. I would never pay 60+ bucks for a game that only works half the time, I've all together given up trying to connect some days and straight up went to play a different game. I got this game for my wife and I both on steam sales, wouldn't have bought it otherwise.
My suggestion is wait for a killer steam deal the game has it's moments. Plan to play on a PvE server starting out. PvP in this game is nothing but purposeful griefing.
I would still like to give Wildcard the benifit of the doubt but the moves the company has made I would not suggest buying this game at any full retail price. If things get better by their release date I'll be happy to change my review.

If you've watched the trailers and liked seeing the cyborg ninja action, you're probably going to enjoy this game. This game allows for some awesome action to be had, it has a nice bit of a good amount of story, lore and overall has a good comunity. I also like how the game on the whole has a max of 4 players in a group so you won't have any of that dodgy mmo jerky movements.
However your experience can be comprimised by internet conection, the occasional bad community experince, unlucky loot drops, steep learning curve, large updates, what can be repetitive play & the occasional drop outs, but these things are common amongst online games.
If you're thinking of starting, here's a few tips to make the game more enjoyable, or at least less frustrating.
1. Play with friends. - If you're interested in playing, it's best to start with some friends, prefereably ones that are in the same room so you can back each other up. (that is after the initial solo quest) Advanced players may murder things quite fast leaving you with a walking simulator.
2. If you are playing with friends in the same room. - Download the game seperately before going over to your friend's house. It's a large game and splitting bandwidth 4 ways can make for some boring wait time.
3. Adjust your graphics settings. - I know we all want to play games on the best graphic settings, but make sure you have a smooth running game first.
4. Don't spend platinum on anything but slots in the begining. - Platinum is the currancy that you pay for with real money. Before you run off and but some shiney cosmetic, it's better to spend it on slots so you have a chance to play the game with a variety of warframes. That way you can see if you want to continue playing rather than being stuck with the 1 frame.
5. Open the star map. - By opening the starmap, you'll gain access to more mission, get to understand more of the different mission types and gather the resources you need to advance. Also they missions should be appropriately leveled for a new comer.
6. Tutorials - If you're ever stuck there's heaps of tutorials and warframe for beginner videos on youtube.
7. Be nice and enjoy the game. In my experience, most of the community is nice, let's keep it that way :)
Hope that helps.

Ark is a great game, if you decide to play by yourself, you can tame dinosaurs to keep you company or you can play with your friends and make a great base. You can also go online to join one of the many servers accessible through the internet. With its intriguing lore and beautiful landscapes coupled with the fact that it is modifiable give you an entire range of things to do and places to see, not to mention people to meet. The price spike I can see as far as a programming perspective mainly because of Ark is starting to accelerate its development into a full release, shown by the massive amounts of content and bug patch updates that have been rolling out. At first Ark spiked a lot of interest in me, but I didn't hear about it for a while. I saw how much it has changed and I see how much potential it has. the games original price seems to be matching it in those far off early days of development, but now with all the work that has been put into it, it is fitting for a price increase. Just think about it, people pay 60$ for Call of Duty when they release a new title every year (mostly) and no one complained about that. with all the great games out there, 60$ is a fairly common price. Along with that, if you have bought the game before the price change, you can still keep it. If you really liked that game, you would of got it when it was in development to help the developers make it into the great game both us and them know it will and can be.
EDIT: little post note, they also are adding a lot of extra free content in too. Content that usually is 5$ to get.

Great game, especially since it is updated so regularly. One of the few games in early-access that, apart from a few bugs, have felt like a completed game for a long time already, with only more content and more options constantly being added. The price change is also understandable: ARK is a full game that deserves a full game price now. There have been dozens of creatures added, and even two extra free maps, tripling the content since original launch. Just be happy that it was available for half price due to it being early access.
Positive points:
- Devoted dev team which brings out regular updates and fixes
- Good taming system for dozens of different creatures
- Personalised gaming experience: you can adapt most of the game settings, and choose to play single or multiplayer by creating own servers which cannot just be joined by anyone
- Extensive crafting and building system (enhanced by the modding community too)
- All the different biomes, resources and items have been well thought out, creating a world with its own ruleset that also makes sense.
Negative:
- Harder to play when you don't have a great computer, even when setting graphics to low, since the game demands high cpu
- Still a few bugs that cause the game to crash or players to become stuck, especially in caves.

I highly recommend this game. The premise for the game couldn't be any simpler, yet the game has an incredible amount of depth. Interesting decision points are frequent, micro and long term strategy are both relevant, and the gameplay remains engaging for hundreds of hours.

Before you bother reading all of this, know that this review is in response to other negative reviews in light of the game's price increase, and not actually a detailed review of my experiences with the game. I don't love ARK, but I don't hate it either. I just think the game deserves the right to come into its own.
Imagine a game with no story, graphics more than 5 years behind its time, and essentially no basis for play other than pointlessly running around and making♥♥♥♥♥♥♥out of dirt. Imagine this game is pushed out in Alpha by the developers, saying that they need some time to improve before a retail release. Now imagine that game hits market with a $5 price tag, but as time goes on, the game improves, and as more features and items are added, the game comes to cost more and more. Fast forward a year and a half into the game's life cycle, and it gets a full release, with the price finally settling at nearly $30, about 600% of the game's initial cost. The game you're imagining is Minecraft. Now hold on to that thought for a minute, I promise it'll make sense soon.
Is ARK perfect? Absolutely not. Is it ridden with bugs, performance issues, and countless other problems that make it one of the most notorious "your-machine-is-not-worthy" games of all time? Definitely. Is it the most engaging, exciting, balanced and well-designed games I've ever played? Not by a long shot. But does the game deserve to be written off because of a price hike? No, no it does not. It's still a fun and unique experience, and if that's something that you want, the price point really shouldn't sway you.
The reality of a game like ARK is that it's released in an Early-Access state in order for the developer to make money to support the game's development while it's happening. Part of the charm but also the crutch of picking up a game like this is that the early adopters are basically also beta testers who are paying the company to find their bugs and issues for them. You need to keep in mind that any Early Access game you pick up and play might change and pivot in a completely different direction at almost any time. Just look at Rust, that game has changed countless times in the past few years of development and they still haven't pushed it out of Alpha yet.
My point here is that as a kickback of investing your time and money into a game that isn't yet finished, you usually get to pick it up at a reduced price since the collective feedback actually impacts the development and direction of the game, at least to an extent. This has been the case with ARK. I'm sure that if large studios or well-known developers decided to take the Early Access route, their games would probably be released at a lower inital price point as well, since nobody would pay $60 to help iron out the bugs of a game that they would normally expect to release as close to perfect as possible. Take Kickstarter for example, usually if you back an early concept and want to be part of the first wave of something new before it reaches mass production, they offer their product to you at a cheaper price. Not because that is meant to be the intended retail price, but because you're investing in the company's future and helping them work out the kinks. Is this always the best method? No, not really, and in the case of ARK, it probably would have been wise for the developers to outright mention that the Alpha price wasn't final, but again, that is something that's technically covered under the guise of the "Early Access" moniker.
So in saying this, to the people who already own the game and are giving it negative reviews solely for the increased price, I can't really see how it makes any difference to you at all. You got the game at a cheaper rate, and you want the game to improve, yet you're making negative reviews to chase away any possible revenue for the company to both allow and incentivize them to improve their flawed game. Chances are, the people who want to pick up the game are already aware of the buggy and poorly-optimized experience that they're in for, and they're going to buy it anyway since they legitimately just want the experience. Or they already own it, since high interest would probably lead them to pick it up sometime over the past year and a half of development.
All in all, does the price hike suck for those who haven't adopted the game yet? Yeah, it does. But is the game altogether not worth that price? Not at all. The game is what you make it, and if you want to run around in an honestly very beautiful and fairly enjoyable dino-world, ARK is worth it either way. Is Minecraft worth its $30 price tag and entirely without bugs or issues? Not really, but it's one of the most successful games of all time. I'm sure the people who picked it up at $5 are probably thinking that the people who are buying it now at $30 are wasting their money and that the game isn't worth it too, but that doesn't make it a universally bad game.
TL;DR the increased cost of the game is something that has been transparent on the Steam page since ARK hit Early Access, and for a game this technically beautiful and potentially packed with hundreds of hours of amusement, you should pick it up if you want it regardless of price point, and the extra money, player base and support for the developers will only go towards improving the game since they'll want as many people as happy as possible (so stop whining and giving the game negative reviews if you want it to get better, previous owners)

Okay, but seriously now. Warframe is a third person shooter set in the far future, long after human civilisation as we know it today, after the fall of a highly advanced human empre known as the Orokin, with Earth ruined by giant genetically altered trees of Orokin origin, and the solar system embroiled in constant conflict. On one side is the Grineer, an army of clones originally used as slaves by the Orokin suffering from genetic deterioration that has resulted in hereditary psychosis and a reliance on cybernetics. On another is the Corpus - a human faction that claims Orokin ancestry that worships money and seeks profit through conflict and any other possible means without concern for morality. In the third corner is the Infested, a sentient hive-mind virus that was created by the Orokin as a weapon (The Orokin were total♥♥♥♥♥♥♥that did a lot of very bad things, in case you couldn't tell by this point) that infects organic matter and twists it into nightmarish abominations that threatens to over-run the entire solar system if not kept in check. Other factions are also creeping into the picture, shadows of an Old War that little is known about.
The Tenno - the players - fight a gureilla war on all fronts to prevent any one side from gaining too much ground while more permanent solutions are not yet available.
Warframe has a tonne of content that is still being added to by the developers. A lot of the game focuses around very fast movement as you control the Warframes - basically like character classes, but all of them are Space-Ninja-Wizard-Warriors that have their own unique abilities. You also have an extremely large choice of primary, secondary and melee weapons, cosmetic options out the wazoo and the entire game is free to play. Like actually free to play - very little is hidden behind paid transactions and you can even trade the premium currency (Platinum) between players in exchange for other things in trading.
The only things that actually require Platinum are a lot of the cosmetic items (not even all of them - there are cosmetic items that look quite good that don't require Platinum) and inventory slots, which is a pretty standard idea in F2P games. Everything else you can get fairly easily with some time.
People do complain about 'the grind' but the game offers many ways to mitigate the grind, and while your weapons and warframes have build times you can easily occupy the time by doing other things and queueing up other builds - you can have as many Foundry items running simultaneously as you like. For that matter, the star chart is very large and you'll always have some other goal to work towards for a good couple of hundred hours or more, easily. And working through those missions will probably be quite fun, as the game features pretty satisftying gunplay and many ways to look and feel really cool while cutting your way through legions of enemies.
I will say one word of warning in that the game does not explain itself very well, leading to a pretty rocky new-player experience if you don't have a lot of personal initiative. For where to acquire items, what warframe powers do, and many other bits of information, you should definitely check the wiki:
It is also worth noting that your real power comes from your mods - the things you slot into your equipment - rather than your equipment itself. Even the starting rifle can handle high level content with the right mods, but even the 'best' weapon in the game won't help you if you don't equip and upgrade your mods as you go. This is a common stumbling block and is something the game fails to explain adequitely, so definitely keep that in mind.
If you want a third person shooter that oozes style, Warframe is definately worth a try. The entry cost is literally zero, after all!

Excellent game and worth every penny. It is obvious that Wildcard cares about making this game as great as it can be, which is to their bane and benefit.
On one hand, they have pushed many more features and dinosaurs than they originally described when they went into early access. They promised a survival game with over 100 dinosaurs, and we got 143. We got VR support(that needs a lot of work, but was pushed early due to demand), procedurally generated maps(again, needs work), a free esports style mode in Survival of the Fittest, full mod support including sponsoring modders, and 2 free maps as official DLC(made and maintained by modders, but they are paid by Wildcard), and tek tier items. Most of these features feel polished and well done, especially on private servers, and they still have a month left until official release to bug fix and optimize.
On the other, using their resources on these features may have detracted from or slowed down core development, which has obviously been frustrating for some members of the community who only want a polished form of what they were promised. Wildcard has been no stranger to controversy either, by releasing a paid DLC during EA, and by hiking the price before release(which they said they were going to do).
Most of the negative reviews that I have seen at least, focus on these issues first and foremost, but they have nothing to do with the game itself. Many of these reviewers have hundreds of hours into the game and will admit that they like or love the game, but leave a bad review based on outside factors that have nothing to do with the gameplay experience, so please take that into consideration if you are considering making a purchase.
As far as the game itself, I have never played a game that has given me as many hours of fun and excitement as Ark has. Especially on a private server, I am able to tailor the experience in any way I want to by using fantastic mods, altering the rates of harvesting and taming, or limitless other options to change to my liking.
Taming a new dinosaur, especially early to mid game, feels exciting and rewarding. Losing a dinosaur or rare piece of equipment due to poor planning can feel hard, and you experience a real sense of loss if your favorite dinosaur dies due to a mistake you made. Everyone complains about this game being some "Pay 2 win" game, and they claim they're veterans.
Simply put; if you truly believe that, you're an idiot.
Warframe has it's Pro's and Cons, of course, just as does every single game.  However, the Pros of Warframe heavily beat the Cons.
First off, Warframe is a very grindy game, so DON'T play if you don't enjoy grinding, farming, and RNG.
Second, Warframe's developers aren't the best, but they are definitely among the top.  They're friendly, frequently listen to the community, and they have some of the best animations I've seen.  (The cutscenes are really, really good.)
Third: THE GAME IS NOT PAY TO WIN.  You could argue that it is pay to win FASTER, but it most certainly is NOT pay to win.  The in-game currency that can be bought (Platinum, as opposed to credits, which you can't trade) can also be traded for.  If you farm for some rare parts, or just happen to get some good items or mods (etc.), you can trade it with someone in the trading chat for platinum.
Alright, those being said, let's get to the Pros and Cons.
Pros:
-Good Developer team
-Not p2p/p2w
-The game is free
-In game graphics are very good, even on lowest settings (Can run rather well on lowest settings too; this comes from a guy with a potato disguised as a computer)
-Cool parkour mechanics
-Lots and lots of unique weapons
-Warframes suited for pretty much every aspect of gameplay
-Everything in the game, except certain accessories, can be obtained as a non-paying player.
-Quests almost always meet to the expectations set.  This is opinion based, but it's also based off of user reviews, and it's almost always positive.
Cons:
-Developers don't very much cater to end-game players/founders.
-Many, MANY tiny bugs.  Most don't ruin your game, but occasionally you can get screwed over by one.
-New aspects are brought into the game, then abandoned for a long time.
-The price for platinum is too damn high.
-The grind can get a bit too repetitive at times; sometimes just outright annoying and unnecessary.
-A few members of the Warframe Support team (The moderators, usually of forums, etc.) are rather rude.  If you do happen to run into them when seeking for support, re-file the support a week later and you should get a different support member.
If I didn't mention anything it's either because I forgot or it's just there in the game, good to stay, no reason to go.  It ain't good, it ain't bad.
So would I recommend this game?
Well, if you have lots of hours to spend on a rather fun game, I'd most definitely say yes.  Warframe is easily the most fun RNG-based progression game I have come across, because it not only makes you farm for your items, but it makes the farming process actually fun, and usually not just a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥

This game is so deep and intriguing. Such is its mastery that the eagerness of knowing that which remains hidden obscures any possible flaw it may have, immersing your poor baited self deeper into its darkest, most unthought of secrets.
On a more serious side, this game is like a very good book. I'm always willing to grind a bit in order to progress and discover more items, locations, stories, and characters. At first I was overwhelmed by some of its psychedelic art and some other mechanics that didn't make sense to me, but most of the latter makes sense once you advance enough in the story.
One of the things I have found unique from this game is its community, it has to be one of the friendliest in any game ever, so far from the puke-inducing hordes of underaged teenagers looking to gain value from other's demise and deception, like Dota, or CS:GO. You will always find someone to play with, and if they are in a higher level, they almost always babysit you like it was their responsibility, no matter how "random" the individual may seem. They will also answer your question, sometimes even if you didn't read the wiki, and they will not judge you for not knowing what you shouldn't know.
Gameplay wise its mechanics are very basic, but they cover many functions and most of the time it doesn't feel like you are just hammering the keyboard, and, if you are, you're most likely being lazy and not taking advantage of all that your character has to offer.
The developers are very close to the community and the events are very frequent, there are also many modes in many worlds, and it just keeps growing.
If you are looking for a good time every now and then and enjoy a lore-heavy game with an actually nice community, I invite you to try this game.

Don't be fooled by youtube vids, they are played on private servers for the most part - a public PvP one is as brutal as rust.

A review as seen from the eyes of an Atlas player:
The world is hard.  Sometimes people will tell you "You're not good enough", or, "There isn't room for you here.  Git gud."
Well I have only one thing to say, er, do to those people.
I punch.
I punch harder than the likes of which you've ever known.  I punch faster, stronger, and more accurately in order to show this world that I am strong enough!
Sure, I could do something "meta", I could do what everyone else does, or I could punch things!
Warframe is a punching simulator.  When you run out of energy to punch stuff (you won't), you start punching stuff with normal fists.  Then you get more energy for punching stuff again.  It's a cycle of amazing.  Nothing can withstand the might of your fists!
Sure, you could build a wall.  You could turn your enemies to stone, or even summon rocks to fight for you.  But why bother?  Why do anything but punch?  You'll eventually just grow in power, as time goes on.  You'll grow to the point that you can one-punch anything you desire!

This game is filled with grinding and waiting. With that said, Warframe is a great game. It has a nice sci-fi graphical theme, a wonderful community, a dev team willing to listen to the community, and an extensive roster of characters, weapons, and modifications for both. I've played this game for only a short while compared to many others, but I still come back daily to it to enjoy practicing new ideas or tricks. This game is a COMMITMENT but not an mmorpg commitment. For newer players, there lies a steep learning curve, but with a little reading and guidance from the Guides of the Lotus (players that volunteered to help newer players), this game is wonderful. Taking a month off also won't cause you to be left behind.
Oh and on a final note: if anyone tells you how to play, take their advice with a pound of salt. No one knows the "perfect" way to play.

Official server multiplayer: Wouldn't recommend for the price point right now. Issues with lag, servers going offline, item duping etc... They have a lot to work on here.
Unofficial server multiplayer: Highly recommend. Play with friends on more stable servers (or make your own). Use mods to increase longevity and have control over the grind rate. For people who work or have any life at all, the grind is insane. Being able to speed things to normal-people levels is great.
Singler-player: Highly recommend. I would pay this money all over again for the hours I've enjoyed in this game. Sped up some rates to decrease the grind. Option for mods is available. There is so much to do in this game it's insane. Taming, breeding, exploring, killing everything! It's a great ride. Singler player gets boring after long enough but you can always jump on a server or create a server with friends when that happens. I still got 10x the enjoyable solo hours on this game than most AA games that cost similar.
There's still issues with opitmization that need to be fixed. The game is HUGE. It'll fill an SSD easily and it really plays better with one. Load times can be crazy, driver crashes happen too. My computer can handle it usually but my friends can not. If you're playing on a potato I would not recommend this game right now. When playing official rates the grind is huge. I wouldn't recommend playing official for casual or sane people.
My final word is that this game is beautiful and really well done. Even if it never gets fixed past this point (trust me, I'd be angry) I would STILL re-buy this game so I could continue playing it. Based on that alone I have to recommend it. I've had a blast!

If you've watched the trailers and liked seeing the cyborg ninja action, you're probably going to enjoy this game. This game allows for some awesome action to be had, it has a nice bit of a good amount of story, lore and overall has a good comunity. I also like how the game on the whole has a max of 4 players in a group so you won't have any of that dodgy mmo jerky movements.
However your experience can be comprimised by internet conection, the occasional bad community experince, unlucky loot drops, steep learning curve, large updates, what can be repetitive play & the occasional drop outs, but these things are common amongst online games.
If you're thinking of starting, here's a few tips to make the game more enjoyable, or at least less frustrating.
1. Play with friends. - If you're interested in playing, it's best to start with some friends, prefereably ones that are in the same room so you can back each other up. (that is after the initial solo quest) Advanced players may murder things quite fast leaving you with a walking simulator.
2. If you are playing with friends in the same room. - Download the game seperately before going over to your friend's house. It's a large game and splitting bandwidth 4 ways can make for some boring wait time.
3. Adjust your graphics settings. - I know we all want to play games on the best graphic settings, but make sure you have a smooth running game first.
4. Don't spend platinum on anything but slots in the begining. - Platinum is the currancy that you pay for with real money. Before you run off and but some shiney cosmetic, it's better to spend it on slots so you have a chance to play the game with a variety of warframes. That way you can see if you want to continue playing rather than being stuck with the 1 frame.
5. Open the star map. - By opening the starmap, you'll gain access to more mission, get to understand more of the different mission types and gather the resources you need to advance. Also they missions should be appropriately leveled for a new comer.
6. Tutorials - If you're ever stuck there's heaps of tutorials and warframe for beginner videos on youtube.
7. Be nice and enjoy the game. In my experience, most of the community is nice, let's keep it that way :)
Hope that helps.

I will say this - the game isn't perfect. Things do become a grind after a while, even if you are switching weapons and frames and playstyles, and what-have-you.
But from what I've seen, the Developer, DE, genuinely cares about the community. They want to make this game the best it can be.
Premium currency is tradeable between players, cash-users still have to grind with the freemiums. The cosmetic helmets can drop from special alerts, and anything that affects balance (like the reactors and catalysts that double your mod capacity, which would be restricted to cash-users in most other games) can and does drop for free if you run the right missions, or wait for the alerts that happen.
Warframe is the best example I've seen on how to handle a freemium game. Anything that affects the balance of power is free, and can be bought (cheaply, I might add.) either from the ingame market, or from other players.
The game itself is a freaking blast before you hit the grindwall, and even then, when running the more popular mission modes, you can always find more experienced players in your group helping to push the group further.
The community can be more than a tad whiny, but the complaining HAS gotten things fixed in the past, especially with the nightmare that was the few days after The War Within dropped, and a certain new item caused the community to flip out. That's still being tweaked, but much of the complaining HAS gone away.
In all, I do reccomend Warframe - It's fun all the way up to Pluto, after you beat The War Within (about 100 hours in, for me). After that, be prepared to grind for credits, relics, and everything else under the sun. But by that point, you've probably already spent ten to twenty dollars pimping out your robot ninja, and you just don't care anymore.

Okay, but seriously now. Warframe is a third person shooter set in the far future, long after human civilisation as we know it today, after the fall of a highly advanced human empre known as the Orokin, with Earth ruined by giant genetically altered trees of Orokin origin, and the solar system embroiled in constant conflict. On one side is the Grineer, an army of clones originally used as slaves by the Orokin suffering from genetic deterioration that has resulted in hereditary psychosis and a reliance on cybernetics. On another is the Corpus - a human faction that claims Orokin ancestry that worships money and seeks profit through conflict and any other possible means without concern for morality. In the third corner is the Infested, a sentient hive-mind virus that was created by the Orokin as a weapon (The Orokin were total♥♥♥♥♥♥♥that did a lot of very bad things, in case you couldn't tell by this point) that infects organic matter and twists it into nightmarish abominations that threatens to over-run the entire solar system if not kept in check. Other factions are also creeping into the picture, shadows of an Old War that little is known about.
The Tenno - the players - fight a gureilla war on all fronts to prevent any one side from gaining too much ground while more permanent solutions are not yet available.
Warframe has a tonne of content that is still being added to by the developers. A lot of the game focuses around very fast movement as you control the Warframes - basically like character classes, but all of them are Space-Ninja-Wizard-Warriors that have their own unique abilities. You also have an extremely large choice of primary, secondary and melee weapons, cosmetic options out the wazoo and the entire game is free to play. Like actually free to play - very little is hidden behind paid transactions and you can even trade the premium currency (Platinum) between players in exchange for other things in trading.
The only things that actually require Platinum are a lot of the cosmetic items (not even all of them - there are cosmetic items that look quite good that don't require Platinum) and inventory slots, which is a pretty standard idea in F2P games. Everything else you can get fairly easily with some time.
People do complain about 'the grind' but the game offers many ways to mitigate the grind, and while your weapons and warframes have build times you can easily occupy the time by doing other things and queueing up other builds - you can have as many Foundry items running simultaneously as you like. For that matter, the star chart is very large and you'll always have some other goal to work towards for a good couple of hundred hours or more, easily. And working through those missions will probably be quite fun, as the game features pretty satisftying gunplay and many ways to look and feel really cool while cutting your way through legions of enemies.
I will say one word of warning in that the game does not explain itself very well, leading to a pretty rocky new-player experience if you don't have a lot of personal initiative. For where to acquire items, what warframe powers do, and many other bits of information, you should definitely check the wiki:
It is also worth noting that your real power comes from your mods - the things you slot into your equipment - rather than your equipment itself. Even the starting rifle can handle high level content with the right mods, but even the 'best' weapon in the game won't help you if you don't equip and upgrade your mods as you go. This is a common stumbling block and is something the game fails to explain adequitely, so definitely keep that in mind.
If you want a third person shooter that oozes style, Warframe is definately worth a try. The entry cost is literally zero, after all!

Playing on a vanilla version with all of the standard settings is awful because of how time consuming and tedious it can be, but you can tweak all of these settings to your liking. Gameplay in general is a lot of fun. Who doesn't like the idea of taming a dinosaur and riding off into battle on it lol. The building mechanics are pretty good but can be a bit frustrating to get something just right. Graphics CAN be amazing but you need a pretty good build to make it run well. All these positives aside, the game is filled with bugs, glitches and optimization problems. In the last few weeks, I have put in a little over 50 hours with friends and I have dealt with graphical glitches, user interface problems, crashing, and TONS of network issues. The only thing that fixed this was to close the game completely and validate your files. This happened at least once an hour and for no apparent reason. A friend could connect just fine, log out for a moment and then time out over and over just minutes later while trying to reconnect. For some reason every time a player would either log out or get a certain distance from me, any part of their character model that had clothing would be invisibe and the only way we found to fix it was to remove the clothing and put it back on. But this happened so often that after a point we just ignored it. This game has tons of content, but the lack optimizations and sea of bugs to encounter absolutely kills it at times. The only way this game would be worth $60 is if they threw in the Scorched Earth DLC that they made before full release as well. Otherwise, just wait for it to go down during Steam's sale events. Just before this price hike, I paid $15 during the summer sales for a copy of this for a friend. Why should anyone pay $60 for it now? And don't give me any lame "well the retailers are demanding we increase the price" bs. If that were really the case, just stick to digital sales. No one NEEDS a hard copy of anything these days. Point being, you can put all the content in the world into a game but if it is poorly optimized and full of bugs, it just isn't worth the headache. Fix your s*** devs.

Warframe is a Free to Play MMOFPS. Gameplay is a game with a lot of grinding and optimizing of different builds through their weapon's mod systems. The great thing about warframe is even though it has a premium currency it is not pay to win. You can get 95% of the items in the game without spending anything, and some items you can't get with money even if you are willing to pay for them. None of the premium items really give an unfair advantage. The game generally uses a foundry system to make items where you collect a blueprint and requisite materials and an item starts crafting on a timer which you can rush using the premium currency or you can just buy the item outright with premium currency. This system works great because some people have the time to farm out items, but not the money. Other people have the money to buy some items but not the time to farm for them. Also even if you are a free player there are easily available items that you can farm and trade with other players for their premium currency without spending a penny of your own money. If you don't mind some grind its a neat 3rd person shooter with magical space ninjas. Just don't listen to DE when they give a timeframe for an update, instead of just releasing it when it is ready to go they always impose an odd deadline on themselves that they very rarely meet and wouldn't have to try to meet if they didn't tell their players thats when its coming out.
It is a great team and free for all game, but be careful you can hurt team mates.

There are so many things to say about this game, both good and bad. Chivalry is an entirely different game for experienced players than it is for new players and I have to say that after learning how to play the game and getting used to it, I have a lot more bad things to say about it than I did when I first started. With that being said, the game itself is actually really good, it just happens to be plagued with many significant issues.
The game is not only imbalanced but also very broken with more game breaking bugs than a tropical rainforest. Because of these issues the game is unbelievably frustrating at times, especially for someone who wishes to play the game competitively at a high skill level. But for what it's worth, the game still manages to be very addicting when you look past its flaws.
The way the game  is designed combined with its cancerous community provides a very hostile environment for new players but the atmosphere of the game and the overall feel of being a part of it more than makes up for getting completely demolished both verbally and physically. I was having so much fun just playing the game when I was new that I didn't even care how poorly I was doing nor what other players were saying about me.
The game is deceivingly complex and has quite a steep learning curve and an even larger skill ceiling but is enjoyable enough for casual players and begginers alike. The games flaws only become apparent when you actually realize how big of an issue they are. The great thing about the issues is that they are not design flaws, and need only be fixed by the developers. With the game still being fairly new and the developers working steadily, I believe Chivalry will only become better over time and is well worth every penny. For an indie game, it is far better than most of the garbage we get nowadays and never ceases to amaze in every way. If you're into this kind of game, you won't regret buying it.

With 1003 hours in game (playing pretty much since the beginning off and on), overall I have to give this game a positive review, but with a few caveats.  Why the caveats?  Well, the official servers are, and have always been, a mess.  Even on PvE servers you get a LOT of griefing (just a few examples of this are people luring aggressive dinos to destroy your buildings etc, people dragging your sleeping body into the sea to drown you whilst you are logged out or people building foundations near to your base so that you can't expand at all), they're also VERY laggy quite often.  As to PvP servers, they seem to have attracted very toxic PvPers, a quick look through the discussions and you will quickly read about mega tribes cheating etc, or the age old problem of killing new players the second they spawn, before they can even get started.
After those caveats you're probably wondering why still the positive review?  Well, basically I am reviewing the game itself, NOT the servers.  Pretty much the entire time I have been playing I have either rented my own unofficial servers, or have hosted them myself for my family to play on together.  Sometimes the rented ones have been terrible, with bad lag etc, and this is the exact same problem that the official servers have, hosts overselling them to the point of them been rubbish.  There are plenty of unofficial servers out there though with a good community playing on them (including nice clustered servers where you can move between maps freely), along with the options of renting your own, hosting one yourself or even just playing single player.  Sure the game itself has some bugs, but these are continuously been worked on.  The state the game is in now has improved MASSIVELY upon the state it first entered Early Access in.  Sure it won't run at all well on anything low end hardware wise but that's just the march of progress pushing as always.  It's the very paradigm of PC gaming.
Another caveat I am going to give is the lack of any real story or structured content.  This really is a game that is best played with other people where the players make the story and the content themselves, a sandbox if you will.  You have to put a lot into the game to get any real enjoyment out of it, setting yourself goals, challenges etc.
As to the price, well I'm reviewing the game not the price.  Would I pay nearly £50 for the condition the game is currently in?  No, but luckily I got it during EA.  Wait for a sale to get it, there are plenty of them.
TLDR; To get the most out of this game you need to find a good unofficial server, with a good community on it, or set up your own.  Wait for a sale to purchase.  It's a sandbox game, it doesn't spoon feed you story or lead you through the content.

Chivalry is a game unlike any other. It holds elements of the Mount and blade series, and other such medievel settings, however it is not a vast world like Mount and blade. Chivalry sets place somewhere in the medievel times (duh) and has it's own little story about how mason is this elite group, but then betrays their king. Nobody cares about the story anyways.
You play in different servers, with a few different game modes. The first and most noticable one is team objective, which lets you do different things like storming a castle to kill a king, which is player controlled, push a wagon to enemy lines, and various other objectives.
then we have some basic game modes like team deathmatch, free for all, capture the flag, and duel. Duel being very interesting to certain people who likes the one on one experience.
The combat in Chivalry is unlike any other combat system you have experience i feel. You are looking through mainly a first person perspective, but you are allowed to change it to third person, however i would not recommend this, since a lot of the charm is in getting in close and personal to your enemy, instead of being some hovering camera. As you fight your opponent you have different moves to your disposition depending on the weapon you are using, but mainly these are: a normal horizontal swipe, stab, overhead, kick, and a possibility to feint to trick your opponent. However feinting is frowned upon since people are casul.
You have a wide arsenal of weapons, from spears, daggers, longswords, bows, crossbows, throwing knives, shield, and so on. Every weapon has an unique feel to them, and allows you to master every weapon specifilly, by learning the range, speed, and other factors that will determine your profiency in combat.
All in all, i heavily recommend this game. My review does not give this game the honor it deserves, and it is a game you should experience for yourself. If i were to score the game i'd give it a 8/10, as it is not perfect, but i enjoy playing it way too much.

Okay, but seriously now. Warframe is a third person shooter set in the far future, long after human civilisation as we know it today, after the fall of a highly advanced human empre known as the Orokin, with Earth ruined by giant genetically altered trees of Orokin origin, and the solar system embroiled in constant conflict. On one side is the Grineer, an army of clones originally used as slaves by the Orokin suffering from genetic deterioration that has resulted in hereditary psychosis and a reliance on cybernetics. On another is the Corpus - a human faction that claims Orokin ancestry that worships money and seeks profit through conflict and any other possible means without concern for morality. In the third corner is the Infested, a sentient hive-mind virus that was created by the Orokin as a weapon (The Orokin were total♥♥♥♥♥♥♥that did a lot of very bad things, in case you couldn't tell by this point) that infects organic matter and twists it into nightmarish abominations that threatens to over-run the entire solar system if not kept in check. Other factions are also creeping into the picture, shadows of an Old War that little is known about.
The Tenno - the players - fight a gureilla war on all fronts to prevent any one side from gaining too much ground while more permanent solutions are not yet available.
Warframe has a tonne of content that is still being added to by the developers. A lot of the game focuses around very fast movement as you control the Warframes - basically like character classes, but all of them are Space-Ninja-Wizard-Warriors that have their own unique abilities. You also have an extremely large choice of primary, secondary and melee weapons, cosmetic options out the wazoo and the entire game is free to play. Like actually free to play - very little is hidden behind paid transactions and you can even trade the premium currency (Platinum) between players in exchange for other things in trading.
The only things that actually require Platinum are a lot of the cosmetic items (not even all of them - there are cosmetic items that look quite good that don't require Platinum) and inventory slots, which is a pretty standard idea in F2P games. Everything else you can get fairly easily with some time.
People do complain about 'the grind' but the game offers many ways to mitigate the grind, and while your weapons and warframes have build times you can easily occupy the time by doing other things and queueing up other builds - you can have as many Foundry items running simultaneously as you like. For that matter, the star chart is very large and you'll always have some other goal to work towards for a good couple of hundred hours or more, easily. And working through those missions will probably be quite fun, as the game features pretty satisftying gunplay and many ways to look and feel really cool while cutting your way through legions of enemies.
I will say one word of warning in that the game does not explain itself very well, leading to a pretty rocky new-player experience if you don't have a lot of personal initiative. For where to acquire items, what warframe powers do, and many other bits of information, you should definitely check the wiki:
It is also worth noting that your real power comes from your mods - the things you slot into your equipment - rather than your equipment itself. Even the starting rifle can handle high level content with the right mods, but even the 'best' weapon in the game won't help you if you don't equip and upgrade your mods as you go. This is a common stumbling block and is something the game fails to explain adequitely, so definitely keep that in mind.
If you want a third person shooter that oozes style, Warframe is definately worth a try. The entry cost is literally zero, after all!

After over 1000 hours of play and spending well over £100 on a Founder's Package and several Prime Access packs, I can safely say that this game will get it's hooks in you and once it does it's not letting go, even when I take breaks from the game due to burnout(more on that later) I still think about this game and returning to it. This game's update cycle has been a journey, from a very basic third person shooter with rudimentary and tacked on parkour to this fast paced, frantic off the walls looter shooter, it has been a very interesting ride. DE keeps this game updated frequently, one of the reasons why so many people stay, and are always trying to pump new life into this game.
Two issues you might want to be aware of before you play: The new player experience is really dull, you start with mostly crap gear, barely any money or resources and it will take you quite a while to get anywhere in this game without friends, especially without friends who have been playing for a long time as they can hook you up with some good mods and some plat(Platinum, the game's premium currency) to get yourself going. The last one, at least for me, is that this game can cause some serious burnout as this game is very farmy, you will spend HOURS doing the same missions over and over and over again just to get one blueprint, or one component, or to farm a specific resource and that can wear down on you pretty hard after a while.
With all that said though, the best way to learn about this game is to try it for yourself as a picture is worth 1000 words, the game is free so all you're losing is time. Now if you'll excuse me, I'm gonna go stand in a relay for 2 hours showing off my Founder gear like I've got nothing better to do. Cheerio!

Clicker Heroes is undoubtedly one of the most unexpected hits of 2015. Following in the footsteps of games such as Progress Quest & Cookie Clicker, Clicker Heroes has expanded awareness of the progress genre and in the process redefined what a game can be.
Playsaurus manages to reduce the complexity of some of the most successful, time-proven, positive reinforcement loops in game design to create a highly addictive gaming experience that appears at first glance as a simple game about clicking your mouse a few times when your bored.
At first, that is exactly what you will do. Click. I have clicked over 250,000 times as of writing this review; but beneath the surface there is much more than that.
Fundamentally, Clicker Heroes is about progressing. How is progress defined? A resource called Hero Souls. There is a beauty to the simplicity of it. The more Hero Souls you have, the stronger you become. The stronger you become, the farther you can progress. The farther you progress, the more Hero Souls you can earn. Ad infinitum (to a degree).
This simple pattern of play, without a doubt, produces a sense of fleeting satisfaction; and because the hero souls cycle is self-reinforcing, it happens regularly enough to build in intensity over time. The different systems employed by this game work so well together that Clicker Heroes reaches World of Warcraft levels of addictive potential.
It will suck your life away, one "Ascension" at a time. At the end, it may even provide you with the opportunity for introspection and reflection on questions you have never asked yourself before. Questions like "What is the meaning of life?" and the corollary "What am I doing with mine?". Reaching the end of this game, if you ever do, will likely be a life-changing event (if for no other reason than you aren't playing Clicker Heroes 24/7 anymore). I know I for one want to go outside again. Is this game intentionally and truly evil? I don't believe so; but it warrants further study.
Oh, and it's completely free.

Let me start off by saying that I do recommend this game and that it IS fun (at least when you are playing with a few friends on a private server with a few things enhanced like breeding, farming, taming speeds and harvesting boost). The only reason I am downvoting it right now is because of the massive price hike, which when combined with the expensive $20 DLC makes this game cost $80 USD (For people like me in Australia, that is $105 which is price gouging to the nth degree for a game like this). It is not worth a $60USD pricetag in it's current state as a vanilla game.
Pros
-The game has a lot in it and progression is fair, there will be no shortage of things to do while you are making the long grind to get the best dinos and gear.
-The game has nice graphics, a lot of terrain variety and biodiversity, you will probably find yourself getting lost in its beautify before you get 2-shot by a lv 80 carno in the safest regions
-The game presents a decent pve challenge throughout your start, if you misjudge that Dilo or attack that Troodon without noticing the other 4 of them coming to swarm you then you will be in big trouble
Cons
-The price. I dunno why the developers doubled the cost but considering the cost of the DLC too I can only assume it is for greed. The developers had a kickstarter where people like us backed their project generously and funded their opportunity to do what they enjoy and make money doing it too, this is a VERY poor way of honouring the good will and generosity that was shown to them, not by rewarding the people who paid early but by punishing the people who didn't... Most of whom are our friends who wanted to join the party late.
-The lack of small-party presets. Yes it is great that you can change your settings to make the pace or difficulty of the game easier/harder but the game is clearly designed with large groups of people working together in mind. Many of the harder dinos take lots of difficult to make food and take days or weeks to tame, the same goes for breeding new dinos or farming or pretty much anything, unless you plan on being around for days on end to tame your one dino and to make sure it doesn't wake up or get eaten.  For those who do not want to play in a big tribe or only want a few friends on a private server be prepared to go through a lot of pain and text/ini file modification to make your  server friendly to having only a few people on.
-Unbalanced dinos. This really irks me personally but some of the dinos in Ark are very over/underpowered which makes playing the non "meta" dinos almost a total waste (Might as well noth bother with any low lv dino besides the Trike), Dinosaurs like Pachy's are useless from the getgo because of their overall poor stats and mechanics to other low level dinos like Trikes. After the sky creature nerf Dinos like the Pteranodon and Pelagornis are very weak and can hardly fly due to their really low stamina compared to almost all other flyers like the Argentavis, Quetzal and Tapejara (the Pelagornis saddle is such a high lv, why does it have such awful stamina??!!!). If you want diversity or to play the underdog in this game then be prepared to be punished for it.
-Icthyornis. Never in my life would I have ever imagined I would complain about a single creature in a game like this but the Icthyornis will terrorize low and high lv players alike. It will fly in a way which makes it nearly impossible to kill with any non-assault rifle projectile weapon (and even if you do it could take up to 12 crossbow shots to kill like mine did), it flies quickly and it will swoop down and eat WHOLE stacks of food which you can NEVER get back. Of all the things the developers have added this is by far the most cancerous thing alive. Beware 4 of them being mate boosted and migrating over you house.
-Making the game as bad as possible for new players. The Icthyornis stealing mechanic is just a solid example of the developers catering to the "pro survivalist" crowd, by adding in mechanics to make the game as hard as possible at the start for new players on a server, this skews the game even further in the direction of those with the most experience and who get the most progression first.
-Poor optimization. From my personal experience, if you want to play Ark then you need at least 16GB ram otherwise you will be experiencing visual glitches and total pc lockups every 5-30m, even then don't plan on running background programs that are ram-intensive.
All in All, it is a fun game, even more fun with friends but I do NOT recommend buying it for it's current pricetag, currently imbalanced game mechanics and poor optimization, only buy the game if it goes on a good steam sale or if they lower the price again.

Yes it is great that you can change your settings to make the pace or difficulty of the game easier/harder but the game is clearly designed with large groups of people working together in mind. Many of the harder dinos take lots of difficult to make food and take days or weeks to tame, the same goes for breeding new dinos or farming or pretty much anything, unless you plan on being around for days on end to tame your one dino and to make sure it doesn't wake up or get eaten.  For those who do not want to play in a big tribe or only want a few friends on a private server be prepared to go through a lot of pain and text/ini file modification to make your  server friendly to having only a few people on.
-Unbalanced dinos. This really irks me personally but some of the dinos in Ark are very over/underpowered which makes playing the non "meta" dinos almost a total waste (Might as well noth bother with any low lv dino besides the Trike), Dinosaurs like Pachy's are useless from the getgo because of their overall poor stats and mechanics to other low level dinos like Trikes. After the sky creature nerf Dinos like the Pteranodon and Pelagornis are very weak and can hardly fly due to their really low stamina compared to almost all other flyers like the Argentavis, Quetzal and Tapejara (the Pelagornis saddle is such a high lv, why does it have such awful stamina??!!!). If you want diversity or to play the underdog in this game then be prepared to be punished for it.
-Icthyornis. Never in my life would I have ever imagined I would complain about a single creature in a game like this but the Icthyornis will terrorize low and high lv players alike. It will fly in a way which makes it nearly impossible to kill with any non-assault rifle projectile weapon (and even if you do it could take up to 12 crossbow shots to kill like mine did), it flies quickly and it will swoop down and eat WHOLE stacks of food which you can NEVER get back. Of all the things the developers have added this is by far the most cancerous thing alive. Beware 4 of them being mate boosted and migrating over you house.
-Making the game as bad as possible for new players. The Icthyornis stealing mechanic is just a solid example of the developers catering to the "pro survivalist" crowd, by adding in mechanics to make the game as hard as possible at the start for new players on a server, this skews the game even further in the direction of those with the most experience and who get the most progression first.
-Poor optimization. From my personal experience, if you want to play Ark then you need at least 16GB ram otherwise you will be experiencing visual glitches and total pc lockups every 5-30m, even then don't plan on running background programs that are ram-intensive.
All in All, it is a fun game, even more fun with friends but I do NOT recommend buying it for it's current pricetag, currently imbalanced game mechanics and poor optimization, only buy the game if it goes on a good steam sale or if they lower the price again.

Ah Warframe.
A game where you are a space ninja with guns.
A game where it is much easier (and faster) to get around by jumping all over the place instead of sprinting.
A game where there is a surprising amount of customization options for you, you just have to realize that they are there.
I could go on like this, but Warframe deserves a better and more comprehensive review.
Not that I will be writing it.
Warframe is a game for those people who want a game without a clear end. If you enjoy playing games like Diablo or Borderlands after you finished the main storyline, you will find that Warframe is much like that.
Ofcourse, there are some key differences.
Warframe is a 3rd person mobility focused game. What this means, is that you will need to keep aware of your surroundings and keep moving constantly. If you fail to do either of these things, you will die if you have passed the introductory levels.
You can play each mission with strangers found via matchmaking, you can go into "friends only" mode or even "solo" mode. What this means is that if you do not feel like playing with other people, that is fine, toggle on solo mode and no one can join your game, nor will you be sent to another persons game. That Warframe even has this option when it is clearly meant to be played as a multiplayer game, is quite impressive.
I only intended to write a few lines recommending this game, but it seems I have overdone it a bit.
I can only say that I thoroughly enjoy this game, and that even if things take a long time to acquire without the use of the ingame currency, it is possible to have a good gaming experience without paying anything at all.

Warframe is a space ninja third-person shooter, hack n' slash co-op MMORPG, to summarise in one sentence .I've played Warframe almost since its launch and for a game that I've faithfully followed over the years, I can say that this is one of the best MMO experience out there. There are so many good things about this game but there are a few that I’d like to point out.
- Tons of weapons and Warframes!
Not just a bunch of similar looking objects with different stats, but many weapons in the game have its own unique mechanics that distinguishes itself from other weapons. Considering there are hundreds of weapons out right now, that's pretty damn impressive, and definitely a ton of fun to try them all out.
- The lore!
Since update 18, I can officially say that this game's lore IS one of the best things about this game and that it is executed remarkably well through a series unlockable quests. It's definitely a quality that you wouldn't expect of a F2P game that already nailed every other aspects right.
- The community
No online multiplayer game is ever a truly a great experience without a great community. It may be due to the cooperative nature of Warframe, but the player base is overall very friendly. Most importantly, the Devs always listen to its community and releases updates frequently with that in mind.
Overall, Warframe is definitely a game that I have enjoyed over the years. Sure, it’s a grind-heavy game and there are some stale moments in between the major updates, but when the update hits, it really hits home. 10/10, highly recommend!

Came back to this game after about 2 years, and I'm glad I did.
I quit cause the game was too grind-heavy and the core gameplay loop was kinda boring. Acquiring new weapons and frames was a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥and multiplayer was buggy as hell.
Now, the grind feels a lot less painful, the multiplayer just works and acquisition was relatively fast and you feel like progression is a product of playing, rather than the other way around.
They removed or improved systems that were a hindrance to the players and made the game truly feel like you were an OP space ninja.
The game isn't perfect though. The core gameplay loop HAS improved since then but it does get repetitive eventually. Some people will enjoy the grind, some people just want something specific, which will be extremely frustrating for many people, I feel.
I think warframe is more about the journey than the destination. If you're a fan of trying out new things, doing the same things over and over with a bunch of variety as to how you do that thing, or if you just have a lot of time on your hands and like killing things with a vast arsenal of weapons and space-ninja abilities, then I highly recommend this game.

I enjoyed minecraft when it first came out and this takes it to another level. Since the map is not randomly generated, the detail put in really shines through. There are so many caverns and areas to explore and an amazing amounts of dinosaurs to discover and tame.
As far as optimization goes, this game runs pretty poorly. Yes, it will run on a wide range of hardware but that's if you don't mind turning most of the detail settings off (and there is a huge difference between low and epic in this game). Even on a 1080ti this game struggles to hit 60fps constant at high to epic settings.
TLDR; despite having great gameplay, I currently cannot reccomend this game at this ridiculous price.
