Let me start off with this:
While this may be a problem for some, it may not be for others.
Warframe is a game that is based on a HUGE grinding system. To get almost anything valuable, you have to farm for materials and craft it. And even after you get all the materials, the crafting process may take from 12 hours to a full 3 days for the most valuable items. However, what this means is that the game, althought it may appear to be on the outside, is NOT pay to win. Almost everything can be gained from hard work and a little bit of luck. This lengthy process also leads to what feels like a big payoff. You've been grinding up materials and waiting for this amazing weapon to finish, and when you can finally click "Claim" you have a sense of accomplishment -- YOU worked hard for this, and YOU got a sweet rewards that YOU have been waiting for.
And now let me start with the pros.
This game is beautiful. Warframe is notorious for its sense of flair, and every environment and visual effect was designed with what seems to be painstaking effort. And even if you turn off a ton of the settings, the game still looks better than Minecraft.
There is something for almost everyone. Warframe includes several weapons for several play-styles. Then it includes mods to narrow down your play style. And then it includes the Warframes, which are basically like classes, to narrow it down even more. Want to be a stealthy ninja? Ash warframe is there for you. Want to be able to pick off your enemies from afar where they can't shoot at you if they can even see you coming? What's this? Oh, a nice deadly sniper rifle? Well isn't that just great. Wait, there are mods to make your sniper rifle 120% more deadly AND make it 100% silenced, even to enemies you are standing next to? Wow, you are about to become the deadliest, stealthiest player in the game. And you know you are, considering your warframe has mods and even special ablities too!
The movement system is great. And I mean the system that includes running and jumping. There are wall dashes, slides, 'bullet jumps' -- and while this may not seem like a lot, Warframe's environment is designed to help those who can't make full use of their movement arsenal, as well as to let those who know their stuff to show off.

In the beginning, you click. A lot. You click so much that you can't even believe it. And when you think you can't click anymore, the game says "Ascend..." So you do. Which just puts you back at the beginning, but with the souls of fallen heroes powering your click engine even further. So you click even more. And ascend again, even more powerful.
But the souls are just a new form of currency, allowing you to summon ancient forces to do your bidding. Making your spells stronger, your gold piles larger. Turning each click into nuclear hellfire that pushes you further. But no matter how far you push, the monsters always overpower you, drawing you into a stalemate that you must escape. Only to repeat your mistakes.
Then you meet Siyalitas. He shows you another way. "Click not, and I shall unleash my power" Then the idle times begin, allowing you to gather hundreds, then thousands of souls to feed the ancient's hunger. You learn that your weakest heroes will become the strongest. Clicking becomes only a last resort against an unstoppable foe. You pass hundreds of levels, knowing there are thousands more to conquer. This is where I find myself. Is this my new life now?
I basically haven't stop playing for a month and I've barely scratched the surface. But everything now is just math. Which hero will help me the most? Is my DPS higher with souls or a fed ancient? How high can the numbers get? It feels like exporation, but is it?
Am I still having fun? I'm not sure. I know that I did for a long while. That's more than I can ask from a free game.

Clicker Heroes
Another game people will either love (for unknown reasons) or simply disregard due to its nature.
You click on static monsters and each click will deal damage. When the monster dies it drops gold. You accumulate gold and purchase upgrades which makes your clicking stronger. Monsters only vary in visual display and have no abilities or resists. Only an ever increasing pool of health which is depenant on the zone level. Killing 10 monsters in a zone level will open up the next zone level. Every 10 zone levels there are Bosses. Special monsters with much more health which only give you a timewindow of 30 seconds to beat before they restet to full health and the time window starts anew. You must kill these in order to progress and can see them as "benchmarks" to check if you are ready or not.
Apart from active play the game will simulate your progress (measured by your DPS, not clicking damage) even if you are offline tho you cannot progress passively (yet). Entering the next zone is an active thing but if you are missing out on gold to purchase that next upgrade you can let it run in offline mode for an hour or two and continue from there.
Clicking is only your first layer tho. You quickly open up new heroes which provide you with your second layer of gameplay. DPS aka Damage Per Second. These heroes deal damage over time on their own. Even if you stop clicking damage will continue to pour in. So DPS is kind of like a passive buff for your game. Apart from buying heroes to become active (first purchase to level 1) you can continue leveling them up to make their DPS stronger in turn enhancing your killing power of the monsters on the screen.
In addition each hero has a set of abilities which unlock at certain levels (10, 25, 50, 75 and 100) providing better capabilities or ACTIVE ABILITIES
There are 9 active abilities you can trigger at any point. Each one has an effect duration (usually 30 seconds) and a cool-down preventing you from spamming them. Effects range from more click damage to more gold per kill to support buffs and even a permanent damage buff. Unlocking these abilities and timing their use will become a key part of defeating higher level Bosses
There will be a point where you ll run into a "wall". Monsters will become so powerfull that it takes a long time to kill them and bosses will eventually become so mighty that you will be unable to beat them even if you use all your active abilities. This is the point where you use the "Ascension" feature for the first time.
At first it doesnt sound like anything anybody in his right mind would do. "Creates a new universe, much like the current one. This will restart your game and you will receive XXX Hero Souls".
Wait.....It just resets my game to level one....all gold and hero levels are gone and I simply start over? LAME!!!!!!
But wait....whats these hero souls then?
Hero Souls are kind of a permanent currency coming through an ascension. Each one you have banked (read....showing in your display) will increase your damage by 10%. Its accumulative so if you have 5 your whole damage will increase by 50%. With 10 of these babies you ll DOUBLE your damage. So even tho you have to go through all the levels you beat beforehand a second time.....THIS time will be far easier and much quicker to get to the point where you grinded to a stop before and continue past that point.
And thats not all. As a permanent currency they open up the market for a special sort of heroes. The Ancients.
What makes these heroes special is that they also....just like Hero Souls transfer through an ascension and you gonna keep them. There is a whole list of them and each one buffs your game in a special way. Purchasing them costs hero souls. Leveling them up costs hero souls and you ll need to start thinking about what will give you the most bang for your buck (read....do you keep the HS banked or do you invest them?)
You ll soon realize that many ancients support each other so getting the "right mix" of ancients can massively increase your efficiency at going through the treadmill (ascend and go through all those levels again).
Now the game shows its true color. With all these features unlocked you are ready for the neverending(!) "management and improvement of resources" to push further on a new try which makes so many other genres successfull.
4x
RTS
RPGs
ARPGs
Economy Simulations
If you enjoy any of these genres chances are you ll LOVE clicker heroes. Its free to play so what do you have to lose?
Me...I find myself booting it up almost every day and even tho I ascended more then a hundred times already it doesnt really get old. The asciension is more like a "test run" by now to see if you made the correct choices on spending your hero souls and which ancients to get and level. Its this "game within game" which makes me come back....certainly not the clicking. Theres some form of "grinding" to get enough HS but many games have this so not really a problem.
Its a most simple game and the fact that its so addictive is baffling in itself.
For myself I can say that its been a great way to "waste" my freetime so far. I dont regret picking it up :)

Because this game is getting negative criticism due to it's price alteration I thought that I'd make a review to help people understand why this is and why it's not a negative thing.
Ark: Survival evolved came out on pc in 2015 as an early access title and because the game wasn't finished starting at a full retail price would be madness so they went with 27 euros (or so). Back then people like me who bought the game weren't certain if the game would ever be finished or if it would ever meet our expectations so the price was right at that time. We also had to play a game infested with bugs, glitches and other exploitable/gamebreaking issues.
RIGHT NOW it is going to enter its full release which means that it basically becomes a new game so adjusting the price is FAIR. up until now they have updated the game continuously and even added MORE than they said they would. They even set up a program for modders and other creators to make maps for Ark and get them into the official game and as of the ragnarok dlc update you can also unlock/craft items and fight/tame monsters that were previously locked behind the scorched earth dlc paywall! FOR FREE!
Ark: Survival evolved is easily one of the best early access titles I've bought (second after subnautica) and is a prime example of how Early Access should be done. You can play this game for hundreds of hours and still not get bored of it if you know how to keep yourself busy in a sandbox world. So instead of only 20 hours of gameplay (most games these days only clock about that amount of time for the same price) you can play hundreds of hours and explore 3 giant maps and chances are more free maps will be added in the future aswell as paid dlc's.
So are hundreds of hours of fun worth the 60 euro pricetag? one word: YES
Sidenote: I may only have 130 hours on this game on pc but I have to remind you that I bought this one ps4 aswell since I wanted to introduce more friends to this game via console where I probably have a few hundred hours more playtime.

Yes, it's another one of those grindfest games... but setup in a different way. Unlike an MMORPG you may be used to, this is 3rd person, p2p, 4 player co-op created by those people who made Dark Sector. It sort of plays like Borderlands in space with the addition of crafting the weapons and tailoring them to your liking. You level your weapons, your frames, your account, and the game continues to develop. I'm looking forward to if they do more cinematic quests because many quests are a bit dull. Some missions can get repetetive, but as said, GRIND FEST. Grind this missions X times to craft Z weapon. Its backstory is about as complicated as the Marvel universe. ONE nice thing though is that this game is NOT pay to win, Theye make it where that even if you buy and item, you still have to work to level it up. Recently Digital Extremes has added a few other PvP related things to do. AND on a random note... this game has its own annual convention... like Payday2 does. That's saying something right there. I just wish they'd make more merchandise for fans to buy...
[After Plains of Eidolon update 22]
The Warframe at Digital Extremes has hit it out of the park with this update. It definitely adds more content to work for and work with and adds some more layers to the game. They've even confirmed work on making more areas like this update on other planets in the game. Can't wait until the next one drops. This game is definitely one that's entertaining.

Warframe
You become a space ninja that can kill anything
Pros:
+ FREE
+ Good graphics
+ Runs well
+ Good Music
+ Multiple enemy factions to fight
+ Lots of different kinds of weapons (axes, daggers, swords, bows, shurikens, maces, rifles, sniper rifles, grenede lauchers, pistols, SMGs, bows, crossbows, staves, boomerangs, glaives, katanas, laser beams, etc.)
+ Has some cinematic story quests that are great
+ Some interesting side characters
+ Varied environments that are randomly generated so almost every mission is slightly different
+ Fun third person shooter gameplay
+ Parkour allows for lots of mobility
+ Can have companions that include cat-things, dog-things, and robots
+ Frequently updated, varying from quite frequent small ones to every so often big ones
+ Tons of custimizations (visually) for your warframes, companions, ships, and weapons.
+ Tons of custimizations for warframes, weapons, and companions with mods
+ Pretty friendly community for a free game
+ Interesting future sci-fi setting
+ Multiple mission types
+ Can use a space jetpack
+ Everyting you can get for free just by playing (well almost everything, some things have been "retired", you can still get them just not by playing, you have to play to get things to trade to buy the retired things)
+ FREE
Cons:
- PVP isn't the best (mainly a PVE game, PVP its just a bonus here, so don't bother if you play only PVP )
- Does require grinding. If you do not enjoy grinding, skip it.
- Minor bugs (some examples are: sometimes doors don't open, falling under textures/out of map, etc.)

When new stuff comes out: Check it, do it, get some lore bits, get some shinny new mechanic with huge flaws, everyone plays it for a week, DE never fixes it and moves on to make another heavily marketed failure, everyone abandons that mechanic then moves back to grind more for actually working stuff. Hence, more grind for prime stuff/rare mods to sell them for platinum. (Limbo, Titania etc.)

Enjoy the game. I can't enjoy it anymore.

If you're new to Ark and seeing all of the bad reviews take a look at this one before you read them and I think you'll find it helpful, I do have 1600 hours. Now before you say anything about my recommendation. Overall yes I do recommend this game, very very much. To start with Pros because everyone does. This game, despite what half of the people say, is very good. It's very solid, it's very fun, it will eat your life in a good way. I have been through the ups and downs of this game and it's Dev's and I still can support it despite the bad.
1)Graphics. They are fantastic, beautiful landscapes (if you have a more than decent pc) and wonderful terrain to explore which you never will because there's so much!
2)Gameplay. This game has so many mechanics never before implemented in other games it's really unique and good. The FPS gameplay and controls are.. ehh clunky but you can ride dinos, swim dinos, fly dinos, fly with scifi Tek gear. In other words, quantity over quality in this case. There are so many mechanics of gameplay and factors that you will find the OKAY way they work acceptable at least. Taming is really fun, riding your tamed animals is a blast. When you go to unofficial servers it changes. Those are where the chill people are at that are sick of Hackers and PVE and toxic players. But in all reality every game has toxicity so Ark isn't special when it comes to that. Expect toxic people when playing online but I find most players are adult and mature. Most.

There will be mistakes, but they have been fixed. The game breaking ones at least. People don't seem to understand that when they play an alpha game, they are playing a game as it's being built.
If you choose to live in a house that is currently being built. Why would you complain that someone is hammering a nail in and that it is too loud and you can't watch TV? Because you forgot you agreed to live in a house that is being built. Because you liked it. Players don't understand this or forget and blame the Dev's for their Toaster of a computer to play this game.

You might say that makes sense but it doesn't if you know anything about marketing. No one is going to buy Ark the day of release if they make it 60 bucks the day of. In two words: Melee Counterstrike (plus arrows, of course).
Like chess, it's simple to learn but difficult to master. There's a ton of depth to what is otherwise a simple set of game mechanics (3 types of attacks: stab which has the farthest reach, overhead when attacks from above and does the most damage, and horizontal slash which is the easiest to land and can hit people to the side of you, plus parrying/blocking strikes and dodging/strafing), just like how in CS you're basically just pointing your cursor and shooting people, yet there's also the matter of crouching to move silently, effective use of cover, and being able to accurate hit people and score headshots while not getting killed yourself. Yet even here, the gameplay has even more depth to it than CS, and being able to effectively parry enemies' attacks and not get hit while at the same time being able to hit them without getting parried or blocked is very challenging. The challenge is what makes it fun for me though, and what keeps me coming back for more. The weapons in the game are also very balanced for the most part, there is a lot of variety in the weapons each class can use.
Just like CS you can quickly jump into a game and be instantly in the action, either playing many rounds for a long time or just playing a couple to kill some time and then dropping it. There are also several different game types, ranging from FFA and Team Deathmatch to team objective-based game types.
So really, the best comparison I can make in terms of gameplay is to Counterstrike, just with swords/axes/spears/etc (with associated close-combat mechanics) and (cross)bows. I highly recommend this, as I have found it to be a great alternative when taking a break from Natural Selection 2 (which you should also get lol).

Not interested in Tribe wars and cautious about buying Ark as a single player? There's plenty for a solo player here.
At over a thousand hours of gameplay I still haven't run out of things I'd like to try in this game. I've played mostly solo and so haven't even tackled some of the greater challenges yet, such as tek tier/boss fights ... but that just goes to show that casual single players can also find a lot of enjoyment in Ark.
As a solo explorer in single player games or as a host for a private server you have a ton of cheats at your command to go full out sandbox buildermode where you can take advantage of a ton of cool mods and maps to completely customise your gameplay, or you can rule your own tribe/server as a legit Admin and play with friends at customised rates.
Official PvE servers offer you a chance to work together with other tribes online, and Primitive servers or those using the total conversion mod Primitive Plus change the game to a more rustic, relaxed version of Ark. Yes, ofc online servers come with the potential for trolls, but that's sadly to be expected and I've managed to have great luck with the servers I've played on finding friendly, cooperative players wherever I've settled.
Official Pvp servers are a whole different kind of fun. Realistic mindset required. Yes, you will die. Many times (if they can catch you). Yes you will be raided and have your base levelled and all valuables stolen (if they can find you). If you're building out in the open as a small tribe, there will always be a bigger tribe *or a crazy solo lady armed to the teeth* ready to take what they want. I'd recommend staying small and out of the way, with multiple bases/spawn points and item caches. Being creative and compact with base designs to stay hidden can be a fun challenge, and guerilla style pvp can have very lucrative rewards with some luck and good timing.
All arguments over bugs and paid dlc aside, I think the hours played by the average purchaser speak for themselves. I read a lot of hate for the game in the comments, posted by people with more hours played than myself. There is enough to do in this game, even in its current state, to totally justify buying it imo. Ofc if you can grab it on sale, even better ;)

I actually played this game originally on Kongregate, so I was pleased to see it on here. And you know what? The dev STILL does in-app purchases correctly. No nagging, no baiting, and best of all, you can get the in-game purchasable cash (rubies) through normal gameplay - so nothing is locked out, only slowed. This has impressed me so much that I dropped a fiver on rubies now that I've got money - hopefully this encourages other developers to follow the same model.
As for the gameplay, let's be honest - it's a clicker. It has some neat pictures and neat little stories, but those get old after the first few times. The real draw is the interesting rebirth/ascension/etc. system that lets you tweak your game in a direction that fits your gameplay style - you spend your ascension currency (hero souls) on various "ancients" that have in-game effects - anything from boosting the effect of a particular skill to a flat DPS boost. Sure, there are ideal builds, but if you're into doing everything by the numbers... well. I pity you. :p

Short story: the immersion in the game is mind blowing. The world of Ark seems real, alive, true. Depth is tremendous, content is huge. Ark is one of the most if not the most addictive, intense and epic game I have ever played — and I played many.
Long story: Ark Survival Evolved is a mix between Monster Hunter, Minecraft and of course survival games. But its appealing universe, its brilliant gameplay, its unique mechanisms push it a step above all other games. Ark’s huge content makes it the GTA online of survival games.
After 85 hours I have just scratched the surface of the dinosaur. 3 official worlds (plus 1 DLC so far). 3 modes of playing: single player, coop multiplayer and PvP. Not to mention the mods (including 1 official) which expand the already tremendous game length.
Deep games are incredibly hard for developers to balance. Ark has solved this headache, at least in solo: the player can tune his universe. Alpha dinos are invincible ? Turn them into regular dinos. Eels make the sea unplayable ? Remove them. Grinding is tedious and slow ? Boost the harvest rate.
The difference between a good RPG / adventure / survival game and an awesome one is end-game content. In this area Ark delivers a formidable challenge with bosses and ascendency.
Now why are Steam reviews mixed ? Why so much rage and whining in the forums ? Because of spoiled brats. Before developing this point, let me say that this loud negative community is a small minority of Ark players. How many reviews on Steam ? Around 116 000. How many Ark copies sold ? About 3 million. So less than 4% of players have reviewed the game on Steam. The loud minority vs the silent majority is common in politics. See Brexit or American elections.
So the spoiled brats use bomb review, a common practice on Steam. What enrages them ? Devs sold a paid DLC before finishing the main game. Spoiled brats couldn’t understand that Studio Wildcard lost 40 million $ in a lawsuit and needed fresh money. But spoiled brats care only about their passion ! Even if they don’t recommend this passion they played 500+ hours…
What else ? Game doesn’t run smoothly on highest graphics details. Spoiled brats are furious ! They have the most powerful PC and demand the epic details ! That makes them sick to have only gorgeous graphics. They want EPIC graphics !
Recently price has been raised because final release is coming. Spoiled brats can’t accept it ! Even though devs have always said prices would go up at the end of Early Access. Even though Ark was at 13 bucks during the Steam Summer sales. Even though they already own the game. They cry the game is not finished and so not worth 60. Well I prefer a raw diamond than a polished plastics.
To sum-up, don’t listen to the spoiled brats and buy Ark during the next discount. And even at 60, the game is so great that it’s worth the money.

Ah Warframe.
A game where you are a space ninja with guns.
A game where it is much easier (and faster) to get around by jumping all over the place instead of sprinting.
A game where there is a surprising amount of customization options for you, you just have to realize that they are there.
I could go on like this, but Warframe deserves a better and more comprehensive review.
Not that I will be writing it.
Warframe is a game for those people who want a game without a clear end. If you enjoy playing games like Diablo or Borderlands after you finished the main storyline, you will find that Warframe is much like that.
Ofcourse, there are some key differences.
Warframe is a 3rd person mobility focused game. What this means, is that you will need to keep aware of your surroundings and keep moving constantly. If you fail to do either of these things, you will die if you have passed the introductory levels.
You can play each mission with strangers found via matchmaking, you can go into "friends only" mode or even "solo" mode. What this means is that if you do not feel like playing with other people, that is fine, toggle on solo mode and no one can join your game, nor will you be sent to another persons game. That Warframe even has this option when it is clearly meant to be played as a multiplayer game, is quite impressive.
I only intended to write a few lines recommending this game, but it seems I have overdone it a bit.
I can only say that I thoroughly enjoy this game, and that even if things take a long time to acquire without the use of the ingame currency, it is possible to have a good gaming experience without paying anything at all.

Yes, it's another one of those grindfest games... but setup in a different way. Unlike an MMORPG you may be used to, this is 3rd person, p2p, 4 player co-op created by those people who made Dark Sector. It sort of plays like Borderlands in space with the addition of crafting the weapons and tailoring them to your liking. You level your weapons, your frames, your account, and the game continues to develop. I'm looking forward to if they do more cinematic quests because many quests are a bit dull. Some missions can get repetetive, but as said, GRIND FEST. Grind this missions X times to craft Z weapon. Its backstory is about as complicated as the Marvel universe. ONE nice thing though is that this game is NOT pay to win, Theye make it where that even if you buy and item, you still have to work to level it up. Recently Digital Extremes has added a few other PvP related things to do. AND on a random note... this game has its own annual convention... like Payday2 does. That's saying something right there. (Don't let my PC hours mislead you, I have played Ark on PC and PS4 combined for well over 1000 hours, my friends were on console so I was mostly there and I played single player on PC.)
First, I would like to say that compared to when I first started playing this game, there is almost three times the amount of content in the game. Almost every AAA game that I have played I may play it for 100-200 hours and then never touch it again because I did everything that there was to do in the game. With Ark though, I can potentially create my own experience interacting with other people, customizing my gameplay experience through experience/tame/harvest rates | engram points per level | mods | unofficial servers. And if I wanted to keep it simple, I could go for the hardcore grind on the official servers.
I've gotten more value out of Ark alone than I have any AAA $60 title that I have played in sheer consistent play-time alone. They have done a great job updating, and I'm proud of them for not becoming one of the early access games that never leave early access. While I thoroughly believe that this game is in one of my top 3 favorite games to play right now, it, like any other game, isn't without issues.
1) I truly believe that they should have waited until full release to raise the price. I believe that Ark is worth $60 and I am glad that I bought it when it didn't cost that much, but I wouldn't have had any qualms with paying $60 for the game for the amount of enjoyment that I've gotten out of it. People should have had an announcement for a last minute opportunity to purchase the game for early access price.
2) The Official Servers still have a lot of unchecked cheating that needs to be addressed before the game reaches full release, or it will significantly decrease my respect for Wildcard. Also, if they have in-fact been giving out high-end items to streamers to help them win wars (Read that in another review below), then I will immediately lose all respect for them and uninstall the game on principle regardless of how much I enjoy it. I haven't seen any proof of that though.
3) The DLC is a tough one in my book, because I don't mind the $20 price since it adds a new map with a way different way to play, but I can see where that would bother a lot of people. It is not necessary to enjoy the game though, because you can still use the DLC items, you just can't go get them yourself. So if you don't want to fork out an extra $20 for the DLC, then you won't really be missing out (UNLESS you play on a server where the Alpha tribe has Wyverns and grief people with them)
Overall, I think they could have handled things in a much better way, but I would honestly recommend this game for anyone wanting to play a fun survival game with your friends. If you are prepared for the sense of accomplishment you get when you finally tame a large dinosaur, and get your base built up, then I would say dive in it's worth it. But if you don't want to be hassled because the Official servers are rough starting out, then you may be better off hosting a dedicated or private server for you and your friends because people have the ability to grief you on PvE servers as well. Decide for yourself girls and boys, reviews can only tell you so much.

Pros:
+ Extremely smooth and fast-paced movement and combat; you can cover ground really quickly with a double jump and flips, take no fall damage, and have a vertical jump that can cover several stories.  You can shoot, reload, or cast powers while doing almost all of this
+ Beautiful art style across the board.  Warframes, weapons, and tilesets all look great (especially newer ones)
+ Highly customizable loadouts (cosmetically), there's tons of skins, accessories and colors to choose from.    FashionFrame (customizing your warframes to look exactly how you want), is joked about as the true endgame for a reason.
+ Highly customizable loadouts (performance-wise).  The amount of warframes, weapons, and mods makes for many different ways to play.
+ Solid F2P business model overall
Cons:
- Grind is the main gameplay, if you find repetitive missions boring I would recommend staying away from this game
- Some stuff is just better than others (notably mods and weapons).  This is inevitable to an extent, but there's always room for improvement.
- Since the game is F2P there is a lot of chances to pay to skip progression, notably that new weapons and warframes will take 12 hours to 3 days to craft, which can be rushed by using platinum.  There are a lot of great things to buy with in-game currency from the market but some of them are also ripoffs
- Overwhelming new player experience.  How to get things and the modding system are confusing at first, and the lack of power you have starting out is pretty discouraging
I know that's a lot of cons, but overall the game is a solid 8/10 to me.  Definitely would recommend.

600hrs later into this Hell of a game, I think it's time I write my thoughts on this game.
It's definitely not the easiest thing to get into. From the fact that this game has a notorious tendency to not explain the mechanics of anything beyond the absolute basics and the fact it
throws you into the wide open world after the first quest line with no sense of direction... Yeah, it's a beast you gotta learn to tackle.
But once you get past that initial barrier, you find yourself chest-deep into a game that just keeps hooking you in. New weapons to try, new warframes to add to your arsenal. This game encourages you to try everything, which is an interesting concept in massively-multiplayer games like this.
Definitely find yourself a SMALL clan to roll with. Personally what's kept me with this game so fervently is the social aspect I've gotten out of it. Even if a burn-out is inevitable with a game like this (it's essentially a diablo-esque gear grind, honestly) you'll find that your time with this game was exciting and worth the thrill of it.
And hey, don't forget the best part about this game: The
endgame, Fashionframe. ;)

Optimization is indie beta level, not AAA

I normally don't review games, but after reading the ones below I felt I should.   I've currently played this game for over 1400 hours.  To say I've been a little addicted at times is probably an understatement.  I do not play on official servers so I won't comment on what happens there.  In truth I tend to play with a just a few people on a private server or solo.  There was times that I had serious problems with the optimization, but I've seen that get better over time until now I have no problems at all.   Was I thrilled about paying for an expansion while the game was in early access?  Not really, however, I found the expansion to be worth the money.    Do I have problems soloing in the game?  Not at all.    The lack of engram points are an issue if you play straight vanilla, but why would you do that?  This game , like Skyrim, has so many mods out there that can make this game into whatever you want.    The worlds are beautiful and the game is challenging.  I find that while the developers may not address everything that people want (what game does), they do address a lot.   Basically if you want the game to be everything and do everything you want you'll be disappointed in this game and any other game you play.  If you want a beautiful sandbox that can be a challenge to survive in and that has a ton of options in the way of mods to let you play the game your way, then this may be the game for you.
Now I see people are complaining about the price.  Would I pay $60 for this game? No,  but I wouldn't pay that for any game.  I'd wait until the price dropped and then buy it.  However, I won't complain because of what Wildcard is charging.
Do people  REALLY think the game when released would stay at the Early Access price?   This has been on Steam for a very long time and everyone has had the opportunity to buy it while it was at early access prices or even on sale.  I feel people shouldn't be crying now because they didn't purchase it while it was cheaper and  they now have to pay a more expensive price or wait for the prices to drop.  For those that did purchase it in early access and are complaining about the price, why does it matter to you what the price is, you already own it.
To sum it up, would I recommend the game. Definately!  Does it have room to improve? Sure, and I hope they do.  Is Wildcard releasing an unfinished game?  In my book No.  This has been one of the best early access experince I've had (and I've played many).

Chivalry is an amazing game and deffintly worth the full price in my opinion. The game has several fantastic modes ranging from FFA, team deathmatch and my favorite, team objective. Team Objective is simple yet a blast, one team has to complete objectives usually over 3 stages such as burn the enemy farm, then push a battering ram to the gates. The other team must then defend those objectives and stop the enemy. There are 4 classes all with varried unlockable things, the man at arms, med arm, med speed, nice weapons. Archer - self explanitory - range weapons. Vanguard, - pole arms - knight, heavy armor, heavy weapons. The weapons are unlocked through the process of getting kills, each unlock requiring more kills then the last. There is a nice variation of weapons and many choices to choose from such as axes, maces, javalins, cross bows, bows, 2h swords, halberds and much more. All for your slicing pleasure.
The game is fantastic, mostly balanced except that the pole arms of the vanguard do much damage and usually one hit their unfortunate targets also with alot of m1 spammers that enjoy no skill in their methods of striking. Otherwise I'd reccomend this game for its full price, but if you can get on a sale then its a must get in my opinion.

I normally don't review games, but after reading the ones below I felt I should.   I've currently played this game for over 1400 hours.  To say I've been a little addicted at times is probably an understatement.  I do not play on official servers so I won't comment on what happens there.  In truth I tend to play with a just a few people on a private server or solo.  There was times that I had serious problems with the optimization, but I've seen that get better over time until now I have no problems at all.   Was I thrilled about paying for an expansion while the game was in early access?  Not really, however, I found the expansion to be worth the money.    Do I have problems soloing in the game?  Not at all.    The lack of engram points are an issue if you play straight vanilla, but why would you do that?  This game , like Skyrim, has so many mods out there that can make this game into whatever you want.    The worlds are beautiful and the game is challenging.  I find that while the developers may not address everything that people want (what game does), they do address a lot.   Basically if you want the game to be everything and do everything you want you'll be disappointed in this game and any other game you play.  If you want a beautiful sandbox that can be a challenge to survive in and that has a ton of options in the way of mods to let you play the game your way, then this may be the game for you.
Now I see people are complaining about the price.  Would I pay $60 for this game? No,  but I wouldn't pay that for any game.  I'd wait until the price dropped and then buy it.  However, I won't complain because of what Wildcard is charging.
Do people  REALLY think the game when released would stay at the Early Access price?   This has been on Steam for a very long time and everyone has had the opportunity to buy it while it was at early access prices or even on sale.  I feel people shouldn't be crying now because they didn't purchase it while it was cheaper and  they now have to pay a more expensive price or wait for the prices to drop.  For those that did purchase it in early access and are complaining about the price, why does it matter to you what the price is, you already own it.
To sum it up, would I recommend the game. Definately!  Does it have room to improve? Sure, and I hope they do.  Is Wildcard releasing an unfinished game?  In my book No.  This has been one of the best early access experince I've had (and I've played many).

I'll say this, the game is buggy but all in all you can play 1669 hours in it (going off my own hours) the last 500 hours only clocked the last month, There is so much content, so many things to do and play with and explore especially with the modding community, if I didnt already own it, I would be more then willing to pay the new price for it, simply because in comparison to most AAA games that are 60 bucks content wise they don't match up...
I'll use Resident Evil 7 as my example... I know tons of people who picked that up played through it once and now its doomed to their shelf, most AAA games are very directive and have a very limited amount of content when in comparison to a game like Ark.
As far as people complaining its buggy, well no more so then Skyrim or hec any Bethesda game ever released... Dying Light was a massive mess when released, All the GTA games, hec one of my favorite pass times is to look up hysterical glitch videos for videogames. Ark isn't much more buggier then any regular old AAA game (Sims 3 a prime example;), the only issue with it is so many people want to play it who can't get the full scope of it due to the type of PC it requires, it was like a game that was intended for the hardware specs and graphical specs of the PS5 being tested on a PS4, it was always meant to be for the next generation specs, which yes leaves a ton of people unable to play it or run it well unless they have massive pc's, to which as quickly as PC become outdated and updated, (I bought a  Gtx TI980 Videocard when they where still new, only to find out a week later the 1000series was releasing.) In a year or less those who cant play it now because the computer it takes to run it will be far more affordable due to being at least 2 if not 3 generations of new tech outdated, and the game will drop back in price pretty quickly as all AAA games after release tend to drop in a year if not two... So like those of us who wait for the PS5 to come out so the PS4 and games drop in price to buy them on sale and wait to play them when they are more reasonably priced due to being outdated,,, This is no different.
I mean hec ya wanna talk about greed... Instead of making new video games presently AAA companies are just rereleasing the same exact games to you in multiple fashions and reraising the prices... (Skyrim 59.99, Skyrim Remastered 59.99, SKyrim VR either 59.99 or 69.99,) and the whole reason they are doing it this way is specifically to milk any money they can out of the consumers. (I havent seen Rockstar drop or even put GTAV on a single decent sale as of yet... Meanwhile Wildcard has made sure continuously to make their game constantly affordable to people who wanted it. Even when they needed the money for development they participated in sales, while GTAV did not.)
When you look at everything as a whole in terms of gaming... this is hardly that bad of a move by Wild Card... At least in comparison to AAA games...

Take all the fun and tactics in team fortress 2 but replace it with a middle ages theme and you get Chivalry. Don't be fooled by your first encounter with its combat system, it may look like "spam to win" at first but you will soon realize this isn't the case.
As you delve into the game, you will soon realize that combat is about exposing an opening in your opponent and timing your attacks. Its loaded with tactics like directional attacks that have different speeds and effects, feinting attacks, directional blocking, docking, shield bashing, kicking,  stamina based hits that counter spamming, locational damage, friendly fire, siege equipment and much more.
The map objectives are even better and actually make sense. One example is where you have to attack a village by burning the houses and killing villagers while the other team defends it. Once successful, your team has to push a battering ram to the castle gates and actually ram it and avoid all the ballista fire and burning oil. Once you're done you have to kill the king, who is actually a real player and that is only one map! Oh yes and there are 4 classes each with different load-outs. Knights, ranged, Vanguards and men at arms.
If you like the setting and tactical combat, then don't miss it. And yes, it is way much so very better than war of the roses.

Quickly approaching 1,300 hours of playtime on Warframe, I figured I'd leave a review for it. I'll try to make this as short and sweet as possible.
Warframe is F2P done right, full stop. The system is not perfect, but it's head and shoulders above any other free-to-play systems out there. You can obtain nearly any item in the game with enough hard work. There are very few 'pay-only' items outside of the Prime Access packs, and those are excusively cosmetic in nature (the Prime Access deals cater to the whales anyway).
Gameplay-wise, Warframe has one of the most satisfying combat systems I've come across. It's perhaps not as fluid as it could be when transitioning between gunplay/melee, but it gets the job done and really delivers the promised 'space-ninja' fantasy. There aren't a lot of unique missions/tilesets, and if you grind with any urgency you're going to run through them fairly quickly. Having said that, the combat is fun enough to where you don't mind the repetitive environments so much.
It's also worth noting that the game is updated quite frequently. Big patches with new stuff come about once a month, with hotfixes coming once or twice a week. If I had one gripe with Warframe, it's that it very much suffers from the "hurry up and wait" mentality of many F2P titles. For example, one has to wait 3 whole days to finish building a new Warframe under normal circumstances. You can speed this process up with platinum, but it still seems like a restrictively long timeframe.
All in all, Warframe is not a perfect game. But it's as perfect as free-to-play has gotten, and Digital Extremes genuinely seems to love their community. For the most part, the playerbase are very kind/helpful towards new players, and even at my noobiest, I never felt as though I was being a burden to my teammates. If you haven't yet tried Warframe, do yourself a favor and jump into a mission or two. The simple-yet-addictive gameplay may surprise you.

My generaly pros and cons
Pros:
- The game is very good looking (assuming you can run it) if you can't expect to run this game at low settings to get 60fps *the ingame graphical recommendations are as follows (Medium - GTX 760 High - GTX 970 Very High - GTX 980ti Ultra - Titan X )
- The game is very entertaining so long as you have friends to play with. not saying you can't enjoy the game in singleplayer i have multiple saves myself in singleplayer and have enjoyed the solo experience
- The game releases many free updates to the game with at this price point is very needed (this is a con for me personally *see con section*)
- The modding community is better at creating content than that of the company (im pretty sure they hired some modders)
Cons:
- The game cannot run at decent graphical settings on most systems.
- Studio Wildcard adds more content over fixing the optimization issues present in the game.
- The game can get very boring after a while after finishing most of the games bosses and taming all the current tameables
- Playing on offical servers can be a very hard grind so creating a private server is recommened (Which in mine and my friends took a HELL of a long time to setup although i can't say that is an issue for everyone)
- The price as of 11th of July 2017 is £49.99 or about $60 which is a normal price for a triple A game (which this is not)
Conclusion:
Don't get this game YET, i still believe this game has a very large potential to turn into something great even if it has to fall down a mountain to do so. If they optimize the game then maybe my opinion on the game will change but until im able to run the game at what the game recommends me to play at High - GTX 970 then i won't say this is worth the money, not now and not before.

So how is this game different from Mount & Blade, the progenitor medieval combat title of the hardware-accelerated era? It's not TOO terribly different, I'll get that out of the way now, but it does some things better, other things worse.
First, unlocks are persistent, where M&B has a Counterstrike-style purchasing system. I like persistent unlocks. I don't have to limp along for a round or two before I can use the stuff I actually want to.
Control defaults are laid out pretty strangely, and is probably Chivalry's weakest point. I prefer M&B's more intuitive mouse-gesture system for determining what kind of attack I do. With a bit of practice I've memorized how to attack how I want, but binding attacks to mouse-wheel up and down still feels weird. Clicking attack with your shield up does not bash, as it does in M&B, but it just performs a normal attack. Again, unintuitive. Kick and bash share their own key, and if you want to feint, that's another key you have to press while you're in the middle of a swing you clicked the mouse to initiate. It feels a bit like patting your head while rubbing your stomach. Hopefully more practice on my part irons this out.
The game is prettier than M&B (though most games are) and maps make more use of terrain, enterable structures, and vertical gameplay. There are only six maps, but most of them have an objective mode which is a bit more interesting than cut-and-dry deathmatch (though deathmatch is your best bet for grinding unlocks). Oh, and you can chop off heads, arms, and legs—M&B doesn't have that!
Infinitely more fun with friends than just pubbies, but hey, what game isn't? You can also hide text chat and mute voice chat entirely, so if you want to play but don't feel like seeing people whine in chat, just hide it and pretend you're playing against bots.

Pros:
+ Extremely smooth and fast-paced movement and combat; you can cover ground really quickly with a double jump and flips, take no fall damage, and have a vertical jump that can cover several stories.  You can shoot, reload, or cast powers while doing almost all of this
+ Beautiful art style across the board.  Warframes, weapons, and tilesets all look great (especially newer ones)
+ Highly customizable loadouts (cosmetically), there's tons of skins, accessories and colors to choose from.    FashionFrame (customizing your warframes to look exactly how you want), is joked about as the true endgame for a reason.
+ Highly customizable loadouts (performance-wise).  The amount of warframes, weapons, and mods makes for many different ways to play.
+ Solid F2P business model overall
Cons:
- Grind is the main gameplay, if you find repetitive missions boring I would recommend staying away from this game
- Some stuff is just better than others (notably mods and weapons).  This is inevitable to an extent, but there's always room for improvement.
- Since the game is F2P there is a lot of chances to pay to skip progression, notably that new weapons and warframes will take 12 hours to 3 days to craft, which can be rushed by using platinum.  There are a lot of great things to buy with in-game currency from the market but some of them are also ripoffs
- Overwhelming new player experience.  How to get things and the modding system are confusing at first, and the lack of power you have starting out is pretty discouraging
I know that's a lot of cons, but overall the game is a solid 8/10 to me.  Definitely would recommend.

(TL;DR) It's NINJAS.. In SPACE.. and it's FREE!
Alright, with that out of the way I just got to say that even with that steep learning and git gud curve.. it's still the best game i'd binge play. Coming from a Console Tenno to a PC Tenno made me realize that the definitive Warframe Experience is on the PC. I sunk hours trying to get back mods and weapons, even as far as to grinding much hated weapons. All-in-all.. It was time well spent. I managed to surpass my Console account in about a month (even though I'd be saying bye to the Primes that were vaulted during this. In terms of Microtransactions, the game doesn't force you to do so, sure you'll be getting stuff faster, but it's no P2W.. All the items (except for cosmetics) are attainable in game even if you don't pay.. paying just makes things easier to acquire, even then so i'd recommend playing without spending on Platinum.. if you like the game, sure why not.. but seldomly, log in rewards give you 75% off on plat which is in my opinion the best time to buy plat.
PROS
+ Space Ninjas! SPACE NINJAS!!
+ A Cinematic Storyline that can put some AAA games to shame
+ FashionFrame is EndGame
+ Microtransactions aren't Forced
+ Clem.. (GRAKATA!)
+ Lore Rich
+ Cool Community.. Devs Stream and talk with the Tenno Community on updates every other week
+ Enemy types Vary per planet/node
+ Agility and Parkour made this more than a Generic Hackn'Slash Shooter
+ Vaulted items come back every once in a while..
+ Updates.. FREE UPDATES! (Have you seen Plains of Eidolon!?)
+ It's Forever Free.. NINJAS PLAY FREE!
CONS
- That Steep Learning Curve Though..
- Mods are a pain to acquire.. and even a lot more painful to max (Imagine my pain trying to get and max every essential mod TWICE..)
- Max Builds take time (or Money.. take your pick)
- That Grind Though..
- Trading is a Double-Edged Sword.. You could get ripped off by paying 20 Platinum for a 10 Platinum item because they're the only one selling or willing to sell it..
- Slots cost Platinum.. (Painful for a Collector of Weapons, Warframes) (There's 200+ Weapons in game and you start with 8 and it costs 12 Platinum to get 2 Slots; There's 30+ Warframes and Variants now and you'll only start with 2 and it costs 20 for a single slot)
FINAL VERDICT
Graphics - Surprisingly at par with AAA titles.. 10/10
Gameplay - Stealth or Assault, Agile or Head-On, Guns or Melee.. The Playstyle is up to you.. 8/10
Replay Value - Missions are the general "Defend This or Kill X Enemies" But helps to grind a mission you love 8/10
Soundtrack - The OST of The Cinematic Quests are LIT! 9/10
Overall - I Love it and very much recommend you try it... Ten out of Tenno

I awoke to find myself naked on a beach surrounded by dinosaurs. I travelled what I soon found to be an island, searching for any possible way off. There were none. I decided to make the best of my situation and hunkered down. I began gathering resources, and even starting hunting. In time I became a force to be reckoned with, equipped with automatic weapons, a base castle that would put Dracula from Castlevania to shame, and of course a legion of ferocious creatures. During my time I discovered pieces of paper torn from various journals, putting together the experiences of what others who came before me had gone through. I hunted far and wide, from the tallest mountain peak to the darkest pits of the lowest caves, searching for a clue as to how I can leave and show the world my discoveries here. Instead I found strange artifacts that look reminiscent of the obelisks. I brought the artifacts as well as some of my legion to the pillars, and they reacted, transporting me to a place with massive and powerful creatures. The battles were hard fought and I lost many good creatures, some that I had raised from birth, but I came out on top. After beating the monstrosities I made my way to the volcanoe which had reacted to the monsters defeats. There I took what remained of my army and went into a structure I found there. This cave was not a natural formation. We fought our way through hordes of some of the most powerful creatures the island had to offer, until I arrived at the end of the cave, and I was the last one standing. I made my way up the strange alien pathway, where I was met with a console. I pressed a few buttons on it and a beam of light surrounded me and I began to float into the air towards the cieling. A bright flash of light filled my eyes and when it cleared I saw the Earth, shattered by some unknown force, as I continued to fly through space in the beam of light.
Then I came home and played Ark. It's a pretty fun game.

Ark: Survival Evolved is an exelent game that offers a great deal of opportunity for any dinosaur or exctinct creature lover to have tons of fun. However, durring its early access time, leading up to its official launch, there have been bugs and controversy related to its development, including the release of a paid dlc during its early access phase, and a recent price hike. This has led to comunity backlash, especially as many feel that rather than optimizing the game, the developers have been focused on adding new content. I will attempt to fully address these topics.
Arks gameplay is great. A player can roam freely about the island where they spawn, taking in the sights of majestic mountains in the distance, forests blanketing their slopes, and rivers cutting through the valleys, observing Brontosaurs moving about above the lesser dinosaurs as Pteranodons fly overhead. Then promptly get killed by a Raptor, or one of the other preadatory creatures, Jurassic Park style. A player literally has to use their own two hands to start crafting primitive tools and carving out a base, using primitive resources, and then creating more refined ones to stay alive. Your progress is greatly aided by the very creatures that can and will kill you, as you tame them and use them to defend you or gather valuble resources. Each tamed creature fills a unique role, and there is very little overlap between them, resulting in a base that will quickly have a huge stable filled with almost all of the islands prehistoric creatures. However, the sheer wonder does wear off a bit, as gathering some resources, especially end game ones, like metal, can be dificult and tedious even with high end dinosaurs. In addition to this, the default taming speed of dinosaurs can be incredibly high, leading to a large time investment. Outweghing this is the imense satisfaction of having a dinosaur army, and a base that you designed yourself. Furthermore, Ark has a story, told in the fragmented journals of past survivors, that adds to the athmosphere and provides a player with rewards, but a player is equally free to disregard the story, as well as the various caves that dot the landscape, and do as they please. This is a very nice balance between the full sandbox of some games that leave you with absolutely no direction, and the story driven plot of others. The culmination of your efforts, should you choose to pursue it, is delving into several dangerous caves in pursiut of special gear rewards and artifacts, that allow a player to fight massive bosses with their dinosuar army, and rewarding victory with tek equipment, a sci-fi themed end game tier of equipment that provides inumerable benefits. Some find thie inclusion jaring, but the tek equipment actually fits into the apearance and style of the game very well. Also, special mention must be made for the dinosaurs themselves. While artistic liberty has been take with the apreance, and especially size of the creatures, they are still remarkably well crafted and breathtaking beasts, that follow the scientific discoveries related to the spiecies remarkably well, and justification is also provide for deviations ingame. This is a sharp contrast to many other dinosaur games, that just throw out spiky monsters for players to kill as an achievement. Overall, it is an incredibly fun experience.
Ark is designed for multiplayer play primarily, and the gameplay experience is greatly enhance when you play with friends, forming cooperative tribes and working together to dominate the ark server you are on. However, the multiplayer comunity, is like most online comunities, a mixed bag. For every friendly player, there is one who will treat everyone like trash, and the multiplayer pvp expereince is extremely unbalanced for any group of players trying to get on their feet on their own. PvE aleviates this, but brings its own problems in the form of overcrowding of stategic locations with bases, also making it even more dificult for a new player to get started.
Now, this game does have a fair amount of bugs. However, the dev team is dedicated to fixing them. I experience one where my tamed dinosaurs would vanish. However, within a week of me noticing this, a patch was released that fixed the bug. Players complain a great deal about new features being added while performance increases are being postponed, but I personally have had minimal performance problems, and the developers have stated that performance increases are the thing coming at the end of the development cycle, as we begin to leave early access. This makes sense, as you do not want to go through all the trouble of optimizing your game, only to risk adding a new planned feature that screws it up. It is simply how game development works, get the features done, then optimize them. Especially considering that a major part of early access is its open beta feature, leting you develop and get feedback simultaneously accross a wider platform than normally possible.
The release of paid dlc in the form of the Scorched Earth expansion while in early access is a big alarm bell. The fact that a paid for addon exists for a game that is incomplete is a problem, and should not have hapened. That being said, this dlc is not oblivion horse armor. It is a full blown expansion, that adds a host of new creatures to the game on a new map. This reduces the shock somewhat, as is the fact that the dlc was apperently developed in tandem with the game, and managed to get done before all features were added. While still a problem, it does make sense to release it if you have it done. There is also speculation about the Scorched Earth dlc being relased to help pay off some lawsuits that the developer has suffered. Make of it what you may, but remember: YOU ARE NOT BEING FORCED TO BUY THE EXPANSION. If you do choose to buy it, you can be content knowing that you are getting a quailty addition to your game, and dragons, three types of dragons, that you can RIDE.
Another controversy is related to the recent price hike, which for me, is a change from  $30 to $60 USD, bringing the price up to a full priced game at the store. Now, I don't think the should have raised the price up until the game was launced in august. The developers claim they have raised the price so that preorders of the hard copy of the game aren't out competed. Make of it what you will, it's your opinion. The fact of the matter is that we are in semi-uncharted waters, as the early access model has still not been codified into a set system, the rules are still being written. Do I consider Ark to be a $60 game? Actually, yes I do, however, would I prefer it have a smaller price point? Of course. Who doesn't want cheaper, quality games? You may complain about how a full priced game shouldn't have the bugs, or that the price hike is unfair to people to who waited for launch.  These are valid concerns, but they also bring us to another problem.
We as gamers are a whiny, inconsistent bunch of people, that ask for one thing, without really knowing what we want, and whining and crying when what we want dosen't live up to our expectations, while still praising things that have the problems we claim to detest. Just look at The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim. It was relased at full price in 2011, but it had tons of bugs. And I mean tons, so many in fact, that it rendered play on the Playstation 3 impossible at launch, and the dlc wasnt even avalible for PS3 until the developers had virtually finished with all of their development and bugfixes, amost a year after the first dlc was released for xbox. And even after the Developers closed up shop, there are still many bugs. That being said, We still sing its praises. I love that game. We have simply set ourselves up for buggy releases.
There is some more I would like to say, especially about the paid mod program, and how it is the best version of paid mods I have seen but I am out of words. I hope this review helped you.

People complaining about the price hike are stupid.
First the game, it has a serious memory leak for me that makes it so I have to restart the game every 2-5 hours of play time (not everyone has it, I think it is a system conflict or something). It's INCREDIBLY annoying but the game is still playable. There are other bugs as well, however the worst is when your flying dino disappears into the sky or random location if you die while they are following. This needs to be fixed. Official servers are boring, Alpha tribes are usually annoying and rob new players which is an instant fun killer. Buy your own server or join an unofficial one. You have to do some searching. There is also a considerable grind, the game gets great after about 3 hours of play. Don't do what I did, start exploring when you start up with nothing to level.
That said, the game is a lot of fun and an absolute time vampire. I would say the game is unplayable single player but if you find the right server with friends its great fun. Planning and building out from nothing is frustrating at times but surprisingly crazy amount of fun. The game has incredible complexity (Some of which means you have to go to the wiki, they probably should add something in game to explain) something you just don't see in many games these days. Naming dino's and riding them is awesome, and experiencing their deaths is heart-breaking, RIP salacious b. crumb, my level 100 Jerboa. Taming and breeding dinos takes a stupid amount of time but that is fixable via server settings. Be prepared to log on once a day to feed your dinos ect and make sure they are alright. Think tamagotchi, if you don't like that don't buy this game.
Now for the paid expansion, Shut up. If you don't want it, don't buy it. It's not even close to required and you can get free DLC maps created by modders which add all that content anyway (not the map, just the items). It should have been included in the base game or they should have waited till after release but oh well, it's a reasonable offer and worth the money if you like the base game.
Now the recent big deal, the price hike was a dumb marketing move. BUT... The game is by enlarge worth every penny of it. If you find the friends to play and you think the above stuff is acceptable and sounds fun, its worth it. There are plenty of videos everywhere that will give you a great idea of what the game is for the value it provides. I'd recommend watching some NEEBS gaming for funny videos on it, but there are countless others. Oh and steam sales are still a thing last I checked, and there was one recently that dropped the price in half. Where were all the people complaining? Did they buy it? Then why are they complaining? Warframe is F2P done right, full stop. The system is not perfect, but it's head and shoulders above any other free-to-play systems out there. You can obtain nearly any item in the game with enough hard work. There are very few 'pay-only' items outside of the Prime Access packs, and those are excusively cosmetic in nature (the Prime Access deals cater to the whales anyway).
Gameplay-wise, Warframe has one of the most satisfying combat systems I've come across. It's perhaps not as fluid as it could be when transitioning between gunplay/melee, but it gets the job done and really delivers the promised 'space-ninja' fantasy. There aren't a lot of unique missions/tilesets, and if you grind with any urgency you're going to run through them fairly quickly. Having said that, the combat is fun enough to where you don't mind the repetitive environments so much.
It's also worth noting that the game is updated quite frequently. Big patches with new stuff come about once a month, with hotfixes coming once or twice a week. If I had one gripe with Warframe, it's that it very much suffers from the "hurry up and wait" mentality of many F2P titles. For example, one has to wait 3 whole days to finish building a new Warframe under normal circumstances. You can speed this process up with platinum, but it still seems like a restrictively long timeframe.
All in all, Warframe is not a perfect game. But it's as perfect as free-to-play has gotten, and Digital Extremes genuinely seems to love their community. For the most part, the playerbase are very kind/helpful towards new players, and even at my noobiest, I never felt as though I was being a burden to my teammates. If you haven't yet tried Warframe, do yourself a favor and jump into a mission or two. The simple-yet-addictive gameplay may surprise you.

This game has presented me with the greatest simulation of first-person medieval combat that I have ever seen.  Fast, brutal and utterly satisfying.  Gone are the simplistic "click to attack, repeat" mechanisms of most medieval FPS games.  If you thought Skyrim had advanced combat mechanics, this game will shatter your mind.  If you enjoyed Mount & Blade's more advanced system of blocks, parries and alternating attacks you will greatly appreciate how Chivalry takes that concept and makes it fluid instead of clunky.
Attacks are tied to the left mouse button and the mouse wheel.  The left button will perform a regular attack with whichever weapon you have (typically a slash), whereas the mouse wheel will stab if you roll it up and chop if you roll it down.  Stabbing someone in the face feels more satisfying when a quick flick of your finger on a wheel gives the command.  Tapping Q mid-swing will feint, which can trip up opponents and leave them open for a follow-through.
All attacks can be blocked.  The general idea is to aim for the tip of the opponent's weapon and use the right mouse button to time your blocks.  This won't always work if you're out of stamina or if you aim poorly (or attempt to block a giant axe with a dagger), but I've had ridiculous exchanges where my opponent and I danced around parrying eachother's attacks for a solid 30 seconds, getting in little jabs and cuts where possible.  My♥♥♥♥♥is placed solidly on the edge of my chair for the entire duration.
One of the best aspects of Chivalry is the sheer staggering level of violence you'll encounter while playing.  You can behead (and be beheaded), dismember and otherwise mutilate your foes.  Blood is gratuitous without feeling overdone.  Screams and cries of agony echo throughout the battlefield and many hilarious taunts and commands you can shout through a context menu add to the flavour.  It is possible to run a man through, spam laughter while watching as he sinks to his knees, and then place a solid kick to his face (optional, but why wouldn't you?) that sends him toppling backwards.  Few games let you interact with your foe even after he has died.  This all works together to create desperate battlefields filled with severed limbs and the screams of the dying.  Sudden death can arrive from all sides (even teammates), and is usually surpising and hilarious enough that even getting killed is a lot of fun.
The weapons come in a healthy variety.  Each of the four classes have three primary weapons, which in turn have two unlocks each.  You gain unlocks by killing foes with said weapon over the course of many games, and they remain on your record forever once obtained.  An unlock is not necessarily better than previous weapons, just different.
All of these weapons and classes (and their respective strategies) are enjoyed over a number of maps and gameplay modes.  There is no single player to speak of, aside from the tutorial.  Everything is online, and it's great fun.  Deathmatch servers have maps that include such locales as an arena filled with death traps, a town and a battlefield.  Mission modes exist where one team must complete objectives while the others try to hold them off.  This leads to sieges and ridiculous melees as people scramble to push bomb carts to a gate, defend the King, burn down a village or use ballistae to sink boats off the coast.
Overall a very satisfying game, and shockingly good for an indie title.  Considering the low price tag and the fact that it seems to be on sale frequently, I highly recommend that anyone pick this up as soon as possible.

Ark can be a fun and engaging game, and it can also be one of the most frustrating, unfufilling games you'll ever play. I genuinely enjoyed my time with it, but don't spend $60 on this game. Wildcard has created an interesting and compelling concept and worked hard to create a strong and welcoming multiplayer community, but they've failed on too many key issues. Single player (for those who want to avoid the toxic and alienating multiplayer community that plays this game) is a series of boring chores occasionally interrupted by exciting gameplay. The bugs are rampant, gamebreaking and routinely ignored by developers (it's not Early Access once you start charging full price). You'll frequently encounter gameplay mechanics that make you wonder if the designers even play their own game. And while you'll see many beautiful videos of a vibrant and visually stunning world, you're machine probably can't run it anywhere near that level due to shoddy optimization issues. If ARK is steeply discounted when you read this, take the risk if you want, but right now it's overpriced and underdeveloped.

Ark can be a fun and engaging game, and it can also be one of the most frustrating, unfufilling games you'll ever play. I genuinely enjoyed my time with it, but don't spend $60 on this game. Wildcard has created an interesting and compelling concept and worked hard to create a strong and welcoming multiplayer community, but they've failed on too many key issues. Single player (for those who want to avoid the toxic and alienating multiplayer community that plays this game) is a series of boring chores occasionally interrupted by exciting gameplay. The bugs are rampant, gamebreaking and routinely ignored by developers (it's not Early Access once you start charging full price). You'll frequently encounter gameplay mechanics that make you wonder if the designers even play their own game. And while you'll see many beautiful videos of a vibrant and visually stunning world, you're machine probably can't run it anywhere near that level due to shoddy optimization issues. If ARK is steeply discounted when you read this, take the risk if you want, but right now it's overpriced and underdeveloped.

I really enjoyed my first few tries at this game. I also enjoyed building bases and exploring the Island for the first time. And even the Center. But that charm wears off fairly quickly.
First off, progression is way, way, way, waaaaaaaaaay too slow. It will take you 60-75 hours just to establish a base. It only takes PvPers about 15 minutes to destroy enough walls to take everything or kill all your dinos. (I never had this happen to me but it is a major risk I've seen happen to my tribe-mates.) It also takes upwards of 12 hours to tame a dinosaur. 12 hours of babysitting and hoping a bronto doesn't step on it accidentally.
So some of you are probably thinking, just play on a modded server! And you know what, I did! I often played on 8x or 10x servers and it STILL takes 4-6 hours PER DINOSAUR to tame. If you get unlucky and lose your top two or three dinisaurs you can easily lose 18-20 hours of babysitting and extra time actually levelling those dinos.
The AI for dinisaurs will destroy you as well. If you don't know where the safe spots are to build, or if you don't get a massive stone wall up immediately you will get tracked down by every predator and murdered in about two hits and there will be nothing you can do about it.
After 169 hours and maybe 3 different servers I cannot say my time was well spent. My last escapade on a 10x server still took me 70ish hours to build a wall and tame some dinos. I had metal but that was about it. Everything was going great but one of my main dinosaurs fell in to a hole and I died. I thought no big deal, there was no message that my dino died and it wasn't in my tribe log, so I grabbed a bird and flew in to the cave. I searched everywhere, but there was no dino to be found. We even had a mod on that tracks dinosaur locations for your pets and it said my dino was alive, but it wasn't accessible, stuck in the terrain or something.
Which leads me to my final point because writing this review only annoys me and makes me remember how I regret the time spent in this game. The bugs. There are some ridiculous bugs such as your dinos mysteriously disappearing in to walls. Collision is also insane, sometimes you can barely be bumped and you will go flying up diagonal edges, after landing you will die because you feel too far. Even tho if you got hit with that same speed on a flat plane you would have barely moved six feet. Objects clip through the walls making it really hard to build furniture in a base without it being accessed in some unintentional way. Item stacks are so small you can barely carry anything on your person. Most servers I play on have increased item stack size which can lead to freezing the entire server if you decided to split your stacks of meat in to 1 piece each so you can get spoiled meat for crafting. (I have witnessed my server freeze twice because I split up about 500 pieces of meat. The game does not handle that many individual items in your inventory at all and the whole server almost timed out when the meat spoiled.)
Pros:
+The graphics are pretty.
+Soundscape not bad
+Lots to initially explore and craft and tame
Cons:
-Time sink, get ready to spend over 10 hours taming a single dino you have your eye on. Hope it doesn't lose all its levels to a random bronto that walks by or a pack of raptors.
-PvP too easy. It can take you 70 hours to build a base and in 15 minutes and 2 C4 you can lose everything.
-Buggy. Get ready to die to bugs, and I don't mean poison either. I mean clipping through terrain, getting hit when you're inside shelter, falling when you shouldn't be falling and then dying to fall damage. Etc.
-Way too slow. I'm not exagerating when I say time sink. You will spend 10 hours collecting sticks and rocks to build your first shelter and then you will found out it's not even big enough to set up your crafting.
As for DLC, I'm neutral. The desert DLC was ok but way too hard and I never got in to it. The newest DLC I have no interst in buying so I'm not gonna slam the game for it alone.
If you have 500 hours to spare and don't mind the slowest progress of any sandbox game in the world, then this game can be alright. Just DO NOT PLAY ON DEFAULT SERVERS. You will spend over 16 hours taming high level dinos. Have fun with that.
