Ark: Honest Review.
I bought this game a long time ago and now that it is nearing its official release; I felt obligated to review it.
First off: This game is more fun with friends. While lonely seclusion of being in a dino-infested environment can in fact make this game a bit scary. My first night, starving wounded, and cold. Fending of predators and collecting just enough berries to survive.
The first time on a raft and a fin broke the water just as a whale took a chunk out of the back.
And finally, the first time I tamed and flew on a Tavis. Just to get dismounted and have the ground scream toward me.
I will remember it all and to this day still feel uneasy at times alone. despite masterwork armor and weapons.
But with people. A tribe. It’s a whole different experience.  Organizing your tribe, optimizing engrams. Taking down a big Dino or a boss. Working together in a cave to maybe find something of value. Or on the more light-hearted notes; Making a custom food item or even roleplaying. Having a race with Dino's. Sometimes just sitting at base and building something cool.
It’s a versatile experience.
The size of the map. The plethora of Dino's and other creatures. The ability to use primitive plus to somewhat make the game grittier. On a fully optimized machine, this game is amazing.
However, with the good; there is bad.
I still don’t get what exactly is going on? The notes do paint a vague picture but,  the free exploration of the game does not give you any reason to progress though the bosses’ other than advancing tech. Why not bring up the level of the native creatures with each boss level cleared? Add to Drops or even offer more of a glimpse into what the creators of the Ark are trying to do? Just go here and survive? Why not have a twist and make it so there are intelligent Dino’s or even….. anything really.
You kill everything in a volcano and have an acid trip to ascend? Roll credits and now we should lay off the naroberries.
That’s if you can even survive on a beach longer than 5 min when a Rex  is already eating you as you spawn in.
You need a high-end pc to enjoy this game and even when you do, the textures occasionally look cartoonish or buildings just re-appear. Dino's or people explode into a mass of twisted physics flesh like a 13-year-old playing with Gary's mod when they are shot.
Glitches like dinos materialize inside of rocks or trees. A massive Rex head clipping through a two-foundation thick, five wall high barrier (players get this) and you can punch it to death without taking damage. Metal walls reflecting light as if it was the sun itself (yes paint does kind of help).
The lists go on both ways though. I don’t expect a masterpiece. In my opinion, this game is fantastic despite the glitches and immersion breaking.
While I hope they fix the last few bugs and make this game a lil- more low-end friendly. I still will play it for a long time.

What I'd like to see? : Maybe more furniture or practical storage not reliant on a mod. Metal less reflective. Perhaps a menu based manager for dinos and behavior rather than the current in game wheel.
Maybe a real endgame boss. I’d find it rather humorous if it was a Dodo in tech armor. In a small chair. Like Dr.Evil.  And yes, mean the small bird, Not the Rex

Not at all a bad game, but not optimized, not complete, and not worth the shiny new $60 price tag. I'll admit there is a honeymoon period where "holy crap there are dinosaurs" will have you loving this, no denying that, however here are the brass tacks.
As an early access game, and for the previous price this was well worth a spin..... That being said, since the developer has decided to charge full box retail AAA prices ahead of their launch and before the game is complete, I'm going to review based on full box retail AAA expectations.
The best description I can give you in terms of crafting and UI is "clunky but functional".
The graphics are well done, but there are clipping problems galore and the whole thing is poorly optimized for performance leaving you stuttering on even serious gaming rigs. Think I'm kidding, go look up the list of most taxing games of 2017 on gamespot from 7/3/17.... this comes in at #5. Some of that is the engine, but a lot of it is optimization.
The server browser and netcode are..... okay
The controls are.....okay
The replayability is solid, and there are a LOT of things to do, but the overall play once the new wears off is super grindy and time intensive. The time sinks are only that much worse if you should be so foolish as to play solo or with a very small group on a private server. Sure the arguement could be made that this is meant to be played in large groups on large servers, and while that is trus again I would argue that as a AAA game charging AAA prices I counter with the fact solo/offline is an option and that it is weak at best.
Also, I know it is old news, but for those just getting to the party... this developer also has gone to the well by issuing paid DLC for an early access title. Their price hike is not unexpected, but is disappointing, and leads me to a negative review.

So I don't normally post reviews but considering it didn't take long for me to really love this game I will.
First off just to get it out of the way I will say that I cannot recommend this game to friends or anyone for that matter in its current state.
With that out of the way let me expand on why.
The gameplay though buggy is not the primary issue as developers can fix those over time.
The issues are connection related and population related which I believe have a profound effect on one another with this game.
Hackers, dupers, DDOS'ers, and griefers (griefers are to be expected and not really an issue TBH). The first three all have a direct affect on ones ability to even play the game and they have been ongoing since early access when live (Not going to link as you only need to look at developer forums or even steam forums for examples).
Hackers are self explanatory. Can't be killed. Extremely lethal and destroy a dozen players on site without being damaged, ect...
Dupers crash the servers all the time.
DDOS'er like to either hold servers hostage which seems to be happening more often recently and they also like to send attacks if they are either losing a raid or to clear a server before a raid to ensure only their people can log on. This has been going on for quite some time and is also common in other games but due to the nature of how ARK is DDOS is downright devastating in this game. I havent seen much developer input as far as combating these frequent attacks and that is sad. If there was not a way to combat them then no online games, websites, or the internet as we know it would be able to function because everything would be DDOS'ed all the time.
Bottom line is if you play on official PvP servers expect alot of downtime due to people being childish.
The other option is to play on non-official servers but that is a crap shoot for admins and you will likely have low population all the time which makes the game very hard because there are no people to trade with.
Now with PvE servers you have the above issues plus more. On PvE servers you have people that spam structures everywhere so if you want to start there you cannot because there is no place to build anything that won't be blocked by another person's structure and by the nature of the server being PvE you cannot destroy the trash blocking everyone from building. This leads back to non-official servers where a good admin would be the only way around this as they can dictate the rules of the server with the power to enforce them.
Bottom line is there are too many bad egg's in this game in it's current state that the community or the developer can do little about. These people ruin the game for 100's.
I love the game and wish them the best but if the stability issues don't get resolved quickly this game will go the way of no man's sky before long.
I think I had a life before.

Not at all a bad game, but not optimized, not complete, and not worth the shiny new $60 price tag. I'll admit there is a honeymoon period where "holy crap there are dinosaurs" will have you loving this, no denying that, however here are the brass tacks.
As an early access game, and for the previous price this was well worth a spin..... That being said, since the developer has decided to charge full box retail AAA prices ahead of their launch and before the game is complete, I'm going to review based on full box retail AAA expectations.
The best description I can give you in terms of crafting and UI is "clunky but functional".
The graphics are well done, but there are clipping problems galore and the whole thing is poorly optimized for performance leaving you stuttering on even serious gaming rigs. Think I'm kidding, go look up the list of most taxing games of 2017 on gamespot from 7/3/17.... this comes in at #5. Some of that is the engine, but a lot of it is optimization.
The server browser and netcode are..... okay
The controls are.....okay
The replayability is solid, and there are a LOT of things to do, but the overall play once the new wears off is super grindy and time intensive. The time sinks are only that much worse if you should be so foolish as to play solo or with a very small group on a private server. Sure the arguement could be made that this is meant to be played in large groups on large servers, and while that is trus again I would argue that as a AAA game charging AAA prices I counter with the fact solo/offline is an option and that it is weak at best.
Also, I know it is old news, but for those just getting to the party... this developer also has gone to the well by issuing paid DLC for an early access title. Their price hike is not unexpected, but is disappointing, and leads me to a negative review.

Chivalry is a multiplayer medieval battle arena game, built using the Unreal 3 engine but based upon the HF2 mod "Age of Chivalry". Its gameplay is very simple, even to the point of being called shallow, but its entertainment value relies on this simplicity to deliver thrilling gameplay and high replayability to a general audience. Chivalry lacks a campaign mode of any kind, and really its only reward for playing which carries past an individual game is a weapon unlock system. The enjoyment an individual will have with this title relies almost entirely on their enthusiasm for the gameplay mechanics, because at the end of the day, this is all that Chivalry offers you. That all being said, I cannot recommend this game highly enough if medieval combat is even a passing interest to a gamer. I'm excited to see what can be done with this franchise in the future.

There's versatility packed in here, too. You can have private servers with friends, join public PvP/PvE servers, or simply play by yourself offline.
So far as the performance goes, it's fine for the most part. Forget the whiners who jabber on about bugs and glitches and demand refunds, I use a low-end laptop to play on the lowest settings, and it works great for me -- I'm not too picky. It's crashed once before, but apparently the game auto-saves, so no big deal. It's still going to get updates and patches to fix whatever problems come up, anyway, just like any other game.
Overall, if you haven't played ARK, you're missing out big-time. This game is easily my favorite out of any title I've ever played, AAA or otherwise.

The map count is somewhat small, but each one is expertly designed to suit the gametype it is designed for. The siege maps are particularly awesome.
Graphic quality is nice and its design demonstrates a great attention to detail. Netcode seems stable and the controls are responsive.
Haven't honestly paid much attention to the music, but the sound is well pulled off (with free gargling sound when downed enemies drown on their own blood).

This is such a wonderful blend of arcade action and simulation, and there is very little like it. I would argue, however, that melee could have been a bit faster (would make things much more interesting!). Nevertheless, Chivalry manages to be quite satisfying due to dismemberment and the intense effects that hacking, stabbing and bashing have on yourself and your enemies.
There are several modes to play in which range from FFA mayhem, to objective-based battles and there is a wide array of weapons to choose from. Most importantly--in my opinion--Chivalry garners quite an amusing spirit. The things that take place during a match and the voice commands gives it a flair that is similar to the whimsical and delightfully over-the-top Pirates, Vikings and Knights II. I would also say the same philosophy I mentioned in my recommendation for PVK, applies to this: don't take the game too seriously or you should prepare yourself for heavy frustration and rage quits!
Overall, the community is fairly mature, but you have to grow a thick skin to survive the exploitative nature of combat with veterans. There's is quite a lot to learn and it's not all immediately obvious.
My biggest complaints:
- Some of the weapons could use more polished mechanics
- First-person should have been forced.

I've left and came back to Ark so many times. The fact I keep coming back shows that there is something here. To me Ark is all about the adventure and fulfulling some sort of childhood dream of living with and riding dinos. That being said: there is still a ton of content here. Is it buggy? Absolutely. I recently re-downloaded the game and since then I've had issues with crashing and general memory hogging but I STILL PLAY. lol. You can lose yourself in a world where you make the decisions and every decision be it minor or major (like base locations) can have grave consequences. Losing a tame or picking the wrong battle can set a player back days which I find to be an extremely challenging angle to its gameplay. Yes, once you get established and have a nice dino fleet the little things don't matter as much, but the process and dedication that is needed to be fully decked or even "alpha status" is almost unfathomable yet still motivating.
I do really wish they would improve the overall performance of the game. It's really indefensible in my eyes that the game still runs poorly on 90% of the rigs out there and has so many issues but I've found thru all the issues and bugs there is still a very fun, deep, and entertaining game here with more content than really any other game in its genre.
I find I like the beginning grind the most. I've started on hundreds of servers. Built bases, raised fleets of dinos, then never went back. It does get stale to me when you start doing end game grinds but the beauty of the game is; there's always a new server with new settings that might fit your playing style better.
If you are new to Ark: be patient. It's worth it if you are able to work around some minor bugs.

The review I'm posting only relates to its performance on Mac. Simply put: DO NOT BUY if you are using a Mac.
For reference here are my computer's specs:
OS Sierra 10.12.5
iMac (Retina 5K, 27-inch, 2017)
4.2 GHz Intel Core i7
32 GB 2400 MHz DDR4
Radeon Pro 575 4096 MB
My experience with the game has been brief simply because it is hardly playable. I went into the game knowing that it doesn't play as well on Mac as it does on PC. What I didn't realize is just how awful it plays on a Mac (even with a top tier iMac). The game's max resolution is 1600 x 900 which causes everything to be blurry and low res. The top layer of water is a solid gray color. There is tearing all over the place, and virtually everything looks awful.
I personally think it's just bad business to offer the game for Mac if the product is in such poor shape for the OS. It shouldn't be available for Mac users to purchase in it's current state. It is obvious that the Devs have put minimal effort into optimizing the game for Mac, so why even offer it for purchase? Especially when the game's price has risen to $60.  Unbelievable.
I shouldn't be expected to pay an extra $120 to buy Windows and then run the game on Bootcamp. I'm sure the game will still run poorly even then.
The game itself looks amazing and I really wish I could play it. Unfortunately in its current state I will have to just let it sit in my library.
Please please please work on optimizing the game for Mac before allowing players to purchase it (especially at full price).

Warframe is one of those few games that I enjoy coming back to, even if its sometimes a grind for things. Once you completed all of the basic tasks to learn how to do stuff, and understand the curve of things it gets really nice to play. The combat and movement is fluid, theres a lot of weapons and frames (pretty much characters/classes) you can utilize and have reason for being there (for most of them, im looking at you seer). And the few missions of actual story are well written. The only flaw to that is the story missions being too short.
The many frames you can choose is impressive. Theres 30 frames in all you can choose, and thats leaving out most of their prime versions. And not only can you customize your chosen warframe, but you can also change the look of your weapons and how you holster them as well. Same with your companions that you can bring along beside you to battle. And yes, while it might get boring after awhile (my point was at the 200 hour mark), you might feel yourself coming back to it after some time.
And if you decide playing after reading all of these reviews, keep in mind that it may look like its behind a buy wall. Its not true, but there are things that you can buy to speed up the game a bit and make it more easy to manage (extra weapon slots, upgrades that increase capacity, resources, etc.) You can also obtain most of these things and even helmets for your favorite frames. And hey, you might be seeing yourself love this game as much as I do and spend a few bucks on it. Who knows. But I would give it a shot since its a f2p anyways.

Have you played cookie cutter before? This is a long version of that with a couple other cool things in it. For those of you who haven't let me break it down for you:
- You start out with nothing and low damage and see numbers pop up.
- Every monster you kill drops gold.
- You use said gold to buy upgrades that let your clicks do more damage.
- You purchase henchmen to help you deal damage.
- You level those henchmen up with gold and buy special abilities, things like making them do more damage, getting more gold, and so on.
- You can click on rare bird-type objects that give you a large amount of gold.
- Think it's over after a few hours? Think again. Numbers get so high that they don't even represent them as numbers. It only goes to 99,999. After that you are at 100K. Then when you break 99,999K you move up to 100M, and so on. No, seriously. It goes on for basically ever.
- Once you get high enough and collect/upgrade certain things you can 'restart' the game in a way, except with 'Hero Souls', which increase all your henchmen's DPS by 10% each. The treadmill continues.
All in all, I am pleased with this game...pleased enough to shell out $10-20 ish dollars to help support it. Also, if you were curious how it's free to play, you can pay money to speed things along by getting free gold, hero souls, and restarts (restarts are called ascensions)

This game, in my opinion, is worth $29.99 but after the raise in price to $59.99 I simply cannot recommend it. The game has provided me with over 250 hours of playtime and in that 250 hours not once have I regretted my decision to but the game.
The game provides a beautiful world (I'll talk about performence later) for you and your friends to run around in annd enjoy together. The early game can be a strugle to get armed befor you are eaten. More often than not you are eaten befor you can do anything. This is not a bad thing as it provides a good motive to stay in the more safe areas early game.
Speaking of early game, it's a rather slow start as you try to scrape togeather enough resorces to get a starter base or tame your first dino. Playing with mods such as Annunaki Genesis can make the early game a bit easier as they allow you to "passive tame" most passive dinos simply by walking up to them with some meat or barries in your hotbar and hand-feeding them.
The late game gives you one main goal. To kill the three bosses in the game. To avoid spoilers I wont say any more about the three bosses to avoid spoilers, although in my opinion they are not much fun to fight. There are other smaller goals aswell, like taming some of the later game dinos such as the Giga, and building a base that can defend against other players (If you're playing on a PvP server).
The moding in this game is what gave me so much more playtime. I did play on PvP servers but most of my playtime was spent in single player with a mod list that took upwards of 10-15 min to load. Earlier I mentioned the mod Annunaki Genesis, this is one of the biggest mods for ARK and one of my personal favorites. It is a mod that adds many new "elemental" dinos as well as many new bosses to kill. These bosses are much harder to fight than the vanilla bosses.
The performance of the game is terrible. After modifying the ini and launch options I was able to get 60-90 fps on a 1070 and a i7 4790 with 16gb of ram. If you dont't know much about the current tech, thats a pretty powerful PC. Without modifying the ini of changing the launch options I would get 40-50 fps on high. Performence will be different on pertty much every PC but thats a base line for people with specs similar to mine.
Overall I can't recommend this game at $59.99, but if you can find it for <$30 then I'd say try it out.

There's alot to like about this game. There's alot to dislike too.
The first thing I want to say is to clarify this game's genre. At first, it plays like a survival game. You struggle to get food, try to keep your body tempurature up, and there's lots of big stuff that wants to (and usually will) eat you. Getting your first hut and bed is an accomplishment, but then you have to defend it if a herd of raptors find you inside it. Survival game. Quite harsh if you spawn in the wrong location, but otherwise pretty good.
As the game progresses, it really turns into an MMO. Tasks take teams of people, and hours to accomplish. I play on a private server with a couple close friends with all the speeds turned up, because 7 hours of close attention is just too much time to tame a rex. You can try to tame every dino with kibble to speed things up, but then you need a whole menagerie of dinos laying eggs for the kibble, which takes a helluva long time as well. I think the idea is a group of 20 people could do it more quickly... but i'll bring that up in a moment.
There are a few points that I think are a bit misleading about the game. First, in the videos, they show dozens of people hunting spinos with spears, or huge land-battles between tribes. Typically, when I get on a server, there's maybe 10 people on. Right now (7pm on a sunday, so prime-time I would think) there's a few official servers with 40 people on, but most have less than 10. When you turn it on late, there pages and pages servers with 0-2 people on them. So I highly doubt many of these big team things happen unless you've got 20 friends to field both sides of the battle. (Also, they don't show you the 2 hours of farming materials to make 2 clips of bullets, or the three hours of sitting around taming the stego)
Second, they show enormous mountainside fortresses, dense medival cities, and elaborate structures like that. I want to be perflectly clear... the building system in this game is the buggiest one I've ever seen. Structures don't snap, or they snap the wrong way with no way to rotate them, connected walls don't line up. Youtube is full of building videos, but most of them are lists of exploits to make objects snap to the places you want them to. It can be done, but it would take hours upon hours of farming resources on official servers, and is painfully frustrating.
My other thought... the game is buggy. Painfully game-breakingly buggy, and realistically it will probably never get fixed. Example: Scorpions are a lowish level tame. You put a saddle on em and sting other dinos with em. Or you line them up in neat little rows and have them lay eggs, because scorpion eggs help you train rexs in less than 7 hours. Except scorpions have eight little legs, and if you fall on a scorpion, you almost always get caught in the air between two of the legs. You're not touching the ground or anything solid, so you can't jump, but you can't move either. You can't even suicide, because they made that an admin command. You can log off and log back in, which sometimes works, but otherwise you need a friend to come move the scorpion for you. Or you can call an admin.
Ok, so it's early access, that kind of thing happens... Except it's been like that for a year and a half. It's a low level dino that you mount/dismount, so lots of people must hit this issue. But the devs haven't fixed it yet. If you have dinos following you, it's pretty common for them to get too close and clip into your dino so you can't move. You have to dismount, mount them, move them, then remouont your first. I've lost so many dinos because of obnoxious little bugs like that. When my friends log on to my server, they are almost always stuck in the floor of their house, and need me to use admin commands to get them out. There are so many ways to get caught an unable to move, both with and without the help of player-made objects and dinos.
Anyway, with that said, there is plenty to like about the game. It is frikin beautiful. There are lots of cool things to do with the dinos. Your buddy strolls his ankylo up the mountain and starts breaking up rocks for metal, while you load the metal on your bronto to transport back to the base for smelting. Of course you don't want to get eaten, so you may have a few other friends on carnos running escort/guard duty. Or perhaps just scouting ahead on a pteradon. I mean... that's cool.
One final point... the game is slow. I've got a private server where everything is 10x faster. Dinos tame 10x faster, resources drop 10x more, dinos breed 10x faster, experience gains are 10x larger. I've got 500 hours in on my server, and i'm just starting to get to think about finishing the game. If you are a casual gamer like most of my friends, odds are you will never ride a raptor, let alone lead a hunting party from atop a rex.
Utimately I have to say that as cool as the game is, it is not at all what it advertises, which is the big part of my thumbs down. Also, the game has been around so long, and they've released tons of new content, including paid DLC when the old content isn't working well. And this new price increase? Egad, the game is good, but it is nowhere near as elaborate or as polished as Witcher or Shadow of Mordor... and those work pretty seamlessly, where this is slow and buggy. (oh and their price is going down, not up)
I paid $25 for this game. It was in early access, and they added alot of content (most of it free, not the DLC, although that has a huge amount of stuff), and I thought that was worth it. $25 for a game this mature with so many bugs? I'd honestly be a bit reluctant. $60? Not so much.

I have had Ark for PC for about a week and a half now. I paid the new $67 price for the game including Scorched. I have had to uninstall and reinstall 3 times to get the game to continue to work. I have done hours of trouble shooting to get the game to open on unofficial servers because of the difficulties the neverending updates on the mods cause for your server.
Imagine this:  You play your main on a server that runs about 10 mods on it. Between the mod and Ark updates you are looking at 3 to 4 updates a day. You logon and your mods are automatically updated, but your server, which restarts 6 times a day just to keep things current, has not updated since the Mod has. I had very few complaints on xbox. I was already upset about having to pay $70 to play on another system, but now I have paid that money and I can't even play the game.
Perhaps Wildcard does not care about user generated content and unofficial servers, but there is no way the game survives without them.
When it takes half a month to raise a Giga, hours to tame things, etc and the majority of people don't have 8 hours a day to devote continuously to ark, how much of your possible customer base are you simply ignoring?
I want to know the mod updating system is a priority to be fixed, or I want my money back.

Smooth and fun combat

Tons of weapons to choose from
Regular updates
Good storylines
Responsive developers
Beautiful graphics

Devs give out large amounts of platinum (F2P currency) very often
Massive amounts of FREE customization
Decent new player tutorial and progression route
Somewhat "solo friendly" as 99% of content -can- be soloed (though you will receive less XP overall due to less enemies)
Cons:
There is a lot of grinding/farming
RNG makes some items very annoying to get
"Prime access" cosmetics and packages are ridiculously priced
PvP is lacking and underpopulated
Has a few archaic systems that need to be looked at
Leads to lack of sleep
P2P-style "servers", making some missions laggy due to a bad host
Guilds (clans) are required in order to build all of the weapons/warframes
Deep endgame can become very difficult if you're not using certain weapons/warframes
Review written on November 25th 2016 during Update 19 "The War Within".

General overview: Fun slugfest! This is an FPS based on medieval warfare. The game is grounded in realistic representation (not a high fantasy game with magic and artifacts).
Graphics: You will be wiping bloody splatters off your face. You can almost smell the blood. Injuries are represented on models (although, it's just general view without particular noticeable wounds). Kills are graphic. Models can be decapitated, and limbs can be amputated. This type of graphical fidelity makes wins more satisfying.
Sounds: Sounds are rich and vibrant. You will hear screams and steel on steel sounds. Arrows will make a wooshing sound when they fly by your face. Both graphics and sounds create an emersive experience.
Gameplay: There is a nice variety of weapons. Although, due to the nature of conflict they all feel similar. Weapons do vary in 3 different characteristics. There are both melee as well as range weapons. There is a variety of special weapons also. There are a couple of different modes ranging from free for all, team deathmatch and team based objectives driven mode. Combat is skill based. Although, all too often it gets too chaotic to effectively utilize blocking and striking techniques. There is a good balance between melee and ranged weapons. The game does everything good, but nothing particularly great. There is a robust online community (at least at this point - late 2013). You should have no difficulties finding games.
Verdict: Give this one a try if you are into online FPS and have an interest in medieval warfare and weapons. There is an expansion you can try if you really like this game.

It's not difficult to amass a small fortune of premium currency just by trading rare items.
Warframe also has the best community of any multiplayer game I've ever seen. Extremely new-player friendly. It's very rare to be berated or teased for not being skilled/knowledgable. Plus, if a new player asked for help (as I did several times) there's always a veteran hanging around in chat who's willing to help you out and give you some tips.
There's a lot more I love about this game- cool visuals, smooth gameplay, exciting combat - but I'm bored now and tired of typing.
Sooooo, get this game, play it for a bit, you'll probably like it. <3

So like, you get a sword/mace/axe/stick and you then run at other people and wag it in their body until the resulting entropy of sticking a large amount of foreign metal into their body causes them to expire. Sounds pretty simple, but takes a while to master and almost any fight can be won with enough skill. Takes a lot of time to get used to peoples reactions and you do better when you know what kind of player someone is, but there are always fatalities when you mistake a defensive player for an offensive one or vice versa. While it's definitely from an indie producer and all, I think the game does melee combat really well, in that it feels very fluid and parrying almost always feels like you actively contribute to not dying. The only downsides for this game are: Limited customization if you're a fan of that, you can get veteran helmets but otherwise your person looks the exact same as anyone else of the same class. There's been the occasional glitch I've experienced but it never persists too long. Upsides: Your personal skill influences how well you do, you can kill anyone no matter what they are using if you can outperform them. Your adrenaline really gets pumping when you manage to win a fight only to realize you're not finished with the other team. Objectives are not confusing although can be tedious at times, but everyone does them. Players are usually very sportsmanlike and will compliment their opponents and such.
Does this game have an end? I'm up to lvl 4000.

EDIT
They have since altered the archwing controls and I enjoy it more again. There have also been a few tweaks so far to "floaters" (the companions), and they even added an openworld like area with a massizve addition. It isn't what I was totally hoping for and doesn't extend the 4-man only size but I always appreciate the fact they are cosntantly adding loads of content and tweaking things for the player.

If you like the feeling of collecting things than this game will be fun. It does have a lot of grind to it but there's a decent amount to pick from. There seems to be minor updates all the time tweaking bits usually for the better which is nice.
Things I am hoping for:
Archwing controls were killed in the big archwing patch and I wish I had the option to go back because I loved archwing before and now it makes me seasick. I also wish there were more archwing alerts and Fissure archwing options for more variety. I also wish archwing had more missions in general (and that alerts told us it was true archwing).
I do wish there was more incentive to use the animals because I loved my Kavat then it got mega nerfed and now I never use it cause it really has no purpose but they look cool (same with the Kubrows).
I also wish there were some open world bits so I could wonder around seeing other people or the ability to dock ships on the guild hall or just change my spawn point to be in the guild hall and have the ability to build the stations we have access to on the ship so we can hang out between missions together.
While playing alone I wish all my stuff would get XP like it does in group (even if it was a fraction of the amount it gets in a group).
And the biggest likely never to happen wish is 5-6 man squads or mission options because we are always stuck with the odd person or 2 out which totally blows.
Having said all that, I do love this game as it has nice visuals and a lot to do for many hours and as it is free there really isnt a reason not to try it. Originally game was okay, and liked it, albeit a bit repetitive, shallow, and bare-bones kind of empty.
However, I've now uninstalled this game and refuse to keep supporting shady developers such as this. Early-Access is a business-deal promise, that the consumer promises to put up the money for the product, so long as the developers continue to develop and flesh out the products.
These developers have grossly violated and manipulated that promise. It seems the devs went ahead, and took the money paid for this product, and rather than use it to keep developing THIS game, they chose to use said money to develop a "paid-DLC" with all sorts of "extra awesome features", and then had the gall to come forward, with this "project" and thank the early-supporters, but inform them that if they wanted the fruition of their initial-investment, it'd cost them an additional $19.99 for a seperate and price-tagged DLC, when the original game isn't even finished, rather bare-bones, and gets mind-numbingly a tad boring after a bit.
Granted, I loved being able to hunt/tame/train dinos, I loved being able to build mutliple bases, I love the fact you can go fishing in the game, and some (myself included) like the multiplayer aspect. But that's about all the base-game, originally priced $29.99 gets you. If you want the "guts of the game", that'll cost you another $20 on top of the original promise.
So ultimately the devs ROBBED us early-adopters to fund their special dev-team to make this other content, just to charge us again, while never fulfilling the original contract/promise. Absolutely disgusting, ridiculous, and one of the giant banes that's bringing down the gaming-industry, and why so many gamers feel anxious/cautious about seriously believing what devs claim, promise, and plan for "their game".
Bottom-line... do yourself a favor, don't buy this money-trap, and check out one of the plethora of other decent survival games out there. Some might even have dinosaur-mods, especially in the upcoming future, to try to pave over the blemish this game leaves on the community!
PS - Forgot to add, base-game still hasn't even been properly optimized, so it runs like horse-dung even on beastly machines. Poor processor/core utilization, poor memory-handling, and massively obnoxious graphic-load brunt (seriously, look it up, there's full fledged extensive guides on just how to get "average" FPS in this game!). Not to mention all the many bugs and glitches, like disappearing dinos, dinos and/or your character glitching through the world, etc, etc, etc, etc...
In Conclusion, best game ever...not

- Tameable/Rideable Dinosaurs
- Good Map Variety & Size
- Real-Time Weather & Day & Night Cycle
- Good Dinosaur Variety (Carnivores, Herbivores, and Omnivores; Land-Based, Flying, and Swimming)

- Weapon Variety & Good Combat System
- Modable
Cons:
- Early Access (Tons of Bugs, Poor Optimization, Connection Issues, etc.)
- $59.99 Pricetag
- Low Server Capacity/Availability
- Constant Crashing Issues
- Little-to-No Mod Support
- Repetitive
- More Fun with Friends
- In-Game Server & Mod Downloads/Updates Take Forever
Take what you will from my review. I'm just disgusted at the new pricetag.

Alright, I'm gonna say, this game is hella fun with friends. I really enjoy just messing around and trying to survive. However, that is the only good thing I can say so far.
Let's start right out by announcing the elephant in the room, this game is NOT worth 60 dollars. The head developer even said so himself on his Twitter acc. The price jump is flat out greed by the publisher. Also not to mention this game's horrendous optimization. I have a GTX 1080 Founders edition with an Intel i7 6700k, as well as 32GBs of RAM and i cant even run this game on medium - high. This game still has a long way to go before its perfect, and the fact that full release is only a few weeks away really scares me cuz they need to do A LOT of work.
As stated before, the 60 dollar price tag is outrageous, or "♥♥♥♥ing outrageous" if you want me to quote the developer's own words. Also add on top the 20 dollar DLC if you want to pick that up, making your total a whopping 80 dollars for a very unfinished product atm. This game is absolutely not worth the price. AAA price for an indie title is never really worth it unless it is a godly game. A 30 dollar price tag would be much more appropriate. I reccommend waiting till a sale (which probably wont be for a while)
I will say, this game has it's moments, it's very fun when youre running from a dino or trying to take on and tame one, but unless youre playing singleplayer or a private server, the MP is terrible. Multiple servers have massive tribes established on them that their sole purpose is to just run around and kill new players. So if you are going to pick up this game, the MP atm is definitely not one of it's strong points.
All in all, I am not reccommending this game in it's current state. The price, optimization, multiplayer, all parts that play a major role in a game's value, are just too outrageous. Also, the gameplay in this, it's like any other survival game, you get wood, you get stone, you make tools, you advance. The only thing this has over other survival games are dinosaurs, and a nice leveling system, but those two things alone are not enough to reccommend this game.
P.S. I have more hours on this game, I used to use a friends account cuz I never wanted to buy this game because I used to have a worse PC and could never run it

This game has been close to my heart for the past 4 to 5 years so much that I have spent 1724 hours of my life on this game but at its current state i can only recommend it to new players who are only going to play the game for maybe a month or two, I say that with a straight face unlike my profile picture because my friend who had only been playing for a few months already gave up on the game. Now let me explain why this game has gone from #1 to #13 in my favorite games list. I was extremely passionate about this game because I thought it had amazing potential but they are slowly destroying that potential.
-There is no endgame
-There are no benefits or rewards to being an older/more experienced player(It seems they dont care about the older community because they have only been making content for the new players coming in with rewards that mean nothing to the older playerbase and its been like that for the past 1 to 2 years)
-Most of the games content is repeating missions for resources
-Most Items are extremely expensive because resources drop in small amounts and building them require a hefty amount of them
-They dont update or fix bugs in content that only a small part of the player base play(I'm talking about Raids/Trials)
-Bugs are extemely common(You could experience one or more everyother game)
In the end this is their game and they can do whatever they want with it but I spent this time to write this review because I once was extremely passionate about this game and it is bleeding right now. Other than these reasons and my personal experiences this game has a strong "skeleton" but the rest of the space is being wasted.

Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ is this game fun.  But it's definitely a niche market.  Not only is it a shooter, but melee is frantic paced.   The kind where it's fun to win but sucky to get killed one tenth of a second after your initial charge into the fray.
Archery is as hard as balls (only ever effective at long range when the enemy doesn't see you), but also annoying for anyone on the receiving end.  Vangaurd is probably the most imbalanced, able to get 2 kills in one swing.
The game has several interesting modes such as objective, the timeless king of the hill, death match, resource (sort of, highest score wins before highest deaths losing), FFA death match and time attack (I think), and the current maps are fairly unique.  Avatar emotes are well varied and don't really ever get old  - always will there be the volley of warcries with each extended sprint before the fray, and the appropriate laughter that comes after getting speared or having your head asploded with a mace - teabagging is less common, probably for that reason alone!
One on one duels, while very fun indeed (probably this game's most major selling point and the reason why they were so common in real life around this period) aren't as common as you'd think - naturally, when there's lots of players on  a map, people are going to mob up, yet simply charging in still presents a disadvantage.  You have to aim your weapon and aim your block.  Hence, players tend to be cautious - adjusting their swings.  In mobs, this still presents the risk of friendly fire - and people will always be mad for it (just like people are always mad at archers, but not vanguards; I guess vanguards are still thought of as cool).
For a big guy with a reach weapon, one swing makes everyone dash for cover, while a lighter attacker is going to be bobbing and weaving about, laying into the enemy whenever possible.  Circle strafing is a challenge, since movement isn't as floaty as you'd find in a game like halo or even gears of war (which has been described as 'magnetic' in the past); anyway, 'floaty' is the verb I'm going for, so try to imagine that.  Chivalry involves less of it.  Simply shifting slightly to the left is enough to screw up an attacker's cunning thrust or a vanguard's mighty charge.
Current Rating stands at:  8/10
For me, this game has a lot of replayability.  Simply having torn banner studios add in a few new weapons (there's many stemming from the early to late 13th-15th century vague time period reflected in this game's setting) that could create endless new strategies.

Lowered rating, because the game is still very punishing to noobs and really, anyone that doesn't have their game on.  On the very negative side of things, I was presented with a lot of connection issues involving laggy gameplay and games simply not showing up on the selection screen.  Rejoining or rebooting the game fixed the latter issue.
Players can get away with a bit of team killing mischief and it can be confusing figuring out how to ban them until you know where they are - banning involves a vote from all players, but the majority vote system prevents any real 'tyranny through democracy' issues in even low population games (most require 55% voting yes to get someone banned from a game rather than 50 or 40 percent).   I haven't found any bugs yet.
Server settings offer quite a bit of customization as far as I can tell, which might allow hosts to cripple certain players favouring certain play styles.  For no particular reason, I found that weapon upgrades can be disabled on some games - wasting the dagger kills I was earning.
Anyway, that's all for now.

This game transports almost every aspect of a contemporary first person shooter style game back through time, to the age of sword and steel.  The multiple style game settings include free for all, providing limitless bloodshed; Team objective, which is centered around working with your fellow brethren to unify as one, to attack or defend a specific point on one of the many highly detailed maps which the game has to offer; Team deathmatch pits each faction against one another en mass, proceeding to cut one another down until there are only the victors who stand; Deul servers, providing opportunities to allow you to develop your pvp skills, and hopefully much more content to come. The game is played from one of three perspectives, which allows you to find the best angle to watch as you decapitate your opposition. The tutorial is designed well enough to prepare you for your first battle, but only the seasoned warriors will rise to the top of the ranks. All in all Chivalry is a well designed game, based around a well thought out concept; I would highly recommend checking out some of the in game footage, and the trailer to see if you're truly ready for such an epic game.

Sadly, after the recent price increase I feel I have to warn prospective buyers away from this game.
ARK IS NOT WORTH $70
Pvp is still completely exploitable by glitches. Ddosing tribes run most of the servers and are not subject to any punishment for their actions (for reference, my current server is on its 4th straight day of sustained ddos attacks and this is pretty typical).
Map glitches can kill your dinos or have them fall through the map and be unrecoverable, which is just swell after you spend 6 hours taming them.
If WC decided to enforce fair play rules on their servers Ark would be in a great place and I might even say it's worth the AAA price. But as it stands right now, please, wait until you hear that WC has started to enforce their own rules, and/or region locked their servers before you fork over that kind of money for an unplayable game.
p.s. I wonder if WC hiked the price in advance of starting some cheating enforcement. That way if they ban people, those people will have to pay doubel to buy new accounts. If that is the case then I am all for the price increase.

Probably the best sandbox survival game on Steam (The Forest being a close second) in my opinion.
Pros:
- An insane amount of rewarding exploration across The Island, The Center, Ragnarok and Scorched Earth.
- Over 100 different dinosaurs, animals and mythological creatures, mostly tamable.
- There are no pointless tames, they all have unique abilities which can benefit you, your tribe and settlement.
- Excellent crafting and building system with very little restraint.
- One of the most immersive environments and gameplay I've experienced ever!
- The Mantis is an absolute badass!
Cons:
- People do play this game, using the controversial 'server hopping' options made available by the developers, purely to ruin it for everyone else. Once wasted 200hrs building a fortress only for some japanese kid who wasn't native to the server to destroy it overnight and take everything I worked hard for - at this point I stopped playing online. Devastating.
- Bad optimisation throughout the early access period and still experiencing memory leak issues now that causes the game to crash unexplainably.
- People do take this game WAY too seriously... maybe go outside now and again eh?
Personal highlights:
- When I quit the server I was playing on I gave my last remaining tames to a neighbour tribe who had helped me rebuild a base after a 'jap attack,' accidentally did it wrong and unleashed a lvl.200+ Sabertooth set to kill on their encampment, rather than a friendly tame gift... oops! (logged off forever shortly after that!)
- Stealing Wyvern eggs on Scorched Earth is incredibly difficult, very monotonous but when it's born and grown, very rewarding!
- All the assistance I recieved from a Tribe on my server when I first started playing, rather than being killed endlessly until I chose a different server to play on - not everyone is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, if you're not an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!
Conclusion:
Should have bought it during early access if you're thinking about it, don't buy it full price although you probably wouldn't regret it after 300+ hours - wait for a sale, don't hesitate, don't give up after you get killed endlessly in the first few sessions - which will happen!
Pro Tip: Watch a few YouTube videos before you start, learn the basics.

I'll start by saying it's a little rough around the edges currently in terms of polish, however as a total package, Chivalry is a really nice multiplayer game— especially for fans of the medieval theme.
Like many great multiplayer games out there, Chivalry is something that's easy enough to pick up, but hard to master.  Combat in this game is deceptively deep, which proved to be a pleasant (albeit frustrating initially) surprise to me based on my premature impressions.  Going into a fight flailing a weapon won't cut it in most situations.  Timing plays a huge part both offensively and defensively, and learning how to play the different classes and effectively utilizing and countering each weapon in the arsenal  is imperative to success.
So if you're a fan of multiplayer combat games and are looking for something fresh and unique from your everyday shooter, Chivalry is a good buy, and something that can provide countless hours of entertainment with the promise of free content patches in the future as well.

Hands down the best Free-to-play game of 2016.
For reference, I've spent roughly $150 on this game collectively since I started playing in 2014.
Pros:
Smooth and fun combat
Dozens of Warframes (Classes) to play as
Tons of weapons to choose from
Regular updates
Good storylines
Responsive developers
Beautiful graphics
Easily playable for an hour or ten
Everything is attainable via in-game means (Excluding a handful of "tenno-gen" cosmetics that can only be bought due to -Steam's- own policies.
Devs give out large amounts of platinum (F2P currency) very often
Massive amounts of FREE customization
Decent new player tutorial and progression route
Somewhat "solo friendly" as 99% of content -can- be soloed (though you will receive less XP overall due to less enemies)
Cons:
There is a lot of grinding/farming
RNG makes some items very annoying to get
"Prime access" cosmetics and packages are ridiculously priced
PvP is lacking and underpopulated
Has a few archaic systems that need to be looked at
Leads to lack of sleep
P2P-style "servers", making some missions laggy due to a bad host
Guilds (clans) are required in order to build all of the weapons/warframes
Deep endgame can become very difficult if you're not using certain weapons/warframes
Review written on November 25th 2016 during Update 19 "The War Within".

Well with nearly 15 hours in this game I think it's time to write a review/reccomendation.
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare has a wonderful concept, one I have been wanting to see for some time, a multiplayer medieval game. However I would not reccomend this game if you are looking for that.
Chivalry: Medieval Warfare has possibly the worst weapon and combat systems I have seen in any game. Newer players are nearly unable to kill those with weapons of a higher tier than theirs, and as such, are unable to level up their own weapons to make the gameplay even again.
The combat system amazes me. How a developer can mess up combat this badly using UDK is phenomenal. They have this wonderful system going, where an unarmed man wearing leather and chainmail can punch a fully armored knight to death, and the knight is not able to even raise his weapon in defence. Every class has at least one weapon that is totally overpowered(Jav/heavyxbow for archer, tier 3 halbard for vanguard, maces for man at arms, and hammers for knights) These weapons are basically uncounterable, unless you have perfect timing or are boxing them, rendering them unable to even block or fight back.

After playing ark for almost 300 hours I have been able to form a pretty solid opinion on the game.  First off this was the first game I played of the survival and building type.  So why did I purchase the game in the first place...There is a simple answer to that.....My love of Dinosaurs.  I am not interested in playing a game on an open world server and allowing some muppet with a cheat code to ruin the hours I have put in to building a character and a base in a matter of seconds.  However when I saw the level of detail on the animals I thought nah I am having that.
So having established I haven't played online with other people in an open world game, you may ask why bother... again a simple answer is I can set up a server of my own and only allow people I want in the game.  Or if I prefer I can set up a single player game... sweet.... so we have the reason why out the way.
Lets break down the game to areas that may interest you.. How easy is the server setup... well very go to the host a game or join a game and decide on what you want to do. if joining a game find a server for you and join away... If hosting a game you will be asked to set the rules of the server and map you wish to load, various different settings for the game settings, like length of night time, how much resources you gather at any time, the speed in which you need food and water and how long it will take to tame the animals then you will be asked if its a private server , give it a name and if so to assign a password. presto you're done.
Game controls...well that's a difficult one to answer , if you have played this style of game before then you will be used to  the gather this and that to make the thing you need. For those of us that have never played this type of game before, the learning curve is a steep one.  However once you understand the whole thing then yes it becomes second nature.  I personally find the normal settings of the game lead to a boring and long winded slog to get anywhere.  So if like me you like you game to run at a more enjoyable rate just tweak those server settings until you are happy.  Once you have your settings to your liking and the game is moving along then it becomes interesting.
One of the first things you will notice is this game like real life is not one that starts you off at an easy level and walks you through a selection of tasks... nope ... This game plops you in a random spawn point on a beach or in the treeline of a forest.  One thing for sure is that everything in the game is at various levels and if you happen to spawn next to a hungry dino, yeah you are on the menu. So quickly move and re-con the area you are in and start gathering stones, sticks and berries, trust me you're going to need em.  One you have established a base camp and have built a house and placed a bed in there then the random spawn point is not an issue.  Once a bed is securely placed this becomes your main spawn location, if you manage to build other base camps with beds in them when you die (and you will die) then you will be give the option of a random span point or spawn at one of your base camps....
All the animals in the game are at various levels and like you they do level up.  Some of them are harmless  others however not so much.  Some just ignor you unless you tick them off and then they attack, others well they just see you as a snack. Learn your animals, and do it as quickly as possible.  One hint I will drop here is don't always expect the big animals to be the nasty buggers... Look out for ant nests they are dangerous as you normally don't see them until it's to late and your sitting on one.
Everyone wants to ride a dino or fly a pterosaur, and there are allot in the game to choose from most of which can be tamed.  There is a small handful of animals you can't ride or fly on but that is a self explanatory due to their size.  Taming a dino can take hours (Yes that is real hours and not game hours ) and it can take allot of work, if you're on your own. If working in a team it will take some serious team work to train some of the larger animals.
The animals on the whole are really impressive, I am personally not really interested in the made up ones like the dragons , giant King Kong style gorilla or some of the over the top sized spiders for me it ruins the pleasure of the game.  The stuff that is based on real dinosaurs though is why I got the game.  I have to say that the first time you round a corner and come face to face with a T-Rex is just amazing, scary as hell but amazing none the less.
The sound in the game is ok, some great animal sounds, nice sound effect when you go from one area to the next, for example when on the beach you are treated to the sounds of crashing waves and seagulls, in the swamps sounds of crickets and frogs, in the forest different howling and bird calls and up in the mountains the sounds of wolfs and the wind.  On top of that you have the different dinosaur sounds and each type of animal has its own call..Again get to know these sounds as they may be the difference of you getting to safety or becoming a side order of a dinos lunch.
Whilst this has been a bit of a long review, I feel that there are two areas I still need to cover , the first being the graphics.  Ark is just unbelievable to look at, the large lush areas of open grass land to the packed tree lines of the forest.  This game looks out of this world.  On a computer with some power behind it and a graphics card to do the game justice then this is a show stopper.  It's incredible to see the animations of the dinosaurs, all of which move very realistically.  Some of the animals could do with a few more frames when turning corners or attacking but that's a minor niggle.
The final thing I need to mention is that the game even though it has now gone gold still has a couple of issues with a random crash if you try and go around the maps from a certain direction or if you move from one area of the map to another and turn around to come back to quickly the game just dumps you out to windows and looses what ever you did since the last save.  This for me spoilt the game and I started again on a different map, which still does it every now and then but not as often.  There is sadly still an issue with the sky and it reflecting back a white ghosting outline of what ever is one the screen, which I am hoping that they get sorted as you have to currently turn off some of the settings in the game to get rid of this problem but then that means that you are not getting the best from the game, so for me I put up with the white ghosting but it can become distracting at times.
So although not a perfect game, it is still really enjoyable. Would I recommend it to other people? No doubt about it of course I would, after pointing out the few problems that it has I am sure anyone with a love of dinosaurs will enjoy this game.  For those of you that like building stuff whilst it is good, it doesn't have the scope of building materials like games such as Minecraft, Creativerse, or Sky Saga. However what is there is good for the game after all, it's about the dinos more than anything....  Go on give it a go, it's awesome.

While it's true that this is an idle game, there is an insane amount of subtlety to it.
You start by clicking a bunch. You quickly move on to the game playing for you (thus the idle genre). You will struggle to raise the levels of your heroes until you grind to a halt. You then ascend, gain hero souls, summon ancients and raise the levels of your heroes and grind on some more.
I was incredibly suprised how much there is to this game.

While the concept is entertaining, there are others out there that do it better.  Rust and Age of Conan just to name a couple.  The building mechanics are choppy and aggrevating to access and the combat is easy enough if you stay behind or to the side of the larger Dino's.  Overall not worth the price, especially now that they've increased the price, and the game is still in Early Access.  They did this before with the scorched earth DLC that you had to pay for, while the game was in EA.  Don't put out DLC until you finish the game, unless you are exceedingly greedy.

I was waiting a moment to write a nice review for my most beloved game in my library, but I could never convince myself that had the courage, or time for it. But after seeing all this negativity because of the price tag, I had to stand up for the creators of this game.
Now sit down kid, I'm going to tell you a story and it won't be brief.
I had ark, at the first week of its release, at that point, I was playing Reign of Kings. I'm pretty much of a decent builder so people used to rent me for building castles etc. At the release of ark to public, most of my friends flocked to it, I was never into dinosaurs, I really didn't like the concept. After getting bored in my half dead server, I had to give it a go and had it.
My first attempt on game was, trying to build a thatch house of 1x1. I'm pretty much of a passive player, I simply can't pvp. I got shrekt at minute one by dangling naked people. It was so early that every server was x1 gather rate. Game was HARD. Everything was hard. Getting a flying animal was most likely to be impossible. I loved it. It was pure survival. The randomness of it charmed me. Nothing was static like we see in other games, everything was on prowl, moving, the map was ALIVE. When you see something, you knew that in a blink of an eye, it could be taken or killed by others. Building was expensive, and it required a teamwork. Gathering metal was impossible for a passive player, you had to get into a cave or climb an equally dangerous mountain. I chose cave because i was pretty much of a retard. The first time Ive seen the giant snake, screamed like a girl with my friend. It was pretty much one of the best moments I had in any game. Game was exciting, frightening and full of suprises. It was hard on my machine, so I could only afford medium low settings for a 30-40 fps with my gtx670M, which was better than other games of the same genre.
After a while of constant struggle, frustration of dying and losing everything, we have seen that unofficial servers had the ability to increase the gather rates. So we joined a x5 server, it was even better. Metal was still impossible for me and for my loser friends. But wood was good enough. Taming hours were insanely high, but you felt like you achieved something in return. Everything was functional. Everything you invest in ark was a help in return, Ive never seen that in any other game. They were mostly dropping bad loots. Taming, riding, these were exceptionally good.
The ERA of MODDING, now this is where everything started to become, BETTER. Ark was very strong on modding side and still is. But the introduction of mods, and the quality of the modders (Hey every modder, I love you all) this game "transcended" into another dimension of gaming. We had everything, they made flyer tame and metal gather easier, after that Ive become admin in various servers since my builds were highly commended. Ive seen that the game had so much to offer. The building system of this game is UNIQUE. Ive played pretty much every game with building option in it. I've never had the opportunity to be so versatile and so independant of rules at buildng in any other game. Ive built pyramids, giant castles, trade ports, cities, battleships, towers, cathedrals, science bases, island bases, sky bases, underwater bases all with unique and different look EVERY SINGLE TIME. Now this is something, that I would pay with everything I had. It tought me alot.
Pretty much later, game had its first dlc, as scorching earth. It had some bad reviews because of the weirdo money hoarder people who cannot appreciate a good game when they see it. Although I was having so much fun, I didnt even blink while buying it. And voila, its ark in a whole new perspective, I felt like I returned back to vanilla in a much harsher and cruel way, it was amazing. It worth every penny I gave. Dragons, Giants, Sandstorms, struggle for water. What a DLC it was, full of content. Thats a DLC you would like when you are paying for it. It wasn't some skins or something that was taken away from vanilla game just to be sold. It was ARK in a different level.
Than we ve seen The Center map. Man. Which other game actually took a mod, and made it official with paying for it. I've never seen such a good development strategy, executed this well. The center was okay, It was free. I just couldnt find some good spots for my taste to build so I stuck with my vanilla island map or the scorched earth in that matter.
Finally reaching to the end, now we have this uncountable amount of mods, paid mods, official mods like primitive+ and everything ark has become a sandbox that you can do WHATEVER you want. If youd dont like an aspect of it, you can remove it, or you can add if you want anything. This game is the ultimate sandbox, and the developpers should be commended for their effort of patching pretty much EVERYSINGLE DAY.
This game had so many patches for bugs and content that as an admin I was pretty sick of patching my server everyday. People were sick that the game was getting patched this fast. Have you ever heard it in any other company before? I did not. And it was not patches of 1 or two, every patch was a patch that we asked for. I cannot even keep the track of dinos we have in game. Probably most of the games in web dont even have this many unique characters in whole singleplayer campaign of theirs and this game is online.
In the end,
To my fellow ark players who comment negative for price tag.
-I've seen most of you had below 1000 hours. Below 1000 hours, you cannot assume that you totally explored this game, therefore your review is pretty much trolley at this point.
-Recognize that this game had the greatest of developments of our last 5 years in gaming history. This game was a baby and it has matured in front of our eyes. We should be greatful that we have such dedicated development who worked day and night to fix problems, add content and listen to our nonesense.
-If you already have the game, why are you complaining about it's price?
-If you do not have the game, why did you not buy it 1 week ago at a VERY low price in steamsale, or any other sale before that. This game was forever in sale.
-Think twice before who you are going to discourage while we have developpers like EA, Bioware, Ubisoft who delivers unfinished games with no mod support and incompetent community assist.
-This game is more AAA than any other AAA games we ever had. It may not be supported by a large benefactor, but it doesnt define how good this game has become after the proper amount of development time.
To my beloved newcomers and people who are willing to buy ARK,
-As Ive mentioned above in my small story, this game has the potential to become whatever you want.
-You can build anything
-You can tame anything, and ride it with few exceptions(yeah I wanted to ride the snek aswell)
-Game has aerial, ground and naval perspective.
-You don't like to be skrewed like me in pvp? go PVE or RP, game has alot of mods that allows people to enjoy it.
-You dont like guns and tech, go for primitive+ mod.
-You dont like dinos? Disable taming them and let people struggle with puny guns and spears.
-Whatever you do not like, can be disabled, can be removed, or can be altered.
-Whatever you like can be modded, added, enabled. From new creatures to new buildings, from non existant skills (yes there is a mod that allows you to bend elements like avatar) to guns weapons armor, maps play styles air conditions.
This game, deserves the price tag it had and it deserves whatever price tag it may have. If you dont like the game, do not play it that's okay, but in my opinion, buy it, so you can encourage these kind and hard working developpers to feel like they made the right thing. Or just persuade the other incompetent half job developpers in other companies (mostly AAA ones) to see that, hardwork and attention wins more than milking series.
ARK, you will always be my beloved.

I first grabbed this a couple years ago in August when v205 was the new hotness.  I played a hundred hours or so, exploring, taming & killing stuff, and building a base.  Recently came back in summer 2017 (v258), and so much has changed.  Sure, The Island is recognizable, but so much is different that it's like learning how to play all over again.  There are new items, new dinos, and new places.  New systems were put into place, and old ones refined/upgraded.
This is all on top of a core gameplay loop which is pretty damn fun.  It's similar to other survival-sandbox games, with building and maintaining a base from materials you've harvested from the environment.  Meanwhile, that environment is trying to kill you.  It does so passively with weather and temperature extremes, but it also does it actively in the form of dinosaurs.  That makes all the difference.
You can tame dinosaurs for defense, mobility, and labor (many dinos are better harvesters than you).  You can breed those dinos to make more awesome dinos that you raised from eggs.  Who needs automated turrets when you have a base defended by patrolling rexes (note: you can also have turrets)?  You like riding huge dinos into combat?  ARK has that.  Maybe you want to command a swarm of little dinos.  ARK has that.  Maybe you need to fly around above your enemies, and shoot them from the back of your flying dino (warning: they shoot back).  ARK has that, too.
And that doesn't even get into the 'endgame' of cave delving, summoning boss monsters, and PvP.  Watch a stream, see if it's your thing.
Pros:
+ Dinos, in all shapes and sizes
+ Crafting & Base-building
+ Shooting, hacking, and punching stuff
+ Exploration
+ Robust server support
+ Beautiful graphics
Cons:
- Huge timesink if you play on a server with the default settings (hint: don't do this)
- Being murdered while logged out of a PvP server (hint: don't play PvP if you don't wanna be murdered)
- Poor optimization.  Low framerates even with awesome hardware
- Whiny community

Only exception to this are the cosmetics (prime accessories) that get included in Prime Access. As of the time of this review, the latest Prime Warframe, Valkyr, is now for sale. Warframe used to be a great way to have fun with some friends while playing a challenging co-op game.
But after an endless series of 'content' patches, the game is in the least fun state it's ever known.
Grinding is an understatement for what you'll be doing in this game. If you aren't a standing veteran, or willing to dump a sizeable amount of money into buying platinum, you'll be playing the same endless series of thoroughly boring missions, just to get ONE piece of an item. Repeat until you get the final pieces for your item. Oh, you wanted to BUILD that item? Too bad, now you have to grind for special mats that will only be rewarded in an alert, or drop in an area you don't have unlocked yet. Want to unlock that area for those special mats for that item you want to build? Well, I hope you enjoying running a whole bunch of missions you won't enjoy.
So you finally unlocked that mission that drops the thing you need, to make the item you want. Well, now you gotta run that mission 10 or 15 times to get the amount of material you need for your fancy gun. You run the missions, get the mats, and FINALLY have the chance to build that fancy gun.
Well it's not over yet. Now you have to wait for the gun to finish building. It's only 12 hours tenno, you can go grind some MORE missions while you wait! Or..... you could just spend some of that platinum to get the gun right away...
But for the sake of argument let's say you've actually managed to build your gun without getting mad. Good job, patience is a virtue.
BUT WAIT! You aren't done yet with that grind tenno. Oh no. Now you have to get MODS! You didn't honestly think the grind for that crappy shotgun was the worst you were going to deal with, did you?
This is all before the latest few patches that managed to make the various grinds LONGER AND MORE RANDOM.
Do not give DE your money or your time. You WILL regret it.

ARK is a good game. It could be polished more, but the progression feels good and the graphics are fantastic. I've played the game off-and-on for a while, it seems like I always get to a certain point then get stuck. But that definitely doesn't mean it's a bad or boring game, so many people love it.
Now addressing the elephant in the room, Dino taming! I haven't played a game that has a taming system like this, especially not with dinosaurs. Tame a Pteranodon and fly the skies, or a Trike to take on aggressors. This game is especially good with a group of friends. I always made the mistake of playing with a small group of 2-3 people, but getting a squad of 6 people can be amazing. The progression will be faster, dino taming easier, and defending you base from hostile dinos will be much more fun. Also, getting a group of people on Trikes or Raptors and attacking a T-rex is really an experience.
I definitely recommend this game, it's fun and immersive. Get some friends, find an unofficial server with an xp multiplyer of your liking, and have a good time!

Alrighty, this one is a little tricky. Not because I'm not sure of the game, but because I'm not sure of YOU. Don't take that the wrong way. It's just that Warframe lies in the same review class as Dark Souls. Which is to say, I love it, but I'm heartely aware of the fact that a lot of people wont. It's a challenge. Not at first, but as you progress, it gets pretty tough. It's not a game you'll really enjoy playing solo, either. This game was built from the ground up to be played co op. Even if it's just with ONE friend, it's far better than solo. And last but not least, and I guess this is actually the biggest gripe for a lot of people... it's a grind. I mean its a BIG grind. A bunch of the gear is locked behind RNG lootcrates called Relics, and getting the item you want could take you a long time. We're talking weeks here.
So those are the negatives, the elements of the game that could stop people from enjoying the game. On to the positives.
This game WILL make you feel like a badass. I don't care how you play shooters. You could be a run'n'gun style of gamer, you could be an assassin, you could be a sniper or a brute. Don't care, does not matter, this game WILL cater to you. At its core, Warframe is fast, furious, and brutal. You feel every hit, and you grin every time you put down an enemy, and OH BOY are there a lot of them. The sharp, satisfying gunplay combines beautifuly with the free flowing parkour system to provide a style of gameplay I've NEVER got from another game. Sure as hell not from a F2P.
And this game IS F2P. Sure, there's an in game shop. Sure, you'll get things a LOT quicker if you're willing to shell out real cash, but the feeling of satisfaction you get from putting that badass new gun together yourself is indescribable.  Now, certainly, there's a PvP element, and I suppose people who buy the latest, most powerful gear might have an advantage. I can't comment though, I don't play the PvP. Its such a tiny element I've never even looked at it.
Honestly, if you have even a single thought that this game looks good, download it. I swear, you'll get something out of it. And hell, it's free, whatve you got to lose?
TL;DR
It's free, it's awesome. Play it.
