I will start with the fact that I have enjoyed a lot of experiences with the game.  I enjoy playing games with my friends and tend to enjoy building aspects of open world games.  There have been a lot of really fun times raising dinos, and doing caves/bosses.
That being said this game is not worth almost any money, and I do not recommend it for anybody.  I play only on official server,  and the hours of timeouts that have killed dinos that we have spent DAYS raising, the glitchy places on the map, the bad AI for tamed/wild dinos, the horrible loading times to render in buildings, and so many other crashes/disconnects/lag spikes cause more frustration and anger than I have had fun.  I do continue to play the game dispite some of these issues because I bought it as an early access game and most of these things are expected, and my friends continue to play it.  We are within a month of the release date they are building up to, however, and I have seen almost no positive change in any of these problems with the game.  The devs have added a bunch of content to the game, but have failed to address any of the problems that people have actually had with the mechanics of the game simply being broken.
There are also issues with the way the devs handle trying to balance the game.  Specifically the flying nerf they did that might have actually reduced one play style that was possibly overpowered and utilized in PVP.  Their fix to the situation was to basically make the dino that had been overpowered simply useless, along with adding more grind and slowing down an already almost unbearably slow, grindy game.
The boss difficulty levels also don't make any sense.  If you want to do any end game content you have to fight the bosses, but the entry level for the lowest tiered bosses are unrealistically high for any but really high already end game level tribes, or teams of a number of smaller tribed.  The problem with the high level of entry is that the rewards are almost negligable.  If you get a few tribes together to try to do the first boss (BM Gamma) you would have to complete it over 20 times (this is based on 3 tribes splitting the 10 element, and the 75 element cost) to make the first end game crafting station that is needed to make any of the end game gear.  The cost also doesn't go dramatically down from the crafting station either, so it's not like you can just save up for that, and then have access to cool gear afterward.  Also, because you can't use the tek gear in boss fights it does not make stepping up to the next teir of bosses any easier.
I did play on a private server previously and a number of these issues were'nt as prevelant, but that is just a smack in the face to those of us who prefer playing on the public official hosts.
If the devs address the bugs, and server stability issues I will come back and probably change this to a recommend rating unless they've totally messed up the game with unnecessary changes or make the problems with the game even worse.  Until that time, though, I can not recommend this game to anyone.

ARK is a pretty fun game, a Sandbox-ish open-world survival game based around Dinosaurs. This game caught my eye initially because as a kid I simply thought dinosaurs were awesome, and then I see this game, and I was like "wowie those are some good dinosaurs"
The game has a lot to like, but there is also a lot to dislike as well, so I'm gonna list them as Pros and Cons (some of which some people may disagree with, but I digress)
-Awesome Dinosaurs, each with their own stats and uses
-A huge open world, leaving much to explore
-You go from being a primitive caveman with sticks and stones to being a highly sophisticated individual with enough knowledge to build a huge base and tame even the fiercest of dinos with ease
-Awesome and challenging boss fights
-Beautiful graphics
-Devs are continuously working to make the game better
-You can transfer your character from one server to another if you want to
-You die a lot in the beginning
-Scorched Earth DLC map is pretty dang hard
-Dinos take a ridiculously long time to tame
-Most of the gameplay is a long grind of gathering resources and leveling up
-Almost all Public Servers are dominated by a select few tribes, meaning (in most cases) you're either part of the big tribe or you get destroyed
-People can transfer their Dinos and Items from one server to another
On official servers you can transfer your Character, Dinos and Items between servers, I believe just your character is fine, since leveling up is difficult in that game, but with dinos and items, Griefers or high level people from other servers can simply transfer all their powerful dinosaurs and their bombs over from their server to yours and blow you and your base up without giving you a chance to really fight back.

Everything I had hoped it would be and more. The combat is all but perfect. Hit detection is perfect as well as different damages based on areas of the body. You can chop off body parts which is super satisfying. The combat is simple but deep, with only a short time needed to understand but a long time to master. There are kicks, feints, ducking, blocking, different hits, and dodging. There are many different weapons and classes with their own unlockables to find your best playstyle suited for you. There isn't a ton to unlock which is actually liberating; you get to just enjoy the game without playing with a carrot on a stick like COD players. The gore is well done and the graphics are AMAZING. How an indie studio did this (thank you Unreal engine) amazes me. Just goes to show you don't need to make pixelated or low-budget 1990's graphics platformers just because you are an idie studio. Game has been on top 5 or top 10 on steam in sales last 3 weeks for a reason. Only multiplayer but well priced. The levels are intricate and varied. Some are small arenas, others have different levels and are large. Now the cons. The death traps are great ideas but only 1 level has them really and it seems too hard to utilize them. Would like to see that fleshed out and expanded a bit. There are many different game types which is a positive. There are however only a small number levels or so, for a multiplayer only game which can get tiring. What all but erases this is the makers said they are adding new weapons and levels for free because of the game success (gotta love awesome developers that care about their fans/community (Looking at you infinity ward, releasing 2 new maps and 2 old maps and nothing else for almost price of entire chivaly game)) The combat also always works and you feel like you get outplayed if you lose. Unless you get double or triple teamed which is just a casualty of the game but happens a lot. Nothing is more annoying than when you are rocking someone and their teamate kills you from behind. The makers are also adding duels which is awesome. Sometimes the combat is confusing how it works. You will get hit mid swing and it will stop you and the guy can attack 3 times before you attack one. But then you may hit him with a faster weapon and he still hits you afterward with a stronger weapon, which makes no sense. The progress system makes no sense. You have no clue how close you are to the next level or what it takes to level up. Some levels took me hours and others took me 30 minutes. There was a customization feature but there were no other options after default even after i was much higher level. That feature must not be implemented yet. The lack of customization does take fun away. All in all great game and support this developer. 8.5/10

Do you like ninjas? Space? Shooting things? Chopping things up? Feeling like a complete and utter badass? Well, Warfraem is the game for you!
Warframe is a very simple yet fun and addictive game where you play as the Tenno in their Warframes, which is essentially an exosuit, and you around like a ninja, shooting things up and completeing missions. It revolves highly around grinding, if you aren't a fan of grinding for materials and crafting items, I highly recommend you avoid this game. It has a HUGE grind. If you can look past that and can actually have fun with it, jump right in, the game constantly keeps you entertained with boss fights, waves of enemies, stealth missions, etc.
Each mission can be played with a maximum of four people, so grabbing a group of friends to play makes the game all the more enjoyable and entertaining. Having 4 robotic ninjas jumping around decapitating people is incredibly funny to see.
Overall, the game itself is great. If you can find yourself to look past the grind of it all, I highly recommend playing this game. Heck, it's free! Why not give it a shot anyway?

I played this game for a week last year. One of the worst expieriances I have had in a while. I wanted to have fun and for a small time I did. Butthe game is plagued with problems. These problems are sourced from all aspects of the game. Things like performance issues are just a small section of it. The problems exist in gameplay, buisness policies, and in you guessed it, optimization.
Let's talk about core gameplay. The core gameplay, is of a survival game. where you have two survival elements. man made tools and structures, and dinosaurs. The the implementation of this core gameplay has issues regarding time usage. This game requires hours of time to play. And I really do mean hours. Want to tame a dinosaur? Better clear your schedule for the next 5 hours. Resource gathering is also a pain, despite the use of dinosaurs, It can take hours to aqquire  the resource you want. That is if you can even get to the resource. I'm not suggesting the environment is the obstacle though. Its actually the player base that is the problem. Due to core design policies multiplayer can become ACTUALLY UNPLAYABLE. See, players will set up their bases ontop of resources pools, and prevent you from acessing it. Servers over time become incredibly hostile to newcomers. So why not choose a pve server then you may ask? Well, you can't. Not because the servers don't exist, It's because pve servers don't allow for the destruction of player made structures, or the ability to make structures within a certain vicinity of other player structures. What this causes, is for players to "reserve servers" by placing indestructable structures every few meters or so, accross spawn zones so that newcomers literally cannot build. ACTUALLY UNPLAYABLE. So, why not play on a pvpve server then? Well, prepare to get raided, becaue you will be, and it will suck everytime. You see, after a certain point, players become unkillable by basic and even more advanced means. So, you can't do public servers. Private servers just don't run. Which brings me to optimization.
Yeah, uh. who programmed this game? Because they have trouble with some of the most basic graphical functions. Object fade in and out on a pixilated mess. Textures are blurry even on the higest settings, foliage has issues. The point is the the game is unable to render even the most basic level of graphics without great difficulty. when I first played I was on a gtx 960. Not a high end card, but I wasn't running high end graphics either. Do not be fooled by the trailers. They are on the highest graphical settigns possible, and are likely not rendered in real time.
This team has a tendency to do that by the by. They have some very scummy buisness tactics. First they release a DLC BEFORE THE GAME IS RELEASED. That is unacceptable. That alone, makes this team the scum of the earth. I don't care about the semantics of early access. The game is not done. Finish your game before you try to get more money. Now they are putting the game at full price and it is still not done. Unacceptable. That is all this game is.

As of 2015
That's what it used to be when it came out, but not today. Because of various mechanic and balance changes, the game has been left heavily biased towards "competitive players" who will use absurd looking tactics such as jumping mid-strike to hit over your block or spinning around to perform attacks backwards, which alienates more casual players who just want to have some stereotype medieval action.
I used to adore this game, but it has been left a mess by gameplay meta tactics and weapons, which can only be matched by stooping to using the same tactics.
Many weapons, while usable with skill, will be heavily outclassed by blatantly better weapons by being longer, nearly equal in speed, and more damaging overall. So why not use those weapons if you'll do even better with the same amount of skill? Does two people sprinting in circles swinging messer swords backwards and jumping in the middle of it sound like a cool medieval fight? Note that this is very common in pubs.
Aside from gameplay, there are also other nitpicks such as future Objective Maps lacking "Go for the Objective!" voicelines for characters, while the original maps did and were great for adding to the experience and gravity of the situation.
Summarily, this game is a husk of what it used to be, and I won't be picking it back up if it stays like this. Who knows, perhaps it will change. If you love learning crazy mechanics and trying to one-up others in rapidly spinning and jumping, go ahead with this game. But if you want an actual medieval looking fight that you can just jump right into without commiting to learning all the meta; go play Mount & Blade.

The positives of the game are that it is vast and has a lot of things you can do to make yourself feel immersed. The negatives are that the game is nearly unplayable solo without heavily adjusting resource gains, taming speed, xp, etc. Luckily, you can adjust all of those figures with ease.
Recent complaint: Lately, people have been grabbing their pitchforks over the fact that ARK has received a price increase to $60; the cost of a finished, wholesome product. What people failed to realize is that the game and its content is still worth that price. For those that didn't read the Early Access information that was put out in June of 2015 (and is still readable), SW explicitly stated that once the game was finished, it would likely have an increased price, as the product would be done. One of their appeals to gamers was to buy it while it is in Early Access because it would cost less. SW now feels that a month from official release, that their product is finished enough to increase the price. For those that read the information 2 years ago, this is far from a surprise, and it is rather justified. The only people complaining about it are ungrateful, frugal gamers, and those that never paid any attention to what SW told them before picking the game up.

I bought Chivalry nearly a year ago when I had choppy 3G Internet. It worked, surprisingly, so I can safely say the netcode is good enough to compensate a reasonably bad connection (however, you'll still get those annoying dropouts that come with 3G and 4G -- don't expect to play competitively).
Internet aside, Chivalry is the most fun, most frustrating, and most intense melee combat game I've played in a long time. The combat feels incredibly good; the sound effects in this game are nothing short of amazing. When swords clash, you know they've clashed. When someone kills a dude, the gurgles and screams are almost chilling.
On the subject of sound, I should also mention the battlecry mechanic. Yes, there's a battlecry mechanic. While your character is running, you can press C by default to scream. Your character says random things such as "For Agatha!" or "Hrrrraaaaaarrrgh!" or "Hyaaangarblegrbselrdf." (Read that last one in Nigel Thornberry's voice, and that's about the right sound.) It's possibly one of the most amazing useless features in any game, though it certainly is kind of inspiring to hear an entire team screaming at once as they charge out into battle.
The graphics are nothing spectacular, but the game is slightly more demanding than you'd expect in that department. On a computer containing a GTX 570 and an i7 960 clocked at 3.2ghz, I sometimes get framerate drops down to the 40 in large battles (e.g. in 64- or some 32-player servers), which certainly isn't bad, but it's not a perfect 60 either.
The movement can feel clunky at times, as your characters will get stuck on odd geometry from time to time, but it's nothing game-breaking (unless you get killed while stuck -- then it's the most frustrating thing in the world and you'll never play this game again as you throw your monitor out the window).
On that note, I'll come back to that point I made in the beginning about frustration. Personally, I'm a calm gamer. I have yet to participate in any in-game name-calling, raging, or other such things. Chivalry can bring me to rage at times, and here's why: for a game so reliant on teamwork (at least in the objective modes), the support for on-the-go voice communication is absolutely dreadful. Sometimes voice chat just doesn't work on perfectly good microphones, and worse yet, the official servers have all-chat enabled by default. If you want to strategize with your team, you have to do it in team text chat, which takes much longer than speaking. Maybe I'm spoiled coming from Counter-Strike, but a team game should always support quick team communication in my mind.
If I was to ask for one thing added to this game, aside from more team objective maps, it would be better team support. This would include better voice chat, some sort of rank-based matchmaking system, and a better indicator of who's on your team. Currently, the two factions you can play as in objective modes are Agatha, blue, and Mason, red. When players get injured, they get their uniforms soaked in blood, and when you're close to death, your screen will become desaturated and everything will look roughly as brown and gray as Gears of War. So when that happens, it's hard to tell your team from your enemy, and that mechanic alone is responsible for hundreds of teamkills I've seen.
Despite its flaws, Chivalry is a ton of fun, and I definitely recommend it to anyone who likes the concept of fast-pased, frantic medieval melee combat (oh, and there's the archer class, so maybe not entirely melee).

There are also 2 main ways to play, idle and active. You can put all your bonuses into click damage or you can gain dps bonuses while idle, which activates after 60 seconds of no damage dealing clicks.
If you like powering up forever or leaving games to farm away or enjoy a stress free flash game, this is for you.

Here is my honest rating. You can decided what you think about it.
Pros:
- No pay2win (Well, not completely)
- Great story
- Wonderful graphics
- Runs great on AMD hardware (This is bloody brilliant!)
- Cloth and basic physics works without PhysX
- Great community
- The game is made with love
- The team is doing casual events on a regular base with livestreams
- The gameplay is great, the control of your player is good, you can do moves and bashes
- Many weapons, Warframes, Skins, Fashion, Mods and other stuff
- You can complete the game without any other players (I think it's possible)
- Great cinematic scenes and missions
Cons:
- Runs only on Windows
- "Fashionframe" (styling your character) is difficult without spending money
- They "killed" farming with the removing of the tower keys
- The dev team likes to fix bugs which result into more bugs to fix
- Steam Controller support is meh, but it works
- Doing the same thing over and over again is not fun after a while
- Their IRC server doesn't allow chatting outside the game, so you have to be in the game to get access which is bad for clan communication
- "Singleplayer" is more multiplayer, you have to be online for playing the game in singleplayer
- This game uses a launcher and a own cdn for downloading the game assets rather than Steam servers which can result into a waaay to long download time
- Some things are just too expensive. 150€ for a single Warframe on prime access? I can get 30 games for 150€.
- There are tons of tutorials missing. You have to learn so much by communicating with other players or regional chat
- They sometimes add features which are not great. This results into a flaming community, but then they decide to fix the issue later.
- Many players with a Mastery Rank >= 20 (That's a lot of playtime) think they are better than everyone and they own the world
- Archwing (space missions) is fun, but it gets boring after a while and it's unnecessary
- Their launcher is written in .NET and uses CEF. The framework is available on other platforms as well, but that does not mean it's easy to port it to other platforms. And I'm sure they never will
- It uses proprietary NVIDIA PhysX technology
At all, It's your decision to play this game. If you care about the things I said, you should not play it. But the game is really well made, so I 'm very neutral for and against this game.
I will update this review later.

I bought this game for much, much cheaper than it is selling for as it gears up toward release. Though I am extremely happy that I paid the price I did early on and not a full $60 for it, I do have to say that I would not be disappointed at that price, either. This is one of my favorite survival games of all time, and I have to say that it all has to do with the dinosaurs. I have always loved dinosaurs and the ability to tame, breed, ride, and (of course) run from different dinos in this game is what makes it more than worth it to me. The other aspects are, quite honestly, pretty typical of other survival games. Worry about food. Worry about shelter. Wait, a raptor dismantled your thatch hut? Build it again. You have to figure out how to manage all of your needs in addition to learning how to best deal with each type of dino. The tricks for one species probably won't work for another.
Having said all of that, I have to admit that I haven't played on any of the official servers. My friends and I stay on a private one, which comes with a whole host of other benefits. Yes, you have to pay a monthly fee to rent a server or you have to set one up yourself physically. However, it opens up a whole host of customization options you can play with. As a server admin, you are able to tweak everything from how quickly your food and water depletes (if at all) to which species of dinos even spawn in your game. You can even change the weight of each species, raising the spawn percentage of some and lowering it for others. Everything has a spawn code, so you can even cheat in whatever you want. When you are running your own show, you can make this game be whatever you want it to be. If you want an island full of Rexes, go for it. If you want to be overrun with dodos, you can do that too! There are even different maps to choose from and the modding community is amazing.
In the end, it's the customization that makes the game totally worth it to me. I have been able to perfectly tailor an experience that my friends and I can enjoy for hours on end, even if it means the extra cost of renting a server.

This is one of the best free games in the world right now, if not THE best. It's simple, elegant and the combat is amazing. I've seen many people complain about repetitiveness, which yes, is an issue, but the fun part is playing online with different people, collaborating to find the best way to do a mission, and there IS actually quite a wide variety of missions. Survival, defense, exterminate, void runs, dark sectors, pvp, quests, even a relay for you to just chill and talk some crap with others. The community of players is great; they're very patient with newbies. I've been very happy with how the players, especially high-levelled ones, patiently deal with the new guys and even people who still kind of suck like me. Melee combat is really fun especially if you have stance mods on, and combat overall flows very smoothly. One moment you could be wallrunning, then the next hanging on the wall and picking those neat headshots, then rolling on the ground and slicing someone in half... You get the idea. Many newbies also complain about the apparent pay2win factor of warframe, but in reality, this is one of the few games left that you don't NEED to spend money on to actually get good. This is currently my favourite game, and as far as I'm concerned, this stands proud among some of the huge paid games around.

This is a hard one to sum up. It's definitely fun, but I found it critically lacking in polish - there are a number of really basic, and repeated glitches and errors that scream 'insufficient playtesting'. One touch I liked was that your weapon occupied real space, meaning that if you were standing in a narrow hallway, swinging sideways results in hitting the wall. On the same note, the friendly-fire is realistic - you can't go swinging into the middle of a skirmish - however, getting insta-killed by a ballista fired by a team-mate 5 metres away is just infuriating, so you need to keep your eyes open and be aware of less intellectually-endowed players. The controls can feel sluggish but realistic, and reward patience rather than gung-ho CoD-style playing. I want to score it less, because the lack of polish is rather insulting, and I want to give it more, because it has the potential to be stunning. I'll give it a 7/10 but say that it'd be worth an 8.5 if they patched it.

Warframe is a cooperative online third person shooter where players take on the role of Tenno, space ninjas in technologically-advanced exoskeletons that give them superhuman powers. Engage in action-packed combat as you run along walls, go down zip lines, perform acrobatics, and cut down enemies with your sword, or blast them all to kingdom come with the vast arsenal of weapons at your disposal. While Warframe does have several PvP options, Warframe is primarily a PvE game. Choose from three starting classes and 17 advanced classes, each with their own roles and playstyles. Work together with friends as you take on armies of space grunts, walking turrets, and hordes of mindless zombies in a stunning futuristic sci-fi world.
Warframe Key Features:
Good Variety of Warframes – choose from a large pool of warframes and customize them with  mods to match your needs.
Smooth Moves – play with familiar FPS controls and use ninja/parkour moves to position yourself.
Constant Updates – the dev team is always tweaking and updating the game based on players' comments.
Awesome Graphics and SFX – the graphics are amazingly fluid and the music heightens the action-packed atmosphere of the game.
Pros: +Fun cooperative gameplay. +Good variety of Warframes. +Great production value (Music/Visuals).
Cons:  -TONS of grinding required. -Repetitive missions. -Feels too easy sometimes. -Limited PvP options.

Alrighty, this one is a little tricky. Not because I'm not sure of the game, but because I'm not sure of YOU. Don't take that the wrong way. It's just that Warframe lies in the same review class as Dark Souls. Which is to say, I love it, but I'm heartely aware of the fact that a lot of people wont. It's a challenge. Not at first, but as you progress, it gets pretty tough. It's not a game you'll really enjoy playing solo, either. This game was built from the ground up to be played co op. Even if it's just with ONE friend, it's far better than solo. And last but not least, and I guess this is actually the biggest gripe for a lot of people... it's a grind. I mean its a BIG grind. A bunch of the gear is locked behind RNG lootcrates called Relics, and getting the item you want could take you a long time. We're talking weeks here.
So those are the negatives, the elements of the game that could stop people from enjoying the game. On to the positives.
This game WILL make you feel like a badass. I don't care how you play shooters. You could be a run'n'gun style of gamer, you could be an assassin, you could be a sniper or a brute. Don't care, does not matter, this game WILL cater to you. At its core, Warframe is fast, furious, and brutal. You feel every hit, and you grin every time you put down an enemy, and OH BOY are there a lot of them. The sharp, satisfying gunplay combines beautifuly with the free flowing parkour system to provide a style of gameplay I've NEVER got from another game. Sure as hell not from a F2P.
And this game IS F2P. Sure, there's an in game shop. Sure, you'll get things a LOT quicker if you're willing to shell out real cash, but the feeling of satisfaction you get from putting that badass new gun together yourself is indescribable.  Now, certainly, there's a PvP element, and I suppose people who buy the latest, most powerful gear might have an advantage. I can't comment though, I don't play the PvP. Its such a tiny element I've never even looked at it.
Honestly, if you have even a single thought that this game looks good, download it. I swear, you'll get something out of it. And hell, it's free, whatve you got to lose?
TL;DR
It's free, it's awesome. Play it.

This is one of the best free games in the world right now, if not THE best. It's simple, elegant and the combat is amazing. I've seen many people complain about repetitiveness, which yes, is an issue, but the fun part is playing online with different people, collaborating to find the best way to do a mission, and there IS actually quite a wide variety of missions. Survival, defense, exterminate, void runs, dark sectors, pvp, quests, even a relay for you to just chill and talk some crap with others. The community of players is great; they're very patient with newbies. I've been very happy with how the players, especially high-levelled ones, patiently deal with the new guys and even people who still kind of suck like me. Melee combat is really fun especially if you have stance mods on, and combat overall flows very smoothly. One moment you could be wallrunning, then the next hanging on the wall and picking those neat headshots, then rolling on the ground and slicing someone in half... You get the idea. Many newbies also complain about the apparent pay2win factor of warframe, but in reality, this is one of the few games left that you don't NEED to spend money on to actually get good. This is currently my favourite game, and as far as I'm concerned, this stands proud among some of the huge paid games around.

So now they just doubled the price of this game to $60 with its countless issues, electing instead to add new creatures instead of doing useful things like:
1. Improving the godawful AI - Every carnivore behaves like it's on a genocidal rampage: no pack tactics, no hunger system...nope...the AI just runs around and attacks everything close to it. The game has very little immersion because of it, which is strange because that's what people want from a dinosaur island survival game. Herbivores are the same story: they don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about their livelihood. They will often just sit there and wait for you to go up and club them in the face. A Parasaurolophus will seriously walk around aimlessly until a T-Rex has taken a chunk of its body before caring about it. I still don't believe this has ever been addressed and this is one of the game's most underepresented yet worst faults. They have ignored changing this for years now.
2. Optimizing the damn game - The game runs like even more♥♥♥♥♥♥than it used to. This is because they have elected to add a lot more "content" to the game. New creatures and engrams do little to spice up the experience when it runs below 30 FPS for a ton of people constantly.
3. The lack of true Depth - It is kinda like No Man's Sky in a way where the devs add a lot of content, but with not a lot of complexity behind them. It's fine that they update the game constantly and add more stuff but it's stuff that should be free DLC later, not crammed into an early access game that just needs the optimization and exploits fixed before launch. Seeing as how the game is scheduled to release next month, I doubt they can optimize it fast enough so it will run like♥♥♥♥♥♥for a game priced at $60.
4. The solo experience is impossible - The game is completely geared for tribes and tribe mechanics. The PvP is reportedly atrocious although I have never tried it. Instead of making every dinosaur truly different and understandable to get to, the goal is always to reach the top combat dinosaurs, which are a joke for a solo person to tame without glitching them against rocks. It's actually so commonplace to abuse the awful AI that it's a legitimate strategy in the game to let dinosaurs get stuck while you sit there endlessly pelting it with tranq. It is legitimately the only way to tranq really fast and dangerous dinosaurs like Gigas.
5. There is no skill, only knowledge of abusing the design matters - You may have noticed this by now from the last one, but the only way forward is to abuse the simplistic dinosaur AI to tame them, to fight them, to do anything. Combat is incredibly simplistic: just spamming one button until you win. The idea is to just get a T-rex or Giga and just spam Mouse 1 while the enemy charges your dinosaur and eventually dies. It's all a war of attrition, the combat in this game.
There's a lot more to talk about here but it would take an essay to cover. My point is, this game is *not* ready to leave early access and is definitely not AAA quality, so why they have bothered to make this game $60 is a complete joke. Do not buy this as I can see them changing the price back after this outcry. It's worth $20 if you got a good PC. It'd only be worth more if they fix it and add more needed depth to its gameplay. Also, what is sad to me is that this game used to be the epitome of what a good early access game was, but now it has been sorta ruined by the devs. Early access is looking worse and worse as a result.

Not mentioning promises that were not kept, the developer's greed was first truly seen when they released their first paid expansion... while in Early Access. Their excuse was that the "wanted to make sure we did DLC right for the future" which could have easily been done with at least a $5 price tag that would have made it more accessable to the community.
Now, the doubling of the price for the "complete" game is what has sent many off the edge.  The game is not complete, the developers quite obviously want to make more money because they believe they can.  Plus, when they release more DLC, you can rest assured that it will be half of the price of the game once more, and they may even find more ways to suck money fom you.
The sad part is, despite the shenanigans with the first greed issue - the first DLC - this game was still worth buying for the $30, because thought has been put into it, and it is a unique game. Some background:
Well I purchased it with some trepidation as I had read a bunch of negative reviews about how the developers hadn't focused on fixing performance issues with the game and doing what the community thought was in the best interests of the game. I was really into the DayZ mod at the time and was looking for other open world games with survival mechanics. One of my co workers who also like survival games told me how he had spent hundreds of hours playing Ark on a private server and that it was a great game. I saw it on sale and I decided to buy it and see how bad it was going to be.
I was rather suprised at how well the game ran. I was running it at the time on mid range hardware. An i5 2500k overclocked to 4.4 ghz with a Radeon 7970 HD Ghz edition that was factory overclocked to around 1.2 ghz. I had 16 GB or ddr 3 1800 ram and a 7200 rpm western digital drive to load it from. The game ran well on medium-high settings with low shadows. I used minimal antiailiasing and turned off ambient occlusion. I got consistent frames in the 40-50 fps range. I thought the game played well and tried out some mods for it. When I was running the game as a non dedicated server I would get pauses every 2 to 3 minutes that lasted about 2 -3 seconds where the game seemed to freeze momentarily. My co worker said that the game wasn't pausing for him during this time. I figured my system just couldn't handle the game and running a server for other players at the same time. With that discovered I found a sale on Scorched Earth and tried it for about 5 minutes but it seemed really lag prone. I soon deleted the game and moved on to other things.
I recently got a new laptop with a Nvidia 1070 gtx graphics card in it. My new laptop is a good bit more powerful than my old computer so when I saw the free Ragnarok map I decided to try out Ark once more. The game runs great for me and I have only had a few problems while playing. Overall the experience has been great.
My Review:
I haven't had the problems that many players have had with this game. Since Ragnarok launched I have put in a couple dozen hours playing and seeing how the game performs.
Gameplay:
Ark at it's core is a survival-lite open world game. I say survival-lite because after a few hours playing you should no longer really be worried about dying from the enviroment. Collecting food and water is very easy once you have a decent base built. Tamed dinosaurs make resource collection very easy as well. A group of 3 Trikes will make resource runs very productive.
So once you have a base what do you do? Ideally you would set off exploring for some sort of better loot or gear. Ark though lets you unlock new gear through leveling up and purchasing Enegrams. So your gear, outside of a few random pieces you may get from dino kills, is not really an issue.
Ark has a story that is told through pieces of journal entries that are scattered about the island. You could track them all down and learn more about the Ark. Unfortunately there are so many journal pieces to get that you soon lose track of who figured out what and so on.
So this leaves exploration and dino taming. Ark is a wonderful place to explore. No matter which map you are on you are sure to see some very beautiful scenery. That alone is worth a few hours of travel on a tamed dinos back to see.
The big game goal seems to be to tame bigger and stronger dinosaurs and to breed them to produce a small army of creatures to make your avatars life easier. Taming is simplistic and basically a time sink that you can spend dozens of hours pursuing so that you can get the exact dino that you wanted. This is fun.
The real draw for Ark is its online gameplay. On a shared server where other players can help or hinder your progress. In this the game is great for the most part. There is end game content to acquire and with other peoples help this becomes possible. It is also the games greatest failing. Ark has a very toxic online community. Many servers are controlled by powerful "Alpha" tribes. If you are not part of these tribes you don't really have a chance to see the end game content because they will hunt you down and ruin everything you have built. This makes the game really unfriendly for new and casual players who just want a fun online experience. These "Alpha" tribes ironically are anything but Alpha. They exhibit terrible manners and little to no understanding of how Alpha creatures actually behave.
Your best bet for the online game at this point is to find a private server that encourages a sense of community so you can fully enjoy all of the games content. If you can't find one then maybe you can start your own. There are many server hosting companies that support Ark and you could get a couple of your friends and rent a server for not much more than a WoW subscribtion each month.
After all of this it must seem like I dislike this game. Nothing could be farther from the truth. Ark has something about it that draws me into it. Whether single player or online I find that the game is simply fun to play. There is something fun about crossing over a hill and being attacked by a pack of Raptors. The game has just enough frustration when you die to annoy you but not so much that you want to stop playing. The fights are fast and brutal. The graphical eye candy is everywhere. The sense of accomplishment is strong. And, when the main game becomes lacking, there are an abundance of player made maps and mods to explore for even more challenges. Ark is simply a game that delivers great content. I can't even say that the price is bad as, even at $60 USD, the game offers enough content for hundreds of hours of gaming solo.
Additional Thoughts:
If I could change one thing about Ark it would be the end game content. I feel that the game needs a way to allow players to build and access this content even if they are not part of the dominant tribe on their server. Offline raid protection is not enough. I think maybe an alternate set of gear and buildings that is just as strong as TEK level that solo players can create on their own could help.
The other thing I wish this game had is a fantasy map with magic spells. You have dinosaurs and mythical monsters already. Just add some craftable magic spells and weapons to make an Ark that is really different.
Note on Hardware issues:
This game is graphically demanding. If you are running on a 290x, 7970HD, 970 GTX, or an even older or weaker card, note that you will not be able to play this game with all the settings maxed out and get enjoyable framerates. You will have to tweak everything. I recommend dropping shadows to their lowest level, removing ambient occlusion, and dropping the quality of anti aliasing to the lowest settings you can. After that set ground cover to its lowest setting. From there you will have to manually adjust the game setting until you are comfortable with the results. This is something to think about before purchasing this game.
This game is also cpu intensive. If you are playing single player or hosting a private server expect to have perfomance issues if your system is not a high end rig. i5 or i7 quad cores are almost mandatory. Clock speed seems to help as does fast ddr4 ram. If you are using an AMD processor then I would recommend nothing older than a Ryzen cpu for this game.
You may still run into stability issues. I am using Windows 10 and I keep it updated. Your performance may vary from mine. I find that the game is relatively stable and runs smoothly for me on my current gaming laptop. I run the game on epic for most settings with shadows and anti aliasing on High. I often turn ground clutter off as it obscures small dino corpses to much. I have run the game with ground clutter on max and the game still ran smoothly for me.

The game is hard to describe. It's like a mix of alot of games (Firefall, The Division), depending on your playstyle. When playing public, it's an arcade shooter for rushers. When playing solo or with a group of friends, you can go in silent and tactical. Good thing is: You can always switch from one to another on a mission-to-mission basis. The game itself is all about trying out different playstyles, as the warframes and weapons really play completely differently. There are not many games that achieve this diversity.
For those who are reading this because it's marked as "free" and are sceptical:
It really is "free to play" and it is not "pay to win" (plus it's mostly coop-only). There is not a whole lot you really NEED the premium credits for. The only things worth buying platinum for are slots for your additional warframes and weapons. And even then you can easily trade those little amounts of platinum with other players. So if you REALLY don't want to spend even a tiny amount of money, you can easily get away with it.
Actually that's it for now. If you want to know how the game itself plays, just try it. It is very confusing at first, but since the last starmap-update, there is more of a red line to follow for new players. Stay with it and you'll be rewarded with very interesting gameplay.

Some background:
Well I purchased it with some trepidation as I had read a bunch of negative reviews about how the developers hadn't focused on fixing performance issues with the game and doing what the community thought was in the best interests of the game. I was really into the DayZ mod at the time and was looking for other open world games with survival mechanics. One of my co workers who also like survival games told me how he had spent hundreds of hours playing Ark on a private server and that it was a great game. I saw it on sale and I decided to buy it and see how bad it was going to be.
I was rather suprised at how well the game ran. I was running it at the time on mid range hardware. An i5 2500k overclocked to 4.4 ghz with a Radeon 7970 HD Ghz edition that was factory overclocked to around 1.2 ghz. I had 16 GB or ddr 3 1800 ram and a 7200 rpm western digital drive to load it from. The game ran well on medium-high settings with low shadows. I used minimal antiailiasing and turned off ambient occlusion. I got consistent frames in the 40-50 fps range. I thought the game played well and tried out some mods for it. When I was running the game as a non dedicated server I would get pauses every 2 to 3 minutes that lasted about 2 -3 seconds where the game seemed to freeze momentarily. My co worker said that the game wasn't pausing for him during this time. I figured my system just couldn't handle the game and running a server for other players at the same time. With that discovered I found a sale on Scorched Earth and tried it for about 5 minutes but it seemed really lag prone. I soon deleted the game and moved on to other things.
I recently got a new laptop with a Nvidia 1070 gtx graphics card in it. My new laptop is a good bit more powerful than my old computer so when I saw the free Ragnarok map I decided to try out Ark once more. The game runs great for me and I have only had a few problems while playing. Overall the experience has been great.
My Review:
I haven't had the problems that many players have had with this game. Since Ragnarok launched I have put in a couple dozen hours playing and seeing how the game performs.
Gameplay:
Ark at it's core is a survival-lite open world game. I say survival-lite because after a few hours playing you should no longer really be worried about dying from the enviroment. Collecting food and water is very easy once you have a decent base built. Tamed dinosaurs make resource collection very easy as well. A group of 3 Trikes will make resource runs very productive.
So once you have a base what do you do? Ideally you would set off exploring for some sort of better loot or gear. Ark though lets you unlock new gear through leveling up and purchasing Enegrams. So your gear, outside of a few random pieces you may get from dino kills, is not really an issue.
Ark has a story that is told through pieces of journal entries that are scattered about the island. You could track them all down and learn more about the Ark. Unfortunately there are so many journal pieces to get that you soon lose track of who figured out what and so on.
So this leaves exploration and dino taming. Ark is a wonderful place to explore. No matter which map you are on you are sure to see some very beautiful scenery. That alone is worth a few hours of travel on a tamed dinos back to see.
The big game goal seems to be to tame bigger and stronger dinosaurs and to breed them to produce a small army of creatures to make your avatars life easier. Taming is simplistic and basically a time sink that you can spend dozens of hours pursuing so that you can get the exact dino that you wanted. This is fun.
The real draw for Ark is its online gameplay. On a shared server where other players can help or hinder your progress. In this the game is great for the most part. There is end game content to acquire and with other peoples help this becomes possible. It is also the games greatest failing. Ark has a very toxic online community. Many servers are controlled by powerful "Alpha" tribes. If you are not part of these tribes you don't really have a chance to see the end game content because they will hunt you down and ruin everything you have built. This makes the game really unfriendly for new and casual players who just want a fun online experience. These "Alpha" tribes ironically are anything but Alpha. They exhibit terrible manners and little to no understanding of how Alpha creatures actually behave.
Your best bet for the online game at this point is to find a private server that encourages a sense of community so you can fully enjoy all of the games content. If you can't find one then maybe you can start your own. There are many server hosting companies that support Ark and you could get a couple of your friends and rent a server for not much more than a WoW subscribtion each month.
After all of this it must seem like I dislike this game. Nothing could be farther from the truth. Ark has something about it that draws me into it. Whether single player or online I find that the game is simply fun to play. There is something fun about crossing over a hill and being attacked by a pack of Raptors. The game has just enough frustration when you die to annoy you but not so much that you want to stop playing. The fights are fast and brutal. The graphical eye candy is everywhere. The sense of accomplishment is strong. And, when the main game becomes lacking, there are an abundance of player made maps and mods to explore for even more challenges. Ark is simply a game that delivers great content. I can't even say that the price is bad as, even at $60 USD, the game offers enough content for hundreds of hours of gaming solo.
Additional Thoughts:
If I could change one thing about Ark it would be the end game content. I feel that the game needs a way to allow players to build and access this content even if they are not part of the dominant tribe on their server. Offline raid protection is not enough. I think maybe an alternate set of gear and buildings that is just as strong as TEK level that solo players can create on their own could help.
The other thing I wish this game had is a fantasy map with magic spells. You have dinosaurs and mythical monsters already. Just add some craftable magic spells and weapons to make an Ark that is really different.
Note on Hardware issues:
This game is graphically demanding. If you are running on a 290x, 7970HD, 970 GTX, or an even older or weaker card, note that you will not be able to play this game with all the settings maxed out and get enjoyable framerates. You will have to tweak everything. I recommend dropping shadows to their lowest level, removing ambient occlusion, and dropping the quality of anti aliasing to the lowest settings you can. After that set ground cover to its lowest setting. From there you will have to manually adjust the game setting until you are comfortable with the results. This is something to think about before purchasing this game.
This game is also cpu intensive. If you are playing single player or hosting a private server expect to have perfomance issues if your system is not a high end rig. i5 or i7 quad cores are almost mandatory. Clock speed seems to help as does fast ddr4 ram. If you are using an AMD processor then I would recommend nothing older than a Ryzen cpu for this game.
You may still run into stability issues. I am using Windows 10 and I keep it updated. Your performance may vary from mine. I find that the game is relatively stable and runs smoothly for me on my current gaming laptop. I run the game on epic for most settings with shadows and anti aliasing on High. I often turn ground clutter off as it obscures small dino corpses to much. I have run the game with ground clutter on max and the game still ran smoothly for me.

Chivalry is kicking a man off of a cliff. Chivalry is hacking up helpless archers that you blinded with smoke. I have been playing ark for around two years now I started playing just a couple months after its initial release (A famous YouTuber did a better job of making a captivating advertisement than the advertising people the devs hired did). During this time I have seen creative technical players get around game limitations, and I have seen the Devs go completely overboard in their attempts to maintain game balance. I must say however I have more than gotten my money's worth from the game. The game is a bit resource hungry on the computer, but still playable. Sadly most of the public servers have largely been overrun with large tribes of kids with severe alpha complex issues. I would still recommend Ark: Survival Evolved to any of my friends, and recently purchased a copy for my girlfriend so she could play with me, and I still plan on buying a copy for my ex’s kid, despite the recent price increase. It is a fun combination of Sandbox Game, Survival Game, and Multi-Player Environment. Many of the negative reviews I have seen are the result of players being angry at some of the nerfings. Unfortunately many of these nerfings have been the result of attempting to rebalance the game after alpha tribes do things to dominate public servers, or in response to well known creative YouTubers coming up with and publishing ways around game limitations. Enjoy the game, and good luck surviving the Ark.

If you're looking for a fast paced, intuitive, and visceral medieval combat game that still utilizes somwhat realistic combat components, I would definitely give Chivalry a try. Unlike Mount and Blade, it is a multiplayer only title, so those looking for a deep single player experience will be disappointed. However, the combat from the onset is easier and more satisfying than you'll get with M&B. Blocking for instance is just a matter of timing, no more do you have to worry about blocking high/low/etc, just time things right. Feints are easy to perform as well as performing different attacks, no longer do you have to do this via manipulating the mouse directions, which was tricky in M&B since the mouse also dictated the camera controls. The game also seems to have various objectives, the usuals like deathmatch are here as well as objective based modes where you have to do things like defend the royal family from attackers or vice versa. I'd give it a look.

This game is not as fun as it used to be when it first came out, because you didnt have as much to worry about, and they only had 1 map out. When they added 'The Center,'A FAN MADE MAP, and made it cost $20 dollars, I thought it was a bit absurd, since they didnt even put any work towards the making of it. After the addition of the Allosaurus, I started to pull away from playing this game, and I started playing recently, and have had a lot of fun playing it. I would have recommended this game if I hadn't looked at the price now, and realized that they have raised the price for yet a second time, and it is now an INSANE $60. Another reason that I would not recomment the game is the developers over the years have became more ignorant and more greedy for their gamers money, and raise prices, or set prices on other peoples creations. Sorry for such a long review, but I wanted to give my personal opinion of this game from experiences from the past, present and hopes on the future of the game.

This game is actually the best I have played in a long time. The combat system far exceeds that of similar titles such as Mount and Blade: Warband and provides a very vivid and real experience with visceral features including dismemberment and decapitation. While the background of both factions is fictitious, the game still feels very authentic and natural - with smooth controls and fluid animation sequences. The voice acting is unimportant, but mentionable, as it is very well executed. Some glitches can still be found at this point (20/10/2012), although they will most likely be ironed out by further updates in the coming weeks. There is an abundance of active Australian servers, which is good news for us Oceanic folk. All in all, I would warmly recommend this game to experienced medieval fighting gamers and newbies alike, as it provides a great deal of fun - even for extended periods of playtime. I both love and hate this game like many reviewers.
In terms of depth and mechanics and things to do this game is massive.   It's challenging and has many paths and strategies you can take as your character and base develops.    The 3 retail maps and one expansion provide a huge set of lands to explore.     The 100 or so 3d modeled creatures from all eras of prehistory are really great looking and the environments are fantastically immersive.     The game is certainly 'fun' to play and even the PvE can be quite challenging sometimes.
However the flipside is the DEV team really doesn't seem to take a lot of clues from the general public in what they want.   An easy example would be about 95% of servers offer at least a 5x taming and harvesting rates.    NOBODY has the time or inclination to be glued to their computer around the clock for hours on end protecting some high level tame that could easily be lost in game in a hot minute.       The official servers are rife with cheaters and griefers,   there are no checks against teh ultra massive top tribes squashing all opposition.
PvP  is very unevenly balanced,  some dinos are outrageously overpowered while some weapons that require significant materials and skill investment are practically useless in a fight.   Older dinos from a year or two ago are often rendered obsolete by a new late release addition to the game.    Many of the dinos such as the Diplodocus for example are reviled by players as totally useless and simply take up space in the game.    Level progression and tribe power tends to be a runaway train where small tribes or solo players have no chance of being competitive.
The DEVs have really made some public relations disasters in the past two years,  most notably releasing paid expansion content for the game which isn't technically done.     Also in game nerfs even if are logical are often overly severe and have turned off large groups of players.    They really do need a better public relations team to protect them from themselves.
Overall,  ARK is a great game.   I have dumped well over a thousand hours into it.    I have been in some huge pvp battles and have had some real memorable moments.   I certainly feel it was worth my money.    If I bought it today for $60 I'd say it was a fair deal.    Hopefully they can iron out some of the performance issues and improve some of the in game mechanics like dino path finding and make a lot of the buildables and engrams actually functional and useful.  (Mining hat anyone)
I will say do not even consider this game unless you have a pretty meaty computer with a 2GB Video card,  8GB of RAM and a 256GB+  SSD to run it from.    The ROM itself is HUGE and tends to take up a lot of space especially once you start playing on unofficial and letting the client install a lot of mods.
Even in the buggy and unbalanced state this game currently is in, it's simply the best first-person multiplayer experience I have had since Tribes 2.  Can't put it down.

The way I got ARK: Survival Evolved was when I saw some of my favorite YouTubers playing it. Ever since then, I wanted to buy it. I believe I caught a lucky break and snagged the game during a sale, which made me extremely happy. Though my first time on the game was dissapointing. I could not even get on my own custom server because of the excruciatingly heavy system requirements, and when I finally did get into a game, all of my graphics settings had to be set on the absolute lowest possible setting. I (for some reason) believed that my laptop could handle this game, in which it could not. This is not the game's fault, of course, as it has amazing graphics. The problem was when the price was ramped up from a reasonable price (I believe $15.00?) to $59.99. This absolutely disgusts me, as the game is still in early access (meaning it is not complete). You're making people pay $59.99 for a game which isn't even completed yet. The game could change in any way possible in the future, yet you're charging customers nearly 60 dollars like it's a finished game. People don't even know if the game could run on their system, which makes this worse. If someone bought the game and realized they couldn't run it, they'd have to refund it (hopefully, if they still can), or they'd have to live with the fact that they just wasted a full $59.99 on a game which they can't even play.
Another painful thing to live with is the attrocity we call this game's moderation. If the hefty price doesn't tick you off enough, you've also got the the fact that the moderators do not care about their community in any way, shape, or form. You might ask: "Wont the game get better with work?" That's the problem. They do not work on this game. They haven't even finished their main version, and they're already making DLC's and other things for the game. Not to mention the moderators play favorites, giving items and various other things to those who appraise them. The game is also glitchy, meaning you could clip into the ground, get stuck in a rock, your dinosaur could glitch out and die, and so much more. This further adds to the fact that this game is not ready to be priced at $59.99, as it needs an extreme amount of work until it could even be considered viable to be a full game.
In ARK: Survival Evolved, you'll spend most of your time in a cycle. Spawn, get a basic starting, die. Spawn, get extremely far in the game, die. Spawn, try to regain your possesions, die. Try one last time, and you make it. But you still can't get away from the fact that ARK is nothing more than a time-wasting game. You have to spend hours taming dinosaurs, grinding materials, etc. Unless you're ready to sell your life away to this game, do not even consider buying it simply because it looks cool on the outside. Though this game does have SOME good things going for it, it simply isn't enough to cover up the bad. Therefore, I simply cannot recommend this game to any buyer until it is further worked on, and/or the moderation gets their act together. If these flaws are worked out in the future, I will be able to recommend this game.

ARK is a game that will make you lose track of time with the mind set of 'I will just do this', 'I will just tame this dinosaur' or ' I will just complete that'. It has survival, construction, dinosaurs, PvP and PvE which all bring their own challenges. The lack of story or direct goals have both positive and negative impacts on the game, as you are left to do as you please by creating your own story. On the other hand the lack off direction also leaves you striving for a goal of having everything, yet upon achieving so, you have nothing left to do but rinse and repeat.
With that said sometimes the challenges are ones which are not part of the mechanics;
Lag isn't a common occurrence, with the odd rubber band which puts you back about 2 -3 seconds. However this is solely based upon your connection to the server, which could lead to it being frequent or non existent.
There are bugs, some being visual artifacting, lighting & shadow issues and the others being collision boxes on dinosaurs which could use an overhaul, as they partially clip through everything.
Optimisation is one of the games biggest hurdles. With an overclocked i7 3930k and GTX 1080Ti at 1440p the game is unable to maintain 60+ FPS with every graphical setting set to highest. There are a few settings which I have reduced to high to enable a solid 60+ with an Average of 75 FPS.
Aside from optimisation another big letdown is that Wildcard are charging for DLC despite still being in early access development, this is not a game breaker, more so a poor decision on the developers behalves.
Overall ARK is a great game that I have put many hours in and will continue to do, however it is not without its flaws.

The way I got ARK: Survival Evolved was when I saw some of my favorite YouTubers playing it. Ever since then, I wanted to buy it. I believe I caught a lucky break and snagged the game during a sale, which made me extremely happy. Though my first time on the game was dissapointing. I could not even get on my own custom server because of the excruciatingly heavy system requirements, and when I finally did get into a game, all of my graphics settings had to be set on the absolute lowest possible setting. I (for some reason) believed that my laptop could handle this game, in which it could not. This is not the game's fault, of course, as it has amazing graphics. The problem was when the price was ramped up from a reasonable price (I believe $15.00?) to $59.99. This absolutely disgusts me, as the game is still in early access (meaning it is not complete). You're making people pay $59.99 for a game which isn't even completed yet. The game could change in any way possible in the future, yet you're charging customers nearly 60 dollars like it's a finished game. People don't even know if the game could run on their system, which makes this worse. If someone bought the game and realized they couldn't run it, they'd have to refund it (hopefully, if they still can), or they'd have to live with the fact that they just wasted a full $59.99 on a game which they can't even play.
Another painful thing to live with is the attrocity we call this game's moderation. If the hefty price doesn't tick you off enough, you've also got the the fact that the moderators do not care about their community in any way, shape, or form. You might ask: "Wont the game get better with work?" That's the problem. They do not work on this game. They haven't even finished their main version, and they're already making DLC's and other things for the game. Not to mention the moderators play favorites, giving items and various other things to those who appraise them. The game is also glitchy, meaning you could clip into the ground, get stuck in a rock, your dinosaur could glitch out and die, and so much more. This further adds to the fact that this game is not ready to be priced at $59.99, as it needs an extreme amount of work until it could even be considered viable to be a full game.
In ARK: Survival Evolved, you'll spend most of your time in a cycle. Spawn, get a basic starting, die. Spawn, get extremely far in the game, die. Spawn, try to regain your possesions, die. Try one last time, and you make it. But you still can't get away from the fact that ARK is nothing more than a time-wasting game. You have to spend hours taming dinosaurs, grinding materials, etc. Unless you're ready to sell your life away to this game, do not even consider buying it simply because it looks cool on the outside. Though this game does have SOME good things going for it, it simply isn't enough to cover up the bad. Therefore, I simply cannot recommend this game to any buyer until it is further worked on, and/or the moderation gets their act together. If these flaws are worked out in the future, I will be able to recommend this game.

ARK is a game that will make you lose track of time with the mind set of 'I will just do this', 'I will just tame this dinosaur' or ' I will just complete that'. It has survival, construction, dinosaurs, PvP and PvE which all bring their own challenges. The lack of story or direct goals have both positive and negative impacts on the game, as you are left to do as you please by creating your own story. On the other hand the lack off direction also leaves you striving for a goal of having everything, yet upon achieving so, you have nothing left to do but rinse and repeat.
With that said sometimes the challenges are ones which are not part of the mechanics;
Lag isn't a common occurrence, with the odd rubber band which puts you back about 2 -3 seconds. However this is solely based upon your connection to the server, which could lead to it being frequent or non existent.
There are bugs, some being visual artifacting, lighting & shadow issues and the others being collision boxes on dinosaurs which could use an overhaul, as they partially clip through everything.
Optimisation is one of the games biggest hurdles. With an overclocked i7 3930k and GTX 1080Ti at 1440p the game is unable to maintain 60+ FPS with every graphical setting set to highest. There are a few settings which I have reduced to high to enable a solid 60+ with an Average of 75 FPS.
Aside from optimisation another big letdown is that Wildcard are charging for DLC despite still being in early access development, this is not a game breaker, more so a poor decision on the developers behalves.
Overall ARK is a great game that I have put many hours in and will continue to do, however it is not without its flaws.
Audio: 7/10
Graphics: 7/10
Performance: 6/10
Replayability: 7/10
Story: N/A
Overall Score-: 7/10

Have you killed a man with an axe today?  If the answer is no, then take a moment to dig deep and figure out what's wrong with you.  Once you've done that, buy Chivalry: Medieval Warfare and never have to face this truly disturbing situation again.
The game focuses on a simple but fairly deep first person melee combat system (with a few archers thrown in for good measure).  Deathmatch, team deathmatch, and capture the flag modes are available, but I have the most fun with Chivalry's objective based maps.  As the eternal battle of Red vs. Blue continues in this magic-free fantasy world, one team is tasked with storming the enemy castle, burning  villages, or freeing slaves laborers from the finest of volcano lairs while the other team tries to stop them.  There's also a pretty solid duel mode that lets you focus single combat rather than the larger engagements of the other modes.
Chances are good that you've never played anything with combat like Chivalry's before.  Fortunately, there's a good tutorial that will fill you in on the basics of the very rewarding system that Torn Banner have put together here.

Warframe is a cooperative online third person shooter where players take on the role of Tenno, space ninjas in technologically-advanced exoskeletons that give them superhuman powers. Engage in action-packed combat as you run along walls, go down zip lines, perform acrobatics, and cut down enemies with your sword, or blast them all to kingdom come with the vast arsenal of weapons at your disposal. While Warframe does have several PvP options, Warframe is primarily a PvE game. Choose from three starting classes and 17 advanced classes, each with their own roles and playstyles. Work together with friends as you take on armies of space grunts, walking turrets, and hordes of mindless zombies in a stunning futuristic sci-fi world.
Warframe Key Features:
Good Variety of Warframes – choose from a large pool of warframes and customize them with  mods to match your needs.
Smooth Moves – play with familiar FPS controls and use ninja/parkour moves to position yourself.
Constant Updates – the dev team is always tweaking and updating the game based on players' comments.
Awesome Graphics and SFX – the graphics are amazingly fluid and the music heightens the action-packed atmosphere of the game.
Pros: +Fun cooperative gameplay. +Good variety of Warframes. +Great production value (Music/Visuals).
Cons:  -TONS of grinding required. -Repetitive missions. -Feels too easy sometimes. -Limited PvP options.

TL;DR: I don't do TL;DR. Don't be a lazy sack of crap; actually read the review.
ARK, is a very pretty game. It is also a very detailed game, a very fun game, and one of the best sandbox games on steam, in my honest opinion.
It is also, however, one of, if not, THE WORST OPTIMIZED, as well as one of the buggiest, early-access games to have ever left early access. There is no rightful reason for a game of this price to be this unpolished, and no matter what you think of the game otherwise, I believe that we can all agree on this.
The thing is, though, that the developers of this game seem not to agree with any of us on this front, as they seem to only care, at this point, in making more money, developing more overpriced expansions, as opposed to actually working more on the core of the game, making it an actual enjoyable experience for more of the people that actually play it.
I would hazard a guess that at least an eighth to a quarter of the people that have purchased this game have had trouble running the game, but haven't refunded it, because they have a hope in their hearts that this game will one day be improved and optimized, instead of pushing for more content that nobody has asked for.
I might be wrong on this front, but I believe that the game's performance on consoles is entirely worse than on PC, even laughably so, and while I do feel for the console players, that's their own battle to fight, not mine.
I feel that this game is, and always sort of has been, an example of a very prominent game development issue in the modern day, a push for more features, as opposed to solidifying the existing mechanics, and making sure the game is optimized, runs well, and plays well, and honestly, I just cannot recommend anyone buy this game.

It starts with an epic awakening, enemies are all around you.
You are told by a mysterious voice that you are Tenno, a warrior, an ancient force of justice from an old era. Now, the Solar System is torn apart by several factions fighting each other for its control. And you're the only one who can restore peace and balance... by being a badass space ninja, suited in a powerful exoskeleton called Warframe.
Warframe is a 3rd person action free-to-play game developed by Digital Extremes. I have only been playing it for 8 months at the time of this review, but I can tell this game has grown A LOT since it premiered back in 2013. Not only has its wide variety of missions, customization, endless weapon arsenal and increasingly-large warframe list, but also a fascinating lore that keeps growing. The coop element is crucial: nothing beats the experience of a full team of 4 space ninjas, each with their unique powers and weapons, wreaking havoc among hordes of unlucky enemies.
It's very easy to get started with Warframe, but it takes a lot of time and dedication to master all of it. Most of that dedication translates into farming. Farming of exp points, resources, credits, mods, blueprints, etc. Everytime you finally manage to craft that new weapon or warframe is so satisfying,... that's when you get appreciate even the tedious part of the game. And even then, the game's variety makes up for it. In my case, I have been playing it for 8 months straight, but I can see myself spending at least three times that amount of time in the future. That's how hooked I got.
In addition, after all this time, the game has accumulated a lot of story and lore elements that make it even more enjoyable to dive into. The introduction of the cinematic quests, starting with the celebrated "The Second Dream", created a campaign mode in which the solo play is excused, making you feel you're playing the latest adventure of your favorite action saga. Plus these quests tend to unfold mindblowing revelations -the real nature of the warframes- and also new gameplay elements. And there´s nothing like playing them with your warframe wearing the latest fashion additions you managed to acquire after weeks of farming. Because looking fabulous is always important.
Also this game looks pretty. No, that's not quite it... GORGEOUS. There you go.
There's nothing much I can say about this game, other than it keeps growing, let's hope for the better, and I'm sure it will deliver more epic experiences in the future.

I intially wrote a review and couldn't recommend it because a game that was hardly worth its price before and they doubled it. That being said, I will give a review not just off their poor decisions but also for the gameplay.
ARK is fun, and entertaining, however it is the worst kind of grind game. Taming animals can take from hours to days, depending on levels and be killed in minutes. You can spend several days building yourself up, however all it takes is one alpha tribe to ruin all of your advancements and set you back to square one. You might say that this is just how survival games are meant to be -- which is true, but for someone to devote weeks even months into taming dinosaurs and building bases just to have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wipe it in a matter of minutes is unreasonable. When I play this game, I usually play on accelerated servers so I can enjoy the game, and not have to waste an unreasonable amount of time for it to just be wiped.
Ark can't control its players, and shouldn't be asked to, however I believe that nothing should take nearly as long to tame, I believe the max amount of time it should take to tame something is 2 hours, make it more expensive as far as resources go, but I believe that this game should have its rates permanantly increased to make this game more enjoyable.
Breeding is debateable, but I personally don't want to have to spend hours on end with a baby dino ensuring it has its food and its ridiculous that you need to waste that much time to enjoy a part of the game.
You may consider this mostly opinion, "some people want to spend tons of hours building and I am one of them" or something similar, but once a unreasonably large alpha tribe joins your server and your base is reduced to mere rubble in minutes, you'll likely see from my point of view.
Building and taming for weeks and having it destroyed in minutes by hostile players is not an enjoyable game, change the rates so that it takes hours or days to setup a base and get tames and losing it all quickly doesn't ruin your experience.
