Well, what can I say about Warframe?
I love it? Over 300 hundred hours in game would kinda suggest that I guess.
Thats purely subjective though so maybe a little more explaination is called for.
Pros:
- Graphically, its pretty damn beautiful
- Shooting element is very smooth
- Leaping from wall to wall, landing a headshot mid leap from 50 metres away, burning enemies with a draconic effigy all at the same time is pretty cool. You know.... just a little.
- The game just keeps getting more and more added in. The game I play now has so much more to it than it did when I first started playing, and the devs actually care about their game. Which is always a plus.
- One of their quests blindsided me emotionally. Never thought a 3rd person shooter in this style would hit me in the feels but they managed. Any game that actually gets a real emotional response from me is instantly on my praise list.
- A very good free to play model. Theres only a handful of items you can't get by playing the game. Platinum (the real money currency) can be earned by selling mods and parts to other players in game. I've put money into the game but only to unlock more slots for frames and weapons. This wasn't actually necessary as I could have just sold things over the market but... meh. Paid for convenience and to support the game. No regrets.
- Nice pick up put down style game. Log on. Do a mission before going to work/school/that place you have to open your door to access (outside or some name like that... I don't know I try to avoid it whenever I can). Then log out and do whatever. Game will be waiting for you to come back. It won't even judge you. Well, not too much anyway.
It's not all sunshine and rainbows of course. No game is perfect and this is no exception.
Cons
- Controls can be pretty daunting for new players: Once you have this down you'll be leaping around a 3D area and loving every minute, but it doesn't change the fact that; yeah. It's pretty confusing to begin with.
- Pretty samey. I'm gonna expand on this as I know it's a game breaker for some. I personally usually get pretty bored of grindy games. I've enjoyed my fair share of Japanese RPGs but I can count the number of them I've completed on one hand. I start with the best of intentions but after hour 100 of grinding my level just to beat that last boss (I'm looking at you Star Ocean 2. Level 250 to have a chance? Really?) I usually find myself questioning where exactly it all went wrong in my life. Warframe for me, appears to be an exception. Theres a number of different mission types to keep things at least modestly different and fresh, but all of it usually boils down to: Point and shoot until everything is dead. I'd recommend you try it before you knock it as, like me, you may find that actually this is one grind game you can get into.
But it IS still a grind.
- It's pretty complex, what with the numerous weapons, mods, relics, space dogs, space cats (no those last two are real. I'm not making it up), frames and such. There's almost limitless build potential for each weapon, frame or space pet but, obviously, some builds work better than others, generally speaking.
I think this is awesome! So why is it under the cons section?
Because if you're looking at the screenshots and hoping for a straight up, mindless shooter where you hit play and kill everything you're gonna be disappointed. You walk into one of the high tier levels unprepared and theres gonna be a lot of holes in your suit and your patience. I won't say this is a cerebral experience but I will say that there's quite a bit of research, planning and character building goes into making an end game frame and weapon build. Also mods. See previous section about grindiness. 300 hours in and I'm still looking for a number of mods to complete some of my favourite weapon builds.
-RNGesus is stong with this one. No seriously. You are at his mercy almost entirely throughout. Unless you're willing to drop that magical Platinum I mentioned earlier. I personally would have preferred to see a bit more control and a little less of RNGesus' smirking face but.... well I love the game enough to forgive it with only one or two desk slams and curses that would go some way to making me poor dear parents question how they raised their son.
Overall, I would highly recommend this game to anyone for the resons I listed in the pros (and possibly the cons depending on whether you thought of them as negatives or not) but there are a number of elements in the game that may turn people off.
Still, which other game gives you the ability to shed your draconic cloak, tunring it into a stationary dragon turret, and dance in the embers of your foes to the music of their dying screams!
....
OK now I'M questioning my upbringing.

Okay, so a lot of people are complaining about the price and how the game runs. It the optimization and system requirements are kind of insane. Even on the lowest graphic settings it is laggy and does not run very well, and my computer is a pretty decent one. However, the way it ran did not stop me from playing it. It was annoying, but I continued to play. If you have no friends, or your friends can't buy/play this game, then I wouldn't recommend it. I played by myself for a while and at the start it was kind of fun, but it just gets so boring alone. It takes forever to get resources and actually do things and then a t-rex can just destroy your whole base which you spent so many hours making. And if you are playing alone it is quite a bit harder and just boring after a while. If you play on a community server or a random server, it will be a terrible experience. Community servers have hackers and people who will destroy your base, camp you, etc. I tried looking for a friendly server to join and it was just awkward, and they expected me to be super active and be amazing at the game. And now, the price. I got it when it was 15$, and I think that is a fair price for it. Even 30$ isn't TOO much of a stretch. But 60$ is way too much, my friends won't buy it because of that price and they couldn't before since they didn't have the best computers, so now I have no one to play with.
Basically, I would not recommend this game because of how it runs, the price, and how it can get boring and playing alone/on community/random servers is a terrible experience, and everything (from gathering supplies to taming, etc) takes WAY too long. However, if you have friends to play with, you like these types of survival games and a challenge, and you have a lot of free time and you don't mind spending a ton of time on the game (and you have a good computer) then this is the game for you.

The harm video games cause can be evaluated by several criteria, and the most obvious among them is the negative effects they can have on physical health. Though the proponents of video gaming claim first-person shooters and real-time strategies sharpen reflexes, increase concentration, and muscle coordination, in reality, teenagers who spend an ample amount of time playing games experience effects that are not so beneficial.
There is a possibility of the loss of sight. Spending hours on a computer or in front of a TV is one of the main causes of blurred vision among youth. In addition, sacrificing healthy physical activities in favor of video gaming may become a risk factor for obesity. Gamers often do not want to interrupt their playing for meals. They eat right in front of the monitor, and their rations often consist of products that can be easily cooked or eaten immediately, such as crisps, chocolate bars, crackers, or other fast foods. All this definitely does not contribute to the proper and healthy development of a young, growing body.
Mental health can also be affected by engaging in video games at a young age. This suggests addiction and inappropriate behavior. It is a well-known fact that many gamers (especially fans of online games) suffer from addiction, which is no less serious than narcomania or alcoholism. For instance, in August 2005, a report surfaced about the death of a 28-year-old southern Korean gamer who had spent 50 hours playing a real-time strategy game (BBC). For another significant example, one needs to look no further than July 2012, when a Taiwanese teenager fatally collapsed after a 40-hour game session (Crawley). Cases like these are quite numerous and happen all around the world. They make additional arguments to the negative evaluation of video games as an activity which brings harm to young people.
In its turn, inappropriate behavior can be caused by violence in video games. According to research, children and teenagers who play violent video games tend to be more aggressive. They confront their teachers and peers more often and display a decline in academic achievements. Such psychological deviations also do not implicate video games as a constructive and useful occupation for young people (Crane).
Individuals who spend excessive hours playing video games may lack the capability to distinguish between reality from fantasies. Video games often offer simplified and conditional models of environments, relationships, friendships, and rivalries. Gamers use these models to learn to interact with the world around them, and they often lack skills that would be developed by real life experience instead of the simulation (Crane). Therefore, it can be implied that another negative effect caused by video games is the inability of social adaptation on the part of the gamer.
It can be concluded that video games are a form of entertainment which is not suitable for children and teenagers. This assessment is based on a number of negative consequences that excessive video gaming causes. Young people who spend an inexplicable sum of hours playing video games are observed to be prone to sight loss and obesity. In addition, they tend to be more aggressive than their peers who do not play video games, and they experience difficulties with social adaptation. Also, video games can lead to addictions that are no less serious than alcoholism or narcomania, as evidenced in recent media stories reporting on deaths among inveterate video gamers. This collection of facts contributes to the negative evaluation of video games as an unwholesome activity for children and teenagers.

This game is fantastic if you're looking for a fast-paced action game. There are tons of cool, and unique weapons and modifications that you can build. There are also quite a few "Warframes" with their own unique abilties and play styles that they are suited for. That being said, this game is a HUGE grind fest. You'll find yourself playing the same exact mission over, and over again for just a single drop/resource. Once you gather the resources you need to build an item it will begin crafting in real time. This is about 12 hours for weapons and 3 days for warframes.
This game is mostly pay for convenience. You can buy special currency called "Platinum" or you can trade special items in-game to other players to obtain it. The latter is rather difficult because most people will just grind the item out, and if you want to sell an item you have to manually type out your advertisement in a global trade chat... This means you may spend HOURS trying to sell a single item for just a few platinum. You can also use platinum to buy cosmetic items such as new helmets, designs, and color sets.
This game can get very bland, very quickly for most people. The action is very engaging but the grind can become overwheliming. I've put in nearly 800 hours and find myself coming back every now and then but at this point I just can't bring myself to grind anymore. I've become so incredibly bored of the RNG system in this game that I just can't play it anymore. Sure there are resources to grind, and that's one thing because you are constantly getting more resources... But when you are grinding for items it just isn't rewarding. You'll find yourself grinding the same boss for HOURS just to get the last part of a Warframe that just won't drop because it's all RNG based. And if you want Void items you'll first have to grind out the Relics (Keys) which is a job by iteself, then you use those relics for a chance to unlock the item. It's all RNG based, and because of this the game can become incredibly grating. You'll often feel like you're just not making any progress at all.
There aren't really that many quests in the game, and of the quests that there are I'd say they're just downright aweful. They're mostly fetch-like quests. For instance "Go and collect 5 of this item", "Go and kill 50 of these guys", etc. The story is alright, nothing too interesting really. The environment and feel of the setting of the game are fantastic though.
The developers of this game are constantly listening to the community and will take steps to adjust it based on what the community wants. Sometimes they make some questionable decisions, even downright aweful sometimes. However, if the community doesn't like it, then they will most likely make changes until the community is satisfied. The devs also do weekly streams on Twitch.Tv where they interact with the community and give updates on future updates.
If you are purely looking for an action game and don't mind the grind I highly recommend this game. If you can't stand grinding then don't even bother. This game is built around grind, that is the games core. This game is the essense of RNG. Everything revolves it.

I bought Ark because I wanted a good Dinosaur game to play with friends. Priced at $30, the price was a bit steep for an early access game but I got it on sale so I didn't care. Since purchasing it, I've been wrestling with settings for years to have a smooth experience and still find smooth frames impossible on my Intel Core i7-6700HQ processor with 8GB of RAM. Going into water? Be prepared for your game to freeze for 5-10 seconds. Coming out of water? That's another 5 seconds frozen. I figured, over the next 2 years, the game would be better optimized and more poeple could see this game's full potential. I don't know how they did it, but it got WORSE. The "optimization fixes" they so proudly put out only ever deleted my friend's world file and slowed my game down. Every patch is multiple gigabytes and there are no patch notes to read before the patch automatically starts downloading. The game is built for players who want to be in tribes of 50 people, so non-dedicated sessions can never be normal because even with exp and resource multipliers some creatures simply can't be tackled with only four players, the limit for non-dedicated sessions. Also they released a $20 DLC map full of content you can spend engram points on but not be able to create if you don't have the DLC, as the resources for it are not available. Then they promptly abandoned that DLC, leaving it unpatched and unbalanced. Now the price has doubled to $60 and is still unfinished. They say it'll be officially out of early access this August but what does that matter if it still won't be optimized? A change in title, nothing else, only a price increase. The only good thing the ARK devs are doing is paying modders to create content, which should be encouraged. Overall, there's absolutely no way I can recommend this game, even though I'm addicted to it. It's too expensive, it's business practices are too disreputable, and it's optimization is too poorly done.

Strictly speaking, this isn't actually a game.
It's a shiny way to commit chronocide.
It's something to do while you're waiting for what you really want to play to finish downloading or updating, or you just don't have enough time to put into actually playing anything.
Of the various clicking games I've come across (Cookie Clicker, et al), this is one of the better ones. It starts off painfully slow, but if you stick with it, it eventually ramps up. And thankfully, it doesn't require constant clicking to advance. There are skills and power ups, and leveling, and there's some RMT stuff in there so that you can spend money on it and get the trading cards if that's your thing.
There's no skill required to advance, just time. And to get all of the achievements will take months. However, it's not a power hungry game, and your heroes are earning gold while you're not actively playing.
Pros: Will work on any system that can run Steam. There are achievements. Good for when you don't have a lot of time, or you're waiting for something else. Something to do while watching TV. It's free.
Cons: This isn't a game. Clicking gets old fast. It'll probably take more than a year to get all the achievements. It's the exact same thing you can play on the website.
Verdict: If you've got a lot of time to kill and can spare the pittance of space it takes on your hard drive, why not?

I should also point out that once installed ARK takes up over 100GB on your hardrive. The largest game BY FAR in my library.

TLDR; The game is pretty good, runs better than it used to but still not great, dinos look nice but AI is dull. Absolutely not worth 70 euros, get it on a sale.
The game is decent, though default XP/Harvest rates need to be tweaked or the game is an unbearable grind. Its pretty to look at, if your computer can run it well, although it tends to be ruined by things like a bronto stuck halfway into a rock, dinos spinning in place etc. The dino models are great, but I feel like they could've put more work into the AI. Dinos don't really interact with the world, they just walk around until a carnivore kills them because their AI is kill everything in sight. Which means you get things like tiny compys attacking a t-rex because they can't really tell what is a reasonable target or not.
At 15 - 30 euros this game was absolutely worth it. However, releasing a 20 euro expansion before development is even finished feels like bad form to me and with the latest DOUBLING of the price tag I will absolutely not recommend it. I knew a price increase was coming as it says so in the Early Access, but that was for retail. The game is as of now STILL in Early Access with an entire month to go before release day.
70 euros is the cost of a brand new triple-A game from a major franchise, it's incredibly hefty for a survival game that is pretty rough around the edges - far from the "Shining Diamond" Studio Wildcard promises us.

1 Month before Early access ends Studio WIldcard raised the prise from ~30€ to ~70€. It was said the price will change at release. The new price does not include the DLC for ~20€ - ignoring that releasing a payed DLC in early access is pretty mehh.
The game (still) has a memory leak. So you still have to restart at least every few hours or the game will crash.
Playing the game on a public server will eat all your time (or you will manage nothing); playing on a private/small server is way more relaxing and does not require permanent presence.
The game itself is nice and offers enough content to be worth the 70€. But the game is not complete and I personally doubt issues like the memory leak will be fixed. So there is no guarantee to even get a working game for 70€ which makes it not worth it (especially with +20€ for the DLC)

This game is a ton of fun when you have people to play with, and can still be enjoyed when played solo. Unfortunately, Warframe is not very new player friendly, with a lot of weapons locked behind mastery rank. It doesn't take a long time to boost your mastery rank, but the grind is definitely there. The gameplay is solid, and the gun fights are fast and engaging, requiring a combination of warframe abilities as well as the weapons the player is using. The parkour system is marginally better with the new and improved parkour, but most of the maps aren't parkour friendly, so there aren't many opporunities to fully utilize the parkour. Overall I recommend this game to anyone looking for a grindfest of a game that has many, many hours worth of content aside from the grinding.

First, ignore any review with less than 100 hours on it. If someone has less than 100 hours on ARK they haven't experienced the breadth of the game or how much the devs improve things as they go along. To me, that already says a lot, that you need at least 100 hours in a given game to have really experienced it.
ARK is a good game. It's not great, not yet. The critique that many people level towards ARK about it not being optimized is somewhat fair. The game is still early access, if only for a month. Devs have been pushing more and more bug fixes and optimizations these past few months. Perhaps not as many, or as important of them as we'd like, but enough that I have faith a lot of the longstanding issues and lack of graphical optimizations will be addressed on official release.
Gameplay wise, ARK is an in-depth survival crafting game that I've thoroughly enjoyed every minute of. There are many different ways to play, and with heavy access to mods, there is a combination for single player or a server for about every taste. Few things in gaming make me jump from getting spooked. Turning a corner or hearing the sound of a raptor when I'm low level on a new map instills genuine fear and panic in me, if only for a moment. The feeling of triumph when you tame your first big creature like a T-Rex or a Giganotosaurus is exhilerating, and there's hours to be spent building, breeding, and exploring. If you're looking for a game with a ton of play time in it without it getting stale, ARK is it. The only games I have more hours in are Dark Souls I and II, and the Elder Scrolls series which is pretty incredible.
The online community, as with many games, is a mixed bag. Official servers are often the wild-west. Not a lot of "fair" tactics etc. and they're largely ruled by Alphas. The thrill of surviving under the harsh rule of an Alpha, trying to topple one, or trying to become one yourself is a unique aspect of Official servers. Unofficial servers have much more variety and much more active admins. Because of this, most of my time has been spent on Unofficial servers, so take that for what you will. Either way, there are good official servers, and bad ones, just as there are good and bad unofficial servers. With a little looking and some exploring, you can find a server that fits your style and tastes.
In regards to the recent price hike: a lot of people are up in arms about the price going from $20 or $30 to $60 a month before release. While it does kind of stink for people who haven't gotten in yet, from a business perspective, this makes sense. Early Access is cheaper for people because they are essentially guinea pigs. The devs have taken feedback from the players for almost 2 years now. They aren't likely to use feedback garnered by players with less than a month in the game, with days before official release. If they leave it low up until launch day, tons of people will snatch it up for cheap just before hand without actually doing the "work" of early access testing. Sure the game isn't finished yet, but when they ship it in a month it will be. You can think of the price hike as a sort of pre-release price. Hopefully this makes sense to people and they'll cut the devs some slack. As per usual, the biggest critics are louder than the best supporters usually. Unfortunately, ARK has really suffered from people whining about the flier nerf and some folks who wouldn't be happy with anything they ever do. I firmly believe on Official Release, this game will be better optimized and will be a great game instead of just the good game it is now. Either way, it's worth your time.

The most important but difficult feature of this game to master is the customization of your weapons, and frames with special cards that alter the abilities of said weapons, and frames.

Now I know anyone that has ever played this game knows that Oberon is a POS, and well it wasn't always. Oberon was my first frame, and my favorite, and I spent a lot of time researching and creating a fit to make that frame great again. It took a few weeks to do, but I finally did it, though to my misfortune the cards I used were heavily nerfed, the weapons I used were also heavily nerfed, and the frame was nerfed again. Really everything I had worked for just became useless, and while yes I understand the game is in Beta and it has "balance changes" all the time, it still hurts.

Warframe is a great game, but it has lots of issues. I only suggest you play this game if you can tolerate grinding and are extremely patient. This game is an instance based mmo that offers great action based combat, with a nice sample size of frames(characters) to choose from. I will warn you now to ONLY continue to play this game if you absolutely ADORE the combat like I did. There is literally nothing to do in endgame but to grind for gear you don't need to make platinum(premium currency) or trying out new weapons and frames. You will spend hours upon hours grinding pointlessly.
I will tell you now, the frames are definitely all unique and fun to play, since that will be your only fresh of breath air throughout the game, Although the weapons are pretty stale. Sure, there are a lot of weapons to choose from... but only a small sample size of them are even viable in high level content, like 60 minute+ survival missions. In order to be relevant in raids you have to have mods that are very expensive to aquire as they are limited time items that only other players have. You will spend a lot of time doing nothing, as every time you craft a new weapon, frame, or quest item, it takes 12-32 hours to make in REAL TIME. You can of course speed up the process with some platinum.
I am happy to tell you that yes, you CAN get everything in this game for free. Although it will take a LOT of time. There is no auction house in this game, so you are forced to trade 1v1 with other players, negotiating and advertising your items. Again, more of a time sink, and in a sense, more grind, as you have to sit there and spam the things you are selling into chat until someone shows interest in it. It has taken me upwards to 5 hours to sell even highly sought after items, so be warned.
PVP in this game is laughable at best. You start off with no mods for your frame and have to participate in the PVP to get a chance at a good mod dropping that you can actually use. You can also buy the mods with platinum that you make from PVE content, which is probably the better route. So for those that like PVP be warned, you will have to endure getting smashed on by players who have invested more time in it than you to eventually be relevent. Even when you finally do get the mods you need to play PVP enjoyably, you will probably be highly disappointed at the fact that the incredible combat in the PVE portion of this game is not even taken advantage of in PVP. Every player you come across will literally ninja flip constantly and snipe you with high single target guns.
If you can tolerate massive grind and the combat of this mmo is enough to drive you to play it, then by all means give it a shot.

I'll start by saying: this is a very addictive game. Although most of my ~250 hours were spent with the game running idly while i'm doing other things, I still think about it and check on it to level up my heroes often, and feel like I got a lot more enjoyment out of this as a Free game than most games i've paid for on Steam.
It is a idle game at its core, and at first seems like a knockoff of Cookie Clicker, but theres actually a bit more depth and complexity. The longer you play, the more complicated the game gets due to Ancients, Hero Souls, Gilding, etc. It requires some thought (and sometimes math, as the gold/health/damage numbers scale up astronomically) to figure out the best way to 'build' your characters to progress past a certain point.
In the first play-through is a bit slow and you'll hit a wall around level 140, then you have to reset to gain Hero Souls, get a few Ancients, and you find you can clear back up to where you were much faster. do that a few times and suddenly you can progress and buy higher level heroes. As you get more Souls/Ancients/Gilds your power scales up dramatically and suddenly you're clearing up to the 300's in 10 minutes, you could say thats really when the game really begins.

Warframe is a third person, space ninja grind fest...
AND I LOVE IT!
I only have 30 hours in this gane (as of writing this review), but I am hooked. You play as a "Warframe", some cybernetic...ninja thingy who goes around the solar system killing bad guys. Pretty basic. You can unlock new weapons and warframes using crafting materials you come across during missions. Using those along with the proper blueprint will get you a fancy new gun, or dude who shoots lighting bolts.
Pros:
-Beautiful graphics and presentation.
-Interesting and unique story.
-a HUGE amount of missions to play
-Challenging but not impossible difficulty curve
-an udderly insane amount of weapons and warframes to choose from.
-a very open customization system thatlets you change the helmet on your frame, add bits of things to the arms and legs, back cosmetics...ETC! These can also all be colored to your liking, including the color of your abilities themselves.
Cons:
-There is a TON of grinding involved with this game. Prepare to spend hours trying to find a single blueprint or rare crafting component.
-The level design can be slightly repetative at times, as many of the same set pieces are used quite often.
-Although there are a ton of missions to do, they can sometimes get a little repetative too. It gets annoying doing so many spy or survival missions.
Neither Pro nor Con:
Warframe has Microtransactions. Normally this bothers me, but it isn't as bad here as you can trade items with other players for the premium currency. Things aren't very expensive either, so with some effort you can get a decent ammount of Plat in no time!
All in all, I really do recommend Warframe. It's a fun game with very unique and interesting gameplay. The grinding can be a little tedious, but it isn't as horrible as it could be.

You land on an Island/Desert/Vally and have to survive the weather and dinosaurs from all kinds of periods, you craft tools from primitive stone hatchets to gasoline powered Chainsaws.

It starts with an epic awakening, enemies are all around you.
You are told by a mysterious voice that you are Tenno, a warrior, an ancient force of justice from an old era. Now, the Solar System is torn apart by several factions fighting each other for its control. And you're the only one who can restore peace and balance... by being a badass space ninja, suited in a powerful exoskeleton called Warframe.
Warframe is a 3rd person action free-to-play game developed by Digital Extremes. I have only been playing it for 8 months at the time of this review, but I can tell this game has grown A LOT since it premiered back in 2013. Not only has its wide variety of missions, customization, endless weapon arsenal and increasingly-large warframe list, but also a fascinating lore that keeps growing. The coop element is crucial: nothing beats the experience of a full team of 4 space ninjas, each with their unique powers and weapons, wreaking havoc among hordes of unlucky enemies.
It's very easy to get started with Warframe, but it takes a lot of time and dedication to master all of it. Most of that dedication translates into farming. Farming of exp points, resources, credits, mods, blueprints, etc. Everytime you finally manage to craft that new weapon or warframe is so satisfying,... that's when you get appreciate even the tedious part of the game. And even then, the game's variety makes up for it. In my case, I have been playing it for 8 months straight, but I can see myself spending at least three times that amount of time in the future. That's how hooked I got.
In addition, after all this time, the game has accumulated a lot of story and lore elements that make it even more enjoyable to dive into. The introduction of the cinematic quests, starting with the celebrated "The Second Dream", created a campaign mode in which the solo play is excused, making you feel you're playing the latest adventure of your favorite action saga. Plus these quests tend to unfold mindblowing revelations -the real nature of the warframes- and also new gameplay elements. And there´s nothing like playing them with your warframe wearing the latest fashion additions you managed to acquire after weeks of farming. Because looking fabulous is always important.
Also this game looks pretty. No, that's not quite it... GORGEOUS. There you go.
There's nothing much I can say about this game, other than it keeps growing, let's hope for the better, and I'm sure it will deliver more epic experiences in the future.

Warframe is a great game considering it's free to play.
It's action, it has a random level generator and it is mission based. It has its pre-defined campaign missions and scenarios, a lot of weapon leveling and customization, and the gameplay is pretty decent.
The fact that you can completely change your frames' (the multiple characters with unique abilities you control) at any time without needing any silly premium cash item to reset it makes this game one of my favores, because this brings cusotmization to a really deep and enjoyable level. And considering that there are some Mods (like special buff cards you attack to your frames and weapons) that are specifically designed for different types of enemies, being able to change them at any time is actually essential.
The game IS kind of grinding, having nicknames such as "Warfarm" and most of the stuff you can get without ever needing to buy Platinum, you just need to know how to drop and get the things you want to. So if you enjoy an action game with possibilities of playing in a 4 people party or doing "raids" with more people, you like to customize things and slice people with a large variety of melee weapons or just shoot people with many types of guns, this game is for you.
However, quite some time ago, they added an "operator" feature after completing the "The Second Dream" questline, which has such an interesting play, story and soundtrack, that for some reason I found myself crying after realizing what happened in that campaign. It was very well done compared to the other quests which are mostly "meh" and you just go ahead shooting and cutting people.
Still, a solid recommend.

This F2P game is a lot about grinding, but also has a lot of different game elements for everyone. There is a major PVE part, but you also have PVP, quests, minigames, and of course big customization options for almost everything. As a beginner you get easily lost in all the options, not only regarding optical customization but also modding and tweaking all your gear. The first tutorials have quite some room for improvements, but the publisher DE is very close to the community and trying to improve the different game elements all the time and adding new stuff on a regular basis.
As a basic concept of the game you steer different kind of warframes, a kind of parcour superhuman with special powers, each warframe with different abilities. Gear loadouts offer a vast variety of diffferent weapons, which can be farmed and built along the way.
There are almost too many options on what to do each day, since different play modes and mission goals can keep you busy for hours if you want to. This game has me hooked since 3 years and due to the constant updates by the dev team, there seems to be no end to this anytime soon. The community is one of the most helpful and friendly i have ever encountered!
Overall its a game with spectacular graphics, abundant options and play styles, but also tedious grinding for certain parts. I still love that game dearly and can only recommend it, but its surely not a game for everybody...

They really should have spent more time on the systems and LESS times on content. The AI is perhaps the stupidest of any game I have ever seen. Creatures getting stuck between trees amost all the time. Collison detection is also the worst - dinosaurs come through your buildings and can attack you (what the hell is the point of the walls again?). Had my dinosaurs's head sticking through my floor into my capfire so that I could not access the campfire.
The game really should be called "Ark: Grinding evolved," especially if you play with a few people and can't split up the work (and much of it is work). You'll be mindlessly chopping trees and smashing rocks long, long into the game. We've been playing for a while and unlike most survival games, where things get easier as you progress, Ark doesn't really feel that way. You grind and grind and grind, only to reach a point where you grind and grind and grind some more. It is fun to build, but at eery turn you'll be needing to refresh your stock of thatch, fiber, and wood every time you build a wall or two. Even using dinos to carry the load doesn't make it any more fun.
Animaton is choppy, even on a high end PC. Dinosaurs walking follow bizarre angels along the ground. It just feels like an unfinished game with LOTS of content, but little thought to the actual game. No polish on the systems. The character creation gives you lots of flexibility but most of the time (try using the random character generator) you wind up with something that looks like a mutant. Other than weird shapes you don't get a lot of different looks for the characters. It appears to be the same system that was there at EA release. Seems no more attention was given to it.
Building also seems to have been ignored suring the EA term. For example: wooden pillars, if building them after you've laid down a wooden ceiling, stick up throug the ceiling/floor (ceilings are also floors). And stacking pillars stacks the pillar half way into the other pillar, rather than from newar the base down. Water pipes have no ability to turn at anything other than 90 degrees (and only with a T). So you wind up having to build a lot of extra piping just to reach the point you're trying to get to - that's if you've managed to plan correctly.
I could go on and on and on about things that seem unfinished... and I wouldn't have posted this if not for the fact that this thing is supposed to leave EA on 8/8/17. I see that they're trying to sell this thing on Xbox and PS4 for $60!!!  This is not a $60 game. I don't care how much work went into all the "stuff," the labor theory of value is just as wrong here as anywhere else. The developers must either be high, or they've gotten tired of working on it so they're moving on. They'll probably leave a skeleton crew behind to "keep working on Ark." What a shame. What a sad ending for such a once promising title.

Let me start off by sayin that I could write a 5 page report over this game and still not add everything in that needs to be said about this game. I have days upon days of this game under my belt and still have days left to go, with more content being added all the time, sometimes brand new stuff, sometimes more of the same, but the same is good too.
Some things need to be said to preface this review: First, even though this is a free to play with microtransactions don't let that scare you, there is absolutely nothing in this game that you cannot earn with enough time invested and energy, that being said almost everything can be bought or sold, and likely, especially later, you will spend at least some time in the trading chat. The only thing in game you cannot get through trading with others is armor cosmetics. Sweet, preliminaries out of the way? Let's go.
First off, holy mother of balls space ninjas! You play as a Tenno, operating a specialized suit, or a WARFRAME, fighting off various factions in the Sol system to maintain balance. You will grind for gear, you will level up more weapons than a Ratchet and Clank game, and you will like it. You like stealth? We have stealth. Melee? How about a jet-powered hammer. Guns? Pick from snipers, pistols, flamethrowers, rocketlaunchers, DMR's, assault rifles, and the list goes on and on..... Each Warframe has abilities to suit different skills and playstyles, and the way you level up your overall level in this game (mastery rank) is by leveling up the various guns, weapons, warframes, kubrows (space dogs), kavats (space cats), and sentinels (little floating shoulder buddies), as well as archwings (space harness for surving the vacuum and going vroom in space) and the weapons for that as well. There is parkour, tighrope walking, and even ledge grabbing for the Sly Cooper in all of us. You fight several factions, such as the grineer, cloned soldiers that have been cloned so much they are facing genetic degenration, the Corpus, space merchants whose only goal is to profit, and the infestation, basically the Flood from halo, but more variance. The sotry is slowly but surely being added in, and those who like rich story can absolutely find it, but it is not something the developers throw at you, and this game goes great without the back story, and is just as enjoyable. If you play it long enough and then decide you actually want to learn about the story you can always come back and read or rewatch the cutscenes.
Some of my best friends I met through this game, and we always come back to play together. The Developers don't always make decisions that the entire community agrees with, but they are very good about listening, and are very active in the community. They host several different streams, making it extremely easy to keep up with them. There is a culture that comes with this game, you will learn about what potatos are, you will learn that the RNG gods are not merciful, and you will sometimes hate this game with a fiery passion so intense it threatens to destroy the entire universe....... but you will come back, you will place yourself at the feet of the RNG gods until they grant you what you wish, and you will squeal with delight when you finally get that last peice you needed for a prime Warframe. You will make bonds with people who know exactly what it's like to not get what you need 117 missions in a row, and you will always come back for more.

I was hesitant at first to try Warframe because it was another free to play game, with the potential to be pay to win.  I was pleasantly surprised by Warframe because it turned out not to be pay to win--the microtransactions only allow you to speed the process of getting the items and gear that you want and purchase cosmetic upgrades. The game allows you to trade for the currency that real world money buys you, driving a healthy in game economy.  I was also surprised to find that the developers, Digital Extremes, are extremely active with the community and listen to feedback.  You can tell they care about their game and are constantly working on new content and fixes.  The community is also great, most people are pretty kind and helpful, with it being a co-op game this is highly needed, and is nice to see after playing other free to play games with terrible communities like League of Legends, for example.
The basic premise of the game is that you control a "frame" that has its own unique powers, and you get to have a primary weapon (rifle, shotgun, sniper, etc), secondary weapon (pistols and smaller arms), a melee weapon (many different and creative varieties), as well as a companion (type of animal) or sentinel.  You level this equipment up and craft parts and mods for them to increase their power and functionality.  There is lots to choose from.  Also lots of customization options.
The controls are tight, the game runs very smoothly, and looks amazing.  Very well optimized.  Plenty of content.  The game does get to be grindy, as with all loot games, but I feel there is enough different weapons and styles of play to vary things up to keep you from getting too bored.  And if you do get bored, take a break for a few months and come back, there most likely be new content and changes that have occured that make the game interesting again for a while.
The story and subject matter are interesting as well, as its a mix of science fiction with ninja fantasy.  Surprisingly deep for a free to play, co-op MMO.
I definitely suggest if you enjoy fast paced shooters, science fiction, ninjas, and co-operative gameplay.  Best played with friends and its free to play. A quality free to play game, that doesnt feel free to play.

Warframe might be one of the best hack n' slash games I have ever played. It has an overwhelming amount of content and they are making more each day. There is just something about robotic-ish space ninja magic fighters flying through ships and planets to fight the everlasting war for...well what we fight for I still can't really say, except that fighting is just as cool as it sounds.
There is a massive arsenal to pick from as well as over 20 different Warframes, probably best compared to exo-skeletons or suits, with different skills and abilities. There are also multiple followers, both living and mechanical, that aid you on your missions. Tons of customization items and colors is avaliable to make your gear truly unique. The ability to further specialize your gear with the use of mods that are upgradeable which can change everything from damage type to exploding arrows for your bow-like weapons.
There are a couple of downsides to this game though. There is a currency, called credits, that you can buy with real money that you can use to buy most of what the game has to offer. This doesn't mean that this game is pay to win, as you would have to pay out a hefty amount to buy all the better gear and frames, since you still have to play to gain affinity or the games experience. It does however cut down on all the material collecting you will have to do to craft these things without using credits, and the time spent collecting materials will be a lot...A LOT! There is also the way of getting almost everything that you can buy using credits ingame without paying anything for it, however the downside is that you have a very limited inventory for your gear which can only be increased by buying slots using credits. You only have 2 slots for warframes before buying more for example. There is also a vast collection of cosmetics that can only be bought with credits. There is however a way to sell rare loot to other players for credits so it is possible to get this currency without paying real money, even though it will be hard work to gather enough for what you might need.
Warframe has a very active community and the developers, Digital Extremes, are communicating with it a great deal. They have two gameplay streams and one devstream weekly where they show new things added and new ideas for everyone. The forum is constantly getting new ideas for content and tweaks for the game, that the developers do care for and actually add or fix. Digital Extremes might very well be one of the most caring developers of any games I've ever seen...
To round it all up: This is a game worth trying and at least giving a chance more than 2 hours to get past the first step of learning, this game will be very daunting for a first time player. I would recommend trying it out with a couple of friends to make the experience easier since the game has a very steep learning curve and many players might be negative about this. I do love this game though and if you got through this review I hope that you at least give it a try.

Warframe is a third person, space ninja grind fest...
AND I LOVE IT!
I only have 30 hours in this gane (as of writing this review), but I am hooked. You play as a "Warframe", some cybernetic...ninja thingy who goes around the solar system killing bad guys. Pretty basic. You can unlock new weapons and warframes using crafting materials you come across during missions. Using those along with the proper blueprint will get you a fancy new gun, or dude who shoots lighting bolts.
Pros:
-Beautiful graphics and presentation.
-Interesting and unique story.
-a HUGE amount of missions to play
-Challenging but not impossible difficulty curve
-an udderly insane amount of weapons and warframes to choose from.
-a very open customization system thatlets you change the helmet on your frame, add bits of things to the arms and legs, back cosmetics...ETC! These can also all be colored to your liking, including the color of your abilities themselves.
Cons:
-There is a TON of grinding involved with this game. Prepare to spend hours trying to find a single blueprint or rare crafting component.
-The level design can be slightly repetative at times, as many of the same set pieces are used quite often.
-Although there are a ton of missions to do, they can sometimes get a little repetative too. It gets annoying doing so many spy or survival missions.
Neither Pro nor Con:
Warframe has Microtransactions. Normally this bothers me, but it isn't as bad here as you can trade items with other players for the premium currency. Things aren't very expensive either, so with some effort you can get a decent ammount of Plat in no time!
All in all, I really do recommend Warframe. It's a fun game with very unique and interesting gameplay. The grinding can be a little tedious, but it isn't as horrible as it could be.

One of the very few free-to-play games that is actually FREE in the long term. The exception is cosmetic items made by Steam users who have won the right to be put into the game. The in-game currency can readily be traded for by farming up various item parts and blueprints, primarily those that are Primed.
Digital Extremes is a developer I personally respect for their transparency. You will know almost any kind of change that is upcoming, and if it meets with a lot of negative feedback? Chances are it'll be reversed or altered in some way to make it far more acceptable and an overall improvement.
The game itself is a mission-based third-person shooter that can be played solo or cooperatively with up to three additional players. There's also a handful of "raid" missions, though they are not as relevant to Warframe as such a thing would be to a traditional MMO. PvP also exists in the form of the Conclave, where your skill is virtually the only deciding factor in combat.
Warframe's one of those games that I'd suggest anyone with even a mild interest try out. Nothing is required of you except a bit of time and a download. With its fast-paced and visceral gameplay you might fall in love with it like I did.

Overall the game does not get explained very well in the sense that this game has the running joke of being the game needing a wiki to play, since the dev's are very communicative with the community and understand these problems allot of updates do find added new and updated tutorials and more tips to explain a new player what is going on.
Their is many game modes and content to pick from and with the new update to the map content gottten a better direction and more variated constant rewards for players to enjoy and motivate to try out.
Allot of the weapons will feel powerful and cool and some might feel underpowered, this has been a problem since there is many weapons in this game and allot that did not get updated yet.

The monetization of this game is also done in a very good way as in you can get anything in the game without having to pay for it and can even trade its currency used for the store which makes you able to just buy stuff from there by playing enough and interacting with the community.
In the store you will only find ways to fast track gameplay, none that would give a edge to a paying customer.
So far i don't play many shooter games myself anymore, i used to play allot CS 1.6, UT and Quake, this game has been my dirty pleasure of getting played every evening and i will always enjoy myself.
Being able to customize so many aspects of the look and the feel of things in the game makes this a endless sandbox for me to have fun in and even sometimes play it as "fashion frame" that it can rly be fun to dress up for the occasion of murdering.
The latest updates of this game got many praises since this gave it more clarity in story and amazing cutscenes and plot's to enjoy and makes me want to try to experience the game from a new account perspective and see how the long development of this game payed of in giving it a amazing experiences that flow better together now.
The greatest strengths of this game i would say are Customizability, Indepth parcour movement system, Regular updates, Good Community and dev's that communicate well with them.

If you want to improve at maths, play this game. It's more about calculation to figure out the best DPS and fastest way to gain "hero souls" than it is about clicking.
The way it works, you get a whole bunch of heroes. The first one improves your click damage, and all other heroes do DPS, which is an acronym that stands for Damage Per Second. Literally, they do damage automatically and you don't need to do anything for it. You increase their level to make them do more damage using gold dropped by monsters you kill. At certain levels, a new skill unlocks which gives effects ranging from increasing that hero's damage by 100%, or increasing overall DPS by all your heroes by 25%, increasing your click damage by a certain percentage of your heroes' total DPS (which is actually the brunt of your click damage), etc. Some of them teach a skill. There are nine skills in the game. For example, Clickstorm is a skill that automatically does 10 clicks per second for 30 seconds, with a 10 minutes cooldown. Proper use of skills is important to kill monsters faster. Especially because...
There are bosses. You have 30 seconds to kill them. If you don't kill them in time, you can't progress to the next stage. Every stage consists of ten monsters, and there is a boss every five stages, on multiples of five. By stage 100 and above, bosses have a chance to be "Primal", which is a special version of the boss that drops "hero souls". Every boss from stages in multiples of ten starting from stage 100 (100, 110, 120, etc) give a "gild" to a random hero from your list. At stage 100, you also unlock ancients.
Hero souls is a special "currency" that does two things. First, it increases your base DPS (what you have when you start the game) by 10% for each hero soul you have. It doesn't show in your DPS that is shown in your total current DPS shown in the hero tab, but it definitely affects it. Having hero souls is important to improve your damage and general progression, or else your DPS is too slow. However, they also serve as currency to unlock ancients.
Ancients are special "characters" that do various passive bonuses. There are a bit over 20 of them, and four are selected randomly for you to pick one from. It can be rerolled if you don't want them, but that costs hero souls. Anyway, ancients effects include increasing all your DPS by a certain amount but only when you are idle (i.e. not clicking or using skills for 60 seconds), increasing the amount of time you get to fight a boss, increasing click damage, getting a LOT more gold from random treasure chests, etc. Ancients are absolutely key to progressing in the game, so you need to find a good balance between keeping enough hero souls on yourself to keep a good DPS bonus, while still improving your ancients that will benefit you more than the hero souls' DPS you lose for improving said ancients. It can get very technical on a mathematical level.
Gilds are a type of bonus awarded to your heroes. They're assigned to a random hero when you get them from defeating a boss that is a  multiple of 10 starting from stage 100, but it is later possible to move them to other heroes for a cost (in hero souls). A gild improves that hero's damage by 50%, and gilds are cumulative. For instance, having five gilds on a hero increases its damage by 250%. You definitely want those on heroes that gain a lot of "attack bonus" skills on themselves (such as Masked Samurai) rather than on heroes that have other effects that don't involve having a lot of DPS (such as Alexa which mostly improves click and critical damage, Midas which mostly improves gold drops, etc).
Finally, "Ascension" is the other important mechanic to explain. Once you get the skill "ASCENSION" from the hero named Amenhotep, you can learn the skill to do an ascension, which brings you down to the first stage and you lose all your money and your heroes lose all their skills. In exchange for "starting over", you gain a certain amount of hero souls based on a few things.
Hero souls gained from killing a Primal boss are only truly awarded after ascending. Also, each 2000 cumulative hero levels you had before ascension give an additional hero soul upon ascension. When you ascend, you keep your gilds and ancients. With the hero souls you gain, you are able to progress faster than the previous time, and you can get overall further and faster. A lot of the joy in the game is the way you get a little bit further than the last time you ascended, each time you get there.
There's a bit more to the game, but this is most of the important stuff that you need to know. Another thing of note which, to my knowledge, is not explained by the game, is that after level 200, a hero gains four times the amount of DPS as normal, every 25 levels, and most importantly, ten times that amount at level 1000 (and 2000 and 3000). It's important to note because once you get to a certain point and the next hero (Dread Knight) is just faaaaaar too expensive, you want to go back to your first hero and level him up to 1000 which becomes the new best thing, rather than keep increasing the last available hero (Frostleaf) who gains rather minimal DPS. You'll need to ascend many many times before you can even dream of getting Dread Knight, so get those early heroes to level 1000 which is the new meta at that point.
Since a lot of the progression is done through DPS, which is automatic, it's an easy game to play which you can leave running in the background while you do other things and that you can check on once in a while. One thing of note is that when the game is closed, your heroes still are gaining gold from monsters they kill. It's like the game keeps playing itself even when it's closed, although they won't progress to the next level/set of enemies or go past bosses and such. Only gold from monsters of the current highest stage you're at is considered. Since this is such a relaxing game to play, which you don't need to pay a whole lot of attention to most of the time, I recommend it to whoever isn't afraid of doing some maths to maximize their experience with the game. Or following a guide, I suppose. :p
Finally, it is a very known fact that you can use "autoclicker" programs with this game. I personally don't because it's not something I feel is natural to the game's intent and purposes, but it's something you can do, which a lot of people do. When playing without, most of the damage come from DPS and you don't need to click and/or can click only for important stuff such as bosses when you need the extra damage (and/or when using all your skills together for burst damage). Of course having such a program running nonstop will be a large part of your damage compared to someone playing without, especially with relevant ancients that complement that, so keep that in mind.

Warframe is a third person, space ninja grind fest...
AND I LOVE IT!
I only have 30 hours in this gane (as of writing this review), but I am hooked. You play as a "Warframe", some cybernetic...ninja thingy who goes around the solar system killing bad guys. Pretty basic. You can unlock new weapons and warframes using crafting materials you come across during missions. Using those along with the proper blueprint will get you a fancy new gun, or dude who shoots lighting bolts.
Pros:
-Beautiful graphics and presentation.
-Interesting and unique story.
-a HUGE amount of missions to play
-Challenging but not impossible difficulty curve
-an udderly insane amount of weapons and warframes to choose from.
-a very open customization system thatlets you change the helmet on your frame, add bits of things to the arms and legs, back cosmetics...ETC! These can also all be colored to your liking, including the color of your abilities themselves.
Cons:
-There is a TON of grinding involved with this game. Prepare to spend hours trying to find a single blueprint or rare crafting component.
-The level design can be slightly repetative at times, as many of the same set pieces are used quite often.
-Although there are a ton of missions to do, they can sometimes get a little repetative too. It gets annoying doing so many spy or survival missions.
Neither Pro nor Con:
Warframe has Microtransactions. Normally this bothers me, but it isn't as bad here as you can trade items with other players for the premium currency. Things aren't very expensive either, so with some effort you can get a decent ammount of Plat in no time!
All in all, I really do recommend Warframe. It's a fun game with very unique and interesting gameplay. The grinding can be a little tedious, but it isn't as horrible as it could be.

Absolutely love the game. The survival aspect of the game is decent, the learning curve is not that steep and easy to get a hang of. Crafting is fluid. To me personally i dislike the new TEK tier, it makes the game too easy to play, but if you play on a server (or create your own server) that has certain engrams (unlocks) turned off to make it harder, the game keeps being fun. The server i own (10 player server), has all metal structures, all firearms, all patform saddles, all electronics and all TEK related engrams disabled. Additionally there are less dino's roaming the lands and you wont encounter a t-rex around every corner. This way actually finding a rex is a feat on its own and because there are no firearms its a bigger challenge to tame one of those, no matter what the level is. Building in the game has its flaws but its managable, you can create some amazing structures in it. The mod count for the game also keeps the game fun for a longer time and there are some amazing mods out there. All in all, there is a reason why i spent over 1400 hours in the game and trust me when i say that i will reach the 1500 mark soon.

Warframe is a great game considering it's free to play.
It's action, it has a random level generator and it is mission based. It has its pre-defined campaign missions and scenarios, a lot of weapon leveling and customization, and the gameplay is pretty decent.
The fact that you can completely change your frames' (the multiple characters with unique abilities you control) at any time without needing any silly premium cash item to reset it makes this game one of my favores, because this brings cusotmization to a really deep and enjoyable level. And considering that there are some Mods (like special buff cards you attack to your frames and weapons) that are specifically designed for different types of enemies, being able to change them at any time is actually essential.
The game IS kind of grinding, having nicknames such as "Warfarm" and most of the stuff you can get without ever needing to buy Platinum, you just need to know how to drop and get the things you want to. So if you enjoy an action game with possibilities of playing in a 4 people party or doing "raids" with more people, you like to customize things and slice people with a large variety of melee weapons or just shoot people with many types of guns, this game is for you.
However, quite some time ago, they added an "operator" feature after completing the "The Second Dream" questline, which has such an interesting play, story and soundtrack, that for some reason I found myself crying after realizing what happened in that campaign. It was very well done compared to the other quests which are mostly "meh" and you just go ahead shooting and cutting people.
Still, a solid recommend.

Based on mis-informed negativity from new players, I'll start right away by mentioning what they all got wrong.
- "Free2Play" does not equal "Free Game". (This goes for all F2P games out there). It means you can install and start playing without having to spend money upfront like retail games. Sooner or later you will hit a paywall. How obstructive this paywall is differs from game to game. In the case of Warframe, you can actually trade premium currency (Platinum) between players. So you can technically get everything that costs platinum for free. Yes, it will cost time and effort, but if you don't have either of these nor can't/won't spend real money to buy Platinum (with discount Coupon!), then F2P games are simply not for you.
Games costs thousands/millions to make, all that money needs to be earned by developers,  this is called " earning a living".  Angry teens still living at home always scream "greedy developers" without knowing squat about how real life works. Stop embarassing yourselves by coming up with absurd suggestions how you could do it better without any paywalls.
Certain abilities and weapons in the game have been quite powerful in the past. So powerful that unskilled players were immortal gods of war by pressing a single button to obliterate the entire battlefield without even needing to aim, I mean this literally. This made the game utterly not challenging at all, no real effort was required by these players to advance in the game. During special events and missions where a handicap is applied to the players where their nuke button couldn't help them, guess what, these players perform terrible and blame the game.
Once the devs fixed these OP issues, out came the torches and pitchforks. These people, they are BAD at videogames. Plain and simple. Their idea of good videogame design is "Fun = Easy". (somebody actually said that in the official forums). I don't know about today's generation of "gamers" but last I checked playing fast-paced action videogames was always about the challenge. If I just wanted to repeatedly press one button to win, I would be better off playing Clicker Heroes. After all these so-called "nerfs" (and also "OP enemies"), I have no problem destroying the enemies the old-fashioned way: think fast, act smart, make wise judgement calls and
ALL online games have toxic players in them. Some more than others. We will always run into some of them. I have seen some people exaggerate that "majority" of Warframe community are toxic. I frequent the Steam and Warframe forums a lot. Only toxic players I see are the ones who get banned/suspended a lot and they blame the community instead. If somebody claims to continuously running into toxic behaviour in the game itself, they either are universally unlucky or they themselves are the reason they attract toxicity towards them by being toxic themselves but are too much a sociopath to acknowledge it. In general, there are not enough toxic players in Warframe to drive people away. If you're so sensitive about it, then I suggest to stay away from Region Chat. (Any region chat of any F2P game for that matter. They're always filled with the dumbest morons the internet has to offer). Joining a clan is highly recommended. uhh.. yeah. It's a grindy farming game. This game genre has existed for a long time since the Diablo days. Where have you been ? If you don't like grind games, then don't waste your time playing them and don't waste other people's time by complaining about games you never should've played in the first place.  This is not a single player game with an ending followed by credits. It's all about gathering resources and crafting the next best thing to make your gear loadout more powerful. There is no static endgame if that is what you were expecting.
You have reached the burnout stage. EVERYBODY eventually comes to this point in games like these. This is normal. Just take a break and play other games. Okay this is a tough recommendation at the moment for the progress of Ark so I will go through the pros and cons.
Pros:
- A LOT of content
- Subline backstory
- Beautiful game
- New mechanics and content added monthly
Cons:
- A lot of content but very messy and appears out of control
- It is a beautiful game for those who can afford a medium/high end set up
- Early access though it will soon be out so bugs/ glitches are abundant
- Can be difficult to get into (especially on offical servers)
- Most offical servers and mainly PVP are out of control
- The price as of today has doubled to £55
There is good reason behind everybody complaining about the poor optimization of Ark...that being it is VERY poor however despite people claiming the developers do not listen to their fan base, they really do listen. There is many forums and websites where people can talk about a bug or glitch in the game and the developers respond and react quickly. The majority of players are confused about how the devs do not "fix" the game. The devs of Ark want to release as much physical content out before beginning to fix the bugs. It makes sense to get all of the ideas out first and then fix it all instead of spending all of their time fixing things every month. Do not listen to people saying the developers have abandoned the integrity of the game, they just want to provide the players with as many interesting things and mechanics as possible before fine tuning everything.
The community of Ark is varied depending on the servers you visit. In my experience most people on pvp servers are cruel and harsh but I can only say the same for pve. If you brave the journey of public servers, bring friends as it will not be easy. Just stick to singleplayer or private servers where you can modify the Ark to your own desires, wether you want to tame all of the growing amount of creatures Ark holds or to feast upon the corpses of the ultimate life forms. Set your own goals and enjoy the experience.
The sudden rise of the price is strange and at this price I would not reccommend the game, maybe on offer or if you already own the game but uninstalled a while back, Ark is improving and hopefully the need of a powerful PC will decrease. Besides the games draw back I can honestly say that Ark along with other great successors (The Isle for example) is an amazing game with a large crew who actively interact with their audience.
Great game and will hopefully keep getting better!

This game is a must play. It takes a solid couple of missions to really get ahold of what you can do mobility wise and the mastery ranking system, which is similar to an account lvl, helps you to learn all the different aspects of the gameplay. On top of amazing gameplay and an immense amount of weapons and warframes to play it's nigh impossible to get bored of this game also, there are new weapons and frames released all the time. On top of all that, the game isn't a pay to win. Admittedly you can pay to speed some things up or for convenience but, it ultimately isn't a necessary thing. Additionally, if you want to get some platinum (in game payed currency), you can by selling rare items that you pick up from missions to other players via the trade chat.
Moving away from gameplay lets talk about the community and the developers Digital Extremes. They are simply the best! When starting up, players will help you get going in not only helping you complete more difficult missions, but also they will literally give you free upgrades and mods to help your warframes and weapons become stronger faster. I have played many games both competitive and cooperative multiplayer but, none have even come close to how amazing and helpful this community is. On top of the fact that the player base is amazing, DE (Digital Extremes) really works with the players to make things or change things that the community likes or dislikes. DE also recently have been releasing amazing narrative missions with there recently added mocap room which they showed on their Devstream. Also DE does Devstreams where the head of each development department sit on a couch and streams on twitch to talk about incoming updates, give away free platinum, and answer questions from chat.
This game is a must play and is even more fun if you and couple of friends join in together.

If you have loads of time to kill and dont want to spend money on a new experience then there is no better game to throw it towards, out of other F2P games i've came across over the years i believe Warframe to be one of the better if not the best one. The only real thing you will feel like you need to buy at some point is weapon/warframe slots but other than that unless you want cosmetics you can get along perfectly fine without throwing money into it, so i believe it's at least worth a weekend to see if its your thing.

What is Warframe?
It's a Fast-Paced Third-Person Shooter Hack & Slash Action Game with Co-Op and MMORPG elements, among some other things mixed together. It's also completely Free to Play!
It's set in the far future, where you play as an armored cyborg space ninja with magic powers, travelling across the Solar System, exploring and completing various missions, uncovering the hidden purpose behind everything.
In this game, you are the Judge, Jury and Executioner for every member of the various alien factions you meet along the way, dispensing justice in the most stylish way possible with a huge variety of different customizable weapons.
While the game definately can be played as an enjoyable Single-Player experience, it was primarily designed around playing together with other people.
This game breaks all the rules for traditional RPG's, you are not limited to specific classes, skill builds and weapon choices. You can switch and change anything as much as you like.
You can totally be a sneaky stealthy tank healer while using a bow with explosive arrows, dual-wielding machineguns, carrying a heavy two-handed greatsword all at the same time and still be very effective at all stages of the game.
On the ranged side of weapons, you have everything from shotguns, assault and sniper rifles to guns that shoot lasers, rockets, fire, ice, lightning, blades or black holes.
On the melee side of weapons, you have everything from swords, hammers and axes to nunchakus, whips and gunblades. You can also change their entire movement set by using different Stances.
There are very few actual main storyline quests and ever fewer cutscenes, but most of those quests are very well made and can be extremely rewarding to players that invest a lot of time in to the game.
As you progress thoughout the game, you will unlock more and more new gameplay modes and mechanics, the game can always suprise you with something even after hundreds and hundreds of hours of playtime.
The lore is quite interesting and isn't shoved in your face, most of it is hidden away and you have work for it if you're really interested.
This game puts alot of emphasis on style in every part of it, you also can spend hours on just making your Warframe look as terrible or as fabolous as you want it to. It's way better than Space Barbie.
You can also have a Space Dog. You can also have a Space Cat. You can also have a Flying Space Roomba with a shotgun.
Warframe can eventually boil down to just a grinding farming simulator, but that's the nature of every dungeon-crawling type of RPG's, at least in this game you can wallrun and do backflips while your at it.
While you can acquire 99.9% of all items in the game for free, some items can take a significant amount of time and effort to get, so it can get frustrating if you want something specific very badly.
The game is in no way Pay-to-Win, you can easily complete all the content with stuff you can get very early in the game. As far as Free-to-Play games go, this one is quite generous and is pretty fair overall.
The more you play, the more you will understand that there isn't actually anything you really need to spend money on, especially considering you can earn the real money currency in-game for free by trading items.
I would recommend investing just a little amount of real money to make your life a lot more convienient, but it's totally optional and unnecessary to progress through the game.
I personally spent most of my real money currency on purely cosmetic items that I could've gotten eventually anyway, so take from that what you will. #FashionFrame is EndGame.
Solid recommendation, one of the best Free-to-Play games on Steam.

Don't be fooled by the title. This game is more than just clicking on monsters. You build up a team of heroes that will do your damage, and recruit ancients that gives bonuses to several aspects of the game. After a while it's more about min-maxing your ascensions than just letting it idle.
I admit, I sat there the first 1,5h and clicked. I couldn't stop. Then I realized I could let the game click for me, while I manage the team instead. You might think this is dumb, but when you see that you cannot get past level 139... Then you start wondering if it's more to this game than you think... And you have to find out how deep this rabbit hole goes.
First ascension takes like 4 days (active and idle playing). Then maybe 1 day, and after that it's up to you how many times you want to ascend per day. There are ancients bonuses that support both active (clicking) and passive (no clicking) gameplay. So you don't have to buy a new mouse.
It's free to play. None of the micro transactions are really needed. You can even find the microtransactions currency in game. So you can really support the creators without messing up the gameplay.
Addictive little game. It's taken up too much of my time. I log on to it in the morning before I go to work to invest the gold found while sleeping. And I can't wait to get home to do some more ascensions.
Note: The game plays even when closed. As it's based upon time and date. You don't have to have it open at all time to get gold. In fact it's better closed if you cannot be at your computer for a longer time.
