There are very few games that have held my attention for 1,000+ hours over the years, this is one of them. I created an account back when the game was still in Beta (late 2014), back then it was was just a simple module with some enemies to kill with a handful of warframes to choose from. Even then though it showed promise. Over time they have added tons of content, new warframes, weapons galore, new planets, mission types, Archwing (fly in space!), events, clan dojos and foundry, player to player trading system, syndicates to join, player HUBs (relay stations), PVP, 8 player Raid etc etc. If you enjoy third person shooters, 4 player coop, pvp, raiding, RPG's and/or ninjas in space (lol) this game is a dream come true then for you. Being that it is free to play there is literally nothing to lose checking it out.
The game is a constant work in progress and the developer Digital Extremes (DE) is constantly tweaking and adding new content all the time. Warframe has a very decent crafting system and you will most likely find yourself trying many different warframes/weapons combinations to see which one(s) fit your style the best. Believe me the game encourages you to do so, it is surprising the amount of variety in the game. When you find something you like it is a rewarding feeling and you will too it is just a matter of time. Also decent customization for your warframes, weapons, Sentinels (companion), Kubrows and kavats (dog companion and cats too!), Liset (your ship), with a multitude of color choices, skins and attachments.
With the new war withing update there has been updated story. Its amazing, if you want too feel that its more than ninjas in space with guns feel into this game, then completing these missions will be a facinating experience for you. Not going to go into spoilers but a mission named 'The second dream' will give you alot of answers on the story. The fact that the developers accually managed to fit this into a such well made game makes me even more happy. The missions feels like they should be there and not just something that adds on top of the cake. Its what makes the cake delicious.
Every Warframe has its own set of individual abilities, they all have a total of 4. Some are better at being tanky, dps, sneaking (cloaking), solo play, healers, AOE damage, defense etc. There is a Warframe for every situation it seems. You can also make your own builds for each frame based on what mods you have (you attain them while playing missions they are dropped by enemies) For example "Continuity" mod allows for longer power duration time, when you ability is activated. More ammo, damage mods etc etc sooooo many. Making building your perfect Warframe/weapons very flexible and enjoyable. You have the opportunity to have a Primary, secondary and melee weapon. With the opportunity to make your own builds for everything here adds to the games replayability imo. Same goes for sentinels, kubrow and kavat companions they all have their own set of mods, especially made for them.
That being said the game can be very grindy, especially for newer players. That is to be expected though being that it is an MMOish experience. Especially to gather enough resources and credits to craft your items. Well worth it though if you have the time to invest. Sometimes they seem to nerf warframes and weapons for no reason at all and then they rework it again and "fix" it. Nerf/Un-nerf is the nature of free to play MMO' ish kind of games. (Constant "balance" tweaking) This is not an instant gratification game either, the game gets better the more you play it. You can also purchase items with real money from the in game market, it is NOT necessary though.The special money currency can be traded for items you find, between players and they even have there own marketing chat. Most things can be attained by just playing the game gathering resources and crafting them accordingly. Except, of course vanity items, skins, unique color palettes and limited time only items that have been available over the course of the game.
DE sometimes gifts players new color palettes and send them to your inbox (valentine's day, halloween, St. Patrick's day etc.) Free weapons too, they seem to do somethings special on the games anniversary every year. The developer also listens to community feedback and designs and have added many things based on that. Which is always a plus. The game can also get repetitive at times, but with the amount of content in game now that is harder to happen. You just have to mix it up from time to time and try new things within the game.
All in all the future looks bright for this game. A Developer that actually listens to community feedback. Constant updates/hotfixes. Plus there is so much new content coming soon! Game is not perfect of course, but what game truly is right. There is a lot to enjoy here and unique setting and premise to the game, definitely sets itself apart from the competition.

What is Warframe?
It's a Fast-Paced Third-Person Shooter Hack & Slash Action Game with Co-Op and MMORPG elements, among some other things mixed together. It's also completely Free to Play!
It's set in the far future, where you play as an armored cyborg space ninja with magic powers, travelling across the Solar System, exploring and completing various missions, uncovering the hidden purpose behind everything.
In this game, you are the Judge, Jury and Executioner for every member of the various alien factions you meet along the way, dispensing justice in the most stylish way possible with a huge variety of different customizable weapons.
While the game definately can be played as an enjoyable Single-Player experience, it was primarily designed around playing together with other people.
This game breaks all the rules for traditional RPG's, you are not limited to specific classes, skill builds and weapon choices. You can switch and change anything as much as you like.
You can totally be a sneaky stealthy tank healer while using a bow with explosive arrows, dual-wielding machineguns, carrying a heavy two-handed greatsword all at the same time and still be very effective at all stages of the game.
On the ranged side of weapons, you have everything from shotguns, assault and sniper rifles to guns that shoot lasers, rockets, fire, ice, lightning, blades or black holes.
On the melee side of weapons, you have everything from swords, hammers and axes to nunchakus, whips and gunblades. You can also change their entire movement set by using different Stances.
There are very few actual main storyline quests and ever fewer cutscenes, but most of those quests are very well made and can be extremely rewarding to players that invest a lot of time in to the game.
As you progress thoughout the game, you will unlock more and more new gameplay modes and mechanics, the game can always suprise you with something even after hundreds and hundreds of hours of playtime.
The lore is quite interesting and isn't shoved in your face, most of it is hidden away and you have work for it if you're really interested.
This game puts alot of emphasis on style in every part of it, you also can spend hours on just making your Warframe look as terrible or as fabolous as you want it to. It's way better than Space Barbie.
You can also have a Space Dog. You can also have a Space Cat. You can also have a Flying Space Roomba with a shotgun.
Warframe can eventually boil down to just a grinding farming simulator, but that's the nature of every dungeon-crawling type of RPG's, at least in this game you can wallrun and do backflips while your at it.
While you can acquire 99.9% of all items in the game for free, some items can take a significant amount of time and effort to get, so it can get frustrating if you want something specific very badly.
The game is in no way Pay-to-Win, you can easily complete all the content with stuff you can get very early in the game. As far as Free-to-Play games go, this one is quite generous and is pretty fair overall.
The more you play, the more you will understand that there isn't actually anything you really need to spend money on, especially considering you can earn the real money currency in-game for free by trading items.
I would recommend investing just a little amount of real money to make your life a lot more convienient, but it's totally optional and unnecessary to progress through the game.
I personally spent most of my real money currency on purely cosmetic items that I could've gotten eventually anyway, so take from that what you will. #FashionFrame is EndGame.
Solid recommendation, one of the best Free-to-Play games on Steam.

There are very few games that have held my attention for 1,000+ hours over the years, this is one of them. I created an account back when the game was still in Beta (late 2014), back then it was was just a simple module with some enemies to kill with a handful of warframes to choose from. Even then though it showed promise. Over time they have added tons of content, new warframes, weapons galore, new planets, mission types, Archwing (fly in space!), events, clan dojos and foundry, player to player trading system, syndicates to join, player HUBs (relay stations), PVP, 8 player Raid etc etc. If you enjoy third person shooters, 4 player coop, pvp, raiding, RPG's and/or ninjas in space (lol) this game is a dream come true then for you. Being that it is free to play there is literally nothing to lose checking it out.
The game is a constant work in progress and the developer Digital Extremes (DE) is constantly tweaking and adding new content all the time. Warframe has a very decent crafting system and you will most likely find yourself trying many different warframes/weapons combinations to see which one(s) fit your style the best. Believe me the game encourages you to do so, it is surprising the amount of variety in the game. When you find something you like it is a rewarding feeling and you will too it is just a matter of time. Also decent customization for your warframes, weapons, Sentinels (companion), Kubrows and kavats (dog companion and cats too!), Liset (your ship), with a multitude of color choices, skins and attachments.
With the new war withing update there has been updated story. Its amazing, if you want too feel that its more than ninjas in space with guns feel into this game, then completing these missions will be a facinating experience for you. Not going to go into spoilers but a mission named 'The second dream' will give you alot of answers on the story. The fact that the developers accually managed to fit this into a such well made game makes me even more happy. The missions feels like they should be there and not just something that adds on top of the cake. Its what makes the cake delicious.
Every Warframe has its own set of individual abilities, they all have a total of 4. Some are better at being tanky, dps, sneaking (cloaking), solo play, healers, AOE damage, defense etc. There is a Warframe for every situation it seems. You can also make your own builds for each frame based on what mods you have (you attain them while playing missions they are dropped by enemies) For example "Continuity" mod allows for longer power duration time, when you ability is activated. More ammo, damage mods etc etc sooooo many. Making building your perfect Warframe/weapons very flexible and enjoyable. You have the opportunity to have a Primary, secondary and melee weapon. With the opportunity to make your own builds for everything here adds to the games replayability imo. Same goes for sentinels, kubrow and kavat companions they all have their own set of mods, especially made for them.
That being said the game can be very grindy, especially for newer players. That is to be expected though being that it is an MMOish experience. Especially to gather enough resources and credits to craft your items. Well worth it though if you have the time to invest. Sometimes they seem to nerf warframes and weapons for no reason at all and then they rework it again and "fix" it. Nerf/Un-nerf is the nature of free to play MMO' ish kind of games. (Constant "balance" tweaking) This is not an instant gratification game either, the game gets better the more you play it. You can also purchase items with real money from the in game market, it is NOT necessary though.The special money currency can be traded for items you find, between players and they even have there own marketing chat. Most things can be attained by just playing the game gathering resources and crafting them accordingly. Except, of course vanity items, skins, unique color palettes and limited time only items that have been available over the course of the game.
DE sometimes gifts players new color palettes and send them to your inbox (valentine's day, halloween, St. Patrick's day etc.) Free weapons too, they seem to do somethings special on the games anniversary every year. The developer also listens to community feedback and designs and have added many things based on that. Which is always a plus. The game can also get repetitive at times, but with the amount of content in game now that is harder to happen. You just have to mix it up from time to time and try new things within the game.
All in all the future looks bright for this game. A Developer that actually listens to community feedback. Constant updates/hotfixes. Plus there is so much new content coming soon! Game is not perfect of course, but what game truly is right. There is a lot to enjoy here and unique setting and premise to the game, definitely sets itself apart from the competition.

Very casual but a fun little game. Can be extremely addictive!
TL;DR
Click, collect money, upgrade rinse and repeat.
Hero Souls:
What's giving the game some longevity is that after a little while you can (and must at some time) "Ascend". It's a reset back to square,you get this fairly early on the game "unlock from one of the regular heroes". At that time and forward in the game you can ascend at anytime you'd like. You get to keep collected currency "Hero Souls" for your "special" heroes, you also keep your special heroes and their level.
Basic heroes, level, gold and zone progress is reset back to zero.
Sounds tedious, but the dev's managed to "slip" in some "but not much" other things here and there to keep it interesting.
What's keeping me in the game is the hunt for those precious Hero Souls (HS).
HS drops from special "Astral bosses with HS" witch starts to come into play from zone 100.
From now on they can spawn on every boss encounter (every 5 levels). On some run's you can get a lot, some time not so much. You also get 1 HS for every 2000 combined level upgrades of your regular heroes.
Those HS can be used to either buying and/or upgrading your special heroes or you can just horde 'em. They give you a flat 10% damage increase pr HS you keep.
Achievements:
Another thing to mention, this is a game where achievements matter, most of or if not all of them give you a damage boost. Ranges from 3 to 5 % DPS increase. There are a lot of them, and they do add up. Nothing really hard or creative here. You get em for by just playing the game. This is not a review of the achievements, wanted to mention that they have a purpose.
Offline play:
I must mention that the implementation of collecting/farming gold while you are offline is the reason this game was not uninstalled after and hour or so on my part. Feels so good to progress as far as you'd like, and just quit the game or even minimize the game window and surf the web, work whatever. The game farms at that spot, brilliant.
F2P:
The F2P model is good, you get the currency in-game as well so you don't have to spend money if you don't want to. I feel that this game is generous giving you this currency "Red rubies" in-game compared to some of the other F2P games I've tried.
Final note:
You can play this active or passive. Play 5 minutes, 1 hour, 10 hours it's up to you, it doesn't punish you for going offline.

Warframe, is a bit weird game that the dev doesn't really know the point. It wants to be ninja, but its annoying because the game doesn't have deep stealth mechanics. It wants to be Dynasty Warrior type of game, but the enemies hits you like a truck. All I can say, Warframe is a game about Shooting stuffs while doing XYZ Axis movement. The game costumization is deep as well, mods that allow you to add elements, higher damage, critical chance / damage, and so on. The first time player that play this game will be confused as hell, but you gotta keep moving forward to understand how the game works. Do this, and you will get addicted to it.
The game is RNG-Heaven. If you wanna get some materials or even a warframe it self, well good luck because it is chance base. It is not P2W, but kind of? You can buy all of the prime equipments (The better type of equipment) with real money from other people by trading. Farm for relics. Finally get the relic you wanted. Need void traces to make it radiant. Use the relics you didn't want to get void traces to make the relic you wanted into radiant. Find 3 other people who also want to use their radiant relic of the same type. Wait, how many relics are there? Okay, wow, that's a lot. And 3 other people should be using the exact same one? Do they have to? No? Oh, they can just use any normal one. But, we all have a better chance of getting the one thing in the relic that we all want if we all do the exact same relic? Okay, so it's best to find people with the same relic. Each relic has 3 commons, 2 uncommons, and 1 rare. If we all use radiant relics, then we'll probably get the rare item in 2-3 tries. That's 2-3 radiant relics per person, for a total of 8 to 12 total radiant relics. We could get it on the first try, or it could take way longer than 3 tries. That's 100 void traces per radiant relic, and each relic gives a random amount between 6 and 30, then +1 for every person who chose the reward that your relic gave. So, minimum 6 void traces, you need 100, that's 100/6=17 relics minimum. 30, and 1 for each person that selects your reward, that's 33 total possible from a single relic. Which is still 4 relics. May as well be 25-33 per relic at best. So about 4 to 17 relics to make just one of them radiant. You have to collect the reactant to unlock each of those relics, then do the actual mission, then select the next relic, repeat. 4 runs isn't so bad. On average, it's probably closer to 10 runs for each relic. But, not every relic mission is guaranteed to go quickly. A defense mission could take a while. A survival mission is always going to be at least 5 minutes, with the time it takes to get to extraction making it more like 6 minutes. Maybe just wait until the relic missions are captures, or maybe rescues. But, then that's a lot of time to wait, because each mission stays for about an hour. There's sometimes more than one for each of the 4 relic types. Oh, yeah. There's 4 different groups of relics, based on difficulty. Sometimes there's no mission for you to take the relics to. Strange. But, you're waiting for a faster mission, or you're doing the missions that are available, anyways. Lucky if it's a capture. Or even extermination. Don't want to be late to an extermination, though. Especially not in a Lith relic. I'm surprised I even know that's the lowest tier of relic. Well, maybe we'll just wait for a better mission than survival or defense. Really not looking forward to spending the next 5+ minutes babysitting the objective. What else is there to do? Well, there's the junctions. I can unlock more planets to go to new places. New places means new resources that I can gather. New resources means new weapons that I can build. New enemies on new planets. New bosses, too. I love filling the strongest enemy I can find with as many slices and holes as I can make. Now, there's new mission types. What the heck is a "Spy" mission? "Hijack?" Okay, these are interesting. What do I do in this spy mission? There's 3 objectives. Okay. Steal the information, then leave. Sounds simple enough. I'll walk in- and there's now a counter on the objective. Okay,♥♥♥♥♥♥ Is that supposed to happen? Like how survival has a mission timer? It's going the wrong way. What happens when it hits zero? Probably something bad. Okay, so it's like rescue, then? It's like 3 rescue missions? Are you serious? This is annoying. At least there's no operative to babysit. Maybe this can- and I just failed the objective. Crap. Wait, the mission didn't end? Why not? I must be in too low a level mission for just one mistake to matter. Well, next one. Lasers. Laser everywhere. Laser doorways, lasers that can see, lasers that hurt, lasers that trip me, and all of them set off the alarms. Okay, that's cool. Not for me, but still pretty neato. I'll just shoot the robot, so it can't set off the alarms, and- it's got a gigantic amount of health. My arrow did a billionth of its health and now all the alarms are going off. I have no idea where I'm supposed to go, and now I'm panicking. Neato. Guess this one's also a bust. Think I'll just abort mission. I lose all the mission rewards that I gathered so far, but ♥♥♥♥ it. I still got 30xp for my MK1-Paris. Somehow, it's reached maximum rank. Amazing! So, it must do something cool, right? Now that it's maximum level- and the wiki says it does the exact same thing as if it was unranked, it just has more mod capacity. Neato. So, mods make weapons more powerful, not ranks. Then, I'll just put this mod on it, and now it does 20% more damage. What's a billionth of an enemy's health plus 20%? I don't know, math number? It's still totally nothing. Wait, you get Endo to upgrade mods to make your weapons stronger. Yeah, gotcha. So, farming for Endo? How do that? Hmm.. Warframe is one of the most game mechanically satisfying games I've played in my life. The movement system and unique abilities of different warframes really makes you feel like a space ninja. There is a vast amount of content, including cosmetics, weapons, and one hell of a storyline. All this in an F2P game. The games unique aesthetic is also a big plus.
The game is quite centered around resource grind, but thanks to the great game mechanics the grind is actually fun. The modding system allows you to take even something like a simple assault rifle and make it spit out pure death.
Also one last thing, which is why I love the game so much: The devs. DE are some of the best developers I have witnessed in recent years. They listen to the community, and actively communicate with us. They have many times screwed up, but they admit their mistakes, and always strive to improve the game in the next patch.
Definitely one of my favorite games of all time.

Warframe, is a bit weird game that the dev doesn't really know the point. It wants to be ninja, but its annoying because the game doesn't have deep stealth mechanics. It wants to be Dynasty Warrior type of game, but the enemies hits you like a truck. All I can say, Warframe is a game about Shooting stuffs while doing XYZ Axis movement. The game costumization is deep as well, mods that allow you to add elements, higher damage, critical chance / damage, and so on. The first time player that play this game will be confused as hell, but you gotta keep moving forward to understand how the game works. Do this, and you will get addicted to it.
The game is RNG-Heaven. If you wanna get some materials or even a warframe it self, well good luck because it is chance base. It is not P2W, but kind of? You can buy all of the prime equipments (The better type of equipment) with real money from other people by trading. But, if you suck at how to move and understand how each equipment works, you gonna have a bad time. The game required skills to do it, not just by some sicko who bought all of the prime equipments but still doesn't know how the game works. The skills to do it is deep it self, basically you can't play this game just in 100 hours and know how the whole game works.
Let's talk about the Dev. Digital Extreme, really like this game. They always give this game updates, but they are a bit lazy to polish the new introduced mechanics. Archwing, the gundam like gameplay, was released with a lot of hate, but they didn't do anything to polish it up and make it more enjoyable. They just keep pumping new mechanics and ignore the old ones. Also the dev loves to livestream and talk about the next update. They do this every 2 weeks, which I really appreciate because they want to be open. Sometimes they hear the community feedback, sometimes they don't. I don't really get it as well.
All in all, Warframe is a very unique game that is a RNG-Heaven. The dev doesn't know what's the point of this game. The quality is rising each update, and you can see how they are improving themself.

I've been playing this game for around 3-4? years now and seen it go through multiple design revisions and changes.
This is hands down the best free to play co-op action shooter on the market. If you like the core gameplay loop of abilities, gunplay and insane movement then you can just keep going and going with Warframe until you're sick of it.
100% recommended on that alone. Even if it's not your thing, try it out. No nickel and dime microtransactions, no Pay2Win ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t (it's co-op with optional PVP after all). I went a year and a half before I spent a penny on this game. If you've got a good haggle hat you can even trade special items for in-game currency and NEVER spend a dollar on the game at all and still get the cosmetics. Everything with the exception of cosmetics in this game you can obtain without paying money for. Some of the grinds are stupid and RNG-based (Ivara, Equinox) but if you're enjoying the gameplay there's really no loss.
This is a collectathon at heart, you get resources and credits to build weapons which you level up for mastery which feeds back into helping you level things easier. There's no real "ending" to this game until its story quests are fleshed out to have a specific start and end point in canon, and because this is an MMO with constant development and updates, that's not likely to happen for a very long time.
That being said, the story quests that do exist are damn good and the team behind this game kicks♥♥♥♥♥for the most part (looking at most of the nerfs honestly but you gotta do what you gotta do i guess)
This game is worth your time, and the team behind it are worth any amount of money you choose to spend on it.

I think Ark is quite frankly the best Survival Game out there. Instead of being boring after just a few hours (20-50) like Rust, 7days, etc. it really captures your attention and has you playing for days on end w/o even reaching the high end game.
The concept of taming Dinosaurs to help you take over your little place in the Ark is simply amazing and increadibly fun.
I'd generally advise you to play with friends (you get additional XP for leveling with clan mates) as it provides additional "defenses" for your base (in PvP everything can and prbly will be destroyed once in a while. But that's why this is a Survival game).
Generally I find the community to be quite nice and forthcoming with tips and tricks for new players. And with new Servers being added on launch next month, I can't wait to return.
Personally, I don't understand the whining about the increased Price Tag. Literally, this was planned from the getgo:
Have the game be cheaper (20-30 bucks) for the Alpha and then make it be a "normal" price tag on launch. And that's basically what happened.
I see people comlpain that 60 bucks is too much when they have spent 1000 + hours on the game. If you got that amount of enjoymend out of anything else it'd be worth loads more than 60 bucks.
I just hope they'll open a lot new servers and mark them for new players on launch so that there won't be a flood of new bees stumbling into a server controlled by a 40 man Alpha Tribe waiting to destroy every new base that pops up.
I loved the initial rush in Ark and hope that we can have something akin to that on launch.
tl;dr: Go get the game if you're into survival games and have the time for it. If your pc isn't high end, just play on the lower settings of the game; it has worked fine for me.
Worth another look with the new update, adds a little more to the lore, but doesn't really add anything worth while for new players.

For me it's simply the best F2P game out there and one of the very, very few that really are free to play. Seriously, you don't have to pay anything - a clan mate of mine amassed several thousands of platinum (that's the game currency) by trading alone.
In a distant future you play as a powerful Tenno who can control Warframes, sophisticated humanoid combat drones, each with its own look and special powers. With time you can modify them to your personal taste and needs. These modifications are the central key to a Warframe's power and you can refit your Warframe as it suits best to a given task.
You work for the mysterious Lotus (voiced by Digital Extremes' very charming community manager Rebecca Ford) who sends you out into our solar system to keep the mighty factions of the power-mongering and degenerate Grineer (think of  Dune's Harkonnen) and the ever-greedy, technocratical Corpus in check and the mutated Infestation at bay.
There's a wide range of play and fighting styles: offensive, defensive, stealthy, utilarian, combo-heavy, melee, from distance and any combination of these. There's a dozen of helpful companions and hundreds of weapons and you can customize all of it to your liking. You can buy the stuff with real money, but you don't have to: you can hunt down the stuff in missions or trade for it in game.
Learning curve for newcomers is high and you might feel a bit overwhelmed at start. But take your time, read some guides about good starter weapons, get a helping clan. It's worth it.
The game is constantly improved and the best looking space ninja game out there. To my amazement the developer constantly polishes the game's engine and characters while mainting its performance. A cool thing I'm really fond of: the Tennogen stuff. These are skins (and remodels) created by talented members of the steam community. You can only buy em for real money of which 30% go to the creator, cool. Some have created rather outstanding artwork.
Curious? Test it, it's FREE!

Short answer: Yes - Ark is definitely worth buying. If your PC has the power and you have the time, Ark has the capacity to provide hundreds of hours of gameplay.
I should say that Ark is really meant to be played with friends. Everything in the game is much easier and safer with a group. If you dont have anyone to play with, most players within Ark are kind and helpful people, who just want to advance their technology and power. It wont be long before you find a tribe that is willing to take you in.
In the beginning, Ark is all about staying alive (Finding food, staying hydrated, gathering resources, maintaining temperature, and fighting/running from predators). But after leveling up and learning the game's mechanics you will find that Ark is less about surviving and more about thriving. Taming, building, trading, breeding, and exploring become every day tasks.
Pros:
Endless hours of gameplay
Decent community (Most Alpha tribes are kind)
Great Graphics
Lots of maps (Canon and Community)
Wyverns, Griffins, and other crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥br>Incredible amount and variety of prehistoric creatures
Cons:
Lots of grinding in the early stages
Taming can take quite a long time
Some servers have been taken over by malevolent mega tribes
Overall Ark is a great game with few cons. Most of which can be negated by simply playing with friends and finding a good server before commiting too much time. I look forward to getting back into Ark this summer as a few of my friends recently purchased the game.

So many things can be said about this game, both good and bad, and honestly I'm reviewing this as the first dino survival game I've played. You play as either a man or woman, able to customize it to look...interesting and basically survive the island (default) or other maps in the mod servers.
So...what's good?
- DINOS
- Looks good in terms of what is offered (not graphically speaking)
- Buidling your fortress in anyway you'd like along with having your dinos sit out like horses on stables
- Different mods can make the game more enjoyable (there's a godzilla mod, summon it and tame it)
- Different domes with unique weather system that force you to adapt.
- RIDE THEM MOFO
- The skill tree provides many items to craft which counts as "end-game" material like a mmorpg (kind of)
- Fun when playing rp (role play) style with friends or friendly communities out there
- Death animation (you as a man yelling) provides quite an entertainment
- Pve Servers, Pvp servers, and PVEVP servers so...idk thoughts?
- Pokemon mods make the game so brutal (you can tame them and kill them, also they have their actual game voices so... D:)
So..what's bad?
- Pvp servers can and will provide an unsatisfying gameplay due to many people either enjoy ruining the fun of others or simply any bs aspects of a survival pvp server games.
- Not as optimize, but could be worse. (unofficial servers provides "better" fps as far as I am concern unless it's different now)
- (Not sure if it's better or different) When you log out, your character's body stays in-game which allows either random carn dinos to attack your base to attack you or players simply taking their time to get to your base, kill you, and loot everything.
-Some bugs can be annoying.
-20 buck dlc in an early access game that connects you to a completely different world/land...err...20 bucks?? D:
TL;DR
You're buying exactly what you are seeing in either this review or others. I don't like the idea of having the option of a 20 bucks dlc in an early access game that you need 60 bucks base game for. I know they want support from players so that they can improve the game, but I have never seen something like this before so yeah. You have a choice of which type of servers (pvp, pve, pvevp) to connect to, so if this is your first time playing a survival game, you have been warned. Overall, I liked the experience when I bought it within the year it came out or a year after, I love being in a world of creatures that you can tame, ride and use in battle (leveling both you and the tamed beast(s) is a plus). There may be other dino survival games that I've never heard of, so do check those out if you're interested, otherwise this is no rush to buy this game since it's still getting those updates for improvement. I will not review "survival of the fittest" mode as it's a battle royal with dinos (very debateable whether or not it's worth playing). Honestly, I wish there was another option where you don't have to press the recommend/not recommend button as this game I have mixed feelings for. It's not a bad game, not the best game, but if you like/love dinosaurs, then who am I to judge.

I've been playing this game for around 3-4? years now and seen it go through multiple design revisions and changes.
This is hands down the best free to play co-op action shooter on the market. If you like the core gameplay loop of abilities, gunplay and insane movement then you can just keep going and going with Warframe until you're sick of it.
100% recommended on that alone. Even if it's not your thing, try it out. No nickel and dime microtransactions, no Pay2Win ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t (it's co-op with optional PVP after all). I went a year and a half before I spent a penny on this game. If you've got a good haggle hat you can even trade special items for in-game currency and NEVER spend a dollar on the game at all and still get the cosmetics. Everything with the exception of cosmetics in this game you can obtain without paying money for. Some of the grinds are stupid and RNG-based (Ivara, Equinox) but if you're enjoying the gameplay there's really no loss.
This is a collectathon at heart, you get resources and credits to build weapons which you level up for mastery which feeds back into helping you level things easier. There's no real "ending" to this game until its story quests are fleshed out to have a specific start and end point in canon, and because this is an MMO with constant development and updates, that's not likely to happen for a very long time.
That being said, the story quests that do exist are damn good and the team behind this game kicks♥♥♥♥♥for the most part (looking at most of the nerfs honestly but you gotta do what you gotta do i guess)
This game is worth your time, and the team behind it are worth any amount of money you choose to spend on it.

Writer's Note:
I am only reccomending this game because I feel like it has some aspects that are worth your time, even if only that of a download and a tutorial mission.
I will not be breaking this review down into Pros and cons, this game has many facets to it that I believe need to be addressed in full. Other reviewers in this section can fulfill your TL;DR needs, should you so desire.
What is Warframe? Well, it is certainly not "Ninjas in Space." That is a marketting lie, and I feel like it needs to be addressed first and foremost. If you are coming to look for exciting stealth-based gameplay, I'm afraid you've found yourself in the wrong place. There is stealth in the game, but it's not very good and can be easily cheesed by simply killing everything before the alarm sounds in that particular room. If you're looking for agility, parkour, etc: Yeah, the game has that, but it's done far better elsewhere (Mirror's Edge and Titanfall 2 come to mind.) The ninja thing is just a marketting ploy, and you will quickly find that once you move past your starting frame, that all falls apart incredibly quickly. You will get a much better experience playing Metal Gear, Mark of the Ninja, etc. if you are looking for stealth; If the parkour is what you came for, there are many games that do it better.
So You're still here? Interesting. The gameplay, what is it like? You play a Warframe, one of several uniquely-suited protagonists that all have different powers and other cool do-dads. You are under the watchful gaze of the Lotus, who appears to tell you things you already know, lie to you, or cause melodrama between you and your space-pals. You shoot things, swish-swish-stab things, and sometimes do different objectives during missions, but that's only the basic gameplay. You run around ranking up your very poor starter weapons and frame to earn "Mastery". What is Mastery? Well, it's a metalevelling system that depends in whole on your starchart completion and the amount of things you've used until rank 30. Unfortunately, upgrading from these is a minefield as there is quite a large schizm between things that are plain bad, mid-tier, or high-tier. This goes with Frames as well, as you'll find frames that are Always good, situational, or rarely good.
Now, the realy gameplay is grinding. You will be playing the RNG for: Resources, Blueprints, materials, Frame parts, Weapon parts, Rare loot, Rewards, Keys, Mod stats, Mods, Alerts, Damage procs, level layouts and some other things. This means that, at any given time, you may not be gaurenteed the parts or even things in relation to the parts you're looking for. While this system has seen some improvement, it is still the biggest random quantity unto itself. I cannot stress to you how many times I have rolled the dice and been utterly unable to get the things I needed, even with new improvements that allow part-sharing. I promise you that you will burn out, and that you will find periods of time where you are standing around doing nothing. This game loves to induce periods of waiting: Everything from building weapons to gear is done through the foundry; The timers are all real-time, too. An example is the average Warframe build time. It will take you 36 hours (3 parts @ 12 hours) to initiate a build that will take 72 hours to complete. The total of this is 108 hours if all 3 parts are not built in tandem. Another example, and one that is much more painful, is the part-reliant quests. For a period of time, the Developers thought it was a good idea to lock quest progression behind parts. You would have to build a part in order to continue the quest, which would require 12 more hours of waiting. Or, if you're trying some of the newer frames: Waiting for a Nitain Extract alert which will yeild one (1) of your 5 required Nitain.
Lastly, is the game Pay to Win? In a word: Yes. But that needs more explanation: While the most powerful items in the game (Primes) are not specifically able to be purchased by buying them from the Developers, you can instead spend the premium currency: Platinum (or Plat) in order to buy the parts from others. While this does eliminate the need for a relic grind, it does still require the player to build each part. You can get some of the most powerful weapons this way, however.
So, if you're still interested in the game after reading all of that: I do reccomend the game. Why? Because it is fun, and the art style and experiences one can have with friends are quite worthwhile. The Dojo/Clan system is fair and allows all players of all group sizes to build their own space without overburdening newer players with prices that border extortion.
Secondly, the artsyle and design structure of this game is gorgeous. It is insanely pretty to look at and worth playing to see all of the lights and flashes. Since the PBR and Dynamic Lighting have been introduced, this game can yeild some amazing beautiful moments.
Lastly, While the Lore in this game takes a Dark Souls idea of "Less is more" and often fails to properly execute anything worthwhile, the Cinematic quests are wonderful and can really flesh out the universe and act on the potential this game has had for so long.
Which brings me to the reason why I hesitate to reccomend this: I have been playing since Update 7.0, I may not be the longest playing person in this game, but I have been here for Three years. I have seen and heard many promises and witnessed many mind-blowing things. I have been part of the speculation and fanart, and intrigue which surrounds this game. I have seen it carelessly tread the line between amazing and dull, fun and boring. In all that time, I have seen the problem of New Player Experience become one of issue, action, and ultimate misunderstanding. I think the biggest thing a new player faces is the overwhelming nature of the game is simply thrust upon you. Another problem dominates the New Player Experience: Impact and retention. The Cinematic Quests are beautiful, the soundtrack for them is wonderful, and the lore is top-notch, but I worry that it has a diminished impact on newer players. For older players, these were answers to questions that had been bouncing around in our heads for years full of speculation; but for newer players I feel this is lost. The impact is far less than one can comprehend from an outside-in perspective. The other problem is retention. Only one of the people I started this game with, of an Alliance of amazing Warframe players, is still active frequently. The Grind and it's subsequent burnout can majorly get to you.
I hope this review has helped inform your decision on whteher or not to play this game.

This is hands down the best free to play co-op action shooter on the market. If you like the core gameplay loop of abilities, gunplay and insane movement then you can just keep going and going with Warframe until you're sick of it.

If you've got a good haggle hat you can even trade special items for in-game currency and NEVER spend a dollar on the game at all and still get the cosmetics. Everything with the exception of cosmetics in this game you can obtain without paying money for. Some of the grinds are stupid and RNG-based (Ivara, Equinox) but if you're enjoying the gameplay there's really no loss.
This is a collectathon at heart, you get resources and credits to build weapons which you level up for mastery which feeds back into helping you level things easier. There's no real "ending" to this game until its story quests are fleshed out to have a specific start and end point in canon, and because this is an MMO with constant development and updates, that's not likely to happen for a very long time.
That being said, the story quests that do exist are damn good and the team behind this game kicks♥♥♥♥♥for the most part (looking at most of the nerfs honestly but you gotta do what you gotta do i guess)
This game is worth your time, and the team behind it are worth any amount of money you choose to spend on it.

For me it's simply the best F2P game out there and one of the very, very few that really are free to play. Seriously, you don't have to pay anything - a clan mate of mine amassed several thousands of platinum (that's the game currency) by trading alone.
In a distant future you play as a powerful Tenno who can control Warframes, sophisticated humanoid combat drones, each with its own look and special powers. With time you can modify them to your personal taste and needs. These modifications are the central key to a Warframe's power and you can refit your Warframe as it suits best to a given task.
You work for the mysterious Lotus (voiced by Digital Extremes' very charming community manager Rebecca Ford) who sends you out into our solar system to keep the mighty factions of the power-mongering and degenerate Grineer (think of  Dune's Harkonnen) and the ever-greedy, technocratical Corpus in check and the mutated Infestation at bay.
There's a wide range of play and fighting styles: offensive, defensive, stealthy, utilarian, combo-heavy, melee, from distance and any combination of these. There's a dozen of helpful companions and hundreds of weapons and you can customize all of it to your liking. You can buy the stuff with real money, but you don't have to: you can hunt down the stuff in missions or trade for it in game.
Learning curve for newcomers is high and you might feel a bit overwhelmed at start. But take your time, read some guides about good starter weapons, get a helping clan. It's worth it.
The game is constantly improved and the best looking space ninja game out there. To my amazement the developer constantly polishes the game's engine and characters while mainting its performance. A cool thing I'm really fond of: the Tennogen stuff. These are skins (and remodels) created by talented members of the steam community. You can only buy em for real money of which 30% go to the creator, cool. Some have created rather outstanding artwork.
Curious? Test it, it's FREE!

A strange game that I laughed at as at a joke, but that's actually kind of intriguing. Take a typical RPG with group-based combat and character progression, then remove the combat and the story; this game is what you have left. Monsters can't hurt you in any way or even do anything at all; you just click to damage them until they die and drop gold. You use the gold to buy and upgrade heroes. Every hero after the first provides passive DPS, which means that you soon won't need to click at all, and can just watch your heroes automatically killing enemies. Every fifth zone contains a boss, which is different from the others in that you only have 30 seconds to kill them. If you can't do enough damage, you have to go back to the previous zone and farm mobs until you can make your team good enough to defeat the boss. Almost every hero upgrade is a straightforward DPS upgrade, but there are also 10 special abilities you can acquire, such as "Clickstorm" which "Automatically performs 10 Clicks Per Second for 30 seconds. Cooldown: 10m". These are mostly useful to get past a tough boss faster. Every once in a while, the game will create a chicken in a random place which you can click to get a lot of gold. This rewards actually looking at the game occasionally.

A strange game that I laughed at as at a joke, but that's actually kind of intriguing. Take a typical RPG with group-based combat and character progression, then remove the combat and the story; this game is what you have left. Monsters can't hurt you in any way or even do anything at all; you just click to damage them until they die and drop gold. You use the gold to buy and upgrade heroes. Every hero after the first provides passive DPS, which means that you soon won't need to click at all, and can just watch your heroes automatically killing enemies. Every fifth zone contains a boss, which is different from the others in that you only have 30 seconds to kill them. If you can't do enough damage, you have to go back to the previous zone and farm mobs until you can make your team good enough to defeat the boss. Almost every hero upgrade is a straightforward DPS upgrade, but there are also 10 special abilities you can acquire, such as "Clickstorm" which "Automatically performs 10 Clicks Per Second for 30 seconds. Cooldown: 10m". These are mostly useful to get past a tough boss faster. Every once in a while, the game will create a chicken in a random place which you can click to get a lot of gold. This rewards actually looking at the game occasionally.

Almost purely singleplayer experience (with some private server gameplay with one other person):
I adore this game.
Definitely the most enjoyable game I've played in a long time, and now the game I've put the most time into on steam. Although it can be hard to get started, especially with many, many more dinos than when I first started playing nearly 2 years ago, its certainly worth waiting out the hours of dying repeatedly. There are over 100 unique dinos to tame - from the cute and fluffy to the oh-god-please-don't-eat-me variety, almost every time I play there's something new to explore.
With the looming release this August, the last couple of major updates have been optimisations and general bug fixes to improve performance and enjoyment. Although it's not a game that your standard potato from the 1990's can run, it's definitely worth looking into if you have a decent computer. I'm certain that before the full release we'll see the further optimisations allowing for a greater percentage of the player base to experience ARK in all it's glory. I recently upgraded from a GTX650 Ti Boost to a GTX 1070 and the game changed to something that is quite frankly, beautiful. The detail on the terrain and models is quite outstanding, and definitely noticeable at the higher settings. There are optional launch perameters that can be added for people with lower-end computers to help boost performance (and there are plenty of guides available to do this).
With 3 free DLC (The Center map, the total conversion Primitive + and the most recent addition of the map Ragnorak) and one paid DLC (The Scorched Earth map & dinos, that are all available in the standard game to be spawned, and Ragnorak will be updated to contain most the Scorched Earth dinosaurs and a desert area) the game provides plenty of different experiences. As well as a wealth of mods through the steam workshop and a few sponsored mods, there is so much customisation available to provide the experience YOU want.
I honestly cannot recommend this game enough. If you're even considering buying it, you've thought about it too long.

This is a review and warning for newcomers. Me personally, if there's one word to describe this game it's tedious.
Reason for the amount of time played is because my fiance plays it on my account, if it was up to me I would get this refunded a long time ago.
Half of your gameplay on here will be spent just waiting for things, whether it's taming, crafting or dying and trying to reclaim your stuff back but good luck with that.
Countless times I've tried to set up bases on the safe areas which are beaches but instead I get greeted with the message of "Too close to enemy structure" because some other player has place a wooden beam near by or a random campfire is lurking in some bushes. So I go further in land to try and find a buildable spot to build and instead get mauled by the many predators of the woods. Sometimes it isn't even the woods, I've spawned on a (Easy) difficulty beach and as my character is doing her waking up animation two raptors was on top of me and as soon as the animation ended I was dead.
Even when you do manage to set up a little base don't expect to be riding dinos anytime soon, (And if you do it will be dinos given to you by other players or awful low tier dinos which are not fun to have and come with their maintenance which isn't worth it) that will come hours later when you have grinded out some levels to build saddles and gained the ability of making narcotic and narcotic arrows.
And once you have all that stuff you will have to get out the trusty wiki guides as each dino has different needs and knock out times so you better attend your Ark lesson on the wiki or else you will almost certainly fail your Ark exam of actually taming something for once. You put food and narcotics on a dino that is unconscious and that dino wakes back up? Well kiss all that equipment goodbye because it's now gone.
Finally the bugs and lag for me is the cherry on top, in a dangerous situation with dinos that require reflexes? Well good luck because your biggest enemy here is the lag as it will fling you back and front like you are in the ♥♥♥♥ing movie jumper and it will get you hit and eventually killed. The size of peoples bases and the amount of dinos they keep can send high end computers to a crawling hault, that's always fun!
Then as I'm traversing the map up a cliff, I end up sliding down into a crevice with no equipment, unable to jump out and now I'm just stuff with this other geezer next to me unconscious who has given up just like me. Reminded me of the scene from 127 Hours... so now I'm waiting for myself to go hungry or thirsty as nothing else can kill me and so far I am up to 40 minutes.
Had another glitch where something called a eurypterid floated up on to a beginner beach, knocked me out in one hit then killed me. Confused I looked this thing up and it's a DEEP SEA CREATURE! So this deep sea creature was in the shallow beach area and me, being admittedly curious took a look at it without going in the water and it literally just floats out of the water and is in mid air coming towards me before killing me and having to start again with no materials.
To add as well the building is hot garbage as all structures look like utter♥♥♥♥♥♥ more eye sores than anything and trying to actually build is a uphill struggle due to snap points choosing to fly all over the screen and build the wrong way round when there's no way of knowing which is the right way, this gives you two options, live with an out of place wall or demolish and rebuilding losing some resources in the progress.

Free-to-Play Pay-to-skip cooperative 3rd person space ninja shooter
Premium currency is gained by selling parts and items in-game or by purchasing it with real money. You can get a 20 - 70% discount as a daily log-in reward. Devs also have a livestream every week and there they giveaway ~1000 premium currency 3 times in a stream (which is a good amount). Premium currency can be used to skip the grind and waiting by just buying the complete items instead of grinding for parts and resources and crafting.
Game involves a lot of grinding and waiting (90+ real hours to craft a warframe/weapon) that can be a major turn-off for new players. It is the only way of reaaally progressing and it does sometimes get on my nerves as well.
There's a lot of weapon and class/ability variety, and each item has some background and/or description to tell something cool about it. There's a lot of weapons with cool mechanics.
The gameplay in my opinion is quite solid, combat is colorful and quick paced (most of the time), the level system might be hard to figure out, but you get over it once you've played a few hours and seen what type of enemies are what level etc. Interface is somewhat customizable, nothing insane. You can't swap he places of UI elements, but you can scale or hide most of the elements.
Personally I'm glad that I've played this. It is a time consumer but I have fun doing it.

What I wrote above I wrote when I had very little hours in the game and now that I have about 470 hours I feel I can write a more in depth review. This game will consume your life if you get hooked on it. I got my friend into this game earlier last month and every spare second he had he would spend on this game. This game will not only hook you but it will also rob you of your wallet. All of the purchases that can be made in this game are mainly optional but when you log on and recieve that discount on platnium you will buy the platnium. The game is also extremely fun. The way the gunplay and the movement system work together to create this extremely fluid experience is really refreshing compared to what we get with most shooters, with the exception of a few. Another thing I would like to say is that this game is not really an mmo but a multiplayer shooter with mmo elements sprinkled in such as trading, global chat, and clans full of many people. There is also a huge amount of things you can do with your weapon in this game it is insane. You could almost change one weapon into a whole new weapon. I would also like to touch on the newest update the Plains of Eidolon (PoE). PoE is a brand new update in warframe that adds an open world to the game. There is also a town outside of the open world that allows you to purchase many things such as tools for mining and fishing, you can pick up bounties, you can also make custom weapons for your operator, and you can pick up custom weapons you made. The best thing of this update are the Eidolons. Today I killed my first Eidolon and it was one of the most rewarding things you can do in this game. When you finally figure out how to kill that boss and everything just clicks you feel great. In the end I would give warfame a 9/10.

ARK: Survival Evolved. As of yet, Early Access game and has been for roughly two years. I bought it February 2017 and have put nearly 1000 hours of play time in so far and i don't want to stop anytime soon. It is not a perfect game, it has it's bugs some annoying (Fertilized egg's falling through the world to sit just below the surface) some entertaining (Texture glitch on active and inactive players as well as dino's getting stuck everywhere plausible and several places not plausible), and it has it's flaws (Catered to PvP, server instability). Overal, i can and will recommend the game because despite it's flaws it is a great time sink to me. There are good servers and bad, as to be expected of dealing with people. For this game to improve, some of the things i would like is to have stable servers, and to have a little more TLC for the PvE community. Not all of us (Or possibly a majority) are interested in PvP. I personally hope that they do a blank slate wipe when this game goes official, but i highly doubt they will do so. Mores the shame. But if you are looking for a game to spend a lot of time in, i would highly recommend ARK to you. If you are impatient, if you are a snowflake, or if you want the easy life, ARK is not for you.

It's a great and fun game. It seems much more than a "collect resources and fight off predators" game- it has much depth. There is a massive variety of creatures, environments, and other hazards to your survival that give the game a "spice" that makes it just so much fun, and I've had one of the best times ever playing with my friends.
Negative reviews will tell you otherwise because, just like any other online survival game, there are toxic players out there that are bent on wrecking your♥♥♥♥♥♥ But that's literally any other survival game- minecraft, miscreated, dayz, and a lot of other survival games will /always/ have those "elite" players and this game should not be discredited as a great game because of it. Bad reviews also make it seem as if the game has no singleplayer option, and as if there aren't any servers with PvP disabled- but there are many pvp/raiding-disabled servers out there and singleplayer has been there since day 1- and you can even host private games with your friends.
Obviously, yes, the survival gets easier and easier as you put more and more effort into it and work your way up, because this is how survival works, and even how technology works- you start off with bad weapons, tools, etc. and get better, more efficient materials. But it takes a LONG time to reach this level as you need to learn engrams, etc. and even when you do reach this point, there will always be different areas to explore, weapons to try, etc- this game leaves it up to you by being a sandbox-survival game, and I love that about it.
So yeah, the negative reviews aren't lying- but their point is somewhat insignificant when you consider how that is how survival works, and how multiplayer works. You can't control people who play multiplayer- there will always be elite players in any given games and you can't really fix that unless you were to completely alter how this game's multiplayer works. And as stated before, there are pvp-disabled servers, etc- there are tons of community-hosted servers out there that will fit your needs.
It's a great game and the negative reviews should not influence you to leave this game alone. Go and try it- and don't forget its still in early access and don't give the game bad reviews due to the fact. Probably one of the best, packed early-access games I've ever played.

Ark Survival Evolved is a prehistoric survival game set on the mysterious island of ARK. You are equipped with nothing but the clothes on your back and your two hands to survive the harsh, unforgiving enviorment. In the game, you have the ability to tame and use dinosaurs to your advantage, be it for flying around, carrying heavy resources, or attacking any unwanted predators, which allow the player to progress through later stages of the game.
While appraised and welcomed by fans of the survival genre, there are as many flaws and problems that absolutley cannot be overlooked. Unfourtanatley these issues bring down the quality of the game by heaps. Here is a rundown of them all:
There is no denial that the influence and popularity of Minecraft, a simple voxel-based survival game shook the gaming industry. An influx of Survival-Genre Games have been in the marketplace for years now, and it is because of this that there is a lack of new and original game mechanics and ideas being pumped into the genre. If you read my review on Subnautica, you would know that a major influence in it's great score is how the game flips the genre on it's head. It is so incredibly different from Minecraft, or in this case ARK, that makes it such a great game. Travel is much different. Instead of on-foot travel, you're in a submarine, navigating around rocky seabeds and alien flora. Another example is the methods of combat. In Subnautica, you have to think outside of the box. There are two weapons, one being a basic knife. ARK has quite the opposite, plentiful amounts of weapons that function mostly the same.
My point with this is that ARK really dosen't bring any new ideas to the table. I've played the game before, in the form of other much more interesting and well thought out adventures.
This point has been discussed by other reviews numerous other times, but I'll go into the basics. I use a 2014 iMac with a 2.7 GHz Processor. The game states that you only need 2GHz to run Epic settings smoothly, which is to put simply, a flat out lie. I have every single possible graphic set to it's very lowest, and I run the game at 10fps at the very most. This is a big problem when my first impressions of a game is seeing trees render 7 feet away from my avatar at 5fps. It still leaves a bad taste in my mouth that I don't think could ever be washed out.
To make it worse, the game has been having worse and worse preformance over the last couple months, if not years. This is a quote by N1kaz from the ARK Subreddit on the matter:
When playing ARK for the first time, I made sure to not look at a single guide, wiki page, or video about the game, to keep the experience as new and fresh as I could. I soon relaised that I couldn't do that due to it's lack of explanation about pretty much every mechanic. I didn't know about hunger or stamina, about resources or taming, or even where different dinosaurs were. I died aproximatley twelve to sixteen times before properly settling in a southern region. While I eventually knew what and what not to avoid through trial and error, it was an extremley infuriating experience for myself. I had to later call in a friend just to tell me what to do and how to do stuff such as learn 'Engrams', recipes for stuff to advance up the tech-tree.
ARK is not an inherently bad game, there is fun that could be had and adventures to be made. The game's lack of originality or understanding of what makes a survival game fun, paired with it's abysmal preformance that lower the quality of the game by heaps. The biggest, most dominating factor in my opnion of this game is the simple fact that I legimatley
want to play this game any further.

This game is really good one. I played it from it's beta-version, but forgot about it later. After i came to it there were so many changes which i liked. So, to stop mumbling:
+ Voicing - they not awesome, but they're pretty good, i even wonder which actors that was.
+ Main plot - i don't really know how far we are in the storyline after last huge update, but the whole story itself is interesting and i, personaly, couldn't remember any similliar lines
+ Audio - not all of it good, but sometimes the music is both dinamic and atmospheric and this is what called a good audio in my book.
+ Levels, characters, weapons, game design itslef - yeah i really like the whole game desing. Planets, spaceships, ancient ruins but not only maps. Warframes and weapons are looking pretty cool and deadly at the same time. The style of the game itself is soo good
+ gameplay - ninjas in f***ing space, mate! And yes. They are! Walljumps, twisted flight, evading and every swing of your choosed weapon is made with grace. Warframe abilities are awesome and i can't really tell which one of them is most useless. Guns are fantastic and there can be really huge af weapons aswell. Also archwings missions are nice, but they kinda boring, buuut still good change of a gameplay if you tired of running and gunning trough the planetsides and spaceship's interriors
+ shop - yeah there's a ingame purchases and microtransactions, but you don't really need them. If you want a cool gun, warframe, melee? You can buy a blueprint and forge it in your spaceforge (wut). There's even a weapons that requires only "parts" of them, so you don't really need much resources for it. Btw as everyday bonus you can get a huge discount on in-game wallet which can be 75-90% off! And it happens realy offten
+ developers - i don't really know much about them but they are totaly cool dudes and chicks :D. Have been laughting everytime reading those in-game PSAs. Also they monitoring community for feedbacks and even adding fan's artworks in the game's gallery! They also have a steam workshop support form where they allready added most skins and helmets
+ community - i never met a raging, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ing, salty and etc players in that game. I dind't played it sooo much but for that time i got in i didn't find any players like those. Only nice and helpfull people
Let's see the -
- in-game shop - because sometimes some weapons and skins is so hard to get but that's not really a huge con
- hard to be the newbee - yeah in every game it is, but i allready met so much people which were lost in barely begining of the game but maybe it's all about people's preferences
- lack of variety in levels - cause after a few days in game you will actually see that so many things are looking veeeeery similliar
- warfarm - yeah. Sometimes you have to farm just way too much maybe that's why new people are leaving
- weapon balance - not every weapon in this game is usefull also there are many "meta" weapons that are still a thing
- rang system - you can only get "level ups" trough level uping your equipment, so if you rang 3 and stick to your own weapons and warframe setup which you really enjoy you have too trash it and get something new. Yeah, you allways neeed to improve your skills and try something new out, but when it comes to this system... I think it's forcing player to doo it
- invetory - sadly, but if you want to get more warframes at once or became a space famous gunholding mister you have to pay for it with real money. Yeah as i said before they're cheap and  not hard to purchase but that's can be a huge con if your budget is low
To summarize
It's really good free MMO game. Maybe the best i played ever (i didn't try out warcraft yet lul). And it's totally worth playing. So if you are in ski-fi, "dark future", ninjas and asian culture you will definetly love this game

After playing this game for sometime now and buying during a sale, I can say I really love the detail that has been put in this  game and I love playing to some extent.
For those trying to decide to get this game, I recommend it but that doesn't mean your have the best time on the game.
Me and my friends started on PVP which was big mistake on offical servers at least I haven't tried un-offical but I would guess they are similair.
We have been raided repeatedly by more powerful tribes that can have one or two people just come to out base and destory everything we have built and at this current time of writing we have just lost our tenth base after switching servers like 5 times as well.
You may ask why not go to PVE well since levels will not tranfer from PVP to PVE we didn't want to start over but we might do that now instead of continuing on PVP.
Now you wondering, why are you complaining when you recommend this game because I love this game, I can never stop playing but when your stuff gets destoryed over and over and the raiders just say your saltly its stupid. Thats why I recommend either come on with a big group of friends or join a big tribe that can help you survive instead of being the victim of one of their raids.
This is the one major issue I have with Ark while I like PVP as an option knowing if you play at this point on any Ark server that there is a gaint more powerful tribe on the server the minute you join, that will either leave you alone or destory and leave you with nothing but the tribe log of what died and was destoryed is depressing.
However, the good thing about the game our everything else:
I have found other friendly players in the same boat but even then we can't survive.
The things you can make is amazing with so much detail to the point you can nearly paint everything even bone costumes for dinos.
The taming feels good when you spend the time to tame powerful dinos like the Rex and yh still couldn't stop the lastest raid. The Breeding with kinda falls in here as well as amazing to raise a baby dino and see it grow as you care for it and make sure to keep it fed, which I wanted to do again today but sadly my pteranodon egg and every other egg is gone.
A good amount of creatable defence but you need it quick and early to survive on PVP.
Lots of ways to get different resources though some ways wont be as good as others.
Lots of different dinos and creatures to tame and join you and one of each still won't be enough for those metal runs.
Freedom to build your base nearly anyway or anywhere you choose unless near a enemy base/other player base.
Exploration is great still haven't explored any caves, or island the main island in the island map.
I love this game but the players on PVP can just be looking to grief or raid you and are just traveling from server to server just to kill you and throw your stuff away. So if you play PVP Good Luck! and make sure before making friend they will defend you or they be poweful enough that everyone else will stay away from you.

The only free-to-play game where I've tossed in more than just a few dollars, solely because I'd like to give the devs money for even a fraction of the time I've spent playing this game. The fluid action, beautiful graphics, and constant stream of updates is a wonderful bonus.
I've heard people describe it as a sort of poor man's Desitny on PC, which isn't completely inaccurate but doesn't quite describe what the game actually is. It's focused on fast-paced third person action, and instead of a large open world you have various missions in different level zones to complete. You earn resources and rank up, progressively unlocking more and more equipment and new zones. It was a lot to take in before they rearranged the world map and pacing, but it's a lot more consistent and straightforward than it used to be. There's also a lot of timed alerts and other events that rotate around, cycling a lot of content and providing a lot of extra stuff to just DO if you hit a wall in terms of progression. They have also been much more focused on getting cinematics and lore into the game, such as the recent War Within update, which is something that the game has been lacking for a long time.
Overall, the controls are tight and work really well. The parkour is a lot more responsive and easier to use than other games I've played, keeping up with the fast pacing of the combat. There is incredible depth to the possible customization you can do for your characters and weapons, both for their abilities and their appearance, that rewards experimenting with and ranking up the equipment you like instead of what's 'strong'. For example, the gun I've most recently been messing around with shoots low-damage chain lightning but is capable of hitting multiple targets at once with a 100% chance at an excessively high critical multiplier. There are other weapons better suited for the task, but it's a lot of fun to just build something goofy.
There's a few improvements that could be made to help certain characters feel less outclassed by others and to improve the general grind (which is a lot of finding resources, waiting real time to build something, leveling it, not liking it, then selling it to make room for new items), but these sorts of things are being addressed very consistently. They're actively working on tweaking abilities so each character can contribute to a squad without any one of them seeming like an absolute requirement, and the big content update from over the summer drastically improved endgame grinding by altering how loot rolling is done for rare equipment only obtainable from certain missions.
The community is one of the best I've been a part of, and are actively in contact with devs - there's weekly dev streams, along with frequent outreach and participation on the forums (both on the game's site, the subreddit, and here). The update this month has also drawn a lot people back into the game, so now's an excellent time to pick it up and play with people.
