Ok. I've put off writing a review for as long as possible in the vain hope that things would improve with this game. However, it is abundantly clear that the developers are - if anything - making a bigger and bigger mess of what started out as a great idea, that in spite of their lack of professional standards, customer support and communication skills,  Wildcards business unit (if they have one) have failed to force the "creative" side of Wildcard to take their fingers off the trigger and listen to some common sense and that - above all else - Wildcard really doesn't listen to their customers, despite some virtue signalling from the companys appointed bubble-headed, blue haired moron to create an illusion to the contrary.
"Early access" be damned: these are people taking not insignificant amounts of money in PAYMENT for a product (AND for additional content!) that should - by definition of "early access" - be IMPROVING as time goes by, but it simply is not. The company has exposed its developers for the shoddy simpletons they really are.
The only possible conclusion is that Wildcard are a somewhat fly by night group of amateurs, determined to "take the money and run", with little or no intention of sticking it out for the long haul.
As an I.T. professional of 20+ years (most of which spent as a lead architect) and a small unofficial server owner with ~20-25 active players, I can honestly say that it is rare for me to experience first hand, a group of individuals profiting so much for such sub-par work. In any other industry, they would be fired; it is that simple.
Opinions are like a-holes: everyone has one, very few are worth listening to ;)
However the facts are incontrovertible:
1) Complete - and I mean, complete - lack of presence, support and interaction by wildcard devs, admins or even support workers on their OWN OFFICIAL SERVERS. Having played both official and unofficial (and now running my own) I can honestly say that Wildcards approach is a bad joke. Myself and my admins give a lot of support (usually in terms of workarounds for Wildcards stupidity, I might add) and we all work full time. Wildcard doesn't even try. Take a look at their bug reporting mechanisms FFS. During my career, I've encountered small (less than 30 people) organisations that do far better with far fewer resources and much higher numbers of customers. As an organisation, Wildcard is appalling
2) Updates are Frequent, but almost always cause more issues than they solve, with most updates being aesthetic, superfluous nonsense. Updates ALWAYS result in the developers breaking more things - usually critical game mechanics - than they fix, resulting in server code that looks like the product of an incestuous relationship between Frankensteins monster and an evil goat to any professional worth a damn. The patch notes published by wildcards answer to Q & A in the guise of a blue haired buffoon, are also a joke with garbled or - more frequently no - explanations for the entries, spelling errors on items as important as server config commands (?!!), important items left out completely (presumably to facilitate them sneaking in unpopular changes, prefering their paying customers to find out changes for themselves...)
3) Game Mechanics are universally awful. This is - I am now convinced - the result of a severe lack of problem solving talent within Wildcard. Every time they encounter something - some way that the players are CHOOSING to play the game - that Wildcard perceives as problematic, rather than taking stock and looking at various SENSIBLE solutions, they almost always pick the simplest, most frustrating and game-breaking approach without considering the long term ramifications. This fact has been demonstrated over and over and has been a constant source of facepalming amongst those of us with any common sense; it really is like letting a monkey loose in the plantation.
4) The game is supposed to be - and was marketed as - a sandbox type, persistent world yet the developers are - more and more - steering the players towards a narrower and narrower gaming experience where building elaborate boats, playing solo and generally doing their own thing is being eroded. It was never their place to tell people how to spend their time and that they think otherwise suggests that someone in Wildcard has gotten a little big for their boots. When you fail to understand that ALL you have to do is provide a vehicle for people to have fun and instead start thinking that it is your place to persuade, cajole or hand hold players into playing a certain way, you've lost the plot.
5) Ark is so poorly optimised, even those of us with high end systems see quite abysmal performance, relatively speaking. To put this into context, to say that the hardware on which I run our unofficial server is overkill would be an understatement. However, the server still locks up / freezes on a frequent basis in the same way that official servers do. I see a fraction of the FPS that I see on other, more demanding AAA games. My workstation and server hardware & configuration have been analysed over and over. But in the end, examination of the server code reveals - and by wildcards own admission - that the game needs a lot of work.
However....a year on, we're still seeing the same "A bit further out..." message in relation to optimisation. If you're in any doubt whatsoever that it will ever happen, you're right to think that way. After all, an organisation that puts the cart before the horse and thinks that making something look pretty should be a higher priority than making it POSSIBLE for people to play it properly in the first place may have dipped too far into the special educational needs inclusive recruitment barrel. Scraping even.
6) Abject failure by Wildcard to understand or even identify its player base, prefering instead to rely on some very misleading statistics. For example: quite a high percentage of players actually build elaborate boats (ships even) based off of the standard raft. Yet Wildcard saw that there was a high number of abandoned rafts on coastlines and elected to handle that by a) introducing a raft killer specifically to automatically handle the destruction of said rafts b) repeatedly "accidentally" crippling boat building by disabling players being able to extend rafts. This in a game where head mounted laser cannons (and even cannons) are touted as "progress" while in the real world we as a species had multihull boats for a millenia before the iron age! And yes, I know this is not supposed to be the real world, but it smacks of monumentally thick people at the helm when you feel raft building is an issue, fail to offer anything other than a wooden raft or a motorboat despite sea being more than 30% of the game map and mastery of it being essential for progression...
Another example is the absolute failure by Wildcard to realise just how many of their players PREFER to play solo. Crippling those players through their engrams is - it has to be said - rather foolish.
7) I always felt bad for the poor Barstewards that play on console. Wildcard really doesn't show them much love. It's almost as if they are an afterthought, with patches occurring infrequently, late or not at all and with a number of features missing completely from their experience. I don't play console myself but wildcards treatment of our console brothers is pretty appalling.
If you are considering buying this game, my advice to you would be: don't. It may be the case that Wildcard eventually pulls its collective head out of the horses behind, but in reality that is unlikely to happen. Whatever good idea this game was, has been swallowed up by repeated failures to listen to the customer, failures to establish even rudimentary support and infrastructure and a complete unwillingness to backtrack on its mistakes, fix them properly and learn from the experience. Such an organisation has no future, long term.

WARNING: This game will make you behave like a drug addict.  If you have even the slightest vestige of OCD tendencies, then for the love of Doge, STAY AWAY from this game or it might quite literally kill you.
This is the grind/ding gameplay loop of games like WoW and Diablo distilled to its extreme - just the addiction mechanic by itself, with little to no actual gameplay.  It's kind of like eating sugar packets: you'll enjoy the taste and keep coming back for more, but it'll make you crazy hyper and when you're done you'll feel sick and undernourished.
Before you know it, you'll be logging in at all hours of the night to stoke your upgrades or Enhanced Dark Ritual chain, or research the best combination of ancients, or just tick over the next resurrect on your way to unlocking another meaningless achievement.  You will be fully aware of just how pointless it all is, in some small screaming part of your mind, and yet be unable to stop yourself.  Clicker Heroes will swiftly take over your life until you become just a mindless, drooling clicking machine.

I'm recommending this game because the core gameplay is astounding. It is without a doubt on of the funnest, diverse, and just plain awesome coop third person shooter games around. And it's free.
The graphics are beautiful, optimized, and I'm sure a potato from 2001 could run it on lowest settings. Even so the game is AAA quality on max settings. The sound, music, and everything related to audio is good.
A lot of the people will jokingly call this game things like warfarm, grindframe, etc. They're not entirely wrong but most things are easily acquired in the span of one or two days, and unless you're trying to get everything there is to get it's not noticable. A lot of the game is doing the same thing over and over again, but it's so much fun that you barely notice. There is a bit of a wait to craft weapons, and different warframes (each warframe is unique in stats and abilities) but nothing I know of takes longer than three days, most weapons only taking between 12 and 24 hours to craft. I'd say the waiting is worse than the farming, but moving on.
My biggest issue with the game is end game. Enemies scale so much that it becomes a fight against heavily armored bullet sponges that can kill you in less than a second. It becomes more about bringing abusable skills/weapons than about what is fun as well as effective. However, most things are very usable until enemies hit about level 50 or so, well beyond the level range of a good 95% of the content. The developer is aware of this issue and are taking steps to better balance the game. Only time will tell if they'll be effective.
The 'cash shop' currency can be used to buy practically everything immediately with no wait. There are very very few items, all of which are only cosmetic, which you actually must purchase with real money. You can get everything through in game trading for platinum (the cash currency) and even begin doing this relatively early in the game.
Warframe feels like a AAA multiplayer experience available for free. So there's no harm in at least trying it.

For a completely free game, it can't really get better than this. Tons of content, (mostly) regular updates, great relationship between DE (the developers) and the community and 99% of ingame stuff (and 100% of stuff that matters) is obtainable without having to pay for it with real money. It's grindy at times but you won't mind it because the combat system is pretty good, there's a huge amount of weapons to use and tons of different missions in which you'll be trying them out.
The main "content" in the game is unlocking new fun stuff to use and customizing it to your liking, and Warframe really excels at this - with dozens of unique Warframes with very different skill sets, hundreds of different weapons and accessories, and mods that further allow you to customize them, there's always something new to do or unlock. The last two major updates even added a very cool storyline to follow that already has had a huge impact on the Warframe universe, and added various new progression mechanics to your character.
So if you want to team up with 3 of your friends and just cut through hordes of enemies in an exterminate mission, or maybe stealthily make your way to the data vaults in spy missions, or defend an objective for as long as possible for constantly increasing rewards... this might be just the game for you. Also, it often has huge updates that change the game at its core (which explains the "perpetual beta" in which this game is still technically in) so if you tried it years ago but disliked something, it might be worth a second look.

The only free-to-play game where I've tossed in more than just a few dollars, solely because I'd like to give the devs money for even a fraction of the time I've spent playing this game. The fluid action, beautiful graphics, and constant stream of updates is a wonderful bonus.
I've heard people describe it as a sort of poor man's Desitny on PC, which isn't completely inaccurate but doesn't quite describe what the game actually is. It's focused on fast-paced third person action, and instead of a large open world you have various missions in different level zones to complete. You earn resources and rank up, progressively unlocking more and more equipment and new zones. It was a lot to take in before they rearranged the world map and pacing, but it's a lot more consistent and straightforward than it used to be. There's also a lot of timed alerts and other events that rotate around, cycling a lot of content and providing a lot of extra stuff to just DO if you hit a wall in terms of progression. They have also been much more focused on getting cinematics and lore into the game, such as the recent War Within update, which is something that the game has been lacking for a long time.
Overall, the controls are tight and work really well. The parkour is a lot more responsive and easier to use than other games I've played, keeping up with the fast pacing of the combat. There is incredible depth to the possible customization you can do for your characters and weapons, both for their abilities and their appearance, that rewards experimenting with and ranking up the equipment you like instead of what's 'strong'. For example, the gun I've most recently been messing around with shoots low-damage chain lightning but is capable of hitting multiple targets at once with a 100% chance at an excessively high critical multiplier. There are other weapons better suited for the task, but it's a lot of fun to just build something goofy.
There's a few improvements that could be made to help certain characters feel less outclassed by others and to improve the general grind (which is a lot of finding resources, waiting real time to build something, leveling it, not liking it, then selling it to make room for new items), but these sorts of things are being addressed very consistently. They're actively working on tweaking abilities so each character can contribute to a squad without any one of them seeming like an absolute requirement, and the big content update from over the summer drastically improved endgame grinding by altering how loot rolling is done for rare equipment only obtainable from certain missions.
The community is one of the best I've been a part of, and are actively in contact with devs - there's weekly dev streams, along with frequent outreach and participation on the forums (both on the game's site, the subreddit, and here). The update this month has also drawn a lot people back into the game, so now's an excellent time to pick it up and play with people.

So I’ve change my review from recommended to not recommended for a few reasons. Let me say that having this game on all three platforms, it is definitely not worth $60. The game is a lot of fun, but there are still way too many problems, not just that but there is no story. This is an open world survival game, and that is it. The servers still have tons of problems with rubberbanding, and disconnects. They sometimes feel like they operate on Dial Up. Recently on PC it would take about 15 minutes to finally logon because of server problems. Now when I speak about server problems it’s not that there are too many people online, on one of the servers I was planning on it said there were only 7 people out of 70, but would constantly get errors because the server itself was experiencing problems. This was going on for two weeks, and it always seems to happen during an event that gives double XP. Normally this wouldn’t be too big of a problem but with ARK, the problem is is that you get disconnects.
So let’s imagine this, you’re traveling around with your good gear on a flying mount. All of a sudden you get disconnected for no reason, now you already know that you’re most likely dead from falling from the sky because that’s what happens when flying and you get disconnected. So you go and try to login to get back to your body and retrieve your gear,  but server issues won’t allow it. Your body despawns after 15 minutes so if you cannot get back on immediately and have a second flying mount to get to where your body was, then you might as well kiss all your good items goodbye because they despawn with your body. Or lets say your taming / Breedubg a Dino. Some can take 9 hours as a baby that needs to be constanly hand fed. Which mean you need to stay online with them just running to get food and manually putting that food into the baby dino to feed them. Then you get disconnected. After 15-30 minutes of trying to log back in, and all ready spending hours raising or taming these dinos, you finally get back on only to find that your tame is no longer around or your baby has starved to death. This has been a constant problem for ARK that the developers will not seem to fix. Even now with those of us who bought early, the developers have openly said that they need to finish working on retail before fixing our problems, which in other words say “we have your money already, will get you when we can“. Now if this game is $60 for its entire content,  then I may have a better review and say it could be worth it, but charging $60 for a game that is broken, and another 20 for the DLC is absolute GREED as other reviewer‘s have stated. If I were everyone, I would wait for another steam sale before picking this up, my friends and I were able to buy it for $15 during the summer stem sale so I have no complaints. This review is to warn others who are thinking about buying it.

Do you love grinding for very difficult to achieve items to make yourself more powerful in the long run?! Do you absolutely love the feeling of accomplishment after countless hours of finally achieving your "rare" item?! Well, my friend. Warframe seems to be the game for you! Yes, it may get extremely repetitive and boring over time of you doing the same thing over and over but that depends if you love the feeling of success and accomplishment after doing something a million times. Your main objective in this game is to practically make yourself very overpowered to the point that end-game enemies aren't even a solid threat against your fury. You spent countless hours upgrading your mods, Warframes, weapons, and companions while achieving more in time making it impossible to feel satisfied with what you currently possess. Just a final word of advice for those seeking to play this game. Since it is free to play, almost everything you do in this game takes a hefty amount of time and RNG luck to progress. For a completely free game, it can't really get better than this. Tons of content, (mostly) regular updates, great relationship between DE (the developers) and the community and 99% of ingame stuff (and 100% of stuff that matters) is obtainable without having to pay for it with real money. It's grindy at times but you won't mind it because the combat system is pretty good, there's a huge amount of weapons to use and tons of different missions in which you'll be trying them out.
The main "content" in the game is unlocking new fun stuff to use and customizing it to your liking, and Warframe really excels at this - with dozens of unique Warframes with very different skill sets, hundreds of different weapons and accessories, and mods that further allow you to customize them, there's always something new to do or unlock. The last two major updates even added a very cool storyline to follow that already has had a huge impact on the Warframe universe, and added various new progression mechanics to your character.
So if you want to team up with 3 of your friends and just cut through hordes of enemies in an exterminate mission, or maybe stealthily make your way to the data vaults in spy missions, or defend an objective for as long as possible for constantly increasing rewards... this might be just the game for you. Also, it often has huge updates that change the game at its core (which explains the "perpetual beta" in which this game is still technically in) so if you tried it years ago but disliked something, it might be worth a second look.

Nowadays most rpg-mmo-xpersons-shooter games have all this lootbox craze and entire content locked behind paywalls and such, Warframe dont hide massive new content behind paywalls, there is always a way to get the new items one way or another without of course having to spend a few dollars.
It may not have the super-wonderful desings of games like Destiny 2, but atleast it is honest with its playerbase, and will be staying far away from any gambling or anything

Like DayZ and H1Z1, ARK: Survival Evolved is another Early-Access survival game that has received an explosive amount of attention. But does it provide something different enough to warrant all the publicity? In short, no. You can collect materials, craft items, and tame dinosaurs, but many of those features are not exclusive to ARK, nor are they any better here. Serious functionality problems and lag exist, sapping enjoyment and crippling immersion. Still, it’s not completely awful. Given the chance, you can have a lot of fun. The game can be entertaining at times and frustrating on occasion, but the evolution of survival it is not--at least not yet.
You arrive naked, freezing and starving on a strange island known as Ark. You’ll need to use all your strength and ability to kill, tame or even ride the dinosaurs and other creatures that are roaming the mysterious land.

Aside from some awesome dino interactions, you’ll also need to think about your survival. Growing crops, crafting items, hunting and harvesting, researching technologies and building shelters will become your focus on Ark.

Plus, you can team up with or take on the other players that will start appearing on Ark.

I'm recommending this game because the core gameplay is astounding. It is without a doubt on of the funnest, diverse, and just plain awesome coop third person shooter games around. And it's free.
The graphics are beautiful, optimized, and I'm sure a potato from 2001 could run it on lowest settings. Even so the game is AAA quality on max settings. The sound, music, and everything related to audio is good.
A lot of the people will jokingly call this game things like warfarm, grindframe, etc. They're not entirely wrong but most things are easily acquired in the span of one or two days, and unless you're trying to get everything there is to get it's not noticable. A lot of the game is doing the same thing over and over again, but it's so much fun that you barely notice. There is a bit of a wait to craft weapons, and different warframes (each warframe is unique in stats and abilities) but nothing I know of takes longer than three days, most weapons only taking between 12 and 24 hours to craft. I'd say the waiting is worse than the farming, but moving on.
My biggest issue with the game is end game. Enemies scale so much that it becomes a fight against heavily armored bullet sponges that can kill you in less than a second. It becomes more about bringing abusable skills/weapons than about what is fun as well as effective. However, most things are very usable until enemies hit about level 50 or so, well beyond the level range of a good 95% of the content. The developer is aware of this issue and are taking steps to better balance the game. Only time will tell if they'll be effective.
The 'cash shop' currency can be used to buy practically everything immediately with no wait. There are very very few items, all of which are only cosmetic, which you actually must purchase with real money. You can get everything through in game trading for platinum (the cash currency) and even begin doing this relatively early in the game.
Warframe feels like a AAA multiplayer experience available for free. So there's no harm in at least trying it.

The gameplay on ARK is however truly an amazing experience and very different than ANY other survival game on Steam by far. Oh, this is probably the only time I'll ever write a review for such a smelly piece of garbage of a game.  This is what I would call the proverbial "as wide as the ocean but as deep as a puddle" phrase.  I mean, I'll open this review up right now as the bottom-line statement, "if you love games like minecraft but also love dinosaurs, I guess this is for you".
First of all, I bought this out of pure obligation to join some friends, and boy I haven't hated a game this much in awhile.  Its always run like complete Snail feces.  Its just "farming items so u may simply survive and make/farm better items".  There's a few bosses and that makes things interesting but, ultimately... The base gameplay is shallow, boring, and repetitive.  Swing a weapon, shoot a gun, mindlessly smack a resource to collect it.  Real "fun" amirite?
The world is huge, and I *guess* the game looks pretty good.  I will be honest, my review to a degree is bias since the survival genre I already find to be stupid on a conceptual level but that's a story for another time.
Furthermore, the developers of this game don't deserve a dime.  Decently expensive Paid DLC when they aren't even done with the base game, a game in early access?  A extremely greedy, and bad move.  The game's core fundamental issues such as performance  (I run a i7-6700k w/ 16 GB of RAM, and a EVGA GTX 980 OC) its obvious they spent all their time not developing the game, but taking money from people.  Disgusting.  And now they want to release this horrid-running game that honestly has extremely little content?  (PS No, mods don't count.  Because that's not the developer creating content now is it?)
Ultimately, I don't understand the sheer addiction to this game nor its genre.  You go out and farm stuff in a extremely simplistic environment and "survive".  Just go outside and go camping if u want that experience, it'll be more interesting too instead of toiling away for a few dinosaurs and grinding out resource collection, I suppose this is for you.
So many more games with actually interesting story or lore, like Divinity: Original Sin or with interesting, deep gameplay like the Battletech game coming out or Stellaris.  And if u like anime, some great VNs now exist in english here too.  Oh, and if I want to grind away, I have tons of MMORPGs to play but at least  the gameplay is actually fun.
So to those who enjoy it, well, have fun.  I'll be off doing something actually *good*.

Writing this review as of the very end stages of Early Access.
I had to return ARK because my PC barely ran it on low settings (I have a crappy $800 PC), but I went and got it on PS4 and it's just an immensely fun game. All the core survival elements are there. Food, water, cooking recipes, and so many things you can build and place and use that I can't even begin to go into it here. (There are 100 character levels, and EVERY LEVEL unlocks like 4-10 new recipes you have the option of spending your points to unlock. And the Scorched Earth expansion adds even more!) And you can do it all among the biggest, baddest birdlizards our imaginations have ever known: Dinosaurs. Beautifully sculpted, textured and animated dinosaurs.
The variety of dinosaurs in the game is excellent, and they way they interact with eachother sometimes adds a little something to the game's breathtaking environment. That coel you can stab with a spear and bring home for dinner? The big bird circling overhead can and will swoop down, grab it, and eat it if you don't. You may be next, as a hungry flier will sometimes decide to swoop down and harass you, stealing any berries you carry! Dinosaurs have Hunger and Thirst just like you do, and they'll satisfy their hunger by foraging, stealing your food, or hunting other dinosaurs. In as far as you're a living being in this game, the dinosaurs really feel like they're just as alive as you are.
Add to this that each dinosaur is a little unique. Each individual dinosaur has a level, a gender and a color scheme, meaning no two triceratops, no two tyrannosaurs, no two raptors will necessarily be identical. I'd like to also state that the sheer variety of dinosaur SPECIES in the game is immense. Whether in forests, mountains, water or the air, there are numerous species. Everything from the iconic t-rex and spinosaurus to the lesser known therizinosaurus and troodon are here, each species with a small number of variable appearances. You can potentially tame, ride and hunt alongside ANY of them, and if I'm not mistaken, you can even breed dinos.
The game scratches several itches I've had since I first saw Jurassic Park ages ago. It lets me live among dinosaurs. It lets me carve out a place for myself in that world. It lets me make PETS of said dinosaurs. And from a video game standpoint, it scratches several as well: A deep, impactful survival experience where the line between predator and prey can become pretty thin at any moment. This is a game I legitimately want to seek shelter in once the sun goes down, not because enemies level up or because some unique foe comes out at night, but because the creatures in this game are as terrifying as they are beautiful and I want to SEE THEM COMING, damnit.
It could be better. Any game could. Be it couldn't be a whole lot better, from where I'm standing.
(Do note that I'm essentially reviewing the single-player experience. I dropped into an official server out of curiosity to find my spawn surrounded by locked gates I couldn't break because offline protection of structures was on, and the builder was offline. That was the end of that. I've seen Youtube evidence, though, that multiplayer can be really fun and pretty rewarding if you've got some people to run with. You can build handcuffs and cages, for what it's worth, if screwing with other players suits your fancy. And the tranquilizer arrows you can eventually craft work as well on humans as they do on dinosaurs, I'd imagine, as both players and dinosaurs share the same parameters; Torpidity being the key one here.)

Warframe is a fun third person, co-op, grind focused, leveling shooter, that takes place in a dark space future.
Warning: This game contains microtransactions, while not needed to progress, they do destroy the timewall. If you are someone who dislikes Microtransactions, this game may not be for you. That said, I think its pricing model is reasonable enough. Especially given that with player trading and the ability to "hunt" for warframe parts by doing objectives and killing bosses, its possible to obtain everything without spending a cent. (use your starter plat on weapon slots and a warframe slot)
I've played this game since beta, it's really hard to encapsulate everything in a short review.  The most important part is that its fun. Fluid movement controls, fast paced combat, and a general sense of progression as you unlock new weapons and warframes.  A huge, sprawling map of different locations to visit and destroy with your ever increasing power.
The weapons in this game are varied, though it does suffer from some of the newer content outclassing older content. But thankfully with the recent War Within update adding new "Riven" mods to unlock and roll random stats on, the potential to turn a underperforming weapon into a powerful one is high.
The graphics are pretty, for every issue I've had with Warframe, its art department is not one. The maps are varied, the world looks beautiful, especially given the new lighting they've added recently. And despite these impressive graphics, you can run it on a lower end machine and still have it look  reasonably pretty.
This is a great game if you are looking for a game that will tickle the "horde mode shooter" itch. Warframe is 4 player co-op with (slightly buggy at the moment) 8 player raids. There are clans/guilds for you to join, you can even start your own easily enough. A system that lets you upload a decal (paid function) to represent your clan to everyone else in warframe.
Its got a solid community, you will find a mix of nearly every culture type in warframe. Friendly people, angry people, people who like to solo. But my experience with it thus far is that most are very friendly.
Ratings are pointless, give it a spin and see if you like it, I certainly have.

A lot of people these days are hesitant when it comes to free to play games, and I don't blame them, what with the mobile market slowly tainting the console and pc gaming markets (2K Games). Warframe, however, is actually a good game.
This game is exactly how you do free to play right. Digital Extremes cares about its space ninja babies and has nurtured them to be rifle and sword wielding mega space ninja babies that will slice a greedy milk bag in two without even blinking. DE regularly updates the game with new weapons, cosmetics, quests, and features, and it's all free. It's free to play any update.
Anyone, I mean anyone, is able to get anything in the game without paying real world money; you just either are ok with grinding or have just the right amount of ADHD to give them a few bucks... I might be the latter, but it's only because DE cares about their product.
I know. These days you would think all devs would be locking content behind paywalls and not even batting an eye, but not DE. I am proud to say that I have been playing this game for years now, and I will most likely be playing it for years to come... Unless Activision gets their hands on it, looking at you, Destiny.

Clicker Heroes falls into the category called Idle Games. This means it is a game that pretty much plays itself in the background. It is a type of game quickly rising up since it gives people something to "play" while being at work or doing other activities. For games like these to appeal a lot of moving bars, big numbers and other "addictive" elements need to be added in order for people to keep returning.
Clicker Heroes is a game where you're a hero. By clicking on monsters you'll gain gold. With these coins you'll then hire more heroes to gather quite a large following. They can be leveled up and unlock new abilities doing increasing amounts of damage. Quickly you won't have to be clicking yourself anymore since the heroes will do it for you. Just keep investing gold to level them up and make them stronger over time.
Every 5 levels you'll run into a "boss". This monster has a huge HP pool that needs to be dwindled down within 30seconds. Otherwise the boss will reset and you'll have to retry using cool down bonusses. Or go back a level and farm more gold to make your heroes stronger. These bosses are, in the strictest sense, checks to see if you're doing enough damage to proceed. Similar to dreaded gear checks in ARPG's.
For those players who prefer a more active approach in an idle game there is a way. You can click your fingers off for minimal difference done in damage to the opponent. Even with massive bonusses, crit chance and crit damage there is rarely a reason to click yourself. Only reason to click is for the achievements related to it which grant additional DPS bonusses overall. For this I suggest getting an Auto-Clicker program which can be found through google quite easily.
There is a "reward" aspect to being more active in this Idle Game. From time to time a floating bunny creature will appear at the top of the screen. After repeatedly clicking it this creature will grant a certain temporary bonus. This will make killing easier and thus obtaining gold faster. Another thing that appears, seemingly, randomly is a pair of chicken wings. These will grant additional money and every 3 or so appearance reward you with a Ruby. Every two or so days I was able to obtain 30 rubies without having to buy them for real life money. With these rubies you can get Gilded Heroes or buy other things like an Ascension.
For every 2000 levels you upgrade your heroes you'll gain a Hero Soul. Once you reset the game, through an Ascension, it means you'll have a certain amount of Souls. These give bonusses to damage done. It translates into faster killing and going through levels faster. Obtaining money faster, upgrading faster and in general proceeding faster beyond the point before you reset the game. These souls, however, can also be used to summon Ancients. These are relics that grant even more bonuses. They can also be leveled up using souls.
Overall Clicker Heroes looks like a simple Flash game that you have running in the background during other activities. Such as is normal with Idle Games of this kind. However CH misses a big addiction factor that makes you want to play it for a long period of time. It is fun to try it out, but gets tedious fairly quickly. Therefore I recommend this game for those who want some other Idle game to add to their collection. Since it is still fun for a week or two.

There will be a TL;DR at the bottom for those without the time to read my review. Now, I have spent a good chunk of time playing this game. The hours Steam has logged aren't exactly genuine as I've accidentally left the game on overnight on more than one occasion. But still, I have about 70 days of in-mission time logged on this game. It's kept me occupied for the past couple years, and it's always evolving. It's given my dad, brother and me time to bond and get closer as a family, as we play it most every night. In this review, I'll be going over the various ins and outs that this game has to offer.
As far as gameplay is concerned, it's fairly limited with a few varients on certain game types, but most of the game types do
to keep things fresh. Playing with friends and the many awesome players in the community can also alleviate monotony and "new player blues". Movement is fluid and very satisfying. Most everything can be obtained just by playing the game. Bosses, save for a few, are fun and rewarding to fight, and have interesting personalities and relationships with the player. Progressing is as easy as doing litterally everything the game has to offer, which I still haven't accomplished (though that's mostly my fault). The developers are always coming up with new bosses, mission types, Warframes, weapons, etc. Enemy scaling is screwy (for example, take a lvl 30 Corrupted Bombard versus a lvl 50 Corrupted Bombard. You could probably tank a rocket or three, depending on which Warframe you're using with which mods, from the lvl 30 one, but a single rocket from the lvl 50 Bombard could wipe out a moderately prepared Rhino or Valkyr. Customization is a very important part of the game. You can spend probably half an hour just modding your Warframe--even longer if you like to test and adjust your builds! FashionFrame FTW. Cosmetics are one of the only non-free items in the game. You can build most everything. Not everything in the game is very well-explained, so you will probably have to ask someone in Region chat, the forums, or the subreddit about various things. The community is very supportive of new players, and they will help you understand things if you ask. PvP is fun but it's not the main focus of the game.
Graphics are great and getting better! The animations are quality. Sound design is on point and, for the most part, behaves realistically.
The music is phenominal and really gets you into the game. For example, when you find
, the music and overall feel of the game makes you really feel like you're not meant to be there, more than any other location in the game. It's too bad the enemy levels were so low for someone at my level in the game; I would have actually felt like my Warframe was in danger! A lot of emotion went into this game's soundtrack, and it shows. Level design is good. The maps are tile-based much like any rogue-like game (eg. Binding of Isaac). Certain tile sets are beautiful and awe-inspiring (Orokin Tower,
, just the Orokin stuff in general), while others are mildly infuriating to navigate (Infested Ship, Ice Planet, and sometimes the Grineer Forest). Overall, the level design is satisfying. Warframe design is all over the place, and I love it. Some Warframes look better than others (For example, Nyx Prime is probably my favorite-looking frame, whereas non-Prime, Non-Orphid Saryn kind of falls short in the looks department. She makes up for it in the stats department, though!), but that's what FashionFrame is for! And, I hate to end this section on a bad note, but I feel like I should mention that some of the voice acting is sub-par at best. But, oh man, I love Tyl Regor's voice; so silky smooth!
The community is fantastic, and eager to help newcomers figure the game out. The community is also very giving, and on occasion will help you out with a Warframe slot or something. I can't really say many negative things about the community because there really isn't that much to complain about. Just watch for the occasional toxic player.
I feel it's necessary to mention how awesome the developers are. If you have an issue, they can typically fix it. Just go to the support forums, and they'll quickly respond within a couple of work days. They host a biweekly stream on Twitch and YouTube to talk about the game and what they're doing with it next. They're funny people who are fun to listen to.

to only buy slots and cosmetics, however I'm not in control of your Plat. You get 50 Platinum to start, but it can't be used for trading. Seriously, just be patient and build the stuff.

Warframe is a long running free to play game with premium options to spend real money on.
You'll likely read and hear that Warframe is grind heavy, and indeed it can be, but I've always felt that a grind can be made to feel unimportant so long as the game itself is fun, and the grind does not feel necassary. Warframe is grindy, but it is not a necassary grind.
The actual gameplay, that of third person combat is highly satisfying. The movement feels mostly very fluid and quite easy to manage complex and badass moves that leave you feeling as if you're more than just the common enemies. You're more agile, more skilled, and far more mobile. The weapons range in feel from average shooter, and beyond. Finding weapons that you like and prefer over others, even if slightly weaker, can be very satisfying. Melee weapons are not the best aspect of the game, but they are easy to use and are done far better than most every other shooter game I've ever played. Not the high point, but considering how great most of the guns feel, the melee weapons not being as satisfying is not a gross condemnation of the game by any means.
The movement and guns feel great. The missions themselves are usually fairly short and feature random maps. The maps are not like a lego set with a million different pieces arranged for your running pleasure, rather the map makers have created rooms and hallways that are semi-randomly matched together so that while all of the missions look somewhat similar, the maps themselves are greatly varied. It's a servicable solution to keep burnout at bay for the player. There is much to hide behind and flip about on. The gameplay is further varied by each frame or class that the player can use. Everything from a warframe that can hurl fire and burn everything in sight to a quick cowboy-like frame that blasts enemies with a pair of pistols.
The grind is not severe. It will take a lot of time to attain what you want, but for the most part you don't need any of the truly grindy items. You'll mostly just find yourself setting a goal and grinding for it because you enjoy the gameplay itself, the goal itself is pretty much secondary as you revel in slaughtering hundreds of hapless enemies.
Everything can be attained by not paying any money, though some items may naturally require longer periods of time to acquire without paying real money. The player economy is strong and obtaining the premium currency by trading away valuable items that other players want is not a severe affair, though may require some luck and timing if you're unwilling to negotiate.
Try the game, and if you enjoy the movement and gunplay then you're likely to enjoy sticking around. If the movement and guns, even the starter weapons, don't sound, look, and feel satisfying to you then I'd say that the gameplay will not quite manage to hook you, and so the grind will quickly exhaust you.

As a preface; I exclusively play Warframe through their own launcher and not the steam one, so don't take the hours listed here seriously. As of writing this review I have at least 900 hours in the game.
Warframe may market itself as a game about ninjas, but that isn't really a very good description of it.
Warframe is a player vs enemy randomized dungeon crawler / third person shooter / Hero shooter / grind for progession free to play MMO-like centered around the idea of obtaining and mastering loot and weapons.
The gameplay itself consists of moving around the map quickly through use of your warframe's high air mobility while you shoot enemies while performing an objective on the map. Sometimes this objective IS to shoot enemies. Every mission in the game basically boils down to this. But missions happen in such short spurts and have such a jump in/jump out quality to them that they manage to be addictive and entertaining, despite not being all that varied.
This game is free to play, which means there are microtransactions. Most of these microtransactions are extremely fair, you can get around almost all of them by grinding in the game (Not factoring in trading through the in game economy). The grind is, obviously, not the quickest thing in the universe. It is however much quicker than most other Free to Play games that I have experienced.
There is a lot of grinding in this game, if you enjoy games like Monster Hunter you'll probably have fun here. If you hate the idea of grinding, this game might not be for you. I do find that the grinding doesn't often feel bad in Warframe since Warframe's goal IS getting that next item or maxing that next mod. Unlike other games, progress isn't often locked behind getting that item. Instead, getting that next item IS the progress, and if you arn't happy with your progress towards that weapon you can swap your focus to getting a different one since there are so many of them. This tapers off a little bit once you hit the end of the game as I have, where the things being grinded for (Riven mods and Primed Items almost exclusively) often are based entirely on RNG, so you lose the feeling of every mission you do serving as some form of progress. I do feel that's fair after accumulating the number of hours that I have, however.
The dev team is pretty involved with their community. Even when they don't listen to popular feedback they usually do address the fact that the feedback WAS present and read. Which is more than most devs these days, who seem almost scared to be even slightly open with the community.
The game is constantly updated, and not in the way you expect from most f2ps where it's like "every six months or so they add a pay to play episode that lasts 10 minutes and has unbalanced drops." Warframes quests are always free, and while they've slowed down a bit recently, manage to come out fairly frequently. New weapons are added to the game at a pretty fast pace. There's usually at least one update per week, though the update doesn't always contain new additions.
The game isn't without issues, though. First of which is balance. The game is PVE so balance isn't AS high a requirement as it would be in PVP games, but the lack of balance is still there. Most weapons in the game can perform throughout the entire star chart, but theres very noticiable performance gaps that grow larger and more noticiable the longer you play.
Inventory Slots. Earlier I said that most of the microtransactions are super fair and only save you time. There is one exception to this. You start the game with a handful of slots for weapons and warframes. Each built weapon or warframe requires a slot. Since the game is all about gaining new warframes and weapons the starting ammount of slots, while they will not prevent you from playing as long and to as hard of difficulties as you want, will definitely hinder your enjoyment as you're forced to ditch your weapons pretty regularly. Slots arn't that expensive, and though I think they could give new players one or two slots more, they're still pretty fair considering. You can play with just the starter slots but slots are definitely the area you will feel you're forced to drop money on the most during your time with this game.
Bugs. The game is pretty buggy. Rarely unplayably so, but they're still not exactly rare. DE doesn't really seem to have any kind of large internal testing team, so whenever any new quests or new modes launch, you can expect to encounter a lot of bugs with them during the first two days of their implementation before DE manages to smooth them out some.
The game doesn't explain itself well. A lot of things you will need to look up on the wiki or ask other players about.
I would recommend Warframe if you're looking to just jump into a quick game at your leisure on occasion and don't neccesarely want something that costs much or is in depth. I would also recommend it if you don't mind playing a game with no real goal other than having fun while grinding out whatever looks cool or is new.  I wouldn't say that Warframe is for everybody, but I do think the majority of gamers can probably enjoy it for what it is.

The only game I've played that remotely delivers on the promise to make you feel like a ninja.  No "hold a button while the game plays itself for you" BS here.  You want to pull off rad Hong Kong Blood Opera moves and chain double-jump knee slides radial sword attack wallrun bullet-time leaps?  Pull them off yourself, Tenbro.  Glory is earned through player skill.  Reminds me of the first F.E.A.R. and Mirror's Edge in that regard -- it gives the player the tools to succeed and it's up to the player to use them however he wants.
Also, one of the least-filthy free-to-play systems I've seen in a game so far (not quite up to Path of Exile standards, but what is?), with all accounts starting with cash-shop currency, cash shop items frequently given away through login rewards and numerous in-game events, and most functional cash-shop items can be crafted rather than bought with real-life money.  Yes, it can feel like a grind at times ("lol warfarm," right?), but the gameplay and atmosphere are so excellently executed that even after 600+ hours, I still have fun and it doesn't feel grindy to me, since every mission is an opportunity to take down foes and feel boss while doing it.
Aggressively updated, frequent and numerous in-game events, some of the most satisfying gameplay I've experienced in years.  Digital Extremes has been putting a smile on my face since 1999 and they continue to do so.
Warframe continues to be fully enjoyable even if you haven't paid any money for anything in-game and is consistently, objectively better than Destiny.

This "game," like Cookie Clicker etc, is pretty interesting from a behavioralist standpoint - They've successfully removed all gameplay and reduced the formula purely down to the grinding, but it still makes you want to keep playing. You constantly feel the need to hit the next breakpoint, but it never actually comes, as both you and the monsters are gaining power exponentially. But the numbers are getting bigger, so it must be going somewhere, right?
Clicker Heroes is nothing more than an endless dopamine trickle, which is habit forming in basically the same way smoking cigarettes is, and about as rewarding ultimately. It's very well made, and I'll admit the concept is pretty brilliant in a cynical way, but I really don't recommend anyone play it, as it is actually tangibly making the world a worse place by existing.

Warframe is a fun third person, co-op, grind focused, leveling shooter, that takes place in a dark space future.
Warning: This game contains microtransactions, while not needed to progress, they do destroy the timewall. If you are someone who dislikes Microtransactions, this game may not be for you. That said, I think its pricing model is reasonable enough. Especially given that with player trading and the ability to "hunt" for warframe parts by doing objectives and killing bosses, its possible to obtain everything without spending a cent. (use your starter plat on weapon slots and a warframe slot)
I've played this game since beta, it's really hard to encapsulate everything in a short review.  The most important part is that its fun. Fluid movement controls, fast paced combat, and a general sense of progression as you unlock new weapons and warframes.  A huge, sprawling map of different locations to visit and destroy with your ever increasing power.
The weapons in this game are varied, though it does suffer from some of the newer content outclassing older content. But thankfully with the recent War Within update adding new "Riven" mods to unlock and roll random stats on, the potential to turn a underperforming weapon into a powerful one is high.
The graphics are pretty, for every issue I've had with Warframe, its art department is not one. The maps are varied, the world looks beautiful, especially given the new lighting they've added recently. And despite these impressive graphics, you can run it on a lower end machine and still have it look  reasonably pretty.
This is a great game if you are looking for a game that will tickle the "horde mode shooter" itch. Warframe is 4 player co-op with (slightly buggy at the moment) 8 player raids. There are clans/guilds for you to join, you can even start your own easily enough. A system that lets you upload a decal (paid function) to represent your clan to everyone else in warframe.
Its got a solid community, you will find a mix of nearly every culture type in warframe. Friendly people, angry people, people who like to solo. But my experience with it thus far is that most are very friendly.
Ratings are pointless, give it a spin and see if you like it, I certainly have.

So Ark Survival Evolved....This is my first and possibly only review but I feel after some 4k hours at present in this game I might be able to offer some benefit of my experience.
First off because this may run a little long, this game is nothing short of awesome. I would like to address some preconceptions about this game before I continue. A lot of reviews will say its very buggy and needs an amazing pc to run it. I'm currently using an i5 760 2.8ghz, 8gb ram and a gtx760 and it runs fine on mainly medium settings. Its not the greatest graphically but it suffices and is very playable.
There are also a lot of upset people that will negatively review on the basis that Widcard released a paid for dlc for an early access game. This is neither here nor there for a review of the game itself and they can be safely ignored as gamers who like the game, but are merely upset by a studio's decision to charge for a dlc before the game is released. Personally, I understand the outrage but also that game devs need money to keep going with their project, and that we the gamers have a choice to either keep supporting a concept we love that is moving forward constantly or be shocked that a company needs to pay its bills. Either way the DLC isn't essential so I feel it should be ignored as a games selling point.
The game itself is sooooo much fun at times. You have a constant dread of death especially in the oceans and its a true survival game. Troodons will wreck you as a noob especially at night. Raptors and Allosaurs will tear out of the trees. Argents will swoop out of the sky and chase you down. Rex's and Spinos will tear you apart if you get too close. Its brutal at times and will make you swear a lot, but ultimatley worthwhile. As you level and build more complex structures and items, things will become eaiser to do and new challenges present themselves as you prgress.
The game has changed so much since I started playing with new maps, a tonne of new dinos and a myriad of other alterations yet no matter the changes I have stuck with this game throughout. I have to give kudos to Wildcard who have given this game a huge amount of focus with updates on a sometimes ridiculous basis, but their attention to detail and to the gamers feedback has been amazing. There are still a few issues at the point of writing this such as the building system being more than a little awkward at timesbut I am confident this is being addressed and I would recommend this game to anyone who loves survival games.
My only criticism of the whole thing is that the offical servers take sooooooo long to do anything that people lose interest, but even then, there are so many servers available for both PvE and PvP, along with a huge amounts of workshop content for mods to be able to accomadate almost anyone. I paid nearly £20 for this almost 2 years ago and it paid for itself in entertainment value alone in about 2 days.
Probably the best F2P game outthere.

I've been playing Warframe for two years now. I still come back periodically, but I don't know why.  Warframe is just different from other games.
You control a "Warframe" which is essentially a puppet controlled by the "Operator", which is you. You're a Tenno, a race  which seeks to uphold balance in the universe, fighting either against the Grineer, the Corpus or the Infested. Warfame is a solid 3rd person shooter with original mechanics and gameplay style, centered around parkour and being a ninja. There is a huge variety of weapons and warframes to choose from, some of which you will have to painfully grind for. No game escapes from the plague of grind.
Beware though, Warframe is game best enjoyed in small bursts. While the first appeal may get you hooked, you will soon encounter a problem all veterans have encountered. Boredom. No end-game. Nothing to do once you've mastered all gear. You'll argue that it happens with every game, but it happens quite fast with Warframe.
Pros:
+ Great controls
+ Variety of items
+ Better community than most others
+ Originality
+ GFX (although ageing a bit) and Audio effects
+ Runs smooth and consistant
+ No purchases required to have all weapons and gear, just cosmetics
Cons:
- Replay value dwindles quickly
- Lackluster PvP (You shouldn't play this for PvP anyway)
- Frustrating/cheap AI on harder difficulties
- Rewards for some long tasks are a slap to the face
- Wonky matchmaking system

A seemingly endless cookie clicker game that can be quite addictive. With no story, the game is more about seeing how far you can get and seeing outrageously large numbers of damage and gold.
The game is pretty straightforward although there are a few ways to play it. Click the monsters to deal extra damage, collect their gold and spend the gold on your heroes which increase your overall DPS (the amount of damage dealt per second to the monster when you aren't clicking). Increasing your DPS will also increase your click damage as well. Being active in this way will allow you to get Rubies which would otherwise be bought through micro-transactions in the in-game shop. The other way is to rack up gold by idling, with the game closed you can earn gold when not playing.   Along the way as you level your heroes you can get some unique skills such as increasing the % of gold you earn per kill and ways to temporarily increase your DPS and click damage. Every 5 areas (zones) you'll fight a boss with tons of hit points. There is a catch though, you have to beat him within 30 seconds. This is the standard for testing the way you leveled your heroes and how much effort you put into leveling them.
Recommended for people who are bored, have old/slow PCs or Laptops or just straight up like addictive clicker games like these . Seeing as I'm temporarily (and reluctantly) using an old crappy computer for the rest of this week, I'll be playing this game for a while.

A seemingly endless cookie clicker game that can be quite addictive. With no story, the game is more about seeing how far you can get and seeing outrageously large numbers of damage and gold.
The game is pretty straightforward although there are a few ways to play it. Click the monsters to deal extra damage, collect their gold and spend the gold on your heroes which increase your overall DPS (the amount of damage dealt per second to the monster when you aren't clicking). Increasing your DPS will also increase your click damage as well. Being active in this way will allow you to get Rubies which would otherwise be bought through micro-transactions in the in-game shop. The other way is to rack up gold by idling, with the game closed you can earn gold when not playing.   Along the way as you level your heroes you can get some unique skills such as increasing the % of gold you earn per kill and ways to temporarily increase your DPS and click damage. Every 5 areas (zones) you'll fight a boss with tons of hit points. There is a catch though, you have to beat him within 30 seconds. This is the standard for testing the way you leveled your heroes and how much effort you put into leveling them.
Recommended for people who are bored, have old/slow PCs or Laptops or just straight up like addictive clicker games like these . Seeing as I'm temporarily (and reluctantly) using an old crappy computer for the rest of this week, I'll be playing this game for a while.

text:
As a preface; I exclusively play Warframe through their own launcher and not the steam one, so don't take the hours listed here seriously. As of writing this review I have at least 900 hours in the game.
Warframe may market itself as a game about ninjas, but that isn't really a very good description of it.
Warframe is a player vs enemy randomized dungeon crawler / third person shooter / Hero shooter / grind for progession free to play MMO-like centered around the idea of obtaining and mastering loot and weapons.
The gameplay itself consists of moving around the map quickly through use of your warframe's high air mobility while you shoot enemies while performing an objective on the map. Sometimes this objective IS to shoot enemies. Every mission in the game basically boils down to this. But missions happen in such short spurts and have such a jump in/jump out quality to them that they manage to be addictive and entertaining, despite not being all that varied.
This game is free to play, which means there are microtransactions. Most of these microtransactions are extremely fair, you can get around almost all of them by grinding in the game (Not factoring in trading through the in game economy). The grind is, obviously, not the quickest thing in the universe. It is however much quicker than most other Free to Play games that I have experienced.
There is a lot of grinding in this game, if you enjoy games like Monster Hunter you'll probably have fun here. If you hate the idea of grinding, this game might not be for you. I do find that the grinding doesn't often feel bad in Warframe since Warframe's goal IS getting that next item or maxing that next mod. Unlike other games, progress isn't often locked behind getting that item. Instead, getting that next item IS the progress, and if you arn't happy with your progress towards that weapon you can swap your focus to getting a different one since there are so many of them. This tapers off a little bit once you hit the end of the game as I have, where the things being grinded for (Riven mods and Primed Items almost exclusively) often are based entirely on RNG, so you lose the feeling of every mission you do serving as some form of progress. I do feel that's fair after accumulating the number of hours that I have, however.
The dev team is pretty involved with their community. Even when they don't listen to popular feedback they usually do address the fact that the feedback WAS present and read. Which is more than most devs these days, who seem almost scared to be even slightly open with the community.
The game is constantly updated, and not in the way you expect from most f2ps where it's like "every six months or so they add a pay to play episode that lasts 10 minutes and has unbalanced drops." Warframes quests are always free, and while they've slowed down a bit recently, manage to come out fairly frequently. New weapons are added to the game at a pretty fast pace. There's usually at least one update per week, though the update doesn't always contain new additions.
The game isn't without issues, though. First of which is balance. The game is PVE so balance isn't AS high a requirement as it would be in PVP games, but the lack of balance is still there. Most weapons in the game can perform throughout the entire star chart, but theres very noticiable performance gaps that grow larger and more noticiable the longer you play.
Inventory Slots. Earlier I said that most of the microtransactions are super fair and only save you time. There is one exception to this. You start the game with a handful of slots for weapons and warframes. Each built weapon or warframe requires a slot. Since the game is all about gaining new warframes and weapons the starting ammount of slots, while they will not prevent you from playing as long and to as hard of difficulties as you want, will definitely hinder your enjoyment as you're forced to ditch your weapons pretty regularly. Slots arn't that expensive, and though I think they could give new players one or two slots more, they're still pretty fair considering. You can play with just the starter slots but slots are definitely the area you will feel you're forced to drop money on the most during your time with this game.
Bugs. The game is pretty buggy. Rarely unplayably so, but they're still not exactly rare. DE doesn't really seem to have any kind of large internal testing team, so whenever any new quests or new modes launch, you can expect to encounter a lot of bugs with them during the first two days of their implementation before DE manages to smooth them out some.
The game doesn't explain itself well. A lot of things you will need to look up on the wiki or ask other players about.
I would recommend Warframe if you're looking to just jump into a quick game at your leisure on occasion and don't neccesarely want something that costs much or is in depth. I would also recommend it if you don't mind playing a game with no real goal other than having fun while grinding out whatever looks cool or is new.  I wouldn't say that Warframe is for everybody, but I do think the majority of gamers can probably enjoy it for what it is.

The only game I've played that remotely delivers on the promise to make you feel like a ninja.  No "hold a button while the game plays itself for you" BS here.  You want to pull off rad Hong Kong Blood Opera moves and chain double-jump knee slides radial sword attack wallrun bullet-time leaps?  Pull them off yourself, Tenbro.  Glory is earned through player skill.  Reminds me of the first F.E.A.R. and Mirror's Edge in that regard -- it gives the player the tools to succeed and it's up to the player to use them however he wants.
Also, one of the least-filthy free-to-play systems I've seen in a game so far (not quite up to Path of Exile standards, but what is?), with all accounts starting with cash-shop currency, cash shop items frequently given away through login rewards and numerous in-game events, and most functional cash-shop items can be crafted rather than bought with real-life money.  Yes, it can feel like a grind at times ("lol warfarm," right?), but the gameplay and atmosphere are so excellently executed that even after 600+ hours, I still have fun and it doesn't feel grindy to me, since every mission is an opportunity to take down foes and feel boss while doing it.
Aggressively updated, frequent and numerous in-game events, some of the most satisfying gameplay I've experienced in years.  Digital Extremes has been putting a smile on my face since 1999 and they continue to do so.
Warframe continues to be fully enjoyable even if you haven't paid any money for anything in-game and is consistently, objectively better than Destiny.

I've been playing Warframe for two years now. I still come back periodically, but I don't know why.  Warframe is just different from other games.
You control a "Warframe" which is essentially a puppet controlled by the "Operator", which is you. You're a Tenno, a race  which seeks to uphold balance in the universe, fighting either against the Grineer, the Corpus or the Infested. Warfame is a solid 3rd person shooter with original mechanics and gameplay style, centered around parkour and being a ninja. There is a huge variety of weapons and warframes to choose from, some of which you will have to painfully grind for. No game escapes from the plague of grind.
Beware though, Warframe is game best enjoyed in small bursts. While the first appeal may get you hooked, you will soon encounter a problem all veterans have encountered. Boredom. No end-game. Nothing to do once you've mastered all gear. You'll argue that it happens with every game, but it happens quite fast with Warframe.
Pros:
+ Great controls
+ Variety of items
+ Better community than most others
+ Originality
+ GFX (although ageing a bit) and Audio effects
+ Runs smooth and consistant
+ No purchases required to have all weapons and gear, just cosmetics
Cons:
- Replay value dwindles quickly
- Lackluster PvP (You shouldn't play this for PvP anyway)
- Frustrating/cheap AI on harder difficulties
- Rewards for some long tasks are a slap to the face
- Wonky matchmaking system
Hell, it'll kill a few hours if you're bored enough.

Clicker Heroes is a clicker-like game with RPG elements and leveling systems.
Aside from common idle game fare, you click monsters to reduce their health and once they're dead, you are paid gold.
After that, you use gold to hire and level up heroes, but effectively it's no different at this point than... anything really, only there's about 35 heroes, all with different upgrades (though with reused upgrade icon graphics ;3) that do their own thing, like improve everyone, improve your clicks, or even improve the hero's damage.
The important stat to upgrade is Damage Per Second (referred to as DPS in-game and in other parts of the review).
In other Clicker-like idle games, there is a reset-based progression, and the same is of Hero Clickers, however it is not a menu, rather it is an upgrade, unlike any of the other similar games.
I personally like it like this, also namely because Amenhotep is the one to give it via his 3rd/4th upgrade.
There are potentially infinite levels, all which get tougher as you go along ofcourse. Not sure if there is an end point at all.
In addition to everything, once a hero gets to level 175, they gain 4x more DPS every 25 levels. at levels of thousands (1000, 2000, 3000, etc.) they gain 10x more DPS, and this upgrade is an incredible boost, I love it being here.
On top of all that, there are Gilded Heroes and Hero Souls. Hero Souls are the reset-based currency. Every 2000 hero levels gained across the board gives you one Hero Soul per reset. Each one adds 10% more DPS to everything. Gilded heroes add 1 to a hero's multiplier for DPS, which is applied before upgrades, making them wickedly powerful and required past level 1000 (I hear). These Gilded Heroes cost 30 rubies.
Rubies can be bought with real money or earned via eggs or headcrabs that randomly appear, and are commonly called "Hidden items" or "clickables" they now give massive sums of gold, with a chance for a ruby in addition.
There's more I haven't spoken of, the gameplay feels balanced and nothing is too expensive for no reason.
It's Free to play, so just give it a shot anyways. I personallly like this game, and finally to wrap this review up.
I recommend it, the game looks great, the visuals having about as much quality as alot of games out Now. The visual and Audio quality is very impressive for a Clicker-like idle game and with it's additions that are unique to it's genre, it is a great addition to the idle genre.
For those who desire a score, this game gets an 8/10.
Specific Cons:
- The Music drones on, and the sound gets old after about a few hours.
Specific Pros:
- You don't need to spend a cent to get everything, which devalues buying rubies, but you can get more for your money.

text:
As a preface; I exclusively play Warframe through their own launcher and not the steam one, so don't take the hours listed here seriously. As of writing this review I have at least 900 hours in the game.
Warframe may market itself as a game about ninjas, but that isn't really a very good description of it.
Warframe is a player vs enemy randomized dungeon crawler / third person shooter / Hero shooter / grind for progession free to play MMO-like centered around the idea of obtaining and mastering loot and weapons.
The gameplay itself consists of moving around the map quickly through use of your warframe's high air mobility while you shoot enemies while performing an objective on the map. Sometimes this objective IS to shoot enemies. Every mission in the game basically boils down to this. But missions happen in such short spurts and have such a jump in/jump out quality to them that they manage to be addictive and entertaining, despite not being all that varied.
This game is free to play, which means there are microtransactions. Most of these microtransactions are extremely fair, you can get around almost all of them by grinding in the game (Not factoring in trading through the in game economy). The grind is, obviously, not the quickest thing in the universe. It is however much quicker than most other Free to Play games that I have experienced.
There is a lot of grinding in this game, if you enjoy games like Monster Hunter you'll probably have fun here. If you hate the idea of grinding, this game might not be for you. I do find that the grinding doesn't often feel bad in Warframe since Warframe's goal IS getting that next item or maxing that next mod. Unlike other games, progress isn't often locked behind getting that item. Instead, getting that next item IS the progress, and if you arn't happy with your progress towards that weapon you can swap your focus to getting a different one since there are so many of them. This tapers off a little bit once you hit the end of the game as I have, where the things being grinded for (Riven mods and Primed Items almost exclusively) often are based entirely on RNG, so you lose the feeling of every mission you do serving as some form of progress. I do feel that's fair after accumulating the number of hours that I have, however.
The dev team is pretty involved with their community. Even when they don't listen to popular feedback they usually do address the fact that the feedback WAS present and read. Which is more than most devs these days, who seem almost scared to be even slightly open with the community.
The game is constantly updated, and not in the way you expect from most f2ps where it's like "every six months or so they add a pay to play episode that lasts 10 minutes and has unbalanced drops." Warframes quests are always free, and while they've slowed down a bit recently, manage to come out fairly frequently. New weapons are added to the game at a pretty fast pace. There's usually at least one update per week, though the update doesn't always contain new additions.
The game isn't without issues, though. First of which is balance. The game is PVE so balance isn't AS high a requirement as it would be in PVP games, but the lack of balance is still there. Most weapons in the game can perform throughout the entire star chart, but theres very noticiable performance gaps that grow larger and more noticiable the longer you play.
Inventory Slots. Earlier I said that most of the microtransactions are super fair and only save you time. There is one exception to this. You start the game with a handful of slots for weapons and warframes. Each built weapon or warframe requires a slot. Since the game is all about gaining new warframes and weapons the starting ammount of slots, while they will not prevent you from playing as long and to as hard of difficulties as you want, will definitely hinder your enjoyment as you're forced to ditch your weapons pretty regularly. Slots arn't that expensive, and though I think they could give new players one or two slots more, they're still pretty fair considering. You can play with just the starter slots but slots are definitely the area you will feel you're forced to drop money on the most during your time with this game.
Bugs. The game is pretty buggy. Rarely unplayably so, but they're still not exactly rare. DE doesn't really seem to have any kind of large internal testing team, so whenever any new quests or new modes launch, you can expect to encounter a lot of bugs with them during the first two days of their implementation before DE manages to smooth them out some.
The game doesn't explain itself well. A lot of things you will need to look up on the wiki or ask other players about.
I would recommend Warframe if you're looking to just jump into a quick game at your leisure on occasion and don't neccesarely want something that costs much or is in depth. I would also recommend it if you don't mind playing a game with no real goal other than having fun while grinding out whatever looks cool or is new.  I wouldn't say that Warframe is for everybody, but I do think the majority of gamers can probably enjoy it for what it is.
