The only game I've played that remotely delivers on the promise to make you feel like a ninja.  No "hold a button while the game plays itself for you" BS here.  You want to pull off rad Hong Kong Blood Opera moves and chain double-jump knee slides radial sword attack wallrun bullet-time leaps?  Pull them off yourself, Tenbro.  Glory is earned through player skill.  Reminds me of the first F.E.A.R. and Mirror's Edge in that regard -- it gives the player the tools to succeed and it's up to the player to use them however he wants.
Also, one of the least-filthy free-to-play systems I've seen in a game so far (not quite up to Path of Exile standards, but what is?), with all accounts starting with cash-shop currency, cash shop items frequently given away through login rewards and numerous in-game events, and most functional cash-shop items can be crafted rather than bought with real-life money.  Yes, it can feel like a grind at times ("lol warfarm," right?), but the gameplay and atmosphere are so excellently executed that even after 600+ hours, I still have fun and it doesn't feel grindy to me, since every mission is an opportunity to take down foes and feel boss while doing it.
Aggressively updated, frequent and numerous in-game events, some of the most satisfying gameplay I've experienced in years.  Digital Extremes has been putting a smile on my face since 1999 and they continue to do so.
Warframe continues to be fully enjoyable even if you haven't paid any money for anything in-game and is consistently, objectively better than Destiny.

Your goals :

- collect gold to hire/level up heroes to kill faster

- collect heroes souls fighting randomly primal bosses in universe
- collect heroes souls doing ascension (Ascension reset universe that mean you loose gold & heroes. But you keep rubies, heroes souls, gilded heroes status.) or quick ascension (no universe reset)
- summon ancients to progress faster & deeper
- Heroes gain damages x 4 each 25 levels & x 10 each 1000 levels
- Get 1 relic / ascension after level 99 (and after doing 1 ascension at least before current universe) : relics give 1 or many bonuses like ancients and can bypass ancients caps value
You must choose build betwen :
- click CD damages need to clik on mobs to kill them (damage & critical)
- idle DPS damages auto grind (no need to click on mobs to kill them, no critical)
Idle build work offline too.
Randomly appear treasure chest with huge amount of gold and chance to gain 1 or 2 ruby. No need to buy rubies with real money. You can do if you want to support devs.
Despite his simplicity, Clickers Heroes is full strategic game based on maths. You can't progress without planning carefully your progression.
You start on universe 1. All universes are same but primal bosses who give HS as reward appear in random based on spawn rate %. You do run to universe 1. When you'll be stuck (very slow progression), you have to reset universe doing ascension. Ascension reset universe : you loose gold & heroes. But you keep your HS & rubies. You start universe+1 after ascension. The goal about ascension is to do run in universes to grind HS. You always keep your HS, rubies, ancients.

I'm a big fan of idle games, I "played" Cookie Clicker and other less well known incremental games like Derivative Clicker.
The hook that gets you into the game is the satisfaction of mindlessly spamming a button so you can save up for upgrades and do more and more DPS to kill tougher and tougher creatures. In actual fact, the fun in the game for me (as a fan of the genre) is in optimising the build order to reach the end game faster.
Looking at the maths involved to help decide what is the best thing to buy or save for at any given time from an efficiency perspective and whether or not you are wanting a build designed for pure idling or for more active clicking is where a lot of the fun comes for me. Watching the deepz grow is just a nice side effect of that!
It's a fundamentally pointless game, and I certainly won't be taking part in the micro transactions (I'd rather just pay a fiver for the game instead, to help the devs!), but for a few hours of clicking it's certainly fun and if you get into the end game mechanics of it all and the soft reset function that is seen in many of the more developed idling games, then it has a lot more depth than you'd initially think.

Started playing this game back in March? I can't honestly tell at this point. If you check, you'll see that I have played it literally every day since I started.
PROS:
1- NInjas in SPAAAAACE (Mostly a PvE game, btw)
2- Tons of customization
3- Updates regularly (for patches, and hotfixes) (PvP might as well be a second game because of the modes, and amount of fixes that get implemented there every week)
4- The Devs communicate regularly, and even have live streams that they announce in-game and on the website where they will discuss development, upcoming updates, and projects they are working on.
5- You can get your hands on virtually every item the game has to offer (except for 3 or 4 founders exclusive items)
6- Combat is fantastic. Excellent 3rd person shooter and hack and slash. Easily one of the best, thanks to the mobility your character has.
7- The QUESTS. Oh boy, there are few quests in the game, and you can honestly tell which ones are old, and which ones are new, but as soon as you get to do some of the quests, and start to discover the lore, you will get hooked.
8- The lore: I'm someone who really loves to have a backstory, and good lore for the world I'm playing in. The Devs deliver here. If you want to avoid it, you easily can. However, if you want to dive into it, there is a lot to be had.
9- Player-driven economy: You can make (or farm), and sell items (no, you don't need some super duper cash only stuff for this). It literally took me a couple weeks of play before I got my hands on some things to sell for in-game currency. Go to the trade chat, and you will have buyers, and sellers, for almost naything. From cosmetics, to rare weapons.
10- There is immense replayability value in this game.
11- Several day spanning events that have great prizes for all levels of involvement.
CONS:
1- Major updates aren't as frequent as we would like them to be (for the end game players at least. New players might feel like there are too many)
2- Big events, aren't too frequent.
3- RNG (Random Number Generation, in this case referring to how randomized many of the rewards can be). RNG is both the lifeblood of online games, and sometimes a players' worst enemy. Sometimes, there's nothing more frustrating than doing a mission 8 times to try and get a particular reward. (the upside to this, is that rare items do have value)
4- For end-game players, the game can get repetitive, since you've experienced virtually every mission many times already, and there's little to surprise you. So you need to get creative and create your own fun (like fashion shows, and duels... No, I'm not joking about either. FashionFrame is serious business, XD).
5- We need more Raids (8 player special missions that are very creative, and difficult). Right now there are only 3, so far, all 3 are really good, but we need more. I've memorized 2 of them like the back of my hand at this point.
I hope this review was helpful, and if people have questions/requests, feel free to PM me.

First, disregard the Metacritic rating, as it hasn't been updated since the game came out of closed beta, 4 years ago.
Warframe is, at it's core, a game about getting gear, levelling it to max level, then using it to acquire more gear. It's grindy, but the gameplay, the shooting and movement mechanics, are fun enough to make you keep coming back.
Digital Extremes are some of the most passionate developers in the industry. They update the game constantly, and host bi-weekly livestreams detailing what they are working on.
Finally, Warframe boasts the best F2P model I've ever seen. In-game currency can be easily farmed, the only items you need (inventory slots) are super cheap, and everything else is cosmetic or unneccesary. Some will say it's pay-to-win, because you can buy any gun or Warframe with real money. But if the point of the game is to farm for new items, what is gained by buying them?
Would certainly recommend trying out.

There is platinum (the real money currency) for skins and stuff... most important the weapon and warframe slots as you're limited on how many weapons and warframe you're able to store.
But you can sell ingame items for platinum quite well
, so you can grind stuff
to gather enough platinum for the skin you really want.
You have to like grinding though... if "grind" isn't your thing, you probably shouldn't be playing Warframe... though this same grind is giving you a reason to play it, a goal to reach for. I've personally reached a point were I'm only playing Warframe if there's new content to explore or new items to collect... so it helps that Warframe feels like a never ending beta ;)
P.S. don't be scared by my hours played... first of: I'm always optimizing and verifying my game files.. this takes some time. Second: I'm not one who reaches for the stars right at the beginning.. this means I've been idling at mastery rank 14 for the majority of my play time. And that's quite easy to achieve... You grind through enemies in the same levels over and over and over again.Get experience(here called affinity),loot and more weapons and warframes ('classes') to kill enemies with.How is it different from yet another Diablo-clone?
-Movement:You can do parkour,bullet-time jumps ala Max Payne,somersaults,slides,dropkicks and a lot of other stuff.Flying through the levels like a graceful panther/greased lightning/Damien Walters wannabe feels so...satisfying.And while it's not exactly hard to do,you'll need some practice to master the art of efficient running
-Weapons: There's the usual assault rifles,shotguns,pistols and grenadelaunchers.Then there's every kind of ninja weaponry,in fact,you can easily cosplay as a teenage mutant ninja turtle :) And then there's stuff like microwave gun(actual name I can't remember,but the point is,it 'fries' enemies from the inside),freeze gun,pistol-sized rocket launcher (sends everyone flying after a two-second charge),a few kinds of "organic" weaponry and more.The thing is-you can feel the difference even between different kinds of assault rifles,and there's a lot of them,and trying each gimmiki weapon out is much more fun,than finding a different kind of weapon in other MMO,which is only different in stats.
Oh,and did I mention that there's an entire arsenal of melee weapons available too?You can combine melee with shooting easily-quick melee attack can be done with a separate button,but more fancy stuff like combos,parries and deflecting bullets back at your enemies requires you to take melee weapon into both hands.
-Style:Just look up some videos on youtube-everything in this game is beatifully drawn and I'm not talking about number of polygons per model.The space in this game is gorgerous,planets are different and fascinating each in their own way,and everything looks distinct from everything else and stylish as hell.
-Setting:This is a dream come true for any person who liked the old anime and saturday morning cartoons from the 90's.The story has only a few traditional 'quests',and a LOT of missable and unique events.There's also a description deciphering ala Dark Soul (to a lesser extent-you can scan enemies and some objects and sometimes get an interesting piece of info out of it)
-Active development:DE constantly does something with the game-several game modes were completely changed over past 3 years,parkour was changed,upgrade system and world map ('star chart') changed several times.Maybe they don't always make good decisions,but you can tell that they are trying hard,and in a time,where bugged,unplayable,false-advertised messes slowly become the norm,the game that is constantly being worked on and runs smoothly on a config that was high end back in 2009-well,that is worthy of praise.
Through,to be perfectly honest,the game has quite a lot of noticeable bugs,some of them are serious,through not gamebreaking most of the time,a few can force you to start a mission over.Thankfully,those are less common than they were in 2014.
-It is a true free2play. There's a premium currency in the game,but you can get your hands on it relatively easy-just get some loot and sell it off -> PROFIT. Most of the time I used it to buy more weapon slots in the arsenal(4 more were enough) and some cosmetic items.
Yes it's a grind fest.But if you don't want everything RIGHT NAOW!!! then you can enjoy the game for 2-3 hours everyday and steadily progress through content and ranks anyway.
I played for 300 hours,most of that running with a group of friends or solo,not trying to speed-run missions or staying in one mission for over an hour.
-This game still has some place-holder content,like underdeveloped Player Versus Player system,or Raids (only two in the game at the moment),and there's no real endgame content-it is possible to have a few setups which will make ANY mission into a cakewalk,but you'll need to put 500+ hours in a game at the very least for that to happen.
Conclusion:If you want to rush to the end and get everything ASAP,you will,most likely, be dissapointed,as there's nothing at the end(YET,and that will change somewhere in the future).I reccomend you enjoy this game,it's mechanics,it's beatiful universe,it's stories,at a slower pace.Enjoy the ride-it's not the grandest of the lot,but more unique and fun than most.

Warframe has recently had an Update. The update is terrible- lackluster and short story, no new significant changes. But this review is more about the game in general than a specific sect of content.
Warframe is a third-person shooter with vital elements consisting of parkour, modular playstyles and  grinding- oh my the grinding. If you do not appreciate the grind you WILL NOT like this game as a lot of the enjoyment of warframe is derived from the hardwork put in to attain that character (Frame) or that gun.
A lot of people assume this game is pay to win (the assumption coming from the way it is marketed and the fact that it is f2p) and while it is not at all that, however has the potential to be, it is pay to win faster. Building weapons and warframes has an arbitrary wait time attatched with the option to spped up the process with premium currency, bought with real currency. Cosmetics and other non-essential items are also locked behind a pay-wall. While I find this incredibly frustrating, it keeps me coming back to the game to check if that item is complete, or if that one is. It is a problem shared amongst all f2p games that are under constant development- a man has to eat- however I believe DE (Digital Extremes) have handled premium currency excellently. You as a player who does not buy currency, reap the reward of other peoples purchases through trading items and premium currency in the trade chat. The economy is constantly stimulated by platinum and it allows people who are not able to buy things such as cosmetics, use their time to obtain items and trade for premium currency.
Combat in warframe is excellent. main weapons are your primary source of destrcutiona dn can be gained from many sources and are a vast variety- ranging from energy shotguns, to snipers, to saw-blade rifles to bows! Your Warframe will most likely be your second outlet of damage, or healing, or uselessness. Warframes work with an energy pool gained from energy orbs collected randomly after defeating enemies. These energy orbs allow you to use one of four abilities that could be used to instantly kill an enemy, slow them, heal yourself or hide in a puddle. the character variety in this game is incredible and is one of its most powerful features. there  is always a warframe that you will enjoy playing and there is always a warframe that is useful in certain situations. Your third outlet of damge is a melee weapon. Melee combat is fluid and enjoyable and deals a substantial amount of damage. The Melee weapons are great and fun to use. Your fourth outlet of damge is your secondry- something such as a pistol or kunai. Combat is succinct and crisp and feels empowering.
The story of warframe is interesting but suffers from Destiny Syndrome. The story is barely told in the actual game at all and to view the story, you have to retrun to your ship and read about it. While I personally don't mind this it may be jarring to players who are looking for story.
As a final point- a point that a portion of the warframe community will execute me for bringing up- This game is very similar to destiny (Warframe did come out before Destiny, I do realise that, but suck it up). having played both games for a generous amount of time (Destiny 565 Hours) I think I am qualified to make this comparison. Both games have similar styles of story telling, Similar 3 tiered weapon combat and combat in general, Multiple characters, modular abilites (of the base ability), constant updates and ismilar mission structure. So, If you enjoy Destiny, you will most likely enjoy Warframe and Vice- Versa.
Also, for those who say warframe is better than Destiny or any other game with paid DLC, If DE stopped receiving income from platinum purchases, I can assure you with all most 100% certainty, that the DLC would become paid and perhaps even a subscription fee or one time purchase would be implemented. If you cannot accept that you are reaping the rewards of other people's purchasing in platinum, then you are incredibly Naive.
In conclusion,
If you love the grind, you will absolutely fall for this game. Looking past its F2P nature and occassional glitches, it is a gem of a game and should defintely be given a shot at your earliest convenience.

Pros and Cons;
PROS:
Fun game in general owing to the fact it turns such a simple, childish subject into an enticing, addictive and complex game. With many dinosaurs to tame, fight, breed and ride, you'll never get bored of exploring the mysterious island of ARK.
Whether you want an intriqutely designed mansion and a T-Rex, or a shabby house next to a rock with no roof and seven hundred and sixty four dodos, Ark is easily enjoyable.
For another, the countless recipes and items to craft give you endless missions to complete and create. From starting with a pickaxe made of scraps of wilderness, to your own hard earned rifles and swords to futuristic high tech armour, the goals gradually increase in difficulty, reward and necessity.
Looking for a place to build a simple house and make some friends? Ark!
Looking to make a greenhouse and grow some flowers? Ark!
Looking for challenging fights and bosses? Ark!
Want to paint a Megalodon rainbow colours and write gay pride on its face? Ark!
CONS:
Ark is still in beta, hence the reason it contains many irritating bugs and glitches. Dinos also pick the worst time to pass out when you tranquilize them for taming reasons*coughdrowning*
The game sometimes breaks and forces you to delete your saves*. Some crafting recipes make no sense whatsoever, i.e. smelt hide to make oil. Yeah.
If you want to play with your friends and decide to host your own non-dedicated server, sometimes certain players just can't join. No reason at all, they just can't,
SUMMARY:
In short, this game is my best purchase on Steam. It's my favourite game and my friends probably strongly agree. Please, if you're thinking about this game, it's worth it. Take it from me, I have 182 hours of playtime.

Warframe is a game that takes many risks in its design descisions. Digital Extremes often introduces concepts in an attempt to re-invigorate the playerbase, sometimes going as far as to remake old systems. Whether that new feature is a hit or a flop is pretty much a coin toss, but when it does hit, I think most of its established community can say that it's a great success.
For the main gameplay loop, what you see is what you get. The movement system allows for very agile manuevers in a 3d space, though you might complain when the only path to your objective is through a narrow hallway, other tilesets later in the game allow for greater freedom.
The ultimate goal, as of now anyway, is to collect all of the gear. Since mods are the main source of power, every gear on which you put those mods stays relevant into the late-game. Though beware, inventory slots to keep this gear is locked behind paid currency.
I think this game is ideal for people who wish for more action out of their MMO experience.

Warframe has recently had an Update. The update is terrible- lackluster and short story, no new significant changes. But this review is more about the game in general than a specific sect of content.
Warframe is a third-person shooter with vital elements consisting of parkour, modular playstyles and  grinding- oh my the grinding. If you do not appreciate the grind you WILL NOT like this game as a lot of the enjoyment of warframe is derived from the hardwork put in to attain that character (Frame) or that gun.
A lot of people assume this game is pay to win (the assumption coming from the way it is marketed and the fact that it is f2p) and while it is not at all that, however has the potential to be, it is pay to win faster. Building weapons and warframes has an arbitrary wait time attatched with the option to spped up the process with premium currency, bought with real currency. Cosmetics and other non-essential items are also locked behind a pay-wall. While I find this incredibly frustrating, it keeps me coming back to the game to check if that item is complete, or if that one is. It is a problem shared amongst all f2p games that are under constant development- a man has to eat- however I believe DE (Digital Extremes) have handled premium currency excellently. You as a player who does not buy currency, reap the reward of other peoples purchases through trading items and premium currency in the trade chat. The economy is constantly stimulated by platinum and it allows people who are not able to buy things such as cosmetics, use their time to obtain items and trade for premium currency.
Combat in warframe is excellent. main weapons are your primary source of destrcutiona dn can be gained from many sources and are a vast variety- ranging from energy shotguns, to snipers, to saw-blade rifles to bows! Your Warframe will most likely be your second outlet of damage, or healing, or uselessness. Warframes work with an energy pool gained from energy orbs collected randomly after defeating enemies. These energy orbs allow you to use one of four abilities that could be used to instantly kill an enemy, slow them, heal yourself or hide in a puddle. the character variety in this game is incredible and is one of its most powerful features. there  is always a warframe that you will enjoy playing and there is always a warframe that is useful in certain situations. Your third outlet of damge is a melee weapon. Melee combat is fluid and enjoyable and deals a substantial amount of damage. The Melee weapons are great and fun to use. Your fourth outlet of damge is your secondry- something such as a pistol or kunai. Combat is succinct and crisp and feels empowering.
The story of warframe is interesting but suffers from Destiny Syndrome. The story is barely told in the actual game at all and to view the story, you have to retrun to your ship and read about it. While I personally don't mind this it may be jarring to players who are looking for story.
As a final point- a point that a portion of the warframe community will execute me for bringing up- This game is very similar to destiny (Warframe did come out before Destiny, I do realise that, but suck it up). having played both games for a generous amount of time (Destiny 565 Hours) I think I am qualified to make this comparison. Both games have similar styles of story telling, Similar 3 tiered weapon combat and combat in general, Multiple characters, modular abilites (of the base ability), constant updates and ismilar mission structure. So, If you enjoy Destiny, you will most likely enjoy Warframe and Vice- Versa.
Also, for those who say warframe is better than Destiny or any other game with paid DLC, If DE stopped receiving income from platinum purchases, I can assure you with all most 100% certainty, that the DLC would become paid and perhaps even a subscription fee or one time purchase would be implemented. If you cannot accept that you are reaping the rewards of other people's purchasing in platinum, then you are incredibly Naive.
In conclusion,
If you love the grind, you will absolutely fall for this game. Looking past its F2P nature and occassional glitches, it is a gem of a game and should defintely be given a shot at your earliest convenience.

The achievements are not reachable.
To reach zone 3000, I had to deal around 10^203 DPS.
To reach this number, I needed somewhere around 10^230 gold.
If, say, you need 10 seconds to beat a minion (which is what you need when you start struggling at a boss level and cannot go further without improving your weaponry) and just for that last level, you'll need 10^27 battles of 10 seconds. So, just between zone 2999 and zone 3000 (which is a boss battle), you'll need to spend 10^28 seconds.
Don't even try to do that, you'll be long dead and Earth too before that happens. The Big Bang happened 10^17 seconds ago. You'd need 100000000000 times the age of the universe just to cross that 2999 to 3000 zone line. Of course, it's not a precise calculus, I could be off by a few times or even a million (10^6), the thing is... it does not really matter with that order of magnitude. Oh and don't eat during that "time" and buy a few warehouses of mice too (more than what has been created so far).
So, how come so many people (including me) managed to reach zone 3000? No other choice but cheating. That's sad. If the goal was realistic, people wouldn't cheat. They would try hard, knowing it can be done. But if you know from the beginning the only way to beat the game is by cheating, it's as if the game asks you to cheat.
So, as it is now, I would not recommend it. If a game rewards people for trying hard and playing non-stop for like 3 years, it's already crazy to manage to get the accomplishments. And it's realistic. But gazillions of years ? Be serious.

The game regularly get updated each week, adds new content, such as weapons and cosmetics.
and every ~month new "classes".
I can understand that why there are people who think this game is just "too much grinding", while personally I find working towards getting it is half the fun.
On the side note: Most weapons have a level requirement you have to meet before you can even use them (Most weapons  (~80%) require less than 6 which can be obtained "fairly quickly" (~week), the highest is level requirement for a weapon is 13 ATM).
EVERYTHING* is obtainable without having to pay a cent.
While you can purchase it with "Platinum" the premium currency in the game (yes platinum is tradable with other players). You usually can to craft a weapon with resources and blueprints you find throughout missions.
This game is lots of fun with friends, you can group up together for missions. and even have your own clan and clan building.
The game however is bad at explaining stuff, most of the new players drop it due to lack of direction. I do recommend looking up a guide.
If you are still unsure whether to play the game. There is nothing stopping you from trying the game out since it is free to play.

Everything is grindable, and if you're looking to grab premium credit without paying, there's a market to sell some of the more valuable items you farmed for it.  Essentially, nothing is kept from you.
Warframe is great for Co-Oping with buds, dropping with random pugs, or just solo'ing content.
If you're looking to stealth a mission, it is there.  Want endless waves... they got that in spades.  Puzzles and hidden rooms, in randomly generated tileset maps... that's their M.O.
PvP needs some work, but it's not what you're here for yet, though, it isn't terrible, just very much a work in progress.

It's this a repetitive game? Not if you can manage to click in 1 billion different ways (with your nose maybe?), because OH GOD, this is the most REPETITIVE game ever made. I used to think Skyrim was overrated, I used to think mmorpgs are repetitive and I still do, but I fear no game in existence was or will ever be as repetitive and overrated as Clicker Heroes. I can already imagine what the developers had in mind when they conceived this thing: Hyei I gotz idia,muz combien clic countre frohm internetz adn rpg elemtes. Ermagerd bezt idia evah liets du tis. AND thus Clicker Heroes was born.
Jokes aside this game simply has no challenge to it. Each level starts by giving you a minimum number of bad guys to kill until you can select the next level and also you fight them one at a time. Those enemies don't attack you, they are just "damage sponges" that drop gold, and the way you deal damage to them is by clicking or by waiting (yes you heard that right). To understand how you can kill enemies by doing absolutely nothing (and bore yourself do death in the process) you need to know how the upgrade system works. You can use the gold that drops from those monsters to upgrade how much damage each click does but you can also upgrade the DPS (damage per second) which makes it so that enemies constantly take damage. Oh, and also those upgrades have some pictures with some typical rpg heroes slapped to them and some text to explain who they are but who actually cares? In the end they don't talk, they have no personality besides that sample text and that picture, which is pathetic if you even dare to label this game as a rpg which stands for role playing game. Oh and those "heroes" also have upgrades like more DPS and more gold dropped and skills with huge cooldowns that kill things faster and stuff.
Going back to enemies, the only thing that makes them different from each other is the animation that is shown when they are idle, when they are hit, when they die and the hp bar. That's it, they have no additional abilities since they can't attack. The bosses are just that but with more hp and a timer slapped in there so that you'll have to go back to the previous level and farm so you can beat the boss under that time limit so you can feel you accomplished something so that you can realize you didn't.
Some will hate me for the FACT that I only played 0.7 hrs when I wrote this review but in FACT (pun totally intended) I didn't really miss much since every level plays exactly the same but with different backgrounds, sounds and enemies that after a while start repeating again anyway. Oh and there's some sort of new game plus mode where you gain hero soul points or something and spend them on special upgrades but at this point I really don't care. Seriously, the game is already repetitive enough and guess what you get to repeat that repetitiveness again, GREAT.
Guess what guys? I found an alternative to this game. Here is what you have to do: get a cheap pocket calculator (preferably made in China), turn it on, press "+" then "1", then press "=" multiple times, it works with "-" too. Congratulations you just learned how to use one of the basic functions of pocket calculators. If the calculator breaks don't worry, it's just a flimsy Chinese device that costed virtually nothing, but your mouse isn't.
Look, I understand the idea of an upgrade based game that hooks people with rewards and the simple thought of making your character/s be better, but this thing takes it to the extreme of simplicity where you don't even need a functional brain to play it. OH and remember THOSE THINGS called MICROTRANSACTIONS, yeah, they are here too.
Playing this game feels like playing a really grindy mmorpg but with everything removed aside from the grinding and the more grinding, so essentially you're playing "Everything that's wrong with mmos: the game". On the other hand Clicker Heroes might be a test to see how much time passes until the majority of people become immune to the "upgrade fever" that made them believe games like this are good, or at least until their mouses break from so much clicking.

After a 2 month break and starting again after the last update, I think I should rewrite my review.
Pros:
* Amazing Movement System
* You can switch between Warframes(kinda like classes) between mission, currently 34 different are available, all have noticable differences.
* A few hundred different weapons to choose from
* A lot of mission/scene variety
* A promising story so far
* The core gameloop is very fun, even though its very grindy
* The communication between the devs and the community is really good(Devstreams).
Cons:
* The new player experience is terrible. There are a lot of systems the game never really explains, but the community is helpful and the wiki has a lot of information
* A few warframes are not really good/ at the same power level as the others
* A lot of weapons are♥♥♥♥♥♥and the devs are not going to directly balance them

. The scale of space stations, ships, even your own - they make you feel small and overwhelmed. Warframe is easy to get lost in, staring out into space from your ship, listening to radio chatter. It's really a breathe of fresh air.
The gameplay itself however is that great. All the negative reviews you're seeing bring up valid points about this game, but they are tilted too heavily.  Keep in perspective most of these people have hundreds or even THOUSANDS of hours in this game before leaving a bad review.  How bad can a game be if you've put that many hours into it...?

Overall, this game's positives outweigh the negatives.  The biggest complaint people have about PvP are alpha tribes, and they're right when they say they are cancer.  But they fail to recognize there's tens of thousands of unofficial servers, many with amazing quality of life tweaks to the game, where poor sportmanship is a rare occurrence.  That's also ignoring that there are both official and unofficial PvE-only servers.
The game does run poorly on even the beefiest of systems.  If you think a 1080 will run this at max settings - think again.  My 1080 handles the game quite well, but I've dialed back some settings I don't take much stock in.  The render distance starts becoming an issue as you get later in the game and start flying around.  You won't see enemy structures until you're practically right on top of them.  That's somewhat typical for massive map sandbox crafting games like these, though.  All said, the game looks great and is immersive.
It's a entertaining game to play solo, but even more fun surviving and building with your friends.  You can play coop on private sessions and servers, or you can play publicly with strangers.  Outside alpha tribes, interactions with online strangers is usually pleasant - most people are just trying to survive like you are.
You can easily put hundreds of hours on in this game without realizing it.  Does it have its issues?  Definitely.  Do they make this a bad game?  Not at all.  It easily pays for itself.

It seems to be a common trend on the forums that players have to band together and try to find solutions to the ever-present bugs, while hoping that they may eventually be addressed/fixed by wildcard.  I run the game with a i7 5820K, 980ti, and 16GB RAM. These specs aren't top of the line, but I would expect should be enough to at least RUN the game. Keeping that damn dog alive.

Run. Run away. Do NOT install this game. I repeat, DO NOT! You will be sucked into a world where all that matters is the clicking. You will click and click and click and click and click and click... Day in, day out. Say goodbye to your friends, family, school, enemies, everything.

The game technically has no end, because you can continue to ascend, resetting you back to the beginning, but with the added benefits of more hero souls. The game does "end" though at zone 4725, as the boss on that level has InfinK HP, preventing you from beating it. This information is true as of update 0.17c
Anyways, the game is quite charming in it of itself. It is based off of Playsaurus's game Cloudstone, which is also a very fun game. I highly recommend this, and Cloudstone, to everyone! :D

I love and hate this game. TLDR; The world is gorgeous. The dinos are pretty nifty. I've played PvE on both a private server and official server. Buggy AF. Grindy as hell, even for a craft-grind lover. Tamed dinos that require more time and attention than my real pets? Ugh. I am only playing it on the private server right now because of my friends or I'd have quit two weeks ago. I don't feel like the on-foot combat (against dinos) takes skill as much as luck and reacting in time to slash or shoot things. If you're on a big, bad dino it's all lucky timing.
---
On the private server and with a small tribe, I kind of feel like we have had it too easy, too fast. A couple of dino tames and what's to do or fear? Some of the installed mods make it faceroll-easy, skipping us up the tech tree in a hurry. The tribe is too small to take on the big bosses and even if we do...then what? We'll have way too much power when we already have quite a lot with mid-level tech. The only thing that might hold my interest here after a time is building, which is only interesting if we have a gazillion mods glommed on, which makes load times a pain.
----
Thinking maybe a official PvE server and alliances to fight big bosses could make things interesting, I decided to take a tour to see if we might try our hand there. On the official server, it can be hard to find a spot that isn't occupied. Even the friendly servers seem hopelessly cliquish. The challenge on those comes down to putting down any sort of base with all of the pillars spammed to prevent noobs from building on top of resources. Why don't the devs just make some areas no-build to make the uneccessary? Seems like a crazy oversight at this stage in development. Even so, I suspect you'd still get overzelous "preservationists" trying to protect every damned rock, plant, tree, etc. from having anyone build on or near it.
---
PvP? Hate it, but can only imagine how dreadful it has to be, since those at the top have to be so OP that nooobs have no chance. Not going to bother trying something I hate, just to hate the game more.
---
----
Even when I DO enjoy it (and I still do or I wouldn't have so many hours logged) it is buggy AF. I didn't have many issues when we started out, but a few updates in and it's all hard crashes that require a total PC reboot, which often means complete, punishing losses of stuff in a world where everything will eat you or freeze or drown you if you hard crash. F-that, so that's the main reason it gets a downvote for now. If I loose my stuff doing something stupid or taking on something I underestimated, fine. But because this game can't get get past major memory leaks? No. Bad.
I have yet to try single-player, but that might be where I land with this one eventually. As it is now though, I think they are making a HUGE mistake releasing it as it is now in Aug. unless they plan to do a lot of uppers and smooth out a lot of major issues. I want to love it because of the concept, but doubt it will improve enough to get a thumbs up again.

Spend a few hours grinding and building thatch structures,killing dinos,picking berries,throwing half the♥♥♥♥♥♥away, and losing progress to other players and dinos that are unavoidable and unfightable in your current state.
2 steps forward and 1 step back until around lvl 15-25, you are now capable of increasing your effeciency by means of tools and dinos, if you have not lost everything by now good job. "The hard part is over, now i get to do something different"
Spend 10's if not hundreds of hours grinding and building wood or stone structures, killing dinos through means of dinos, picking berries through means of dinos, and spending hours getting new dinos through the previous tasks,
It looks different and the numbers have changed but it feels the same, but hey, atleast it's different...right? But "The hard part is over, now i get to do something different"

What was once a great game is completely ruined by the poor choices of the game developers.
I was lucky enough to catch the tail-end when the game was at its best.
Ark was a fun survival game where you had to survive amongst dino's, who were fun to ride and tame. But the updates over the last few months have made his game a chore to play. I get it that survival games are supposed to be difficult or else it wouldn't be a survival game. But there is a difference between a fun survival game where danger may lurk around every corner and a survival game where overpowered danger does lurk around every corner.
That is what the developers have been doing. They have released a bunch of overpowered and often annoying dinosaurs into the game that are unbalanced compared to the other creatures.
Then there are the issues with stat nerfing. One of the most obvious examples of this are the flyer stats nerfing. Unless the server has special mods, any flying dino will be useless. The game developers are forcing people to stop using birds. Insteads they expect people to haul all kinds of resources with land dino's. Their reason for this is to make the world feel bigger, with real danger. The fastest way to get around is not by air, but by land dino & raft.
The real danger is not hiking to the top of the mountain to get metal with a Triceratops and going back to your base, the real danger is flying to a mountain top on a bird and hope the server doesn't crash while you're mid air.
Sometimes you have to put your dino on a boat because there is an ocean between islands. It used to be that sharks were the biggest danger in the water, the developers added some whale type thing that can attack any boat you have in the water. This whale thing is massivly overpowered, with too many health points and is capable of destroying any raft in just a few seconds.
And now they have begun with player character stat nerfing. One of the last updates included a speed nerf so you're not able to run away as fast like you're used to.
Another problem with this game is that the developers don't seem to bother with fixing old existing issues, like bugs ( getting stuck in the door after closing it ) or opimizing the game.
What they do instead is, they keep churning out as many new unbalanced dinosaurs as possible so the Let's Players on Youtube and Twitch have something new to show to their audience, which leads to more sales.
This game is ruined now. It's really ashame because when it was great, it was really awesome.
Do not buy this game.

What was once a great game is completely ruined by the poor choices of the game developers.
I was lucky enough to catch the tail-end when the game was at its best.
Ark was a fun survival game where you had to survive amongst dino's, who were fun to ride and tame. But the updates over the last few months have made his game a chore to play. I get it that survival games are supposed to be difficult or else it wouldn't be a survival game. But there is a difference between a fun survival game where danger may lurk around every corner and a survival game where overpowered danger does lurk around every corner.
That is what the developers have been doing. They have released a bunch of overpowered and often annoying dinosaurs into the game that are unbalanced compared to the other creatures.
Then there are the issues with stat nerfing. One of the most obvious examples of this are the flyer stats nerfing. Unless the server has special mods, any flying dino will be useless. The game developers are forcing people to stop using birds. Insteads they expect people to haul all kinds of resources with land dino's. Their reason for this is to make the world feel bigger, with real danger. The fastest way to get around is not by air, but by land dino & raft.
The real danger is not hiking to the top of the mountain to get metal with a Triceratops and going back to your base, the real danger is flying to a mountain top on a bird and hope the server doesn't crash while you're mid air.
Sometimes you have to put your dino on a boat because there is an ocean between islands. It used to be that sharks were the biggest danger in the water, the developers added some whale type thing that can attack any boat you have in the water. This whale thing is massivly overpowered, with too many health points and is capable of destroying any raft in just a few seconds.
And now they have begun with player character stat nerfing. One of the last updates included a speed nerf so you're not able to run away as fast like you're used to.
Another problem with this game is that the developers don't seem to bother with fixing old existing issues, like bugs ( getting stuck in the door after closing it ) or opimizing the game.
What they do instead is, they keep churning out as many new unbalanced dinosaurs as possible so the Let's Players on Youtube and Twitch have something new to show to their audience, which leads to more sales.
This game is ruined now. It's really ashame because when it was great, it was really awesome.
Do not buy this game.

I felt like writing a review for Warframe, so eh, ♥♥♥♥ it. Lets do a simple Pros - Neutral - Cons kinda system.
Pros:
+ Fun with Friends
+ Has a ton of content to see (different warframes, weapons, missions, etc)
+ The game is still being updated as of the time I'm making this review
+ The devs are fun, from my experiences with them anyways
+ Runs really well, considering I have a GTX 745, which is pretty bad, compared to today's standards
+ The game's frickin beautiful man. would you just LOOK AT THAT VIEW
Neutral:
? Prime Vault. Basically some items are "Vaulted" so you cant obtain them anymore, raising prices for people who do have them, but restricting them from being used. It's sort of like a collectors item at that point. It comes out again something though.
? The grindfest. This game is REALLY GRINDY. It's something you can spend hours and hours doing, but when all your effort is for nothing, then it's a bit annoying. If your efforts do pay off on the other hand, then it feels great
? Solo Missions. Some of the main tutorial stuff is solo missions so you have to do it on your own, which the game's so much more fun with friends, and like why would I ever want to do that.
Negative
- The Platinum Currency. Honestly, I dont see this as much of a problem but it is still very slightly P2Wish. KEEP IN MIND that PVP is a very small part of the game, and co-op is what you'll be spending most of your time is, so it doesn't matter that much.
- Crafting Times. You have to spend anywhere from 1 minute to 2 DAYS crafting items to use, like warframes, weapons, and the like.
- If you're a newcomer, I've heard that it's incredibly hard to understand the game very well if you dont have anybody to teach you some of the mechanics. The game is really complex and I highly reccomend you find someone who understands the game well (like me kekekek) if you want to get the most out of the game.
So yeah, I still really like this game, and I've voiced most of my thoughts up above. It's a great game, and I feel like I'm only midway through, with almost 200 hours in. I think that this game has a great community, great ideas, and great graphics. Besides, the game's free, so you dont really have much to lose here. Just go play it, dude. Come up with your own opinions about it!
TLDR: I like the game. It looks great. It's a bit confusing at first. It's a grindfest of a game. It's free. Try it.

Clicker Heroes... A game about clicking and clicking even more to be able to get upgrades so when you click your clicking is better, you do more damage with your clicks as you have to kill enemies and bosses to get to the next stage.
But you don't need to click to move through the levels, you can buy heroes for coins that are dropped in-game these heroes damages the enemies for you. Although by clicking it does go faster to kill the enemy. Once the heroes are bought you can start leveling the heroes and buy upgrades to them or save up coins to purchase a new hero. You can do all that by just using your mouse and then you just point and click. Really simple.
There isn't a huge amount of different monsters but there isn't a too small of an amount of monsters either so you won't see the same enemy over and over again after each other.
You can see your stats and achievements in-game, yes this game has achievements, it has around 60 achievements at the moment. A bunch of levels and heroes, an endless game!
I'd like to point out that it is not Pay 2 Win which is good! But obviously there is stuff to buy for real money but it's not necessary but It's probably easier to progress if you pay. But still not necessary.
Graphics are good.
Gameplay is easy. Not much to do other than clicking and watching.
It has sound effects and in-game music which isn't disturbing, you can easily turn it on or off if you'd like by clicking. But i did wish that they would allow you to lower the Audio in the options instead of either turning it completely off or on, but luckily I found out that you can go to your sound mixer thingy and turn it down a bit there if you'd like.
Options are simple like i said about the audio, wish they made it so you could change the volume in-game. They even have a options to make the monsters tiny, in case you lag it'll help reduce the lag for you :)
If you want to try it you definitely should, doesn't take long at all to install and if you ever get tired of clicking you can keep the game running in the background but make sure you've purchased a hero that can keep slaying monsters for you while you're letting someone massage your clicking finger. I use the index finger for clicking but who knows you may use your thumb.
Anyway good fun game just don't get stuck because it is pretty pointless. But it's a great way to kill time if you're maybe waiting for something or someone.

While graphically impressive, ARK falls into a common pitfall for Early Access games. Updates are focues on more content, more things, all the while building on a faulty foundation. The utilization of the Unreal Engine here is unstable. Crashes are not uncommon. Establishing multiplayer is a confusing mess. And, possibly most importantly, major pieces of the game are just poorly designed or not functional. Pathing has been a major issue since launch, with no solution ever implemented. Your dinosaur companions will constantly get stuck on trees and rocks, and battles between two flying dino will often devolve into a helical rise to the top of the game map.
The survival aspect to this game is also practically nonexistent. Survival is not difficult in this game, not even in the slightest. All of your required resources are easily replenished by a single resource, berries, which are light and can be carried in huge quantities without penalty. The main "challenge" to the survival is the grind to gather exhorberant amounts of resources for the late-game recepies.
When you combine all of this with the absolute audacity to release paid DLC for a game that's still in Early Access and unfinished, it's a strong "Don't Buy" from me.

I play Destiny on a daily basis. Or so I did until I came across this game. I love the grind, I love the Frames, I love the combat! Here are a few reasons why:
-Very Moba-esq combat system with abilities, and ultamite
-3rd Person Combat
-Detailed, Creative Characters
-Customization without having to spend a fortune on skins (unless you like, but more on that beneath)
-Skins that are decently cheap, 4-6 USD
Real quick I will take a break from my list and say that players can submit their own skins thata they make with the TennoGen external program and other 3rd party modeling and image software of their choosing. Back into the list!
-Active playerbase with multiplayer even in the campaign story
-Sub-linear activities, where you must complete some, not all of the missions to procede to the next planet
-Actually somewhat difficult PvE, where you do not feel forced into PvP for a challenge
-Constantly updating with active Devs
Now that I am done there, I have a few cons. Don't let this discourage you from trying the game though.
-Very... confusing, PvP.
-Very complex hotkeys, eg WASD+Ctrl->Space to spin through the air laterally
-Slightly glitchy hud and GUI. Things may appear very tiny, or face the wrong direction
So that tops it off. I hope this helps some of you decide if you are going to try the game or not. If so, please note that this game is not very well suited for casuals, and takes a good amount of time and effort. Also, if you, or your parents are not comfortable with blood or gore, check out youtube videos first to see how much there really is. It isn't Mortal Kombat X amounts, but your enemies do leave bloodstains on walls or floors depending on how you killed them.

Combat is boring and unreliable if it happens at all, building is frustrating as the previews are often incorrect, movement near animals is impeded by horrifyingly frustrating clipping issues (I've even been trapped inside one that ran at me too fast, on multiple different occasions), the ecosystem and AI in general is virtually nonexistent, making it easy to cheese but incredibly frustrating to work with. PVP is almost entirely attacking bases and killing their unconscious (offline) occupants or logging in one day to find your own base annihilated, and it doesn't really matter whether your base was a tiny hut or a huge expanse of metal buildings bristling with autoturrets.
Worst of all is the tedium. Whether you're gathering berries on the beach in your first few levels or maintaining a massive base with all kinds of animals and tech to help, most of the gameplay is boring and the devs realise too late and do too little to change it. Taming takes so long and such little input you can (and I have) done it while watching movies, even after they improved the default rates. Raising babies is even worse, and imprinting fully literally forces insomnia because you can't even get others to help. And neither of those things is remotely fun either, although the movies were nice. It reached the point for me when waking up to find we'd been wiped off the map was genuinely a relief. It's like the game relies on a player's unwillingness to give up on the time they've already sunk.
You can mod it into a tolerable survival game (don't be fooled by the name: character stats, high quality gear from blueprints, and high level tames mean it isn't much of one by default) and/or have some fun playing with friends on a private server (whether you want PvP or PvE), but I can't really recommend this now that release is coming up. I hoped it would be in a very different way by now.

With all the implementations that are regularly added to the game, its gonna be difficult for the devs to keep a game of the scope balanced and there is always the gamer who finds a cheese way to do things, which changes the way a game is played, ruining it for the casual gamer so to speak. The Devs are fantastic, they've been active every week with excellent additions and fixes ever since I bought the game. The graphics are good, providing you have a decent enough system to run them on high end, the music/sound effects are good but nothing spectacular, no complaints atleast. The crafting and dino taming were the strong suits for me, it is obscenely time consuming, which is a bit of a downside, but it makes the finish so worth it, and that is only on official servers. The shear variety, quality and value for money gets my thumbs up. When the devs have added the things they want, I've no doubt they will focus on ironing the balance/cheating out.
I wholeheartedly recommend.

This game is fun. It's crazy, it's exciting, it's terrifying. It's everything that you want from a survival game, plus there's dinosaurs. Who doesn't like dinosaurs?
Now, ARK does have some major issues. The community is toxic as hell, official servers are a nightmare and casual play can be a bit difficult if you play on official servers. Not to mention that the optimization isn't the best.
But.
There are ways to fix every issue you have with the game. That is how ARK has been designed. Customization is the core of this game. Everything can be changed, from taming times to how much damage you do. And if you don't like official servers, there's the unofficial servers you can play on.
Play this game if you like the unexpected, if you like riding crazy animals and feeling that sense of pride as you conquer the island. But whatever you do; do not ever play official servers. They are awful.
- Huge amounts of crazy and wonderful creatures with unique designs, colour palettes, abilities and behaviours.
- Massive area to play in
- Great to play with friends
- Unofficial servers and PvE are a godsend
- Customize it to the end of the Earth
- Constantly improving the game with new content and bug fixes
- Mod support. Anything you need/want can be found in a mod.
- Doesn't run great on lower end systems
- Sometimes AI can be wacky
- Can be hard to start out if you don't know what you're doing
- DLC in early access is a bit of a kick in the♥♥♥♥♥♥ Play Ragnarok, it has the stuff for free.
- PvP, Official servers and the Steam community is toxic as hell.
TLDR: 8/10
- Crap community, good fun game.

I felt like writing a review for Warframe, so eh, ♥♥♥♥ it. Lets do a simple Pros - Neutral - Cons kinda system.
Pros:
+ Fun with Friends
+ Has a ton of content to see (different warframes, weapons, missions, etc)
+ The game is still being updated as of the time I'm making this review
+ The devs are fun, from my experiences with them anyways
+ Runs really well, considering I have a GTX 745, which is pretty bad, compared to today's standards
+ The game's frickin beautiful man. would you just LOOK AT THAT VIEW
Neutral:
? Prime Vault. Basically some items are "Vaulted" so you cant obtain them anymore, raising prices for people who do have them, but restricting them from being used. It's sort of like a collectors item at that point. It comes out again something though.
? The grindfest. This game is REALLY GRINDY. It's something you can spend hours and hours doing, but when all your effort is for nothing, then it's a bit annoying. If your efforts do pay off on the other hand, then it feels great
? Solo Missions. Some of the main tutorial stuff is solo missions so you have to do it on your own, which the game's so much more fun with friends, and like why would I ever want to do that.
Negative
- The Platinum Currency. Honestly, I dont see this as much of a problem but it is still very slightly P2Wish. KEEP IN MIND that PVP is a very small part of the game, and co-op is what you'll be spending most of your time is, so it doesn't matter that much.
- Crafting Times. You have to spend anywhere from 1 minute to 2 DAYS crafting items to use, like warframes, weapons, and the like.
- If you're a newcomer, I've heard that it's incredibly hard to understand the game very well if you dont have anybody to teach you some of the mechanics. The game is really complex and I highly reccomend you find someone who understands the game well (like me kekekek) if you want to get the most out of the game.
So yeah, I still really like this game, and I've voiced most of my thoughts up above. It's a great game, and I feel like I'm only midway through, with almost 200 hours in. I think that this game has a great community, great ideas, and great graphics. Besides, the game's free, so you dont really have much to lose here. Just go play it, dude. Come up with your own opinions about it!
TLDR: I like the game. It looks great. It's a bit confusing at first. It's a grindfest of a game. It's free. Try it.

I can't believe the reviews for this are mixed. This became my favorite game after I got bored with everything else.
Cons:
-When you die, your body despawns after a measly 15 minutes, so you have to trek out and get it or you lose all your stuff. This is literally the only game I occasionally rage in, simple because you can lose everything very easily if you aren't careful.
-Base game is a 72GB download, and it does require a lot of ram to play. It makes sense given the content, but some people's computers probably can't afford to play this game.
-The Official servers are all crap. Just don't bother. They're all taken over by singular, autocratic tribes that ruin the experience completely, or at the very least make it impossible to do anything without becoming a part of said tribe. Also, they block off all beacons so you can't get higher quality item blueprints. It's kinda like corporatism/laissez-faire capitalism -- it just isn't fun.
Pros:
-Dinosaur army simulator
-Base building simulator
-BASE BUILDING ON TOP OF RIDEABLE DINOSAURS SIMULATOR
-A great mod selection to tailor the game to how you want to play it
-Enormous maps
-Great graphics
-Everything is paintable and customizable, but not in an overwhelming way
-Decent levelling progression
-You don't *have* to be part of a tribe to have fun and get far, but it does make things easier. In that way, the game encourages cooperation without forcing it.
-Grief protection is fairly easy once you get stone buildings.
-The communities on Unofficial servers are pretty good, from my experience.
Good game. I wholly recommend it to anyone who wants something immensely fun and out of the ordinary.

It is an online cooperative game, not really an MMO style kind of online game, but it has its own hub to connect players that gives the MMO feeling to the game. This game is superb. It has fluid animations and movements, great gunplay and sword play that are AAA standard.
In this game however, you will have to grind a lot of hours into it if you want to collect the different characters (called Warframes) and weapons to expand your various combinations of play styles. If you want to avoid grinding, you can always purchase the microtransactions which are really helpful in getting what you don't already have immediately. Also, even with microtransactions, the game is not unbalanced, all players do get to be on par as the weapons and Warframes do feel somewhat similar but still provide different styles of gameplay and that is a good thing.
There are no quests, but there are mission objectives or goals in different maps or game modes. There are some examples which include Survival and Defense. When you complete certain set objectives or reach certain goals in the modes, you will receive weapon parts and Warframe parts to create your own weapons and Warframe respectively. This is where the grinding comes into play.
Overall, I like the gameplay a lot. It feels like a AAA game and it mixes the elements of stealth and action and platforming into it. Yet another idle game approaches steam, and many ask one simple question- Why? Aren't these games that you just open in a browser window and play a more fun game overtop? Aren't these games that you shouldn't have to open in a big window and let all your friends see that you're basically playing the equivalent of willingly getting carpal tunnel?
All that debate about that aside, this is a fairly good idle game. I'm a fan of idle games as long as they do something different, and this one is a bit generic, but also does a few new things to spice the "genre" up. The game still has the overall mushy formula of all idle games (click, add a few more 0's to your number, wait more, switch out your 0's for a "K" or an "M") but it adds "dungeons" and "skills" and what would normally be buildings in other idle games are instead adventurers that you level up and unlock special passives for each one. These passives are usually the generic "100% bonus damage" upgrades, but some add critical hits to your mouse, special skills you can use, and probably more as I haven't gotten too far in this game yet.
There's also a cash shop, but it's ridiculously tacked on and you can just ignore it completely and pretend it doesn't exist. It's more of a "donation" button than anything, the bonuses it provides are basically just equivalent of foil trading cards that deal a tiny bit more damage so don't really bother or worry about it
So would I recommend this game? Well, it's the second best "idle" game i've ever played, leagues better than cookie clicker (but less memetic) so if you're into these kinds of things then go ahead and check it out.

The short: Warframe is a game that I would recommend to anyone who likes shooters so long as you follow two caveats: Do not take this game seriously and do not spend a dime on this game.
The long: I can honestly say that Warframe is the first free to play game that I can recommend and I’ve played dozens. It has come a long way since 2013 when I thought that the game was awful. Fast forward to 2016 and I decided to give the game another chance and it was love at second sight. The game is so much better than what I recall from 2013. The game is far more accessible and balanced than before. I guess three years will do that for you. In the game you play as a Tenno, which is basically a bad*** ninja assassin with guns and a blade. Killing the enemy in this game is incredibly satisfying. More so than most $60 AAA titles. In Warframe you level the equipment and not the character which leads me to my first gripe. What’s the point of having all these items in the game if the different between any two items of the same type is negligible? When I play a RPG I don’t really care about how my player looks as long as I’m effective. And in this game you can be more than effective with the default equipment as long as you level them up and have the right mods. Even if you are into tricking out your character and all of his or her gear you can do it all without ever spending a dime if you are willing to grind. A lot. For me personally grinding is not something that I am a fan of. Hence my second gripe, if the gear I use does not matter and I can grind to get any of the gear in the game for free and if I use new gear it resets to level 0 why would I spend any money on your game. The leveling system in this game in my opinion is silly and one of the biggest reasons why I’ll never spend a dime on this game. Even with that said I still highly recommend that you give Warframe a try. After all it's free so what do you have to lose? Download, install, create account, PROFIT!

I've definitely gotten a lot of playtime out of one title but by no means does it make Warframe a good game or one I can safely recommend in its current iteration. It's unfortunate that a game that is in a constant state of development and re-development has become both a shell of what it used to be while at the same time has never really reached it's full potential in the few years i've played.
So many things are broken at time of writing this review; frames, weapons, enemy armor/hp scaling, damage scaling... the list goes on... and yet so little time is devoted to fixing any of these... and I get it, its a F2P game w/ cash shop, they need to get revenue from somewhere, and what better way to do that, then to constantly release new frames and weapons almost bi-weekly. But we're at the point now where there is such a severe imbalance between the frames/weapons that in a game that seems to offer such endless selection and customization, the few outliers or outperforming frame/weapons, just completely overshadow so many others that shatters the illusion of choice and freedom to play how you want.
Why I can't recommend it:
- New player experience is confusing and convuluted. Very little explanation of mechanics or any kind of a clear path of where to go next.
- Archwing is still a nausea inducing mess, doesn't add much of anything to the core game. Archwing missions being forced into parts of main quests is a mistake and doesn't mesh well with the flow of the game.
- Junctions were designed to help guide new players through the star chart, but very little is explained on how to fulfill the requirments to access specific junctions or where to find certain nodes listed in said requirements.
- RNG wall AKA the moon treasure rooms (drift mods) contained within the Sedna Junction are pre-reqs for access to TWW. Accessing these rooms is not fun, the RNG element just makes it worse. I was looking forward to jumping back in when the War Within dropped. After several attempts to find the moon treasure rooms on Lua, I gave up and uninstalled.
TL;DR: If you have a life or take issue with games that require constant reference of game specific wikis and endless grind with no real endgame and trials that are joke, dont even bother.

Summary:
First person survival game with a builders touch mixed with dinosaurs.  There are 70 players per server for every type of map (Center, The Island "Vanilla", Scorched Earth) with the exception being 140 for PvP on untamable dino maps.  You start from level 1 and earn levels which give points to spend on "engrams" used to craft different technology (buildings, weapons, saddles, etc...) working your way towards jets packs and pulse rifles.
Pros
*Easy filter process for finding your characters and servers
*Easy to find which servers friends play on
*Option to customize load, decide how graphics heavy you want before the game starts
*Graphics are beautiful
*Can change your hairstyle with Scissors
*Can play single player off your computer without others if you're a hermit
*Very controller "gamepad" friendly
*Majority of the community are nice "non-troll" is perspective if you play PvP
*Developers listen to the population and care about how the "Majority" feel about the product
Cons
*constant lag spikes regardless of ping
*can't port characteres between PvP and PvE servers
*some official servers disable dino carry with flyers
*The trolls that exsist on PvE (very small population) like to poop pillars all over the map to prevent others from building

Summary:
First person survival game with a builders touch mixed with dinosaurs.  There are 70 players per server for every type of map (Center, The Island "Vanilla", Scorched Earth) with the exception being 140 for PvP on untamable dino maps.  You start from level 1 and earn levels which give points to spend on "engrams" used to craft different technology (buildings, weapons, saddles, etc...) working your way towards jets packs and pulse rifles.
Pros
*Easy filter process for finding your characters and servers
*Easy to find which servers friends play on
*Option to customize load, decide how graphics heavy you want before the game starts
*Graphics are beautiful
*Can change your hairstyle with Scissors
*Can play single player off your computer without others if you're a hermit
*Very controller "gamepad" friendly
*Majority of the community are nice "non-troll" is perspective if you play PvP
*Developers listen to the population and care about how the "Majority" feel about the product
Cons
*constant lag spikes regardless of ping
*can't port characteres between PvP and PvE servers
*some official servers disable dino carry with flyers
*The trolls that exsist on PvE (very small population) like to poop pillars all over the map to prevent others from building

Basically, this game is awesome.
I play Destiny on a daily basis. Or so I did until I came across this game. I love the grind, I love the Frames, I love the combat! Here are a few reasons why:
-Very Moba-esq combat system with abilities, and ultamite
-3rd Person Combat
-Detailed, Creative Characters
-Customization without having to spend a fortune on skins (unless you like, but more on that beneath)
-Skins that are decently cheap, 4-6 USD
Real quick I will take a break from my list and say that players can submit their own skins thata they make with the TennoGen external program and other 3rd party modeling and image software of their choosing. Back into the list!
-Active playerbase with multiplayer even in the campaign story
-Sub-linear activities, where you must complete some, not all of the missions to procede to the next planet
-Actually somewhat difficult PvE, where you do not feel forced into PvP for a challenge
-Constantly updating with active Devs
Now that I am done there, I have a few cons. Don't let this discourage you from trying the game though.
-Very... confusing, PvP.
-Very complex hotkeys, eg WASD+Ctrl->Space to spin through the air laterally
-Slightly glitchy hud and GUI. Things may appear very tiny, or face the wrong direction
So that tops it off. I hope this helps some of you decide if you are going to try the game or not. If so, please note that this game is not very well suited for casuals, and takes a good amount of time and effort. Also, if you, or your parents are not comfortable with blood or gore, check out youtube videos first to see how much there really is. It isn't Mortal Kombat X amounts, but your enemies do leave bloodstains on walls or floors depending on how you killed them.

Ark, a game I personally have a complex relationship with. Let me start with my time with the game.
I downloaded ark almost the day it came out, excited to play, I waited for the long download to complete, then waited a literal half-hour for the game I was joining to launch "single player, thought I would learn the ropes before jumping into multiplayer," then was greeted by a world of melted plastic graphics that refused to load, lag, music cutting in and out, and a Raptor. dead before the game let me hit my first tree. frustrated, I waited for the respawn menu to respond before selecting a diffrent spawn location, hello desktop and crash error message. wonderful. after about 10 trys, most ending before I had even spawned in, and a wasted sunday evening, I gave up.
--- 1 Year Later ---
it was now the next year, and I had heard that the game had been optimised so that it didnt require a God Among Computers to even attempt gameplay. Sitting down, I encountered much the same problems. now let me tell you why this is mind-blowing. I dont have a crap PC, an alien-ware desktop, a year or two old, good condition, not the best mind you, but still pretty good. I had to play this game, with ULTRA LOW-NO SOUND-SETTINGS! it was utterly unplayable, but I played anyway. now I have upgraded my gaming station and am playing at medium graphics, but the struggle to even start playing took cash, time, and hours of trouble-shooting. so problem one, you had better have a next-Gen PC or dont even bother trying to play.
now that I was in game I played single-player mostly, most of my game-play was getting started, as this game is the single-handed most brutal game I have ever played. with every little organism trying to kill you, from fish to bugs, and you having almost zero power, or health, this game creates an endless vortex of spawn, be killed, spawn in again, actually get basic tools, be mauled by a worm the size of your big toe, lose it all, rinse and repeat. so not quite a problem, but a heads up, hardcore survival game expirience required. "I later played multiplayer up to Lvl.45"
once you get your game running, and you have actually gotten a little wood house up and stuff, then you should be good to go, after that gameplay is excellent, here are my Pros and Cons of Gameplay "after Lvl.10ish."
Pros
---------
- AI for dinos is pretty good
- fast-paced progression
- good variety of dinos
- riding and using "leading a hunting pack of raptors, escorting a caravan of trikes carrying metal bars, etc," dinos is really satisfing.
- combat system is not unique, but still effective.
- great survival mechanics
- easy construction system
Cons
---------
- poorly optimised
- glitches "not game breaking, just annoying," are common
- community is iffy and unsupportive at best
- Game demands hours to stay ahead in multiplayer
- Getting griefed is common as progression is built around getting new "killable" dinos, your favorite dino buddies WILL be killed, and their flesh eaten by your rivals
- item count and diversity is unimpressive, might get better in the future.
in the end, ARK is one of the most unique and promising games out there, and it will without a doubt be a wonderful game when finished. my suggestion, if you have a decent PC, buy it, promise yourself you wont rage quit or get frustrated, play the game on single-player to get the ropes, then move to a PvE server, "or PvP if your one of THOSE guys," and give the game a fair chance, if you dont like it now, wait a year and come back, it will probably be a complete new game. Hope this helped!

I hate a scale based rating cause cons for me might be pros for other people. So here is everything I discovered in my 21 hours of play spread across two installs cause I had given up the first time I played this game months ago as well.
- Brilliant graphics, visuals and character design specially the Warframes
- Game is actually fun when you are getting used to it but becomes very repetitive in 20 or so hours. I cannot put in 1,000 hours to unlock everything with the amount of repetition present
- Stuff tied to a paywall: Almost nothing, only very few things are pay to get. BUT everything has a pay to get faster option and otherwise the grind or wait for most things is unbearable. This is understandable and acceptable considering its F2P. That does not make it a good thing
- Platinum costs are all over the place. On average I can see Platinum costs of 75. Even with the largest Platinum bundle(4,300) you can only buy ~57 items. Now that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. I got very close to buying Platinum till I did the math
- Game has been designed for co-op in mind. This is evident from the missions in the 3rd location Mercury
- In my 21 hours of play did not experience a friendly community or people willing to help out. New players are exiles in this game
- Boring to play solo so you better have friends who take a liking to this
- Rich lore filled world I want to learn about
- Rich lore filled world that I am never told anything about
- Bland supporting companions, the Lotus and Ordis
- Over 270 locations spread across a galaxy map with various planets and space stuff. Very overwhelming for new players
- HUGE maps with repeated layout
- Varied missions but eventually it comes down to getting to the objective as fast as possible(slide-bullet jump-slide) and moving on
- Way too many weapons and Warframes to pick
- Way too much stuff to unlock
- Good upgrades system for weapons and Warframes and again way too many mods to apply
- Crafting is a pain
- Challenging difficulty as the game progresses but♥♥♥♥♥♥poor AI doesn't help
- Decent leveling system and good progression
- Mastery progression is painful and worst locks story progress, meaning after a while switch to new guns/Warframes which would likely lead players into buying Platinum
-♥♥♥♥♥♥poor AI unless they swarm you
