The short: Warframe is a game that I would recommend to anyone who likes shooters so long as you follow two caveats: Do not take this game seriously and do not spend a dime on this game.
The long: I can honestly say that Warframe is the first free to play game that I can recommend and I’ve played dozens. It has come a long way since 2013 when I thought that the game was awful. Fast forward to 2016 and I decided to give the game another chance and it was love at second sight. The game is so much better than what I recall from 2013. The game is far more accessible and balanced than before. I guess three years will do that for you. In the game you play as a Tenno, which is basically a bad*** ninja assassin with guns and a blade. Killing the enemy in this game is incredibly satisfying. More so than most $60 AAA titles. In Warframe you level the equipment and not the character which leads me to my first gripe. What’s the point of having all these items in the game if the different between any two items of the same type is negligible? When I play a RPG I don’t really care about how my player looks as long as I’m effective. And in this game you can be more than effective with the default equipment as long as you level them up and have the right mods. Even if you are into tricking out your character and all of his or her gear you can do it all without ever spending a dime if you are willing to grind. A lot. For me personally grinding is not something that I am a fan of. Hence my second gripe, if the gear I use does not matter and I can grind to get any of the gear in the game for free and if I use new gear it resets to level 0 why would I spend any money on your game. The leveling system in this game in my opinion is silly and one of the biggest reasons why I’ll never spend a dime on this game. Even with that said I still highly recommend that you give Warframe a try. After all it's free so what do you have to lose? Download, install, create account, PROFIT!

This game tricks you into a dark spiral of addiction.  It is the leveling up and upgrading process in its crudest form.
The satisfaction we derive from 'upgrading' and 'leveling up' has a power over us, and Clicker Heroes is a fantastic exhibit of that - it's a great insight into what makes games addicting and compelling, what keeps us playing.  It's like a stripped down explication of our brain's reward system; it's a video game version of straight dopamine.

With the release of the latest DLC, ARK Ragnarok, I have these things to say about the game as of 6/20/2017, this may be updated in the future.
GAMEPLAY:
This is a game where you get stranded on an island with varying climates, dinosaurs, and just about every other thing that can kill you. If you punch a tree in just the wrong way, you will die. If you stay in the water for just over the amount of time, you will die. If you even THINK ABOUT ATTACKING THAT SEEMINGLY DOCILE TURTLE, you will be in a special hell. This game is brutal, and it will not forgive you if you mess up even the slightest bit. However, if you play your cards right, you can kill just about anything that isn't yourself. The gather-crafting system is what you'd expect, you build tools to gather resources to get new things. Only thing is: you have to "learn" how to make those fancy tools before you can actually make 'em. There's no getting tranq darts from day 1, you have to work for it. Scattered across the island are fancy items and easter eggs that can give you dozens of levels of experience (I found a dossier by chance and leveled up 14 times on The Island). With the recent expansions, new items and tactics have been added. For example: primitive plus adds a whole new spectrum to how you play the game, and Scorched Earth and Ragnarok unleash a whole new set of buildings and weapons for the player to use, along with new beasts (some not dinosaurs). HOWEVER, there is one shining feature that can degrade all of this, and I feel it is the most imporant part of the game.
PERFORMANCE:
This game is infamous for being laggy at the worst of times, and I have experienced many performance drops in my time playing ARK. From lags on The Island, to crashes on The Center, and mother-humping LOBBY_JACKSON ON RAGNAROK. I feel as though with the price it hasm the developers should be focusing on optimizing their game before they decide to expand further on it.
Right now, if you have a good computer and money to waste, go ahead and buy the game.
If you do NOT Have a good rig, and you do not feel like spending more than $50 bucks on a game that is not optimized, I'd suggest something else.
For me, it's sadly a no.

Quick statement: Is Warframe a good F2P sci-fi shooter? Yep. Is it "10/10 play this and only this" material? No. Is it "solid game that you should enjoy playing often" material? Yep.
DO PLAY IF
-you like sci-fi shooters
-you like stylish moves
-you like playing dress-up-my-mass-murderer
-you like fancy weapons (ranging from hi-tech machine guns to low-tech-but-are-made-high-tech weapons like bows and swords)
-you like using those fancy weapons
-you want to enter a world with some pretty vague-in-the-interesting-Dark-Souls-kind-of-way lore
DO NOT PLAY IF
-you are easily discouraged by butt-hurt rants of how this game is going down the drain and how the devs don't listen to us (in spite of the regular streams devs host, the recently successful TennoCon, and how the game has evolved so much compared to when it was first given that Metacritic rating)
-you are too impatient to wait a bit even after farming to get your stuff
-you want realism (no way in hell are you finding it here lol)
-you don't like having to either pay some cash or farm more to get the currency used to rush the farm, get slightly better, but much cooler looking versions of gear, or play dress-up

First i would like to say that Warframe is a game that was founded in 2013 and has gained a massive community due to it being free. Along with it being free the game has great graphics and game mechanics. Yes it is very grindy and for some who work full-time or even part-time for that matter it may be hard for you to progress into the game, as it requires alot of time and devotion due to it being hard to level and the delay
of when you want to build something.
I would recommend for people who have the time to sink into a game that is as grindy as Warframe, due to the farming system it requires ALOT of time to be able to get anywhere in the game.
Apart from that it is a really enjoyable game, and for the casual player who doesnt want to take massive pocket hits its a great game and you get a lot of content for free. People may argue that its pay to win, but you can have the same or even better items than someone who purchased in-game currency
but it may require more game time to aquire items instead of purchasing them with in-game currency. But, you, the player who hasnt spent a dime on Warframe can still gain this currency as well, as you can farm parts which you can then sell to people who want to purchase those parts, each part has a different price due to 'Rareness' and demand.
The graphics in this game also are great, very attractive game visually even on Low settings. The animations also compliment the graphics and overall the game looks and plays very well. Even on a very low end system you can achieve sufficent frame rates in order to play the game.
Overall i would give the game an 8/10 and it has certainly earned it as i personally have had a blast on the game and will continue to.

The longer version... Warframe is a great game for those that like MMO RPG elements. It works kind of like Guild Wars in the sense that every time you adventure it is instanced so it is not kill stealers all over the place. Would sound like a lonely experience right? Some of the low points that fall in line with pretty much all MMOs is there is a lot of grinding and farming and then once you are done farming for something it can take hours / days to get that crafted together (like a warframe without using platinum -- which isn't all that hard to get in the player market) takes about 3 days to make. I know i know that sounds insanely long, you can craft unlimited things at a time so after some warm up you will have some many things completly crafted waiting for you to pull out that you don't need to worry.

I personally don't like all the patches but that is because they took frames I really liked and balanced them -- but let's face it the game is a living creature and balance patches are bound to roll out to keep content fresh. And that is exactly what they are doing they are adding new things and taking the old things and trying to balance them all together.
There are also people who say there are no choices in weapons and frames for min/max which mathmatically i guess is correct there will always be that one item that is better than other choices -- but you don't 10000% need to do it that way to have fun or be successful at the game. I find the game to be diverse enough for my liking and if I do get tired of playing it then go on a break for a bit but I always some how seem to come back.

If you enjoy the survival adventure genre, here's my shortlist in no particular order:
Minecraft, Subnautica, We Happy Few, The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and THIS game - Ark: Survival Evolved!
Ark: Survival Evolved takes the enchanting open ended experience of the genre as made popular by Minecraft and combines it with the most brutal action you would expect from franchises like Monster Hunter.
Playing the game will have you scrapping for resources starting from stone age and unlocking engrams that will gradually advance your technology to present day much like you would expect to be doing in an epoch based real time strategy game (eg Age of Empires, Empire Earth, etc.).  The interesting thing about Ark is that death is not the end but rather a learning experience where you lose all your inventory but retain any and all knowledge unlocked from engrams for that given character.  The local wildlife isn't the only thing you will need to survive, but (potentially) other players as well.
Whether you're looking to play Ark alone or with others, this is arguably one of the best survival adventure games you can experience.

If you enjoy the survival adventure genre, here's my shortlist in no particular order:
Minecraft, Subnautica, We Happy Few, The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and THIS game - Ark: Survival Evolved!
Ark: Survival Evolved takes the enchanting open ended experience of the genre as made popular by Minecraft and combines it with the most brutal action you would expect from franchises like Monster Hunter.
Playing the game will have you scrapping for resources starting from stone age and unlocking engrams that will gradually advance your technology to present day much like you would expect to be doing in an epoch based real time strategy game (eg Age of Empires, Empire Earth, etc.).  The interesting thing about Ark is that death is not the end but rather a learning experience where you lose all your inventory but retain any and all knowledge unlocked from engrams for that given character.  The local wildlife isn't the only thing you will need to survive, but (potentially) other players as well.
Whether you're looking to play Ark alone or with others, this is arguably one of the best survival adventure games you can experience.

I've been playing since closed beta (right after U6) and I've seen how great DE could be at what they do, that is before they got aquired by their current chicken overlords. As a result the game has been consistently improved upon up to about U11~12, with minor bumps afterwards. It all went well until U15 hit (archwing), it wasn't that bad at the time, but that was the turning point when things started going downhill.
What used to be simple weapon skins, are now completely separate weapons (Syndicate weapons, Wrath/Vandal weps), cause it's easier to slap on some fancy red lines on a skin that has been greyscaled than to actually design a weapon. Hell the only  syndicate weapons that arent simple reskins are the synoid weapons and even they are soley assembled from avocado quarters.
Pretty much most warframes have similar first and last ability, first being a one target damage and he last being some sort of AoE damage. There are some frames that had one or two new abilities, with the rest being either useless or rehashes of the singletarget/aoe damage. It's ironic that one of their best designed warframes is the Loki as he has no damage dealing abilities (making his level scaling almost perfect), leaving him untouched by all the nerfs that happened to those same lazy damage dealing abilities.
Inaros is the latest embarrasment, essentially a frame on which you max out HP and armor and not bother using the abilities as they are largely useless (either pathetic damage or short CC) and with almost 5300 HP and 70% dmg reduction, there aren't many reasons to waste your time by kicking sand into your enemies eyes.
Map design, oh man, don't even get me started on that one.
Initially their design was well done, with varrying rooms and smart ways of asset reuse, as a result keeping the game filesize down to less than 2Gb, which is a nice bonus. Though I wouldn't mind the big filesize if someone wasn't reusing maps designed for a completely different game mode and then blame the players for abusing it.
I am talking about Viver as that was the last time I tried to give them any input on map design basics. If half of all of your warframes have a bigass AoE damage skill and you want to create a gamemode with 4 capture points, don't use the tiny map designed for guaring one point. Guess what is going to happen if you do that? Players are gonna sit in the middle and nuke everything. The result? DE started nerfing frames left and right, reworking the game mode so the neutral points revert to enemy control (Like that actually worked, *cough* Draco *cough*). All because they tried to reuse a map that was designed for Defense mode when it first came out.
To be honest that entire incident and a couple of similar ones can be blamed on the corrupted mods. These mods were and are blatantly game breaking, especially when paired up with their not-on-steroids counterparts. Such powerful mods in any game would be devastating, in warframe they were less severe as WF is primarily a co-op game so the players were rarely on the recieveing end of those mods.
Imagine if something like that was done in CoD/CS:GO/BF or any other competitive PvP game. Ofcourse some of you remember the initial release of R8 in CS:GO, and that isn't even close to how balance disrupting the corrupted mods are in warframe.
So what would be a good solution? Simple, the current idea to rebalance everything separately for PvP is the best one they had in years (and Im not kidding about the "years" part). Rebalance everything for PvP in and then in one big update, slow down enemy power scaling with levels and apply the PvP balancing to PvE. The only problem is, that makes too much sense for DE to implement, so I wouldn't keep my hopes up for it.
The Hit and Run content updates in other words, release an update, add new mods to some new gimmick and then completely forget about it. That's how it started with natural talent mod that used to drop only in interception, nightmare mods, corrputed mods, the moon vault acrobatics BS mods, the void trader mods and I heard theres even more garbage in the latest update (U19), didn't bother updating in all honesty. All of those "gimmicks" got one update that added extra content or two if they are extra lucky (Prime disappointment anyone?). Instead of spreading out new content across all gimmicky gamemodes to keep people playing them, they shove everything into one new flashy thing and forget about it by the time for the next update. Sorties were a good idea as they reused the event exclusive weapons to get the players interested and as usual, they completely neglected adding any new content to keep the interest up.
I could go on like this for the entire night, but I have other stuff to do (like finding a new game to play), but I'll wrap it up with one last point.
The grind. I swear if Warframe was a coffee grinder, it would be able to grind gravel to the finest dust, the coffee would get vaporized. Seriously, it became a joke in my clan about DE reducing the grind, cause it only got worse. The problem is that whenever they wanted to release new content but they wanted to control how fast the players obtained it, they would add a new resource, nav coordinates, research resources and when that didnt work, they added the ARGON. EFFIN. CRYSTALS. ITS NOT ENOUGH YOU BAR EVERTHING BEHIND OBNOXIOUS WAIT TIMERS BUT NOW THE ONE RESOURCE YOU HAVE TO GRIND FOR EVERY PIECE OF NEW CONTENT DISAPEARS AFTER 12 HOURS? Oh and that didn't quite work, so they made some of the existing resources scarce (Neural Sensors for example).
Funny thing is, they actually found the solution for excessive resource acumulation, but they probably have no idea they did. The Powerup pads. Yes, before those most of the WF players I knew then had hilarious amounts of nanospores and other common resources, numbering in dozens of millions. After the update we actually started farming those.
And the worst part is? If it goes on like this, they will kill the game. I tried getting a bunch of my friends into the game, buying them catalysts, reactors, getting them mandatory mods. Guess what happened, most of them managed to start playing after getting lectures about the clusterF the game is. They all gave up after reaching MR4~6 (so far 7 people). So I gave it a try, made an alt account and hoooly carp, they werent kidding, the grind scaled up massively,  getting into the game without any external help is a great feat of patience and willpower, because if I considered starting to play warframe now, I wouldn't even install it. Seriously, nerfing the credits payout? The one thing new players need and veterans don't give a carp about? It used to be the fun kind of a grind, now it's just the normal tedious kind of grind.
TL:DR If you are timetraveling to 2014, do give it a try, its pretty good. If you don't have a time machine and you are stuck in the 2016 with the rest of us, don't bother. Shaving your behind with a chese grate is less grindy.

I have the same problems with this game that I do with every MMO. It's grindy as hell with some elements of pay to win, which is unfortunate because it would have been a great game. The gameplay is actually fun, the art style is neat, and the story and universe are interesting; but it's all spaced out over so much grinding. Honestly, it might not even be that bad if it weren't for the moving goalpost. Every now and then they add more endgame content, making old top teir equipment gradually less useful. This would be an amazing game if it were restructured to have less grinding and more content.
As someone who takes the phrase,"Free to Play," very seriously, I am appalled at the limited inventory space for equipment. This game requires you to level up weapons and warframes to increase your overall rank, so having such a limited inventory for those things is ridiculous. This is probably the most unforgivable way they squeeze money out of the player base, because you can buy more inventory space with platinum, the ingame premium currency.
As a side note, the separation between PvE upgrades and PvP upgrades makes it difficult to go from one to the other. By the time I quit, I was close to catching up to the endgame in PvE, but I was ridiculously under powered in PvP. A good PvP game is more skill based than upgrade based, so I wouldn't recommend trying to get into this one. There's also no real rewards for playing PvP from what I could see.
Final thing, if you're going to play this game, get the Excalibur warframe as your starter. It's overpowered and you can't get it again until much later in the game. Also, join a large clan. Some of the best weapons can only be unlocked through the clans.

Read this if you haven't played Ark before and would like an honest review.
This game, at it's core, is one of the best games I have ever played on both console and PC.  The reason I started playing on PC was because of this game.   However, there are a few things you should know before purchasing it if you're on the fence.
#1.  Most of the recent reviews are negative due to fairly recent updates in the game which basically allow you to transfer your high level dinos to other PVP servers.  This allows alpha tribes to come into an official PVP server with much higher level dinos than are available in the wild and basically take over the server.  Although this is unfair in my opinion as well to a beginner, it looks like it's going to remain a feature in this game.  The good news is, there are other options in the game which brings me to point #2.
#2.  There are a few ways to play the game and really enjoy it.
A.  Official PVE servers are a great way to experience the game if you just enjoy a good crafting/building/exploring game with dinosaurs without the fear of being raided or killed by other players.
B.  Most unofficial servers are a good way to enjoy PVP if you want some action.  You will most likely see increased rates and some mods on these servers which make the game a little less grindy.  Just make sure to do some research before joining the server.  A good bit of them will have info in the title of the server or an actual website describing rules or features of that server.
C.  Rent your own server.  Me and a few friends have done this multiple times.  If you split the cost of the server between 2 or more people, it's an easily affordable alternative for the convience of basically having the island to yourself if you choose to.  I don't recommend this option until you have played the game a while (50+ hours or so) and get familiar with the game and community on other servers so that you know what you like and don't like.  Also keep in mind that whoever will run this server should be somewhat knowledgeable in how to update the server as well as install and run mods if you decide to have them.
#3.  This game requires a fairly decent PC to play it.  No you don't have to have top of the line parts but older PC's with older graphic cards will struggle and the game won't be that pretty and won't run well.  Do some research on Google or even YouTube to see what is needed to run the game smoothly before purchasing to avoid the frustration of downloading the game just to find out your PC can't handle it.
#4.  The last thing you should know before getting this game is this:  Although there are a good bit of negative reviews, especially recently, take a look at how many hours these people have in the game that are giving these reviews.  Most people have north of 500 hours in the game.  I myself have almost 800. Now think about that... can you name any game you've ever played for 500+ hours??  Regardless of how you play this game, there is a ton of content and hours of fun (especially with friends) to be had once you figure out what type of server you enjoy playing on.
Again, this review is mostly for people on the fence about buying the game.  I have played this game on and off since it released.  I bought it for PC and Xbox as well.  I have never been in an alpha tribe or anything close to it because I was never interested in that. That being said, there were weekends that I put in 12 or more hours per day because I didn't want to stop playing.  I quit playing this game and uninstalled it a few months ago due to lack of space on my computer (which by the way, this game takes A LOT of space) but I have recently re-installed it due to building a new PC and am excited to play again.  I have searched and searched steam for a building/crafting game to fill my itch since I uninstalled it and I just couldn't find anything that holds a candle to Ark.
Finally, know that this game is not perfect and you will die a lot whether it's bugs or glitches in its unfinished state or dinos or other people.  However, the fun I've had playing this game always out weighs those bad moments.  I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys building/crafting/exploring games in a heartbeat.

Read this if you haven't played Ark before and would like an honest review.
This game, at it's core, is one of the best games I have ever played on both console and PC.  The reason I started playing on PC was because of this game.   However, there are a few things you should know before purchasing it if you're on the fence.
#1.  Most of the recent reviews are negative due to fairly recent updates in the game which basically allow you to transfer your high level dinos to other PVP servers.  This allows alpha tribes to come into an official PVP server with much higher level dinos than are available in the wild and basically take over the server.  Although this is unfair in my opinion as well to a beginner, it looks like it's going to remain a feature in this game.  The good news is, there are other options in the game which brings me to point #2.
#2.  There are a few ways to play the game and really enjoy it.
A.  Official PVE servers are a great way to experience the game if you just enjoy a good crafting/building/exploring game with dinosaurs without the fear of being raided or killed by other players.
B.  Most unofficial servers are a good way to enjoy PVP if you want some action.  You will most likely see increased rates and some mods on these servers which make the game a little less grindy.  Just make sure to do some research before joining the server.  A good bit of them will have info in the title of the server or an actual website describing rules or features of that server.
C.  Rent your own server.  Me and a few friends have done this multiple times.  If you split the cost of the server between 2 or more people, it's an easily affordable alternative for the convience of basically having the island to yourself if you choose to.  I don't recommend this option until you have played the game a while (50+ hours or so) and get familiar with the game and community on other servers so that you know what you like and don't like.  Also keep in mind that whoever will run this server should be somewhat knowledgeable in how to update the server as well as install and run mods if you decide to have them.
#3.  This game requires a fairly decent PC to play it.  No you don't have to have top of the line parts but older PC's with older graphic cards will struggle and the game won't be that pretty and won't run well.  Do some research on Google or even YouTube to see what is needed to run the game smoothly before purchasing to avoid the frustration of downloading the game just to find out your PC can't handle it.
#4.  The last thing you should know before getting this game is this:  Although there are a good bit of negative reviews, especially recently, take a look at how many hours these people have in the game that are giving these reviews.  Most people have north of 500 hours in the game.  I myself have almost 800. Now think about that... can you name any game you've ever played for 500+ hours??  Regardless of how you play this game, there is a ton of content and hours of fun (especially with friends) to be had once you figure out what type of server you enjoy playing on.
Again, this review is mostly for people on the fence about buying the game.  I have played this game on and off since it released.  I bought it for PC and Xbox as well.  I have never been in an alpha tribe or anything close to it because I was never interested in that. That being said, there were weekends that I put in 12 or more hours per day because I didn't want to stop playing.  I quit playing this game and uninstalled it a few months ago due to lack of space on my computer (which by the way, this game takes A LOT of space) but I have recently re-installed it due to building a new PC and am excited to play again.  I have searched and searched steam for a building/crafting game to fill my itch since I uninstalled it and I just couldn't find anything that holds a candle to Ark.
Finally, know that this game is not perfect and you will die a lot whether it's bugs or glitches in its unfinished state or dinos or other people.  However, the fun I've had playing this game always out weighs those bad moments.  I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys building/crafting/exploring games in a heartbeat.

This game is sadness overall . Not for you , rather for itself . You've probably heard by others that it is a grindfest . Well they are right , but if you think this is the grind that other games have ? OOh no . In other games when you get something after hours of grind you can enjoy it . Here if you want a simple weapon you have to grind for the relics , then grind for the parts , then grind for plat if you want to rush it or wait for the needed time if you decide to craft it normally . You think it is done ? No no . Then you need to grind for mods , then grind for formas , then grind for the rank up since putting a forma on a weapon takes its rank from 30 ( max ) to 0 . Also given that most builds require something like 3-5 formas , have fun doing that . By the time you are done you have most likely lost interest to the thing . Oh , and that's only 1 of the maaaany stuff your character can equip . ''That's diversity'' . Nope , because in certain missions you will instantly equip certain gear . And let's say you have grinded for you frame , primary , secondary , melee , companion and school ( school is like a skill set you choose via the mission progression ) . Ha ! Even more grind because schools require focus ( an xp type of currency ) to unlock these skills . What do you do now ? The game lacks any kind of free roam for you to chill out and see where this grind has gone . Instead you are always in a mission . And let me tell you , a boring one . Then it hits you . You can stay in this game for hours upon hours and the only reason for you to get stronger is to grind more efficiently . It's like a grind to grind so that you can grind better for the grinds to come . Go back and read this , play the game and check it out . You will see what i mean . And it's a lost chance because you can see that the dev team is hidding behind the excuse ''it's a free to play'' . People say the levels are randomly generated so you never do the same thing . Don't you get me started . You go to Earth and see a mission named Everest . Now here is where the devs could go crazy . Destroyed civiliazations , jumping over mountain tops and enjoying a good mission . What do you find ? Oh yeah , a tropical forest . And one that you have played around 1k times. Graphics ? Maxed out doesn't impress anyone especially in a mission where you see the backgrounds . Why ? ''It's a free 2 play'' . Missions.....Oh boy . Here you will see how low the bar was set . The game is so terrible in missions that when you see something actually good , you think it's the best story ever . ( second dream quest ) . I saw some lore videos on youtube , and let me tell you , some parts are really cool ! Buuut , why put them ingame when we can just give more Prime access to people for money ? Remember that get-stronger = grind better ? . Buut again . ''It's a free 2 play'' . Also bugs will accompany you all the time , some even making you restart a mission it took you over 20 minutes . Amazing . This game is ridiculously not worth it because everything was made for you to say ''i will play some more'' . That translates into more hours , and more hours translates into you giving money to the devs . And people will say it's a non pay-2-win type of game .Partially true, you can GRIND stuff that you will trade for platinum ( real money currency ) .Buuut for all this grind to end you will try to get boosters which cost plat, syandanas and other customisation items for your frame and weps that cost plat and it all starts all over again. Lost chance behind a money maker for fanboys that will go on to say that this is better than triple a games . Yeah , sure . Disappointment .

I have the same problems with this game that I do with every MMO. It's grindy as hell with some elements of pay to win, which is unfortunate because it would have been a great game. The gameplay is actually fun, the art style is neat, and the story and universe are interesting; but it's all spaced out over so much grinding. Honestly, it might not even be that bad if it weren't for the moving goalpost. Every now and then they add more endgame content, making old top teir equipment gradually less useful. This would be an amazing game if it were restructured to have less grinding and more content.
As someone who takes the phrase,"Free to Play," very seriously, I am appalled at the limited inventory space for equipment. This game requires you to level up weapons and warframes to increase your overall rank, so having such a limited inventory for those things is ridiculous. This is probably the most unforgivable way they squeeze money out of the player base, because you can buy more inventory space with platinum, the ingame premium currency.
As a side note, the separation between PvE upgrades and PvP upgrades makes it difficult to go from one to the other. By the time I quit, I was close to catching up to the endgame in PvE, but I was ridiculously under powered in PvP. A good PvP game is more skill based than upgrade based, so I wouldn't recommend trying to get into this one. There's also no real rewards for playing PvP from what I could see.
Final thing, if you're going to play this game, get the Excalibur warframe as your starter. It's overpowered and you can't get it again until much later in the game. Also, join a large clan. Some of the best weapons can only be unlocked through the clans.

I am one of those f2p nuts. I look for free-to-play games all the time. I looked for many good games but most of them are pay-to-win. For those people who doesn't know what is Pay-to-win, Pay-to-win games are games where you have to spend your real life money to win it most of the time and it is costly. Of course! Why wouldn't a free-to-play game wouldn't be a pay-to-win? Or else, how are they gonna get money and income for it? People aren't that kind anymore. I was searching for a list of games then I found about Warframe...
I thought warframe was a pay-to-win game most of the time and I didn't download it. I didn't even see one of those youtube videos. In the trailer, looking at the graphics made me think that, "Oh, just another high-graphics game created to be a pay-to-win game or they made a well-graphics game for no reason (Sarcastic Laugh)"
A few months later, I opened my brother a steam account. After visiting the steam store the first time, he chose a game named "Warframe" I told him it was a pay-to-win.. He didn't believed it. Since we share the same computer, that means I can also play. Then I thought, why not try warframe a little? Then it happened,
Playing the story at first made me think, Hm, this must be a mostly-singleplayer game. So nothing to pay real life money for. Then I saw other players, A guy with a prime warframe.. Epic strong. I asked him how did he get that beautiful warframe. He replied, "Grinding its parts for 5 days" I am like wtf, Such a powerful warframe can be grinded? I gotta play this game. I am going deeper, deeper into this game. The story, the references, the action, the war. Its not even pay-to-win! I am becoming more stronger and greater, then I asked myself.. Why would they be so kind? The only things are to pay rl money for is merely heavy decoration. I am impressed more than anything. So, it is time to list the pros and cons:
Pros
1. A great game for grinders
2. Easy way to get enough resources and stuff
3. Many movement aspects and physics
4. Epic storyline and mystery references
5. Frequent updates with many events nearby
6. Co-op, even has PvP. You can play singleplayer if you want tho
7. Bosses and special entities which actually makes a game a good game.
Cons
1. Bad for people who talks without even trying it
2. Bad for people who hates progressing and being such a pay2win turd
3. Bad for people who hates to see other players having the great power known to be patience, making them have no    weakness in a game

This game is one of the best F2P-Games i have ever played so far, let me explain why:
First thing you'll probably notice are the gorgeous visuals. Not only are they on par with modern AAA titles, DE is also always improving on it so if you have a problem playing something that's not visually appealing, you don't have to worry.
Next up is arguably the most important thing for a Third-Person Shooter like this, the gameplay. You have a movement system which allows you, after a small learning curve, to basically "fly" throughout the levels by barely touching the ground  and looking absolutely badass doing so. The gunplay is really fun and you can choose from a wide variety of different and  guns an melee weapons like Hammers, Bows, Shuriken, machine-guns etc etc.
Like the abilty to obtain all different kinds of weapons, you can farm (or pay for) up to 30 different Warframes, your "Classes". Each Warframe looks unique and has different abilities, which you can use to beat up those pesky Grineer, Infested and Corpus. To be honest, farming a specific Warframe or weapon can take quite some time, depending on which you are interested in when staring this game, but it's managable.
So, what's the goal of all this? Why am i fighting in our Solar System? Well, i won't spoil it for you but let me tell you this: the main quests of this game are really interesting and engaging and will certainly result in you getting a whole new idea of what's actually going on!
I'll list some negatives now, which at least bugged me once in a while. When i first started this game i really wanted to get the Hydroid Warframe and since i wanted to do it F2P i had spend a good amount of time, leveling up and farming. (that was before the Map Update) It took me about 100 hours until i was finally able to play him. So you'll have to be quite patient. Speaking of which: What might throw you off as well are the production times for basically anything in the game. Crafting weapons or Warframes require you to get the blueprint/s and resources, and after all of that you need to wait an additional 12-72 hours until it finally finishes.
The ingame-Shop is somewhat expensive as well, but fortunately you're able to trade almost anything (even the currency which you have to buy) except for the visual stuff like capes and alternate helmets, colours etc. with other players, so i was able to obtain some really cool stuff just by trading Blueprints etc.
In conclusion: This game has so much more to offer, but typing everything out  might take a couple days, so if anything you saw/read so far interested you even in the slightest, give it a shot. It's F2P after all.
Is it a perfect game? No, it certainly has it's flaws. However, it's still one of the best F2p games and of it's genre, in my opinion. See for yourself and tell me if this small review has been helpful. :) Greetings from Germany!

Okay I downloaded this game, realized I need to register on a website and then shelved it for about 3 months (so tired of having to pre-reg). However once I got over my laziness and signed up for WF, I found this game to be amazingly fun/additive.
4/5 for game play.
Initnally the game is kind of overwhelming, lot of mods and different way to configure your Tenno. However once you start peeling back the game layers you realize there is so much to do. DE found a way to merge simple with complex. All the while encouraging you to try every aspect of the game.
4.5/5 for graphics, style, ambiance.
I rarely use the word "cool" anymore to describe things but this game is actually pretty umm ... cool. The look and feel of WF aesthetic is consistent for the world. When you first see a stalker or are invaded by an enemy, it looks powerful, intimidating. The way opponents a game should look. It enough to draw everyone's attention and prepare to survive.
Only draw backs are some Tenno frames go HAM with the graphics their abilities output. When you have 4 of those frames in 1 mission all spamming abilities things do get chaotic. Also, mission maps tend to repeat a little bit to frequently for my taste. However the variation of the enemies/modes slightly makes up for it.
5/5 Sound.
The voice overs and ambient sounds are superb! The enemies sound intimating. The world feels immersive.
4/5 Story/lore.
I really love the lore of this game. It's post-post-post-post apocalyptic type setting. Filled with plot twists and requires a little outside delving to discover it all.
They streamline the plot through a few quests to bring you in the world. However, I do believe they could offer a bit more lore this way. The story quest are too few imho and the game would benefit from of them.
Now as I type this they have just released: The War Within. DE seem to remain frequent on updating the story and lore so this could be a good thing.
Community.
For the most part the community seems good. Everyone is super excited about the game and most people are quick to offer explanation or help when asked.
I can't really tell the size of the community because of the way the game is set up. However it seems there are a ton of people a endgame/near end game. And fewer people who are working their way up.
The Devs are very interactive with the community. Often doing a little RP in chat. The ingame HYPE for The War Within on release was wild and energetic. I really like that they thematically hype their own game.
PvP
pvp is okay. The population for pvp is low (at certian times). The balance is questionable. My suggestion to you would be to clear most of the pve before you attempt pvp. Learn how to use your frame, how to move and dash around like a ninja.
Basic New Tips.
It's not p2w imo. It's just pay to get things a bit faster.
If you are serious about the game and actually want to progress faster. Do a little research on youtube/wiki before you start. Clearing planets sometimes requires certain tasks be met. So look for the junction requirements asap and complete the tasks as you go along.
Trying every weapon and every frame is the best way to level.
Join a Clan
Not all missions need to be completed with other players. If you have a hard time finding others just try to solo it.
Use your beginning plat wisely. Also once you find a weapon/frame you like, dont be afraid to
upgrade it early. Yes, better frames will come along but the wait could be a while. It's not super fun to struggle till then (unless you like that challenge).
Keep an eye out for promo codes.
And finally repect CLEM! <3

A fun new take on clicking based games such as cookie clicker or adventure capitalist.  If you like any of those clicking, idling or farming games, then you'll probably like this as well.  Its interesting to keep up to date with your heroes as far as upgrades and levels.  There is just something about these games that makes them so entertaining.  Now the one thing I've noticed is there is micro-transactions and there are people who instantly hate a game because of that, however, consider the following:
-The game is free to play.
-After the fact above, paying for anything else is the only financial support this game will get.
-I don't see this as a traditional pay2win complaint since you don't have to worry about other players doing this unlike in other games with this feature.
-You don't ever really need to buy any of the abilities, they can earned in-game by grinding the crap out of it...like you should anyway.
Other than that, it is repetitive, but all clicker games are in their own way.  I have no real complaints.  Its fun and interesting, auto clicker software works on it, and it can run in the background to make grinding less painful.  With no cost to you, check it out and maybe for once buy some rubies to support this great greenlite game.

As a game that reminds me of Diablo 2 in terms of mindless grinding, this game does take the cake. It's fun for what it is, and plays like any other mindless shooter game. In fact, it's my mindless game of choice.
That being said, DE has continually made it harder and harder to actually go and be a Free-To-Play player. As a person who started at the end of Operation: Eyes of Blight and has unlocked every thing possibly unlocked from that point onward (no Grand Master stuff, no Braton Vandals etc.) I have to say that in the past year and a half of playing, the means of acquiring items has become more and more difficult, as drop tables are continually squeezed and the useful stuff placed behind 2% or less drop chances. In the meantime, end tier content is slowly becoming pointless, as the rewards being given don't match the amount of effort to put in, either due to unreasonable weapon/warframe nerfs, or (more likely) the refusal to rework enemy scaling and levelling to work with the damage output of players. This literally forces players to use exploits in method to either skip the majority of grinding, or to pump money into buying premium currency for the purposes of buying the items desired.
On top of this, I feel that the economy of high value items are slowly trending downward, meaning eventually things that people used to see as "safe assets" when trading for platinum quickly become worthless over time. What doesn't get affected only has their prices skyrocket as the demand way outpaces the supply.
Long story short, if you're looking to merely go out and shoot things for fun, then this is a great game and you'll have a good time. If you're a collector or a completionist, or you're looking for a more serious experience, it's possible but you'll need to understand there is quite a lot of work to put in to completing a full collection.

This game is sadness overall . Not for you , rather for itself . You've probably heard by others that it is a grindfest . Well they are right , but if you think this is the grind that other games have ? OOh no . In other games when you get something after hours of grind you can enjoy it . Here if you want a simple weapon you have to grind for the relics , then grind for the parts , then grind for plat if you want to rush it or wait for the needed time if you decide to craft it normally . You think it is done ? No no . Then you need to grind for mods , then grind for formas , then grind for the rank up since putting a forma on a weapon takes its rank from 30 ( max ) to 0 . Also given that most builds require something like 3-5 formas , have fun doing that . By the time you are done you have most likely lost interest to the thing . Oh , and that's only 1 of the maaaany stuff your character can equip . ''That's diversity'' . Nope , because in certain missions you will instantly equip certain gear . And let's say you have grinded for you frame , primary , secondary , melee , companion and school ( school is like a skill set you choose via the mission progression ) . Ha ! Even more grind because schools require focus ( an xp type of currency ) to unlock these skills . What do you do now ? The game lacks any kind of free roam for you to chill out and see where this grind has gone . Instead you are always in a mission . And let me tell you , a boring one . Then it hits you . You can stay in this game for hours upon hours and the only reason for you to get stronger is to grind more efficiently . It's like a grind to grind so that you can grind better for the grinds to come . Go back and read this , play the game and check it out . You will see what i mean . And it's a lost chance because you can see that the dev team is hidding behind the excuse ''it's a free to play'' . People say the levels are randomly generated so you never do the same thing . Don't you get me started . You go to Earth and see a mission named Everest . Now here is where the devs could go crazy . Destroyed civiliazations , jumping over mountain tops and enjoying a good mission . What do you find ? Oh yeah , a tropical forest . And one that you have played around 1k times. Graphics ? Maxed out doesn't impress anyone especially in a mission where you see the backgrounds . Why ? ''It's a free 2 play'' . Missions.....Oh boy . Here you will see how low the bar was set . The game is so terrible in missions that when you see something actually good , you think it's the best story ever . ( second dream quest ) . I saw some lore videos on youtube , and let me tell you , some parts are really cool ! Buuut , why put them ingame when we can just give more Prime access to people for money ? Remember that get-stronger = grind better ? . Buut again . ''It's a free 2 play'' . Also bugs will accompany you all the time , some even making you restart a mission it took you over 20 minutes . Amazing . This game is ridiculously not worth it because everything was made for you to say ''i will play some more'' . That translates into more hours , and more hours translates into you giving money to the devs . And people will say it's a non pay-2-win type of game .Partially true, you can GRIND stuff that you will trade for platinum ( real money currency ) .Buuut for all this grind to end you will try to get boosters which cost plat, syandanas and other customisation items for your frame and weps that cost plat and it all starts all over again. Lost chance behind a money maker for fanboys that will go on to say that this is better than triple a games . Yeah , sure . Disappointment .

A fun little game. Ironically, despite being named Clicker Heroes, you will likely spend long periods not clicking at all once you are past the first few ascensions. Later, most players move to a hybrid style where the majority of a run is performed idle, and clicking is only used for the last five to ten minutes.
A few points that may put off some people. If you find any of these especially objectionable, this is likely not the game for you.
While usually classed as an 'idle' game, Clicker heroes requires more interaction than most games in that genre, especially during the first few ascensions.
It is also slow to start, usually requiring one to two days to get through your first ascension, and still requiring several hours to get through your next few. Once over that wall however, ascensions can drop down to thirty minutes or less.
Also, as is inherent with most games of this type, there is a lot of grinding, especially in the late game and, as previously mentioned, right at the beginning.
Finally, there is no actual end point at which you can say you have 'beat' the game. At the time of writing, the last defeatable boss occurs on floor 4720, but this may change in future updates, and does not limit the growth of your Ancients.

tl;dr, I can’t recommend this game emphatically enough. Please go play it right now and never stop.
When i first started playing this game, I didn’t know what I was in for. It seemed fun, but as I wasn’t good at shooters at the time, I left it to sit on my desktop for months, more and more unwilling to sit through a long update that only grew more daunting the longer i left it.
I’m proud to say I came back to it, because if I could have, i’d have nominated it for half this year’s awards on its own.
Warframe is the kind of game that defies description. Boiled down to its absolute essentials, it’s space ninjas, but it’s so much more. It’s walking through a massive open field at night hoping the huge ♥♥♥♥-off bio-robot-thing behind you is still occupied with those enemies behind that rock. It’s creeping through the ventilation of a space freighter to hopefully avoid the lasers that will set off alarms this time around. It’s customizing your weapons so that they break energy shields like paper, or turn your foes against one another. It’s walking like a god cloaked in steel and death between the foes who would get between you and your assassination target.
It’s also sitting for like three goddamn days waiting for your new warframe to finish being built because you didn’t want to bust out any real cash. It’s figuring out the opaque and esoteric trading system to maybe earn the game’s hard currency so you can carry more battle suits or weapons. It’s grinding your teeth as you hack through waves of enemies wondering when one of them is going to drop those Plastids you need to craft your next warframe’s Systems component.
It’s none of those things in the last paragraph if you shell out some cash, but eh.
Warframe is not a pay-to-win game, but it is a pay-to-win-quick game. Grinding is a huge aspect of it, and it also has a very dedicated speedrunning community trying to figure out the best methods for farming that mission you’ll need to grind as quickly and efficiently as possible.
Warframe is a game that it’s very hard not to fall in love with, though. It’s visually stunning, and new warframes with new playstyles are making it into the lineup with every update that goes by. Its world is persistent and ever-evolving, and with the Plains of Eidolon release that came out a few weeks ago at the time of this writing, its co-op potential and the truly enjoyable parts of its engine have a chance to truly shine beyond their original luster.
Not to mention, if you’re a nerd like me, there’s some really lovely lore to sink your teeth into in the quests and the Codex entries. I could ramble on like this for some time, but nothing could really compare to playing it for yourself. So hey, download it sometime and go wild. I think you’ll like it. And if you do? Shoot me a mail in game sometime saying so. My username is Llabden for the forseeable future.
Hopefully I’ll see you on a Teralyst hunt someday!

A ninja in space, now how does that sound? Freaking amazing, and that’s what this game delivers. Warframe is a third-person shooter that incorporates all the shooting a gun fanatic can imagine with the grace and mobility a ninja wielding throwing stars and katanas needs to kill, from sliding on the ground and jumping off the walls.
The graphics are among the best you can have, even running it on low specs, there is detail in the suits from its mesh to the folding, weapons are all superb, light reflects and makes colours look great when walking or running around. In the world you will get rain, sand storms, you will see tropical (alien) forests, beacons of light in the form of technological complexes.
The sound is good even if you could have more ambient music variety, for example in the ship you have a frequency radio that picks up a rather short loop of communications. The sound effects are again good but at times not as rich as the environments seem to be, weapons have expectable noises and vary but not by a huge factor, if it shoots a bullet it kind of always sounds the same but with a slightly different pitch, none of this will make a difference when you are in a blood rage murdering hordes of enemies.
This is the cherry on top, gameplay. You will have to learn to walk before you run, but after you run you will start flying, off the walls and in all directions. This game has the most satisfying gameplay I encountered in a while, not only you will master the characters movement but even the flow of weapon usage is great, on the melee weapons different stances allow you to customize the way you wield a blade or hammer. There are two major different game modes, the one and for the vast majority of the game is the one where you control your character and walk about, here like I said the gameplay is superb, the only problem can occur when players try to either force walk in non-passable areas or trying to get out of the map box, both rather avoidable. Now the second mode is where you control your character using a deep space winged rig suit, the Archwing is indeed not so simple to control and the gameplay can become awkward, it can be fun in vast space areas, doing loops and dashing around, but it loses all that fun in narrow areas like many maps have. Indeed you will either move much slower and avoid collisions or try to drift past obstacles only to hit most of them and losing your orientation once again. To make this a bit worse the Archwing is also use in underwater exploration, a very small part of some maps, here all the fun is removed and replaced with slow moving machines that do none of the cool maneuvers you love in the game. This is the only reason gameplay does not get a 10 out of 10, but fortunately in this rather huge game it plays a small part.
The game features an ever growing number Frames, classes if you will, all have different abilities and can impact a group in different ways, from raw damage to healing or buffing your team, combined with what will seem to a new player as a never ending amount of weaponry, you have yourself a whole lot of game to play. If you are the type of gamer that loves collecting all, this game will consume you. Frames, main weapons, side weapons, melee, dog pets, cat pets, sentry pets, ships, even bobble heads. Not to mention all the cosmetics to make your frame unique.
The story of the game is ever evolving, it comes as a set of revelations, you start off very much in the dark and learn more and more, so far only one main plot twist has occurred but the developers are always adding content and future plot twists are expected. Whit out telling spoilers, I can say that you will find a distant time period were the powers present are in struggle, you will act as balance and, well you will find more. Frames for the most part come with a story, except for the initial ones. The lore is present via messages, images you will collect along information, videos, and all over the maps. There is a language that you can decipher. Plus you are always reminded that your actions have consequences.
At this point I wold like to address an important part of any free to play game, the economy. This game contains like most a cash shop, but unlike most the premium currency (platinum), is obtainable not only by paying with real money. The game trade system indeed allows players to trade all matter of goods, for other goods and platinum, and this is where it gets interesting, there is a market for all, yes you don’t need to move mountains to obtain something that is worth platinum to another player. Also the items in the shop bought by platinum are mainly either boosters, like resource farming, or cosmetics, none giving a gameplay advantage.
In conclusion, this game is a superb example that the free to play is not a bin of lost ideas and low budget content, this is an A grade game and I recommend it to all lovers of the genre..

You will feel like a god when you play this game, spinning around murdering anything even remotely hostile with lightning guns or rocket launchers or swords simultaneously electrify and blow up people. Or hell, just punching a guy into orbit is a viable method of murder that this game provides. I found it a great game to play while socializing with your friends; Get a bunch of people together in a teamspeak and play while talking about whatever. At the highest level of the game (read several hundred hours in) most missions can be done with casual ease and discussing different builds and combinations of warframes can keep conversations going for hours.
The biggest downside is that Warframe is undoubtably a grind and time sink. You must gather the credits to purchase the blueprint for a weapon which then has specific material requirements, some exceedingly rare, which must be ground for. once completed then you must wait 12 hours to even get the weapon and even then it will need to be leveled up to become useful. EVEN THEN you still need to upgrade it in two different ways to get the absolute most out of it. total time spent depends on the weapon in question but it can take anywhere from a week to a month to get a weapon from unowned to pinnacle of achievement that weapon can reach. and this is assuming you have all the required mods to reach that pinnacle, which themselves can take a long time to acquire.
However with all that said it is still one of the most addicting games I have ever played. 8/10

Lets start by saying, I absolutely adored(d) this game.
Like many other MMORPGs, the game had a serious grind issue. But it was fun, atleast for me. I loved farming parts to build my new weapon, enjoyed playing Sorties, which are hard missions within the game for rewards, It was fun for me to just 'play' the game, without any objective at all, just for the sheer enjoyment of trying to survive an hour in the toughest void defence with a friend, while you're being overwhelmed by enemies and only your abilities are keeping you alive. Basically, this game was my favourite game for about a half a year. So why would I give it a negative review, you may ask. One simple reason. The support and cheat detection system of the game, and their reluctance to help me after I was banned.
One day, I just logged into my account, nothing special, and noticed I had a duplicate of a maxed mod I didn't have before. I thought to my self, why did I do that? So I decided I wanted to trade that mod for platinum, a premium currency ingame. As I secured a deal, I got presented with a trade-limit, as it told me I have used up my maxed trades for today, when I didn't even trade a single time? We tried at different trading stations, until I tried to join the trading station on Earth, called Maroo's Bazaar. It sent me a message I was trade banned? I decided to go onto the support page, and requested a trade unban, and explained all of what I just said above. A few hours later, I got a reply that I was permanently banned from the game for 'selling my account in trade chat' which as I knew was breaking the EULA. I tried to log in into the game, but I was banned for 19 years? I guess. I wanted to go onto the forums to ask for help, but I got banned from the forums. I decided that the only place I could come back to is the support forums, where I wasn't banned yet. I submitted another ticket, telling them about I was inoccent and I was willing to assist them in anything, if it was to get my account unbanned. I marked the the ticket as 'suspended or banned'. I later realised that someone probably got into my account, being the reason as to why I had that duplicate maxed mod. I updated my ticket with my suspicion, and changed my password. The next day, I was greeted with a beautiful message in my email: I have been banned from the game because I was 'selling platinum, the premium currency for real-life money in trade chat', or something along those lines. Remember what message I was sent earlier? I was selling my account in chat, two different things. And to top it off, they told me that they detected no suspicious activity on my account, and banned me off their helpful support page.
I wasn't even mad, just suprised and sad that even if a player loves their game, they don't care for people who didn't support their game in Beta. If you're looking for a timesink, don't risk it. I was the unlucky one, don't you be another.

I'll start off with a pros and cons list, and throw in my thoughts afterwards.
Pros: -Hours of content                             -Free to play (if you're willing to grind a bit, everything is obtainable)
-Plenty of customization options     -Tons of weapons and characters to choose from
-Amazing graphics                            -Great community of players
-Lots of contests and events            -Devs listen to fans and implement their ideas into the game
-Gripping storyline                            -Awesome gameplay with tons of different mission styles
-Updates frequently                          -Twitch streams every week with free platinum (in-game money) giveaways
-Good trading community, rare blueprints and weapons can be traded between players
-Build your own clan, make your own unique emblem to wear as a badge
Cons: -Can be a grind from time to time    -Certain enemies and bosses are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to fight
-Certain weapons and Warframes are so much more powerful, the less powerful are often not used
-Every so often a bug can render a mission unbeatable
-Don't buy platinum unless you get a 50% or 75% discount coupon as the daily log in bonus
-Barely anyone plays PvP anymore, so you have to form your own private matches
Now on to my thoughts:
After another amazing update with such a rich story, it's about time I wrote a review on my favorite game of all time. Before the Second Dream quest, Warframe's story was fragmented. There were hints here and there about the Tenno origin and lore on the galaxy's two superpowers, the Grineer and the Corpus. However, it always left me wondering "how and why?" I mean, for the longest time many players didn't even know what a Tenno was. Warframes were thought to be piloted by someone physically inside the suit, but it had a unique twist, revealed in the Second Dream quest. It was delivered incredibly well and honestly it got me pretty emotional. The Second Dream showed everyone that Warframe isn't just a great co-op third-person shooter, but also an amazing story that I think even non-gamers could enjoy. The War Within did just as well, with moments that made me feel just as cold and vulnerable as my character. It took me into a world of feeling powerless, when noramally in the game I wield incredible strength. It made my mind race as the past revealed itself after benig long forgotten, while presenting difficult decisions along the way. It filled in a lot of cracks in the universe's story, while opening just the right amount of new ones. Warframe is constantly growing, and it's really come a long way after almost four years. I hope reading this convinces you to try it out, keep playing, or even become as passionate about it as I am.

Warframe is an amazing game, but it's not for everyone.
Game overview:
You play as the Tenno, master of swordmanship and gunplay, and "pilots" of the Warframes. In other words, you are space ninjas with super powers. Your objective lore-wise is to regulate the universe's warring factions and maintain a balance between the powers. It's a very fast-paced third person action-RPG shooter that is primarily co-op PvE. Your squad can consist of one solo Tenno, or up to four total. You can equip your Tenno with a Warframe, Primary Weapon, Secondary Weapon, and Melee Weapon of your choice. Collect materials and blueprints to build more things to equip.
Pros:
-EXTREMELY incredible engine, everything looks and runs amazing even on low-end systems and toned down settings.
-EXTREMELY customizeable Warframes/Weapons. You can build your Tenno any way you want, and try a million different things to explore what's fun and strong! There are something like 250 different weapons, and most of them are completely unique to one another. You will definitely find something you like that fits your playstyle.
-Movement and combat flow incredibly well. You are a space ninja. You can do anything.
-Everything is obtainable through gameplay. All weapons and warframes can be obtained through play with some effort, and the premium currency (for cosmetics, or insta-buys) is tradeable ingame, so you can get things that people want and trade for premium currency!
-Very good community. They're always more than willing to help newbs with any questions or missions. Just ask in region chat, you'll get hooked up with just about anything you need.
Cons:
-EXTREMELY grindy. You will be playing the same, or similar missions, A LOT. Over and over, just to get what you need to make that piece of equipment that you want. Having so many build options at your disposal can somewhat remedy this (allows you to play a different way, even if it's the same mission), but for most people it's still a pain.
-Crafting times are in realtime, somewhat similar a mobile game paywall. It takes 12 hours to craft most weapons, 24h for some. 12h for warframe parts, then three DAYS to combine them into a useable warframe. Obviously that's annoying and it's a turn-off for many. However, you can still actively play the game and collect materials, mods, complete missions, etc in the meantime so you're not BARRED from play, just takes a while to use the shiny new thing you're excited for. Or if you're willing to pay, you can rush the build time with premium currency (Devs gotta make money too :P).
-The developers are always paying attention and active within the community... but honestly do a pretty poor job of delivering what the community wants. Many times when the community asks for a change for something that's usually completely necessary or there's no downsides to it, the developers still won't make the change without adding some kind of catch. "Yeah, we'll do this for you, BUT..."
-Lacks any kind of thorough tutorials. There's a ton of things that are vague and very difficult to figure out by just playing the game. You may as well just ask in region chat or look things up on the wiki if you're confused, because you're unlikely to find the information you need by searching ingame.
Summary:
Overall, personally, I believe this game is definitely worth the time if you're the type of person who doesn't mind grinding. The gameplay is just so phenomenal that it outweighs all of the negatives. The community ALWAYS warmly welcomes new players, and will usually stop on a dime to help them out with whatever they need! Seriously! Watch some videos, play it for yourself. It's free, may as well try it!
If you decide to play and need help, you can message me ingame if I'm online! IGN: CuteNabi

This game is sadness overall . Not for you , rather for itself . You've probably heard by others that it is a grindfest . Well they are right , but if you think this is the grind that other games have ? OOh no . In other games when you get something after hours of grind you can enjoy it . Here if you want a simple weapon you have to grind for the relics , then grind for the parts , then grind for plat if you want to rush it or wait for the needed time if you decide to craft it normally . You think it is done ? No no . Then you need to grind for mods , then grind for formas , then grind for the rank up since putting a forma on a weapon takes its rank from 30 ( max ) to 0 . Also given that most builds require something like 3-5 formas , have fun doing that . By the time you are done you have most likely lost interest to the thing . Oh , and that's only 1 of the maaaany stuff your character can equip . ''That's diversity'' . Nope , because in certain missions you will instantly equip certain gear . And let's say you have grinded for you frame , primary , secondary , melee , companion and school ( school is like a skill set you choose via the mission progression ) . Ha ! Even more grind because schools require focus ( an xp type of currency ) to unlock these skills . What do you do now ? The game lacks any kind of free roam for you to chill out and see where this grind has gone . Instead you are always in a mission . And let me tell you , a boring one . Then it hits you . You can stay in this game for hours upon hours and the only reason for you to get stronger is to grind more efficiently . It's like a grind to grind so that you can grind better for the grinds to come . Go back and read this , play the game and check it out . You will see what i mean . And it's a lost chance because you can see that the dev team is hidding behind the excuse ''it's a free to play'' . People say the levels are randomly generated so you never do the same thing . Don't you get me started . You go to Earth and see a mission named Everest . Now here is where the devs could go crazy . Destroyed civiliazations , jumping over mountain tops and enjoying a good mission . What do you find ? Oh yeah , a tropical forest . And one that you have played around 1k times. Graphics ? Maxed out doesn't impress anyone especially in a mission where you see the backgrounds . Why ? ''It's a free 2 play'' . Missions.....Oh boy . Here you will see how low the bar was set . The game is so terrible in missions that when you see something actually good , you think it's the best story ever . ( second dream quest ) . I saw some lore videos on youtube , and let me tell you , some parts are really cool ! Buuut , why put them ingame when we can just give more Prime access to people for money ? Remember that get-stronger = grind better ? . Buut again . ''It's a free 2 play'' . Also bugs will accompany you all the time , some even making you restart a mission it took you over 20 minutes . Amazing . This game is ridiculously not worth it because everything was made for you to say ''i will play some more'' . That translates into more hours , and more hours translates into you giving money to the devs . And people will say it's a non pay-2-win type of game .Partially true, you can GRIND stuff that you will trade for platinum ( real money currency ) .Buuut for all this grind to end you will try to get boosters which cost plat, syandanas and other customisation items for your frame and weps that cost plat and it all starts all over again. Lost chance behind a money maker for fanboys that will go on to say that this is better than triple a games . Yeah , sure . Disappointment .

Hello, I'm here to give an early access review of the game ARK Survival Evolved.
Look at how many hours I have of ARK, now at those whom typically write negative reviews. Now look back at mine...
Have you ever noticed the people who have made those reviews have lesser hours, such as 300 or less? Let me start off with my review quickly so this doesn't happen to be another rant post that wastes your time. I've had this game for a little over a year now...
I can't tell you that this game is perfect in every way you would see fit. But that's becasue I'm one of the few who take note this is still early access. Yes. This game has poor optimizations. But for the content inside of this game, it's worth it. Surely, I too will hope the game will be better optimized and maybe even smaller in download. I have several of my own friends who can't enjoy this game because their own ARK uses up their whole drive. *Sad face*
There are going to be people who write reviews based on official servers. My best advice is to listen to what they have to say, but don't. Officials was a huge part of my game life for ark last year, up until around November when I discovered unofficials with trusted friends, no wipes, can lead to way more exploration, maps and success for ark due to the better rates. For those unaware, rates mean faster taming, faster breeding, faster resource harvesting, etc. By default, official servers will have your rates at the default taming 150 dinos (depending on what type of dino) for 2-6 hours also depending on your taming method. Official servers also have you raise mammals and dinosaurs over 2 to 7 days realtime. It can take a lot away from you if you have a job. This tends to make you miss out on imprints or moments to feed the dinosaurs causing them to die or be not as good.
Unofficial servers may or may not have wipes, depending on what type of person runs them (ie. People who get bored quickly in their own game and decides to wipe the whole server for themselves). But if you find one, or even decided to play in ****SINGLEPLAYER**** to adjust the rates, you will have a much more enjoyable time with this game. Garaunteed. Not to mention, unofficials also support developing maps, and even mods that improve the game style, or make it more of a challenge!
I'm not very good at writing reviews, but this game deserves an honest one from my side. I've recently downloaded the new map Ragnarok (I played it before it was officially released), and I can't say I am disapointed with the content since new creatures are being released at a consistant rate.

First let me get out of the way that while this is a 'free to play' game, it is also actually a free to play game.  CH was balanced as a clicker game *looooong* before they had the ruby 'pay in' system, and it continues to be well balanced after, aka this is less 'pay to win' and more 'pay to be so amazingly lazy you can't even wait to idle.   So on that front, don't be put off by the overall 'free to pay' movement, pay a couple bucks to support these guys if you like it after messing around with it for a few days and call it good.
As to the overall mechanic, yes it is an idle game, and yes it was likely inspired by CC, but having been a statistical nut for both for quite a while now I can say quite vehemently that this is not a mere CC ripoff.  While the core game mechanic is still stuff happening while you idle, CH innovates in a number of ways by adding in multiple layers of new mechanics, and an overall level of polish most other clicker/idler games lack.  Solid graphics, sound (that given you may be running this for *WEEKS* at a time, idle, you will disable) and an overall focus on really enhancing the play through experience really set CH apart from others in this genre.
Where CC was mostly just a one and done optimize the one linear progression game (albeit one that still had me poking it for a solid year), CH has far more intricate and balanced game systems to optimize and multiple different strategies to pursue.  There is the same basic click to hit things and level up the stuff which can auto hit things that CC started, but rather than simply 'stockpile' rewards from your runs as CC had, now you absolutely need to *spend* them on new game-tweaking ancient idols, and the optimal spending path, and optimal way to procure those rewards is turned on its head, opening up a number of different paths to idle/play.  Do you focus on long deep runs to get as far as you can? or should you focus on maximizing your soul per hour return with multiple short idle runs just getting far enough each time to spend some more souls? maybe do both?
Overall a really really shining example of how to make idling fun, and if you are obsessive on number crunching/stats/optimization probably about as addicting as <pick your controlled substance of choice>.
