Warframe is an amazing game, but it's not for everyone.
Game overview:
You play as the Tenno, master of swordmanship and gunplay, and "pilots" of the Warframes. In other words, you are space ninjas with super powers. Your objective lore-wise is to regulate the universe's warring factions and maintain a balance between the powers. It's a very fast-paced third person action-RPG shooter that is primarily co-op PvE. Your squad can consist of one solo Tenno, or up to four total. You can equip your Tenno with a Warframe, Primary Weapon, Secondary Weapon, and Melee Weapon of your choice. Collect materials and blueprints to build more things to equip.
Pros:
-EXTREMELY incredible engine, everything looks and runs amazing even on low-end systems and toned down settings.
-EXTREMELY customizeable Warframes/Weapons. You can build your Tenno any way you want, and try a million different things to explore what's fun and strong! There are something like 250 different weapons, and most of them are completely unique to one another. You will definitely find something you like that fits your playstyle.
-Movement and combat flow incredibly well. You are a space ninja. You can do anything.
-Everything is obtainable through gameplay. All weapons and warframes can be obtained through play with some effort, and the premium currency (for cosmetics, or insta-buys) is tradeable ingame, so you can get things that people want and trade for premium currency!
-Very good community. They're always more than willing to help newbs with any questions or missions. Just ask in region chat, you'll get hooked up with just about anything you need.
Cons:
-EXTREMELY grindy. You will be playing the same, or similar missions, A LOT. Over and over, just to get what you need to make that piece of equipment that you want. Having so many build options at your disposal can somewhat remedy this (allows you to play a different way, even if it's the same mission), but for most people it's still a pain.
-Crafting times are in realtime, somewhat similar a mobile game paywall. It takes 12 hours to craft most weapons, 24h for some. 12h for warframe parts, then three DAYS to combine them into a useable warframe. Obviously that's annoying and it's a turn-off for many. However, you can still actively play the game and collect materials, mods, complete missions, etc in the meantime so you're not BARRED from play, just takes a while to use the shiny new thing you're excited for. Or if you're willing to pay, you can rush the build time with premium currency (Devs gotta make money too :P).
-The developers are always paying attention and active within the community... but honestly do a pretty poor job of delivering what the community wants. Many times when the community asks for a change for something that's usually completely necessary or there's no downsides to it, the developers still won't make the change without adding some kind of catch. "Yeah, we'll do this for you, BUT..."
-Lacks any kind of thorough tutorials. There's a ton of things that are vague and very difficult to figure out by just playing the game. You may as well just ask in region chat or look things up on the wiki if you're confused, because you're unlikely to find the information you need by searching ingame.
Summary:
Overall, personally, I believe this game is definitely worth the time if you're the type of person who doesn't mind grinding. The gameplay is just so phenomenal that it outweighs all of the negatives. The community ALWAYS warmly welcomes new players, and will usually stop on a dime to help them out with whatever they need! Seriously! Watch some videos, play it for yourself. It's free, may as well try it!
If you decide to play and need help, you can message me ingame if I'm online! IGN: CuteNabi

Warframe is a cooperative online third person shooter where players take on the role of Tenno, space ninjas in technologically-advanced exoskeletons that give them superhuman powers. Engage in action-packed combat as you run along walls, go down zip lines, perform acrobatics, and cut down enemies with your sword, or blast them all to kingdom come with the vast arsenal of weapons at your disposal. While Warframe does have several PvP options, Warframe is primarily a PvE game. Choose from three starting classes and 17 advanced classes, each with their own roles and playstyles. Work together with friends as you take on armies of space grunts, walking turrets, and hordes of mindless zombies in a stunning futuristic sci-fi world.
Warframe Key Features:
1. Good Variety of Warframes – choose from a large pool of warframes and customize them with  mods to match your needs.
2. Smooth Moves – play with familiar FPS controls and use ninja/parkour moves to position yourself.
3. Constant Updates – the dev team is always tweaking and updating the game based on players' comments.
4. Awesome Graphics and SFX – the graphics are amazingly fluid and the music heightens the action-packed atmosphere of the game.
You can run Warframe missions with up to three other players, and while flying solo is definitely possible in the early going or when you're grinding for experience or resources, teaming up becomes necessary as you tackle tougher missions. Fighting your way through fiendish hordes with the help of some allies can be very satisfying, especially when there's a good mix of powers in play. Coordinating with friends is the best way to get this kind of experience, because jumping into matches or having folks join you can lead to lopsided situations. If there's a gap in player level or a mismatch with the mission challenge, as often happens, your cooperative missions can devolve into all-out sprints as players easily cut their way through enemies they far outclass.
To minimize such gaps, you can focus on playing only new missions, since those tend to scale toward the upper bound of your capabilities. However, many of the environments in Warframe are reused frequently. You may be taking a different route through an enemy ship or encountering different environmental effects in the asteroid base, but you can't escape seeing the same spaces over and over again. This repetition combines with the lack of enemy variety (each species has only a handful of different units) to make many Warframe missions feel very similar to one another.
To spice things up, you may want to acquire a new gun, a new melee weapon, or a new suit. Warframe is free to play, but you must spend either time or money to acquire new items. Currently, new suits range roughly from $5 to $25, with new weapons falling close to the lower end of that spectrum. Alternatively, you can purchase blueprints to craft new weapons and suits using in-game currency. It takes a significant amount of time to save up the money for a new blueprint, and then you must spend even more time acquiring the resources to actually craft it.
Even if you skip the lengthy crafting process by using real-world currency, you still have to spend time leveling up your new gear. Jumping into a high-level mission with a brand-new suit is a death sentence, so it's back to lower levels to grind for experience. As your gear levels up, you gain more slots to modify it using boosters picked up during combat. Adding abilities to suits, improving the attributes of your gear, and imbuing your weapon with elemental damage are just some of the things mods can do. Unfortunately, the system to apply and improve mods is poorly laid out and barely explained, leaving you on your own to figure things out.
Some problematic menus pale in comparison to Warframe's real problem: a pervasive tendency toward repetition. Whether you're forging ahead with a high-level suit or leveling up a new one, Warframe repeats enemies, environments, and scenarios too frequently. Without new challenges for your combat abilities, the excitement soon dries up, leaving you without a compelling reason to keep playing. This free-to-play shooter is still technically in beta, so changes may come that make a substantive difference. But as of now, Warframe's interesting combat mechanics are too quickly overcome by the grind of repetition.

Boy oh BOY, where do I begin with this one? Strap in, folks, because this gets a little lengthy.
I suppose I should say this: The game isn't a bad play. It controls well, it's stupidly fun, and it has some great mechanics. Want a shotgun that can blow apart your enemies, all while trying to sneak around? You can do that! Want to slaughter everything in sight with nothing but a sword? You can do that, too! Heck, take out a FLAMING KNIFE and go ham!
But that's about where the fun stops. Sure, running around and coming up with creative ways to kill your targets is fun, but in order to get anywhere in the game, you need new weapons, new Warframes, a trusty companion...Not to mention the materials to make those things. Even when you've gotten your gear to their maximum rank, you still need the materials to take them further, or work on that Grakata you've had sitting around in your inventory for a couple of weeks (that is, of course, if you even HAVE the inventory space, which you have to BUY with ACTUAL MONEY)
And that's where the game becomes a real disappointment. MMO's have always had that grind that players, for the most part, seem to be okay with in general. In THIS game, however, that's what you'll be doing about 80% of the time. Need that blueprint for the Rhino Warframe's Chassis? Go beat this boss! Oh, wait, did you want the NEUROPTICS blueprint? You already have that one? TOO BAD, FIGHT THE BOSS AGAIN! At this point, it should be said that the devs, despite these issues (as well as those below) being brought up by not just new players, but VETERAN players, as well, tend to ignore the idea of making certain things less of a pain in the @$$ to get. They've also been known to implement new features, and rarely address new or existing problems until much later on. Some bosses, for example, are nearly impossible to beat without endless patience or sheer dumb luck. Of course, the same thing can be said about materials.
Blueprints from bosses? Okay, I can understand that. But look at the materials needed for just the systems. With the last update, grinding became an even bigger pain, as a lot of the higher-tier materials were either made stupidly rare, or made impossible to craft without shelling out money from your own pocket to do so. Not to mention the fact that, if you want to get at those materials, you need to improve your loadout. Which requires, you guessed it, better weapons, better Warframes, better everything. Sure, you can mod the living crap out of that sweet 2-shot rifle you got, but it's not going to do anything after a certain point, as the enemies will likely be too strong for your weapon to damage significantly, even with the right mods attached. And, even if you DID have a better weapon on hand, you would still need to grind for those ranks. Wanna know something else? You only have a HANDFUL of weapon and Warframe slots in your arsenal. If you want more slots (which you DO want), you'll have to shell out Platinum for those slots, which requires money. To give you an idea as to how much you'd be spending on slots, 12 Platinum buys 2 slots. Out of the 75 you get from the five buck Plat Pack, you're spending a little less than a dollar. For inventroy space.
And, yes, you can get Platinum from other players. Trade people items they're looking for, like Blueprints, Prime Weapon parts, etc., and you'll have a little Platinum to spend. That's if, of course, you can find a buyer for your items.
I went into this came months back looking for a good game. I thought I had found it. Cyberninjas in space, ridiculous acrobatics combined with guns and blades (bows, too), and a bunch of factions that seem very interesting, with a lot of lore to keep any lorebuff happy for a while. I left it not only disappointed, but with a very bitter taste in my mouth. The grind went from somewhat acceptable to god-awful, the items NEEDED in order to get anywhere are either too difficult for many players to get at, or cost REAL WORLD CASH to get the blueprint for, that way you can completely bypass grinding for hours on end, just hoping to get that ONE. STINKING. NEURAL. SENSOR.
Call me a noob, a loser, a whiner, or whatever it is you high-rnked people call lower-level 'plebs'. It still doesn't mean that the points I brought up are not valid reasons to not play this game. Those points being:
-The grind can often take hours, even days, to give you that one items you're looking for, especially if it is overly rare.
-Items that are locked behind a level-wall that you can't get past, even with team mates, are locked behind a paywall.
Just as an example: 1 Neural Sensor, which is needed for the Rhino Warframe's Systems, is 100 Platinum. You can get 75 for FIVE BUCKS. You're paying for that and then some in order to get a part that is needed at least once or twice in EVERY Warframe, which can hold back players unable to get to the planets with the resources needed, and can hold back those who do not have the extra cash to throw out.
-RNG has made things so difficult to get your hands on, that it sometimes takes hours to get that one thing you need. Blueprints, Kubrow Eggs, rare resources, it covers it all.
-Inventroy space, which is a COMMON and AVAILABLE thing in most other MMO's, requires actual money or more grinding in order to get. And, considering that there are SEVERAL types of inventory slots, the costs add up quickly.
-The devs. Seriously, look through some of the Vets' reviews, and you'll get a pretty good idea as to what sort of BS goes on.
I've stated my opinion on the game. Others have as well. Take all of that into consideration before you begin downloading this game, or consider spend a hundred bucks on this game. Just because a game LOOKS good, and PLAYS good, does not mean that it IS good.

First off, I've only had this game for about two weeks, in that time I have put in about 20 hours of game play. The game looks beautiful, like a truly pre-historic world. This review will only cover single player, as I don't play online and have no desire to do so. That being said, the game is insanely difficult on the default setting at the begining. I spent hours getting killed by a Troodon, which every time it attacked me it put me to sleep, then would run in circle like a moron until I was about to wake up, then bite me again starting the whole process over. At the time I had no tamed beasts, cloth "armor" and I did not know stimberries would wake you up. Each time this happened, it would take about 45 minutes to die, and this kept happening to me, about a dozen times. I went online to find a solution, all I could find was "Troodons don't spawn on the beach, must be a Dilophasur" No, indeed it was not, shortly after reading the afore mentioned post, I purposefuly found a Dilophasur and tamed it. Troodons poison with their bite, while the others spit (acid?) at a target. I almost forgot to mention, when I first installed the game, it wouldn't load at all. "can't find shooter.exe" (at the time I had it installed to my external drive) so I unistalled and reinstalled on C:, it worked, but I had only 12% space left on the drive. Of course, that just wasn't going to work for me, uninstalled and reinstalled on the external again, and (for some unknown reason) it worked. then the repeating death hours, then, the next day I went to load it up and try again and *noop* "Steam recomends you validate your files"...k..."two files are missing and need to be re-downloaded"...k... revalidate...all good! but the whole pocess take about 30-40 minutes and I have to do it EVERY time I load the game. one way to rectify this is to play in offline mode. I found out eventually, that this bug is caused by using settings different frome the default ones, evry time you load up, steam trys to sync your local files with cloud files, and registers that the config file doesn't match, thus triggering the revalidation and download. Now, as for the game itself, awesome cocept, cool gameplay, and who doesn't want a pack of furocious dinos doing thier bidding? I have my PC hooked up to my television as the only monitor, and use steam pretty much like someone uses a console. So, I've been trying to play ARK with a controller, not exactly easy, sometimes (maybe 3-5 times since I've started) the right joystick doesn't work. but the left does as well as the rest of the functions. Exiting and reloading seems to fix it, so far. Combat, gathering and building are fairly smooth, but transfering items is a pain. Screen navagation is near inpossible, when tring to level up your stats are all lit up so you can't tell what you are hilighting, and when you try to scroll down on the Engrams page either nothing happens or it jumps all the way to the bottom. Honestly, I hope they come up with a better user interface and control scheme for the console. If they manage to work out these few bugs I'd happily give the game 10/10, but as it is currently, it's about 8/10.

Please note: my "Hours on Record" is inflated as I leave the game running on my PC.  I'm closer to 1,000 hours as of this review.
First up: tl;dr: I like the game, and would recommend it.  Anyone who says it's Pay-to-Win has a definition of that I don't understand.
Warframe is a free-to-play third person shooter game, where you play "future space ninjas" seeking to free the solar system from various factions.  However, "space ninjas" is a bit of a loose term: each Warframe is more or less a character, each with four abilities.  Frost is snow-themed (creating a bubble of snow that protects allies within it, summoning an avalance), Ash is the stereotypical Ninja warframe, Titania is the warframe that can turn into a little butterfly of death by flying around the map, Inaros is a Egyptian God themed warframe that throws blinding sand and can turn into a sandstorm, etc.  Each warframe is generally overpowered in their own rediculous way, which is kind of needed: sometimes you'll be trying to take on level 100 (or higher) enemies, and it's due to your overpoweredness that your team can accomplish its' goals.
Each Warframe is powerful in what they do, and each one can be augmented using Mods which drop in-game, which can be leveled up against a modification capacity, so even two of the same warframe, through modding, can play differently.  As well, you can swap out your mods between missions, so there is no problem with experimenting with different builds.
The game is primarily PvE, though there is a PvP mode, which includes full-on PvP deathmatch/team-deathmatch, as well as a gametype that is somewhat reminiscent of Lacross-meets-Aztec football.  However, as the abilities of each Warframe can be absurdly overpowered, most abilities in the game work differently in Conclave (the PvP mode) vs the general game.  To be honest, to me the PvP seems tacked on, and I never play it.
Currently, the game has a good methodology of guiding the players through the solar system, unlocking story quests.
The good:  really good-engaging gameplay, multiple "characters" that allow people to experiement and rewards modding and strategy, however can be played in a solo queue.  Later story missions (Natah, Second Dream, Sands of Inaros, The Sacred Grove) have become really good.
The bad: many systems, such as modding, relics, etc. could be explained better, and typically most players end up watching youtube videos to figure out some of the in-game systems, if they don't end up groking them.  The good part is that you can generally get a pretty good ways into the game without understanding the systems before you hit a knowledge wall and need to read the wiki..
The funny: As a Free-To-Play game, most every resource, warframe, or weapon can be bought with Platinum, the currency you can buy from the developers in-game.  Some people (usually people who don't like the game) claim that this allows people to Pay To Win... but it's a mostly PVE game.  And, to be frank, most of the time people use Platinum in-game, is to pay other PLAYERS for items that they have, such as Primed Weapon or Warframe parts (Primed items are in-game "upgrades" to in-game weapons, basically super-prototypes, which can only be obtained in-game by farming), or for specific mods that are difficult to obtain.  The only items that can only be obtained via Platinum, and not by farming, are purely cosmetic items, like different skins for particular Warframes or weapons.
Even if you buy a Warframe or Weapon directly with Platinum, it still starts at level 0, and you need to spend the time to level it up/mod it properly.  And even then, certain weapons are only "good" with specific modifications/build playstyles, so buying the "best" weapon in the game is subjective to the most part.  Yes, there are weapons that are the best Crit-weapons or best Status weapons, but lots of people just play with what is the most fun for them, and can do end-game content just as well as people who only use the L33T OPT1M4L build.
I would NOT recommend spending any Platinum as a starting player beyond the starting Platinum that you get to buy a Sentinel; however, I would recommend buying Platinum if you get a 50% or 75% off Platinum coupon, which you have a chance of getting every day, especially if you've ended up enjoying the game.
The devs are constantly updating the game, usually with new weapons and the like once per week, usually a monthly "special event", bi-weekly reward events, and adding new Warframes and Quests (a major expansion, the War Within, is supposed to come in November).

First off, I've only had this game for about two weeks, in that time I have put in about 20 hours of game play. The game looks beautiful, like a truly pre-historic world. This review will only cover single player, as I don't play online and have no desire to do so. That being said, the game is insanely difficult on the default setting at the begining. I spent hours getting killed by a Troodon, which every time it attacked me it put me to sleep, then would run in circle like a moron until I was about to wake up, then bite me again starting the whole process over. At the time I had no tamed beasts, cloth "armor" and I did not know stimberries would wake you up. Each time this happened, it would take about 45 minutes to die, and this kept happening to me, about a dozen times. I went online to find a solution, all I could find was "Troodons don't spawn on the beach, must be a Dilophasur" No, indeed it was not, shortly after reading the afore mentioned post, I purposefuly found a Dilophasur and tamed it. Troodons poison with their bite, while the others spit (acid?) at a target. I almost forgot to mention, when I first installed the game, it wouldn't load at all. "can't find shooter.exe" (at the time I had it installed to my external drive) so I unistalled and reinstalled on C:, it worked, but I had only 12% space left on the drive. Of course, that just wasn't going to work for me, uninstalled and reinstalled on the external again, and (for some unknown reason) it worked. then the repeating death hours, then, the next day I went to load it up and try again and *noop* "Steam recomends you validate your files"...k..."two files are missing and need to be re-downloaded"...k... revalidate...all good! but the whole pocess take about 30-40 minutes and I have to do it EVERY time I load the game. one way to rectify this is to play in offline mode. I found out eventually, that this bug is caused by using settings different frome the default ones, evry time you load up, steam trys to sync your local files with cloud files, and registers that the config file doesn't match, thus triggering the revalidation and download. Now, as for the game itself, awesome cocept, cool gameplay, and who doesn't want a pack of furocious dinos doing thier bidding? I have my PC hooked up to my television as the only monitor, and use steam pretty much like someone uses a console. So, I've been trying to play ARK with a controller, not exactly easy, sometimes (maybe 3-5 times since I've started) the right joystick doesn't work. but the left does as well as the rest of the functions. Exiting and reloading seems to fix it, so far. Combat, gathering and building are fairly smooth, but transfering items is a pain. Screen navagation is near inpossible, when tring to level up your stats are all lit up so you can't tell what you are hilighting, and when you try to scroll down on the Engrams page either nothing happens or it jumps all the way to the bottom. Honestly, I hope they come up with a better user interface and control scheme for the console. If they manage to work out these few bugs I'd happily give the game 10/10, but as it is currently, it's about 8/10.

Hey people, it's a game.  If you like figuring out things on your own, you like dinosaurs, and/or you like survival games, then this game is for you.
There is no tutorial for this game, you wake up on a beach, (mostly) naked, and it is up to you what to do next.  It will frustrate you, but when you get a grip on what to do next, providing you haven't been killed already, the next challenge will slap you right in the nuts.  It's a thrill-ride all the way.
This game can be very addictive.  You may start playing around 4pm, and look up to see that it is 3am.  Where the hell did all that time go????
There are 3 official free maps to play on, The Island, The Center, and now Ragnarok.  There are also several unofficial maps, that were created by players, which Ragnarok use to be one of them. There is one additional map official map that is a pay to play map, and it is called Scorched Earth.  No beaches, (almost) no water, but tons and tons of sand.
And the choices don't end there.  Each map has the option of being a PvP or PvE map, depending on the server, and there are many official servers that offer strictly "vanilla" gameplay.  It's your choice on how brutal you wish to play.  Are you a masochist?  PvP is the way to go then.  But that isn't all for server choices...ARK also allows private servers to operate within the realm of the game, where you can find a multitude of more choices, many of which include mods to enhance the playing experience.  This all is insane...but it don't end there...yes, there is more....
Also within the realm of the official gaming experience, from time to time, they have special events designed to test out how good you think you are.  Games such as SoTF...or survival of the fittest.  Pretty much a 1-3 hour event (not exactly sure how long it lasts) in a team vs. team, wherein your team must gather as much weapons and dinos before going head to head in a frantic combat to determine the winner.
To further the game experience, and to add extra challenge, there is a version of the game, that has no advanced weapons, where the highest tech you can muster, is a musket rifle.  This version of the game is called "Primative +".
If you wish, you can even purchase your very own server (it will be an unofficial server of course), for a low monthly fee of around $13/mo. USD (last time I checked).  There you can invite players you like, ban players you don't, and be the king of the world.
Last, but not least.  If you are not into all the drama of playing with others, you can even go solo, and play alone.
Now for the bad news.  As of this review, there is a lot going on within the Wildcard Studios world, as they spit-polish the game for it's tentative Worldwide release in August 2017, and there are a lot of updates going on, servers will be disrupted a lot.  You may get into the game, and play for 30 minutes, and learn the servers are going down for an update.  The game can crash a lot also, but in the end, you will keep coming back for more.  I have.

A ninja in space, now how does that sound? Freaking amazing, and that’s what this game delivers. Warframe is a third-person shooter that incorporates all the shooting a gun fanatic can imagine with the grace and mobility a ninja wielding throwing stars and katanas needs to kill, from sliding on the ground and jumping off the walls.
The graphics are among the best you can have, even running it on low specs, there is detail in the suits from its mesh to the folding, weapons are all superb, light reflects and makes colours look great when walking or running around. In the world you will get rain, sand storms, you will see tropical (alien) forests, beacons of light in the form of technological complexes.
The sound is good even if you could have more ambient music variety, for example in the ship you have a frequency radio that picks up a rather short loop of communications. The sound effects are again good but at times not as rich as the environments seem to be, weapons have expectable noises and vary but not by a huge factor, if it shoots a bullet it kind of always sounds the same but with a slightly different pitch, none of this will make a difference when you are in a blood rage murdering hordes of enemies.
This is the cherry on top, gameplay. You will have to learn to walk before you run, but after you run you will start flying, off the walls and in all directions. This game has the most satisfying gameplay I encountered in a while, not only you will master the characters movement but even the flow of weapon usage is great, on the melee weapons different stances allow you to customize the way you wield a blade or hammer. There are two major different game modes, the one and for the vast majority of the game is the one where you control your character and walk about, here like I said the gameplay is superb, the only problem can occur when players try to either force walk in non-passable areas or trying to get out of the map box, both rather avoidable. Now the second mode is where you control your character using a deep space winged rig suit, the Archwing is indeed not so simple to control and the gameplay can become awkward, it can be fun in vast space areas, doing loops and dashing around, but it loses all that fun in narrow areas like many maps have. Indeed you will either move much slower and avoid collisions or try to drift past obstacles only to hit most of them and losing your orientation once again. To make this a bit worse the Archwing is also use in underwater exploration, a very small part of some maps, here all the fun is removed and replaced with slow moving machines that do none of the cool maneuvers you love in the game. This is the only reason gameplay does not get a 10 out of 10, but fortunately in this rather huge game it plays a small part.
The game features an ever growing number Frames, classes if you will, all have different abilities and can impact a group in different ways, from raw damage to healing or buffing your team, combined with what will seem to a new player as a never ending amount of weaponry, you have yourself a whole lot of game to play. If you are the type of gamer that loves collecting all, this game will consume you. Frames, main weapons, side weapons, melee, dog pets, cat pets, sentry pets, ships, even bobble heads. Not to mention all the cosmetics to make your frame unique.
The story of the game is ever evolving, it comes as a set of revelations, you start off very much in the dark and learn more and more, so far only one main plot twist has occurred but the developers are always adding content and future plot twists are expected. Whit out telling spoilers, I can say that you will find a distant time period were the powers present are in struggle, you will act as balance and, well you will find more. Frames for the most part come with a story, except for the initial ones. The lore is present via messages, images you will collect along information, videos, and all over the maps. There is a language that you can decipher. Plus you are always reminded that your actions have consequences.
At this point I wold like to address an important part of any free to play game, the economy. This game contains like most a cash shop, but unlike most the premium currency (platinum), is obtainable not only by paying with real money. The game trade system indeed allows players to trade all matter of goods, for other goods and platinum, and this is where it gets interesting, there is a market for all, yes you don’t need to move mountains to obtain something that is worth platinum to another player. Also the items in the shop bought by platinum are mainly either boosters, like resource farming, or cosmetics, none giving a gameplay advantage.
In conclusion, this game is a superb example that the free to play is not a bin of lost ideas and low budget content, this is an A grade game and I recommend it to all lovers of the genre..

This is a very grindy and self-motivated game about loot for loot's sake; that said, you are a backflipping space ninja with unreasonable superpowers and overpowered weaponry. Basically the core gameplay revolves around running a few basic game types like defense and capture to gear up, level equipment, and collect resources for more equipment to do it all better. Though it is a grind, it's one about setting entire armies on fire or clawing them apart with your bare hands with your buddies.
I didn't think much of it at first, and it certainly looks like a standard pay-to-win time waster, but after a few hours I found myself having some honest-to-goodness fun and a fair environment to have it in. The movement is exciting and the community is refreshingly polite and helpful. It's fairly easy and efficient to grind out valuable items that other players will buy for premium currency, so even the most luxurious MTX cosmetics are within reach.
I do feel a small monetary investment (I've paid $5 so far) is necessary to feel comfortable, but that is a necessary evil of funding a game like this.  The decisions of the dev team can be questionable, but the core gameplay is solid. Just expect the usual "devs plz" ordeal and trust that the overall direction is stable and positive.
Overall I give it an 8/10. It's far from perfect, but for a free (or very cheap) game, it's a heck of a time.
I still enjoy logging in and killing 4 grineer with one arrow while spreading toxic spores over entire maps, and that's enough reason for me to keep playing.

Warframe is a cooperative online third person shooter where players take on the role of Tenno, space ninjas in technologically-advanced exoskeletons that give them superhuman powers. Engage in action-packed combat as you run along walls, go down zip lines, perform acrobatics, and cut down enemies with your sword, or blast them all to kingdom come with the vast arsenal of weapons at your disposal. While Warframe does have several PvP options, Warframe is primarily a PvE game. Choose from three starting classes and 17 advanced classes, each with their own roles and playstyles. Work together with friends as you take on armies of space grunts, walking turrets, and hordes of mindless zombies in a stunning futuristic sci-fi world.
Warframe Key Features:
1. Good Variety of Warframes – choose from a large pool of warframes and customize them with  mods to match your needs.
2. Smooth Moves – play with familiar FPS controls and use ninja/parkour moves to position yourself.
3. Constant Updates – the dev team is always tweaking and updating the game based on players' comments.
4. Awesome Graphics and SFX – the graphics are amazingly fluid and the music heightens the action-packed atmosphere of the game.
You can run Warframe missions with up to three other players, and while flying solo is definitely possible in the early going or when you're grinding for experience or resources, teaming up becomes necessary as you tackle tougher missions. Fighting your way through fiendish hordes with the help of some allies can be very satisfying, especially when there's a good mix of powers in play. Coordinating with friends is the best way to get this kind of experience, because jumping into matches or having folks join you can lead to lopsided situations. If there's a gap in player level or a mismatch with the mission challenge, as often happens, your cooperative missions can devolve into all-out sprints as players easily cut their way through enemies they far outclass.
To minimize such gaps, you can focus on playing only new missions, since those tend to scale toward the upper bound of your capabilities. However, many of the environments in Warframe are reused frequently. You may be taking a different route through an enemy ship or encountering different environmental effects in the asteroid base, but you can't escape seeing the same spaces over and over again. This repetition combines with the lack of enemy variety (each species has only a handful of different units) to make many Warframe missions feel very similar to one another.
To spice things up, you may want to acquire a new gun, a new melee weapon, or a new suit. Warframe is free to play, but you must spend either time or money to acquire new items. Currently, new suits range roughly from $5 to $25, with new weapons falling close to the lower end of that spectrum. Alternatively, you can purchase blueprints to craft new weapons and suits using in-game currency. It takes a significant amount of time to save up the money for a new blueprint, and then you must spend even more time acquiring the resources to actually craft it.
Even if you skip the lengthy crafting process by using real-world currency, you still have to spend time leveling up your new gear. Jumping into a high-level mission with a brand-new suit is a death sentence, so it's back to lower levels to grind for experience. As your gear levels up, you gain more slots to modify it using boosters picked up during combat. Adding abilities to suits, improving the attributes of your gear, and imbuing your weapon with elemental damage are just some of the things mods can do. Unfortunately, the system to apply and improve mods is poorly laid out and barely explained, leaving you on your own to figure things out.
Some problematic menus pale in comparison to Warframe's real problem: a pervasive tendency toward repetition. Whether you're forging ahead with a high-level suit or leveling up a new one, Warframe repeats enemies, environments, and scenarios too frequently. Without new challenges for your combat abilities, the excitement soon dries up, leaving you without a compelling reason to keep playing. This free-to-play shooter is still technically in beta, so changes may come that make a substantive difference. But as of now, Warframe's interesting combat mechanics are too quickly overcome by the grind of repetition.

This review is for PVP as i have never played anything else. I have maybe spent 15-20 hours single player to learn the game a bit.
Most people here complain PVP is♥♥♥♥♥♥ alpha tribes wipe everyone  etc. Any I say, yes, that's true.  But thats a PVP SURVIVAL game for you.I have never been in an alpha tribe, my biggest tribe were 3 active people and one 1 i have never seen ingame.
Still we always survived. Had lots of tames, that lived for weeks, metal bases, vaults, everything. and no-one played more than 4-5 hours a day (evenings etc). And only after ca 300 hours our main base was completely wiped.
This game is a survival game. It's more difficult than dark souls (where i have over 600 hours alltogether) and you need to take it like that. You die? you respawn.
Your dinos die? Thats what they do.
Dont tame 1000 dinos and save them, dont save 1000s of metal, use it and build it. Find hidden spots to build small hideouts. Place your fabricators, smithys somewhere in the open.
Noone destroys them for fun is they are empty. Make them publically accessible.
Build many small houses with beds, so you always have somewhere to respawn. Hide some metal tools over the map.
Build many small bases. Dont put everyxthing into one base. And you will never loose everything and you will never have to start from scratch.
Build up your stuff, level up and always search for really hidden spaces (there are tons of them). And raid what you can yourself.
And then, once you can build c4/rocket launchers, go and raid the alpha tribes. It's not impossible, just difficult, Thats what makes the game fun.
Imagine the rage of them when you kill their 230+ lvled kraken or Rex.
When you with one tribe member raid their whole base which 10 people spent building.
And all from the shadows.
Use the possibility to port between maps for your own good aswell.
Go to the desert rto farm metall.
Go to the island to gather easily cementing paste and polymer from penguins. Have a few ships.
In a week of playing a few hours a day you can already be full metal, with vaults, guns, dinos. Even if you play alone.
All those people complaining are simply not suited for a PVP SURVIVAL.
If you want an easy game, play PVE. If an improved minecraft with far bette crafting, dinos and Roleplay is not for you,
then ARK is not for you. Not every game is for everybody

PvP is awful and the official servers take millions of years to tame a dodo, but here is the good thing about the game. I play normally on PvE because i love making new friends and working together on tames to progress. It is a lot of fun to go around killing everything later in the game, but it starts to get old. That's why there is caves and new bosses to fight. I have not yet gotten too far because it takes a long time to get to the boss era of the game, and it needs A LOT of people to beat some of the bosses. That is why mods are a thing for others to use. Mods are free and there are many servers that are modded and PvE. PvP modded is off the table because how hard that would be for new users, but I probably have half my hours in modded Ark and have in regular Ark. Mods just add so much new content and are constantly updated for the user, and it's made by the fans of the game who know what is wrong with Ark and what is right. I think Ark was a great investment for the money i put on the game, and there are frequent sales for the game.
Summary:
1. PvP and Official servers are bad and op for alpha, so avoid it at all cost.
2. PvE gets boring after the 20th hour you play it, so make some friends and beat bosses and caves.
3. Mods are a thing, and they add so much great content and hours of playing.
4. If you get bored grinding and waiting, just turn up the harvest gathering, xp gain, and taming speed.
5. Single Player is great for casual gamers that don't play Ark that much because if you turn it off, the world doesn't run.
6. If you hate Ark, that means the game is boring to you, or that someone raided you and just play PvE you wimp.
